title: The Complicated Nature of Panthers Legend Cam Newton's 2027 HOF Case
full_text:
Five former NFL players achieved football immortality this past weekend when they were officially inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton.
Legends of the game like former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees and Arizona Cardinals wideout Larry Fitzgerald both received their coveted gold jackets alongside Carolina Panthers icon Luke Kuechly.
With this year's class officially in the books, everybody's attention has now turned to the list of names that will officially become eligible for the HOF for the first time next year, a list that includes another Carolina icon, Cam Newton.
No single player personified the Panthers throughout the 2010s as Newton did. The former first-overall pick and eventual NFL MVP took the league by storm from the moment he came out of the tunnel at Bank of America Stadium as a rookie, and his impact on both Carolina and the league as a whole is still felt today.
There's no denying that the man dubbed "Super Cam" is rightfully viewed as a Carolina legend, but his Hall of Fame case isn't as cut-and-dried. CBS Sports analyst Bryan DeArdo recently broke down Newton's case for earning a gold jacket, and it was complicated, to say the least.
"Meteoric highs and lows largely embody Newton's career," DeArdo writes. "In 2015, for example, he won the league MVP while leading the Panthers to a 15-1 regular-season record and an NFC title. He had a forgettable Super Bowl, however, marked by his lack of urgency in recovering his second fumble of the game, which ultimately set up the Broncos' game-clinching score. Newton also had a short prime that was likely the byproduct of being one of the greatest running quarterbacks in NFL history. It came at a price: exposing himself to major hits."
As DeArdo lays out, Newton's career was one of incredible highs followed by some pretty significant lows. In his prime, there arguably hasn't been a single quarterback as physically imposing as Cam, combining elite athleticism with the kind of size nobody had ever seen at the position before or since.
His 2015 MVP campaign illustrated just how untouchable Newton was at his absolute peak, but the way things ended against the Broncos in Super Bowl 50 has regrettably (and unfairly) tainted that legendary season in the minds of many.
There's also the fact that, while Newton's prime was truly elite, it was unfortunately cut short by his bruising style of play, which has further blurred his HOF case.
All in all, the likelihood of Cam joining Kuechly and other franchise legends like Julius Peppers and Sam Mills in Canton is murky at best. That being said, his status as a legend in Carolina was cemented long ago, and that's something that can never be taken away.

title: Taylor Moton's RT Rank Highlights Immense Loss Panthers Suffered
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are gearing up for what is likely to be a very pivotal season for several reasons, and they will be entering this crucial campaign without one of their key pieces on offense, veteran right tackle Taylor Moton.
Moton, who has been with the Panthers since the team drafted him in the second round back in 2017, was officially ruled out for the start of the season after a blood clot was discovered in his lung in June.
All signs point towards the veteran big man making a full recovery, but the Panthers will still be forced to make do without one of quarterback Bryce Young's key blockers up front for at least the first few weeks of the season, which is a major blow no matter how one looks at it.
Anybody who watched Carolina's offense last season knows just how important Moton's steady presence on the right side of the line was, and Bleacher Report's recent positional rankings further hammer home how massive losing Moton truly is.
Per Bleacher Report's rankings , Moton is currently listed as the 12th-best right tackle in the NFL with a 73 overall grade, firmly within what they term their "Reliable Contributor" tier.
"Moton remained Carolina's steadiest offensive lineman in 2025, starting 15 games and continuing to win with the well-rounded, low-volatility skill set that has defined his career," BR explains.
"Moton's value is rooted in timing, technique and reliability more than overwhelming physical traits. In pass protection, he gets out of his stance efficiently, reaches his landmarks on time and uses active, precise hands to establish early leverage and disrupt the timing of rushers."
"In the run game, he is more positional than forceful, but he understands angles, fits blocks on schedule and can seal or wall off defenders when his footwork stays tied to his hands."
"Moton does not consistently overwhelm opponents with power, movement or finishing ability, but his technique, availability and down-to-down consistency still make him a dependable starting right tackle. He is a classic greater-than-the-sum-of-his-parts veteran whose value is often easier to appreciate inside the building than from the outside."
Any time a team loses a key starter on the offensive line, even for just a few games, it tends to throw the entire offense out of whack. Steadiness at the tackle positions, in particular, is key to a well-balanced offense.
If Moton’s injury wasn’t already bad enough, star left tackle Ikem Ekwonu is also sidelined while he recovers from the knee injury he suffered during Carolina's wild-card loss to the Rams last January and isn't expected to be back until later in the season, if at all.
Replacing one tackle is already a massive challenge for any team, but having to replace both is almost impossible without a noticeable decrease in offensive output. In a division as tight as the NFC South and with an early schedule as difficult as Carolina's, this could lead to the team putting themselves in an early hole that could prove extremely difficult to dig out of.

title: With Final Carolina Panthers Top 100 Rank, 1 Thing is Abundantly Clear
full_text:
The NFL top 100 list is still releasing its rankings as we wind down the offseason and get ready for preseason and Week 1. The Carolina Panthers have had four players ranked before yesterday. Bryce Young is slotted at 98th overall, Derrick Brown at 90th, Tetairoa McMillan at 87th, and Jaycee Horn at 76th.
Even though some of those rankings were surprises , no one thought Young would make the list.  It wasn't totally shocking to see McMillan make the list, but it still didn't feel like a guarantee.
That isn't to say they aren't good; both their position groups are so deep with talent throughout the league that they could've missed the cut.
Brown and Horn were locks; it was just a matter of where. That left one Panthers player who is extremely deserving of a top-100 spot; it was just a matter of where.
Slotting in at No. 27 on the NFL's top 100, new Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd. The former Jacksonville Jaguars LB signed with Carolina on a three-year deal worth up to $45 million in free agency.
This ranking is perfect. Coming off a season in which Lloyd earned his first Pro Bowl appearance and second-team All-Pro honors, there aren't many inside linebackers who can be ranked above him at this point. Lloyd's 5 interceptions tied for second in the NFL last season.
Updated list of #Panthers on the NFL Top 100 so far: Bryce Young | 98. Derrick Brown | 90. Tetairoa McMillan | 87. Jaycee Horn | 76. Devin Lloyd | 27. If this is the end of the list, who got snubbed? pic.twitter.com/xfXaRsrXWt
With this ranking, it means the Panthers won't have anyone else make the NFL top 100. If another Panther did make it, then that would just be incorrect. Mike Jackson at cornerback could be a consideration, but not over Devin Lloyd at 27th.
Since Carolina won't have anyone else ranked, it leaves one big takeaway on Carolina's presence inside the top 100.
Brown being ranked 90th and being the second-lowest-ranked Panther on this list is purely absurd. Carolina's anchor on the defensive line had a great year coming off an injury, notching 73 tackles, 5 sacks, and 7 passes defended. Brown also ranked second in the NFL in run stops according to PFF.
Interior defensive tackle is also one of the most important positions in football. Brown is a consensus top-10 DT, meaning he should be ranked much higher than 90th overall.
Entering 2026, both Brown and Lloyd will be crucial to Carolina's defense rising to elite status. The Panthers ranked 16th in overall defense last season and, on paper, should be much improved.

title: Non-QB MVP for Carolina Panthers May Not Be Who You Think
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have one preseason game under their shoulder pads, a 33-30 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals in Canton, Ohio. Next up are the Buffalo Bills this Saturday evening at Orchard Park.
Meanwhile, the analysis and predictions for the 2026 NFL season continue to pour in regarding a variety of topics. For instance, Jared Dubin of CBS Sports looked at all 16 squads in the NFC , and chose a 2026 Most Valuable Player—with the stipulation that the individual not be the club’s quarterback. So sorry, Bryce Young.
Hence, when it came to Dave Canales’s reigning NFC South champions, Dubin’s selection was former Miami Dolphins’ first-round edge rusher Jaelan Phillips. He spent the second half of 2025 with the Philadelphia Eagles after being acquired by the Birds via trade. This offseason, the five-year pro joined Carolina via a massive four-year, $120 million deal this offseason.
Where’s my Jaelan Phillips jerseys @Panthers (I need them in blue or white) pic.twitter.com/wE88T4vIyt
“When healthy, Phillips has been very good both rushing the passer and stopping the run,” explained Dubin, “he’s heading into his physical prime at 27 years old. Carolina desperately needs someone to get after the quarterback after struggling to do so for the last several seasons…”
That would certainly be an understatement. Dating back to 2023, the Panthers have finished 27, 32, and 30 sacks, respectively. Do the math and that’s a total of 89 quarterback traps—the fewest in the league over that span.
Canales’s club certainly has its share of talent not playing the quarterback position that could vie for team MVP accolades. There are wide receivers Tetairoa McMillan (the 2025 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year) and Jalen Coker, defensive lineman Derrick Brown, new starting linebacker Devin Lloyd, and cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. So what could Phillips do to be a difference maker in his first season with the franchise?
He could start by finishing among the club’s top five tacklers while leading the team in sacks, finishing in double digits in that latter category. It’s worth noting that the last Panthers’ player to total at least 10 QB traps was Brian Burns (12.5) in 2022. Keep in mind that Phillips totaled a career-best 8.5 sacks during his rookie campaign, so getting to the quarterback 10-plus times would certainly be uncharted territory for the five-year pro.
Making those sacks count would also help. The last Panthers’ player to force more than two defensive fumbles in a single season was Burns (3) way back in 2020. Phillips has totaled only two forced fumbles in 65 total contests (including playoffs). And when it comes to takeaways, the still-young defender has picked off only one pass and recovered just five fumbles in five NFL campaigns.
Simply put, Carolina’s high-priced addition likely must come up with the best season of his career. If he does that, he may not only capture team MVP honors, the Panthers’ defense could very well be a Top 10 unit in the league.

title: Tre'von Moehrig Misses Top 32 Rank, Panthers Should Trade for Safety Who Made It
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers signed star safety Tre'von Moehrig to a three-year, $51 million deal ahead of the 2025 season. It was one of many moves that helped spur a league-worst defense to mediocrity.
Moehrig has been as advertised , excelling in the run game and giving Ejiro Evero a chess piece to work with. He's been hailed as one of the league's most versatile players .
That said, he did not rank within the top 32 on PFF's list of the best safeties. He ranked pretty low in that metric, actually around 50th-best. While PFF grades are not perfect, it is a little troubling to be ranked so low.
Fortunately, there is a top-32 safety who made the cut and could be available via trade, and the Panthers ought to jump on that.
Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker did not request a trade, but let's examine his situation for a moment. The Cardinals are pretty bad and they play in an absolutely loaded division. They need assets, and Baker is both aging and expensive.
Plus, with two years of team control left, the safety would likely fetch a pretty decent trade return for the Cardinals. Now, for the Panthers: they need safety help, and Baker would give them a solid duo to play over the top.
Moehrig is a run-defending safety who struggles badly in coverage, allowing nearly 80% of passes to be completed while in coverage. Lathan Ransom, Zakee Wheatley, and Nick Scott are somewhat decent options next to Moehrig, but they're no Baker, at least not yet.
Baker just made the cut for PFF's top 32, ranking 32nd. Bradley Locker wrote, "An eight-time Pro Bowler, Baker is a well-respected player — but one whose advanced statistics paint a more cloudy picture. Baker has sat below a 65.0 overall PFF grade in two of the past three seasons."
Unfortunately, Baker's coverage has dipped in recent years, but he's still a much better and more proven commodity than any of the three options the Panthers are currently working with. Ransom and Wheatley are young, and Scott just isn't that good.
Baker is obviously on the decline, but that just means he can play until Ransom or Wheatley is ready to start full-time, mentoring them and providing improved safety play in the interim. It's a win-win for everyone involved, including the asset-needy rebuilding Cardinals.
And despite Locker's harsh description, Baker did make the top 32, and Moehrig didn't.

title: Panthers’ Bryce Young, Mike Jackson Might Both Be Headed For Career Years
full_text:
Training camp is in full swing as the 2026 season rapidly approaches. With training camps, tension and scuffles always come up, whether it's within teams or in joint practices.
That remains true for the Carolina Panthers , who have been in training camp longer than any other team in the league. Carolina started camp back on July 23rd since they had to prep for the HOF game .
With even more time in camp before the season, it gives more opportunity for scuffles and dust-ups in practice, and this week has been the apex of that thus far.
On Monday, the biggest fight of camp broke out. RB Jonathon Brooks was rushing the ball and was reportedly hit hard by one of the safeties, either Nick Scott or Lathan Ransom; both had been reported to be the one to hit Brooks.
Big fight here. Started when Lathan Ransom tried to hit Jonathon Brooks on a run. Bryce Young took offense. He and Mike Jackson were jawing. An offensive lineman stepped in. Someone got hit in the head.
That’s not the important piece, though, since Brooks is okay. What came after the hit was Panthers star cornerback Mike Jackson getting into it with offensive lineman Luke Fortner, and also heavily jawing with Carolina’s most important player.
Young and Jackson were seen jawing heavily at each other after that play and throughout practice on Monday. The arguments escalated to the point that Jackson and Young had to have a long conversation after practice, along with Scott.
Scott commented on the matter and said the conversation revolved around keeping the team safe while maintaining an appropriate level of physicality. The best quote from Scott on the matter was “If practice was all kumbaya, I’d be worried. But it’s not.”
Later Scott said: “If practice was all kumbaya, I’d be worried. But it’s not.” https://t.co/9FKNRykj5R
Scott’s on the money here. This is competition at the end of the day, and the best way for Carolina to prepare for the season is to compete at the highest level possible at camp.
This situation mirrors another notorious training camp scuffle in Panthers history, one involving the same position groups.
Back in 2015, QB Cam Newton and CB Josh Norman got into a huge scuffle at training camp, which had to be separated by basically the entire team.
To the damn date! The prophecy has begun https://t.co/lIYobYGjkU pic.twitter.com/9juTlz0XUu
Maybe it’s a correlation, maybe it’s not, but the Panthers finished the regular season 15-1 and made the Super Bowl that year. Cam Newton won NFL MVP, and Josh Norman was first-team All-Pro.
Now, over 10 years later, Young and Jackson keep the tradition of QB-Corner animosity going, and if anything, it’s a good sign for the Panthers.
Competitive spirit is higher than ever in Carolina, and that will only help the Panthers going forward. Young and Jackson are focal points on both sides of the ball and could be in for huge years in 2026.

title: Bears Giving Long-Awaited Update on Where Stadium Situation Stands
full_text:
It's been quite a while since Bears president Kevin Warren and team owner George McCaskey discussed anything at length about their stadium plans .
It's finally going to happen on Thursday after coach Ben Johnson holds his regular pre-practice press conference.
The last real meaningful comments from McCaskey on it came during the owners meetings, although he did provide a hint at what the tone will be when the Bears held a walk-through at Stevenson High School in Lincolnshire on Monday.
NBC Chicago caught McCaskey for a second and asked him where the stadium project stood.
“We’re doing some due diligence on a second site in Hammond,” McCaskey said. “I think Kevin and I will have more to report in the coming days.”
The real news was a one-word statement that rang out loud. McCaskey was asked if there was any movement on the Illinois side of the border regarding the stadium.
His answer was a rather emphatic, "No."
This has to be stunning to those in Illinois who believed the team might eventually get some sort of agreement from the state of Illinois after two different plans to help with infrastructure and the tax certainty they sought at their Arlington race track property was defeated in May.
All summer there had been talk of a potential special session in Springfield in August. The dates mentioned were sometime between Aug. 13 and Aug. 23. In particular, it was Aug. 19-20. The reason for this was the state fair begins Aug. 13 and it will be loaded with state legislators gladhanding because of the coming election. It would have been a good time to hold the special session if they planned to actually get behind a plan the Bears would support.
Nothing has happened yet and it appears to be dead in the water until at least the November session of the state legislature.
After the Chicago Bears’ $2 billion offer for a new stadium in exchange for predictable, long-term property tax rules, Governor Pritzker was unable to negotiate the deal and placed 100% of the blame on the Bears. When confronted with blowing billions of taxpayer dollars on… pic.twitter.com/HQFOcjXvn3
McCaskey and Warren had called late spring or summer a time when they wanted to announce a final decision. After the legislative defeat in Illinois, they said they were focusing on Indiana.
The initial Hammond site was near the Lost Marsh Golf Course in Hammond. The most recent site they've been examining is at a location called Wolf Lake Terminal. It is near Wolf Lake and a stone's throw from the Illinois border.
According to Des Plaines Valley News, Village of McCook's Major Terrance Carr has shared a proposal with The #Bears to have the team consider a 150+ acre site for their new stadium. The site is at 55th Street & East Avenue in McCook, a formerly quarry land. The proposal… pic.twitter.com/L7DszX8QNs
Illinois politicians and others have bandied about other ideas for the Bears but there have been no hints the team is even considering those. One was in McCook, a small southwest suburb of about 270 people with a huge tract of land. Another was the former U.S. Steel Works near the mouth of the Calumet River, a plan for redevelopment proposed by Illinois State Rep Curtis Tarver.
The Bears long ago stopped listening to Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson, who more or less stopped them from getting the Arlington Heights project done by opposing it, and forced them into crossing the border to get the project built.
Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson: “The city is being ran exceptionally well right now.” Meanwhile, Johnson is suffering from historically low approval ratings, Chicago remains mired in budget problems, CPS enrollment continues to decline, too many students are failing to meet basic… pic.twitter.com/DvMI0VjA0j
A plan providing what the Bears wanted at their Arlington Heights property has been proposed by State Rep. Martin McLaughlin of Barrington Hills, but no word of a vote on this has been brought forth and it seems no more likely than the other two ideas.
Gov. J.B. Pritzker has shifted his stance on this issue several times, always attempting to land in a position where he could claim a political victory. He has repeatedly played the billionaire card and said he isn't supporting any tax payer money to billionaires. However, the Bears have only asked for tax money for infrastructure. They're putting for the money to build the stadium themselves.
Indiana's plan to fund a stadium in or near Hammond has been ready to go after overwhelming passage of both legislative bodies, and Gov. Michael Braun's signature.
Chicago Bears executives are expected to deliver an update Thursday on the team's stadium plans, which officials in Indiana say continue to center on Hammond where there is ongoing due diligence at multiple locations. https://t.co/b3ryrYmvpy https://t.co/f6eZHipikN pic.twitter.com/SG0XYblw6c
Indiana had some disruption with its approach when Portage County didn't want to get involved in the hotel-entertainment tax being used to help fund the project but it's a small part of the overall plan. Their idea is to build the stadium and let the Bears run it. This way the Bears avoid taxes.
"When we get this across the finish line — we're in the due diligence stage — it's going to be one of the biggest things that's ever occurred to our state, not to mention the region," Indiana Gov. Mike Braun said according to Fox in Indiana. "So we're doing everything you need to do to make sure you get it done."
Braun didn't paint a good picture for Illinois, either, saying the "... urgency is of because they (the Bears) were wondering who was going to listen to them, where it was going to be, and we've done that pretty quickly, made it easy."
Braun said the Bears have been in contact with him twice weekly. It's unlikely Gov. Pritzker has been in constant contact with the Bears.
Illinois long ago frittered away its last, best hope for keeping the Bears as the "pride and joy of Illinois," as their fight song says. It would be no surprise Thursday if McCaskey and Warren simply announce they're building the Indiana stadium.

title: One Expected Starting Bears Training Camp Battle Never Materialized
full_text:
Shortly after the draft and throughout the offseason, the Bears' center position kept getting mentioned in trade speculation.
The thinking all along was Iowa rookie Logan Jones had been taken in Round 2 before many draft analysts expected and the Bears had signed Garrett Bradbury as a failsafe or bridge to possibly a few weeks into the season after the rookie learned and became starter.  Once Jones had his bearings, Bradbury would immediately be expendable. Or so the thinking went.
With the first preseason game coming Saturday, this couldn't look more inaccurate. There never has been a battle for starting center.
Not only has Bradbury made all of the first-team snaps, but he has been forging the critical center-quarterback bond necessary for teams who ask as much from the center as the Bears' offense does. It's even gone off the field, where the two had a friendly competition going at the Bears' Monday team bowling excursion.
"I tried to get competitive with him," Bradbury said of Williams. "He was a much better bowler than I thought he was. I think he bowled a 190 in one of the rounds and I was trying to talk smack and I didn't have much to back it up. But it was fun."
Bears just wrapped up scrimmage (not tackling to ground). Some highlights: - In 1s vs 2s, Caleb to Kalif Raymond screen 25 yd TD - Devin Bush int of Bagent - D’Andre Swift (who had a couple other nice runs) absolutely trucked Dillon Thieneman @cbschicago pic.twitter.com/EdInjQnkmH
They didn't pay Bradbury to bowl, though, just follow Pro Bowl center Drew Dalman after his sudden and early retirement. The praise from Ben Johnson for what Bradbury has done so far further backs up the notion of Jones staying in the background and to learn the pro center position for most, if not all of this season barring injury.
"Extremely sharp, phenomenal communicator," Johnson said of Bradbury. "I mean, he’s loud, he’s clear, he’s decisive. Love where he’s at with all that. I think more than anything, he’s just been trying to feel us out in terms of the expectations that (O-line coach Dan) Roushar, myself, (offensive coordinator) Press Taylor, what we need out of that center position.
"It’s a little bit different from other places that he’s been and yet he’s doing a phenomenal job getting after it. The more reps we get, whether it’s protection-wise, run game-wise where Caleb can help, he might see things that Garrett doesn’t see and vice versa so we are all aligned and in the best position to execute the play. It’s good. It’s really good. I think they get along really well."
They've had their share of communication issues and there have been false starts in practices, some the result of cadence or snaps but some simply players moving early. It hasn't quite resembled last year when the Bears installed the offense and struggled to get plays off, but the flags have been irritants.
The top 10 #Bears based on PFSN Impact Scoring: 1. Darnell Wright (87.6) 2. Devin Bush (86.8) 3. Joe Thuney (84.4) 4. Coby Bryant (84.0) 5. Luther Burden III (83.8) 6. Colston Loveland (83.1) 7. Austin Booker (82.3) 8. D’Andre Swift (80.6) 9. Garrett Bradbury (80.4) 10. Jonah… pic.twitter.com/hZngfh6fGN
"Communication has gone well," Williams said. "We have gotten a lot better over these last couple days. The first couple days we were rolling, kind of like coach said, and then we had a couple off days where communication may have been a little off or cadence or things like that.
"And I think these past couple days we’ve gotten better with it and being more conscious of some of those small mistakes that show up and that happen. And so we have gotten better. And then, yeah, that’s my guy. We’re excited to go into battle together."
When Johnson called plays in Detroit, he had veteran Frank Ragnow as the successful presence at center. They went after Dalman immediately. Now they're seeing the evidence Bradbury can be a veteran type who understands what's unique about the position within Johnson's scheme.
"There’s a lot of ownership," Bradbury said. "I’ve had coaches say in the past, ‘You get the keys to the car.’ You get to take that ownership and make a lot of calls."
Bears training camp scrimmage takeaways: ▪️ Jedrick Wills played 1st half at LT Kiran Amegadjie 2nd half. Both were just OK but Wills had the slightly better day. The consistency still needs improvement—Wills had a false start, and Kiran was called for holding. ▪️ The offense… pic.twitter.com/V3pQfXRQI0
Making calls at the line for blocking change or communicating with Williams are keys, and really something a veteran is normally far more comfortable with than a rookie.
"I kind of love that piece of the game," Bradbury said. "Sometimes it’s a little bit like a puzzle, and you’ve got to solve the puzzle right before the ball is snapped and then you’ve got to do your job. That’s something I take a lot of pride in, not just getting the five O-linemen, but the tight ends, the running backs, everyone on the same page, whether it be run game or pass game.
"I relish it. I love it. I think it’s fun to play in. That’s where the film study and all the meetings and the coaches preparing you for certain looks all comes together. I’ve enjoyed it.”
It's at the line of scrimmage just prior to the snap where the QB-center communication becomes even more important in this scheme.
If Ozzy comes back healthy.  The Bears have a top 3 O line easily. I’d bet Logan Jones takes Bradbury’s job by mid season and never give it back. https://t.co/Ls0RyT407H
"There's a balance," Bradbury said. "There's certain plays where I can't do anything unless he (Williams) wants to and vice versa. At the end of the day it's all about being on the same page, so he needs to hear what I'm saying, I need to hear what he's saying.
"Coaches always say, if we're on the wrong page together, we're on the right page, so it's being together and understanding what we're all doing and what we're trying to get done."
When they're not false-starting, they've been getting things done. And the false starts have declined over the past several days.
None of this is going to hurt Bradbury's chances of holding this job throughout training camp, into the season, and possibly all year. Then his one-year contract will run out unless they see a reason to keep him around longer than the one year they had Dalman — through no fault of their own.

title: Ben Johnson: Caleb Williams' "Best Interception" of 2025 Proves How Great He Can Be
full_text:
Interceptions are not always bad, and quarterbacks are not always at fault for them. In fact, if they occur on fourth down and the intercepting team loses field position by coming down with the ball, then that's a net win for the offense.
We saw an example of that in the Chicago Bears' wild card matchup against Green Bay last season. Caleb Williams took the shotgun snap on 4th-and-6 on their own 40-yard line before rifling an interception into the awaiting arms of Packers cornerback Carrington Valentine at the 12-yard line. Green Bay lost 28 yards of field position by snagging the pick.
Intercepted by Carrington Valentine 🧀 GBvsCHI on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/iEJBLT6emo
As it turns out, that wasn't the only reason why Williams was smart to make that throw. Bears head coach Ben Johnson spent a day with The Athletic's Dan Pompei last week , and he provided some insight into that specific interception, calling it Williams' "best interception of the season".
"In the regular-season finale last year, the Bears defense threw an unusual look at Goff. Johnson thought it was a learning opportunity for Williams, so he showed him the play and gave him the solution. It was a brief conversation. Johnson didn’t emphasize it and didn’t think it would be an issue for Williams anytime soon, let alone the next game. But it was. And Williams was ready. He recognized the look and threw the ball right where he was supposed to. A receiver didn’t have it down like Williams did, however, and the route bust resulted in an interception." Pompei wrote.
At the time, virtually everyone thought that Luther Burden III, who was the unlucky receiver to be on the receiving end of the pass, ran the wrong route. An upset Williams was seen motioning to the pass-catcher after the play, so it was assumed that he was in the wrong for being on a different page than his QB.
As it turns out, they were right, but maybe not in the way everyone expected. We still don't know whether Burden was running the correct route, but we know Williams was reading a different book. One that most QBs with his level of experience probably wouldn't be fluent in after only week of learning the language.
The music coming out of Bears training camp last season wasn't exactly angelic . Growing pains were expected in the first year of Ben Johnson's offense, and they sounded relatively painful early on.
The same can be said for the first few weeks of last season, as Williams was struggling to keep Chicago's offense on the field, and they fell to 0-2 (against division rivals, no less) as a result. However, he had a breakthrough performance in their Week 3 matchup against Dallas. He threw for nearly 300 yards and 4 touchdowns in a 31-14 rout. With a 67.9% completion percentage, you could make a strong case that it was his best game of the season.
However, it wasn't an upward trajectory from that point. The flashes remained evident (and extremely bright), but he struggled with consistency over the next month and didn't look fully comfortable until the team's Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. That game became another strong candidate for his best game of the year, as he threw for 280 yards and 3 touchdowns, added 53 yards on the ground, and even caught two passes. He was all over the field and, most importantly, he looked composed and comfortable until the final whistle blew.
That Week 9 matchup was a launching point for the rest of the season . It was their first of five straight wins in November, and Williams developed a reputation as one of the league's most clutch playmakers . He showed that he not only had a firm grasp of Ben Johnson's offense, but that he could also thrive in it.
The next test will be to show that he can build on the promising performance without benefiting from the element of surprise. He's now a known commodity, and everyone is looking for him to take the next step .

title: How Chicago Bears Could Be Caught in a Tight NFC Playoff Squeeze
full_text:
A question posed by The Athletic's Jacob Robinson has to delight every NFC North team's fans, or at least satisfy many of them.
This thought is, could 2026 be the year every single team in the division makes the playoffs?
Robinson points out how t he Bears' division became the second in modern NFL history with every team finishing above .500 last season . He even makes the comment "Yes, even the J.J. McCarthy-led Vikings had a winning record (9-8)."
This probably infuriates Vikings fans since they actually finished ahead of the Lions in the NFC North standings and Detroit received the last-place schedule and an earlier draft pick.
Who has the best offense in the NFC North? 👀 🟣Vikings: Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones, Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson 🟠Bears: Caleb Williams, D’Andre Swift, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland 🔵Lions: Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown,… pic.twitter.com/BAIzWefzLW
While this would be the first time every team in the division made the playoffs in a season if it did happen, it wouldn't be the first year all of the current teams in this division made the playoffs. In 1994, the Bears, Packers, Lions and Vikings all made the playoffs but there were five teams in the old NFC Central then. Tampa Bay was the other team and did not get into the postseason.
WHERE THE BEARS TURNED AFTER LUTHER BURDEN'S INJURY REVEALS PLENTY
The problem with this idea for 2026 is not the quality of the talent or the teams. That talent level has become obvious over the last few years, and with Caleb Williams' rise even the Bears have a quarterback for once.
WOW! 😱😱😱 #Lions QB Jared Goff is already locked into Mid-season form with throws like this and it’s not even the first week of PRESEASON. Detroit is NOT playing nice this year, the rest of the league BEST be ready. 🍿👀 pic.twitter.com/zueRf3HlAP
What makes it unlikely this year is the NFC West and also the schedule.
When the black and blue division put four teams into the playoffs, they didn't face a scenario with three dominant teams in another division within the conference.
All 4 teams have a legitimate chance to win the NFC North.
The NFC West didn't just dry up and go away after last season. In fact, the Rams look much tougher now because of Myles Garrett and other changes. The Seahawks are defending champs. And the 49ers made offseason improvements, but also couldn't be expected to have as many injuries as last year when they made the playoffs despite bad health.
If three NFC West teams look like locks to get in again, then it's not going to be possible for all four NFC North teams to make it. There are only seven playoff teams and the NFC South and NFC East winners take up two of those. The best the NFC North could hope for would be two teams making it, possibly three if someone in the West falters.
The USA Today has released their official 2026 NFL record projections: Thoughts? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/EoK0JoeCzE
The other reason this can't happen is the schedule.
The Bears have what is judged to be the toughest schedule  based on last year's opponent winning percentages, but they also have the toughest schedule based on the Sharp Football Analysis method of using 2026 Vegas projected win totals. Often these preseason schedule projections are off, but any way you look at it the Bears face a formidable group of opponents.
Nfc north toughest division and best qbs
The schedule situation is even tougher than it looks because the top three NFC West teams this year generally have easier schedules than NFC North teams.
Based on the Sharp method, only one of the four NFC North teams has a schedule outside the top 11 for difficulty, and that's Detroit. However, in the NFC West none of the top three teams have schedules ranked in the top 11 for degree of difficulty. The only team in that division with a particularly tough schedule per Sharp is Arizona, tied  for third most difficult with Green Bay.
Colin Cowherd told me today that the NFC North is the best division in the NFL, and I don’t quite know how to process that idea.
If the Bears do what they haven't done since 2005-06 and make the playoffs in successive seasons, they'll most likely go in with one or no other divisional team in tow.
This probably wouldn't break anyone's heart in Chicago. After all, ask most Bears fans and they'll say their idea of the perfect season is winning the Super Bowl but only if the Packers don't win a single game. Insert the Lions or Vikings instead and that would do, as well.

title: Bears' Ben Johnson Promises a Touchdown for Darnell Wright is Coming
full_text:
When the Chicago Bears hired Ben Johnson to be their next head coach in 2025, his potential with the franchise was exciting but uncertain. On the one hand, Johnson was the architect of a juggernaut offense that turned the historically inept Detroit Lions into a Super Bowl contender. On the other hand, the Bears had their own history of ineptitude, and particularly when it came to the offense.
One thing that no one doubted, however, was that the Bears would soon become a leading purveyor of trick plays. Johnson didn't wait long to dig into his bag of tricks, calling a flea-flicker that resulted in Luther Burden's first NFL touchdown in a dominant Week 3 win over the Cowboys . We even got to see Caleb Williams be on the receiving end of a touchdown pass from DJ Moore at one point.
What will Ben Johnson come up with next in 2026? According to The Athletic's Dan Pompei, a big-man touchdown for Darnell Wright is coming. Pompei spent a day behind the scenes with Ben Johnson during Bears training camp, and he witnessed a brief exchange between the head coach and Wright.
"After the walkthrough, Johnson detours to congratulate offensive tackle Darnell Wright on his just-signed four-year, $116 million contract extension ," Pompei writes. "Wright wants more and asks his coach when Johnson will deliver on his promise of getting Wright a touchdown. It's coming, Johnsons says."
There's more than one way to skin a cat, as the saying goes. But when it comes to football, Johnson has three options for getting his prized offensive tackle a touchdown. On Thanksgiving Day of the 2024 season, Johnson, still the offensive coordinator in Detroit, dialed up a trick play for Penei Sewell that saw him stiff arming defenders as he attempted to throw a pass. It didn't work, but perhaps Johnson could add a new wrinkle to it and give Wright a shot.
However, just as Hugh Jackman's character in The Prestige wants to be the man who ends up on the stage, Wright probably wants to be the guy with the ball in the endzone. That means Wright would either have to take a handoff on a goal line situation or declare himself an eligible receiver and catch a pass from Caleb Williams.
We already know that the Bears have practiced the latter option. During minicamp last year, Johnson had his quarterbacks throw passes to the offensive line , and Wright went viral for his surprisingly acrobatic one-handed grab. Though we didn't see such a trick play emerge in 2025, perhaps Johnson could dial one up in 2026.
Of course, if Johnson wants to go old school, he could design an homage to William "The Fridge" Perry, one of the most famous members of the Bears' iconic 1985 team. Perry is perhaps best remembered for his two-yard touchdown run in Super Bowl XX . Like Perry, Wright is a massive human being, and one could easily see him bowling over linebackers for a two-yard touchdown scamper of his own.
We'll have to wait and see if Johnson can finally make good on his promise to Wright. One important thing to remember is that football isn't just a game for Johnson. This is his life, and he's not going to jeopardize a potential win just for a cool moment. In the same article by Pompei, Johnson said that he wants to beat the NFL single-season scoring record currently held by the legendary 2013 Denver Broncos (606 points in 16 games).
If Johnson wants to realize his twin goals of winning a Super Bowl and setting the scoring record in 2026, every posession, every snap will matter. I'm sure the fans would love to see Wright score a touchdown, and I believe Johnson will do his best to give him that opportunity, but at the end of the day, he's going to do what's best for the team.

title: 4 Chicago Bears Veterans Who Could Lose Their Starting Jobs in Preseason
full_text:
NFL preseason kicks off tomorrow, and the Bears host the Browns for their first exhibition contest on Saturday afternoon.
While some position battles have already been wrapped up (undrafted rookie long-snapper Beau Gardner and center Garrett Bradbury have earned congratulations), others still have yet to be decided. A few veterans are in a rock-solid position to make the active roster, but have a loose grasp on their respective starting jobs.
Which players will need to come out with a strong performance in the preseason (or at least hope their main competition for playing time doesn't make the most of their opportunity)?
Left tackle Braxton Jones has long been considered the front-runner for the starting left tackle job. However, a strong training camp performance from Jedrick Wills Jr. has leveled the playing field. Third-year man Kiran Amegadjie seemingly having a legitimate shot to win the starting job also complicates Jones' situation. As does the fact that he's now dealing with an undisclosed injury that's kept him out of practice over the past week.
Ozzy Trapilo speeding down the road to recovery might be incredible for the Bears, but it's another factor that could lead to Jones standing on shaky ground. It's fair to question whether the front office would have even brought him back for another year if they knew Trapilo could be ready much sooner than expected . He solidified the LT position after taking over the starting job in Week 12 last season, and it feels safe to assume he would've been the unquestioned starter if he hadn't ruptured his Achilles in the wild card matchup against Green Bay.
Is it cheating to call Cam Lewis a starter? Until we get any substantial update regarding star nickelback Kyler Gordon, we don't think so. Lewis is listed as the starting nickelback on the Bears' first official depth chart , and he's probably firmly ahead of the other players in the competition at this point. However, that's not to say that he's already got the starting job locked up.
Fourth-round selection Malik Muhammad II is the most interesting candidate that could challenge for the starting job. While he's listed as Jaylon Johnson's backup on the perimeter, the coaching staff has made an effort to get him experience at nickelback amid the swath of injuries they've experienced in the secondary.
Jaylon Jones and Josh Blackwell (who is interestingly listed as a safety on the first depth chart) are also candidates to win the starting slot corner job with a strong performance in the preseason. While they have a lot of ground to make up, their prior experience playing in the slot under Dennis Allen last season could work in their favor.
Gervon Dexter Sr.'s starting job wasn't expected to be in any danger after the NFL Draft. The biggest critique with their offseason among the masses was that they didn't make any splash additions to the defensive line. However, no one expected sixth-round selection Jordan van den Berg to already receive first-team reps in practice .
While Dexter is all but guaranteed to play a healthy amount of snaps on defense, his role is far from set in stone. Specifically, he will have to improve his get-off and ability to defend against the run if he wants to stay on the field on early downs. Jordan van den Berg is definitely the top candidate to eat into his playing time , but Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street can also make a strong case for themselves if they flash in the preseason.
Dexter is fighting for a new contract this season , and a decrease in usage wouldn't exactly look great on his free agency resume. He'll need to bring his A-game with the increased competition they added to the room this offseason.
The Bears' WR3 job is a social construct. The position isn't even included on the official depth chart, as they opted to include Cole Kmet as a starter alongside Colston Loveland. However, someone will have the edge (even if it's a slight one) in the pecking order.
Right now, Kalif Raymond's leadership and experience will probably give him the edge on the third receiver job. However, head coach Ben Johnson already hinted that the targets will go to whoever earns them in the specific routes and concepts. It's safe to assume the preseason performances will factor into that equation.
In the end, third-round selection Zavion Thomas and Jahdae Walker will probably receive their fair share of opportunities regardless of how they perform in the preseason . However, they can definitely grab a bigger piece of the pie if they play well over the next month.

title: Garrett Bradbury Finds Positives in Bears' Ground Game Emphasis
full_text:
The basis of Ben Johnson's offense is a powerful running attack but until Tuesday's practice there had been only bits and pieces of it because they hadn't fully leaned on it.
Then came the opening series of practice and it was goal line and short-yardage play s with full contact.
"That was ready or not, here we come," center Garrett Bradbury said. "It was physical."
It was also successful as D'Andre Swift broke a third-and-1 play to the outside for a long gain, had a few more substantial gains, and then Kyle Monangai hitting the right side for a big gain — the side defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo was manning.
There are 19 RBs who had >50% of Snaps. The Top 5 in EPA per Play On/Off Splits: 🥇D’Andre Swift: +0.129 (54.1% Snaps) 🥈Derrick Henry: +0.125 (55.9% Snaps) 🥉Jonathan Taylor: +0.096 (83.5% Snaps) (4) Bijan Robinson: +0.088 (79.2% Snaps) (5) Josh Jacobs: +0.071 (53.5% Snaps) pic.twitter.com/wOrLok3AAL
Then they went goal line and although the backs found sledding tougher, they eventually scored. Even Roschon Johnson got a goal-line carry and flashed his old form from 2023-24, when the team used him as the power back in close and short-yardage situations. He plowed into the end zone, then came out and Brittain Brown replaced him.
"You can't really see sometimes in training camp, except the live periods, exactly like what runs can look like sometimes," Bradbury said. "But I think we had a few today bust (for big gains), which was exciting."
Guys I have never been more in on: Dennis Allen Ben Johnson type scenes D'Andre Swift Colston Loveland Darnell Wright
The line was moving bodies out on crucial downs and it's what the ground game is all about.
Bradbury, a former Vikings center before his year with the Patriots, knew when he came to Chicago how Johnson would be committed to the run. It's an offensive lineman's dream, since they'd all rather tee off on defenses with the running game.
"I've seen coach Johnson's offense from afar for several years and there's a commitment to the run game, there's a commitment to the outside-zone game, and things that I feel like I excel in," Bradbury said. "I'm excited to get going with that. It feels like we've been in it forever but we're just getting started.
"It's going to take days like this. It's going to take more walkthroughs. It's going to take some joint practices. it's all gotta come together, but it's heading in the right direction."
Could the Bears look into trading Cole Kmet this offseason after Colston Loveland's emergence? @grotesports thinks Kmet is too important to the Bears' offense with his do-anything-needed attitude and blocking ability. So Grote is a "no" on trading Kmet. pic.twitter.com/RxC7s5w7CD
It didn't get a lot easier as the running mixed with passing throughout one of the toughest and longest workouts the Bears have had this camp. It wasn't quite on the level of last year's famed practice when Johnson turned everyone loose for an entire practice at full speed in pads. Still, it was a battle.
"Coach hit it on the head at the end of practice: We needed one of those days," Bradbury said. "You do during training camp. That’s what training camp’s for. You find out where you’re at mentally, physically, from a toughness level. You’ve got to dig deep.
"He said something last night like, ‘There’s two people on your shoulder: One that’s telling you to quit and one that’s telling you to keep going, and you’ve got to listen to the one that says 'keep going.’ So I had some of those inner dialogue conversations today, but it was good. We got some good work in."
Bears just wrapped up scrimmage (not tackling to ground). Some highlights: - In 1s vs 2s, Caleb to Kalif Raymond screen 25 yd TD - Devin Bush int of Bagent - D’Andre Swift (who had a couple other nice runs) absolutely trucked Dillon Thieneman @cbschicago pic.twitter.com/EdInjQnkmH
Bradbury's efforts are part of the reason for some early practice success on the ground. He was known for his mobility as a blocker in the running game.
"We're cooking right now with him out there," Johnson said. "Really pleased with what that's looked like and you can tell that he and (guard) Joe (Thuney) have played together (in college). There's natural rapport there and I think he's really taken to the (O-line) room.”
Getting the work in now with the running attack is preferable to later. Last year the Bears came into the regular season and the offensive line struggled to open holes. They averaged only 102.2 yards rushing in the first four games, then 153.3 yards a game on the ground from Game 5 through the playoffs.
The idea needs to be to hit the ground running, and the Bears showed in Tuesday's practice they're serious about being in that mode from the outset.
Playing center brings a lot of responsibility for Garrett Bradbury as part of Ben Johnson’s offense. pic.twitter.com/cwsKi7oGLP

title: The Good and Not So Good From Day 12 of Chicago Bears Training Camp
full_text:
The Chicago Bears completed Day 12 of training camp on Tuesday, and as was the case on Day 10 of training camp , practice had to be moved indoors due to inclement weather. Head coach Ben Johnson announced prior to practice that he was going to run a challenging scrimmage. The players received a game plan the night before, just as they would before a real game, but the coaches would call plays in the moment without a script.
According to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune , the offense started off hot with multiple chunk plays, but the defense responded and had the upper hand at the end. That said, here's the good and not so good from Tuesday, starting with the elephant in the room.
After Coby Bryant was carted off with a leg injury early last week, we initially heard that he would not need surgery and would only be out for eight to 10 weeks. Unfortunately, he did in fact get surgery on his knee and will now be out for four to six months. In a best-case scenario, Braynt would return for the last few games and be ready for the playoffs. But any longer than that and he will have missed the entire season.
There's no way to sugarcoat this one, folks. This is a devastating injury for the Bears, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen is going to be challenged to overcome this loss.
Coby Bryant's knee surgery was the second of two significant injury updates on Tuesday, and luckily for the Bears, the first one was overwhelmingly positive. General manager Ryan Poles told Bears reporters Adam Hoge and Adam Jahns that Ozzy Trapilo could return from his injury far sooner than expected . When asked if returning before the end of training camp was on the table, Poles said, "Potentially."
It's hard to overstate what a tremendous development this is for the Bears. Most fans and analysts expected the Bears to go almost the entire season without Trapilo. Instead, he could be back as soon as September. If all goes well, Chicago should once again feature one of the league's best offensive lines.
By all accounts, Caleb Williams has taken great strides in his development so far in training camp. He's far ahead of where he was at this point last year, and a Year 3 leap looks more and more likely. However, Tuesday's practice was a minor step back. Adam Hoge of CHGO Bears reported that Williams struggled with his accuracy, missing both Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond on deep shots after they broke wide open.
Even if Caleb Williams does indeed take a big step forward in 2026, there will inevitably be times when he struggles. That's when the Bears will need to rely on their running game, and that appears to be just as dominant as it was in 2025. Both D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai stood out in Tuesday's practice, picking up big gains in short yardage situations and running hard against the Bears' defensive front.
As Braxton Jones continues to recover from his minor injury last week, it's appearing less likely that he'll play in the Bears' preseason game against the Cleveland Browns this Saturday. Who will get the start in his stead, however, remains uncertain. Both Jedrick Wills Jr. and Kiran Amegadjie got snaps at left tackle on Tuesday, and according to Adam Hoge, neither one separated himself from the other.
Like much of the Bears' defense last year, T.J. Edwards was frequently banged up. He dealt with a broken hand that required surgery at the same time as a nagging hamstring issue, then saw his season ended in the Wild Card round against Green Bay when he broke his fibula. In all, he missed eight games, including the Bears' heartbreaking Divisional round loss to the Rams .
If his performance in Tuesday's practice is any indicator, however, Edwards is back with a vengeance. He was fired up all throughout practice, showing flashes of his 2023 season with the Bears when he racked up 155 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and three interceptions. The Bears are going to be leaning on his veteran leadership to keep the defense together through some major personnel changes this year.

title: Caleb Williams Staying Afloat Even Through Constant Receiver Change
full_text:
To Bears coach Ben Johnson, quarterback Caleb Williams seemed to plateau a bit after a hot start to training camp.
It's easy to understand why, and in a late, physical, Tuesday practice he appeared to be riding the up elevator again despite some earlier consistency issues. It isn't easy maintaining a good, steady flow of production when the receivers are changing each day due to injuries, and Williams seems to have made the adjustment whether it's all due to injuries or another factor.
“He’s  done a really good job," Johnson said. "I mean, he came out of the gate hot there. Those first four practices I thought were really, really good, and then as the volume has continued to go up – and it's my fault as much as anything, just because I think I've put in more this year on offense than I did a year ago by design. I just, I want it to feel like a lot right now – that there's been a level of plateau up to this point.
"Now that things will slow down from an installation point, I think we're going to see him continue to go on the upswing.”
Consistency with receivers would help even more. First he was throwing to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, with Kalif Raymond mixed in some. Then Burden went down and it was Raymond and Zavion Thomas. Thomas has what isn't a serious injury but can't practice right now. Williams was throwing effectively instead to Odunze, Raymond and second-year undrafted receiver Jahdae Walker. Then again, that whole missing pieces routine works both ways as the defense has had to cope with more than its share of injuries.
For Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson, camp is all about growth. pic.twitter.com/1B3w7OhhSO
"I know we have a couple guys down at different positions throughout offense, defense, things like that, even special teams obviously with a bunch of offensive and defensive guys being down," Williams said. "So it’s good being able to see guys step up and make plays because that’s what is going to have to happen throughout the year. You play 17 promised games and that doesn’t mean that every single game everybody is going to play.
"So being able to see the guys step up and have that mentality, that I’m gonna go out there and make plays and some guys made plays today and it was exciting to see and we’re going to keep chugging along."
In the key sequence to Tuesday's situational work, Williams faced a 99-yard field and needed two timeouts to kill off the clock for a win. He didn't like what he saw from in his end zone. Never one who needs to be coaxed out of the pocket, he rolled a bit right and found Rome Odunze for a 58-yard gain.
Ranking Chicago Bears players on if they were to suffer a season-ending injury that the season would instantly end with them: 1. Caleb Williams * The largest possible gap* 2. Joe Thuney 3. Luther Burden III 4. Coby Bryant 5. Darnell Wright On the edge of my seat 😅
On the next play, Williams went 27 yards downfield over the middle to Scotty Miller. Two plays and they nearly went the length of the field when they needed only to get two first downs for the win. They'll take it. The situation work helps greatly.
"Obviously, game week you dice it up throughout each day but being able to get a script and it was plays that we've gone over for the past, how long have we been in camp?" Williams asked. "Two weeks now, I guess? Two weeks. It's being able to just kind of go back over those plays mentally, just the small details. Whether I got to tell offensive line something specifically when I get up to the line of scrimmage, I got to tell wide receiver, we got to change protections or get to cover-zero, Just having a plan.
"And I think I've gotten stronger with that throughout this time, this year. So I definitely want to keep growing. And other than that, I just I want to keep getting better for the guys. I want to be faster with my process, to be able to help the O-line throughout you know long games and things like that, they're sitting in their stances, be able to get the communication throughout, you know whether it's on the ball or whether it's in the huddle, just be smoother and faster and everything so that I can be better for the guys and ultimately that helps us win."
Johnson sees more than just playing to the situations.
"I love the process he has right now," Johnson said. "I mean, he's coming in early. He's staying late after practice, getting extra reps with the route runners, he's taken complete control of what we're trying to do, and so we're on the right track.”
There is no negative side to any of this. Williams has seemed to grown into the role even more than he did at the end of last year. He said after last season he felt in training camp like he was downing.  Now he's able to handle the change he faces daily because of system knowledge. He's not going under.
Caleb Williams on making disciplined throws: pic.twitter.com/EkNBvX0mCa
"I'm head above water," Williams said. "I'm able to get new plays in and be able to go, you know, execute them in a positive manner, I would say better than I have in my past."
Williams said he's handling mistakes better when he does make one or if someone else does.
"And then just being able to encourage myself, being able to get out of those funks where it may take a whole drive for me to you know come to the sideline, you know, get out of it, try to get out of it one or two plays. Maybe after a bad play or you know I messed up on something or we jumped offsides and you know I get frustrated, but I think I've done a better job of that, and I've been more comfortable with that."
The quest for consistency goes on, and it might help to have his regular targets in place for more than a practice or two. However, considering Luther Burden's injury will keep him out until the regular season, Williams will simply have to get used to the Walkers, Millers and even the occasional Kaden Davis.
A year ago at this time, it was the kind of disruption that could have led to a QB drowning.

title: Coby Bryant's Injury Will Put Ryan Poles' Defensive Line Plan to the Test
full_text:
It seemed like the Chicago Bears were dodging bullet after bullet on the training camp injury front. Luther Burden III had a few scares, but the team reportedly feels good about his chances of being ready for the season opener. Cam Lewis was back on the practice field yesterday after some misfortune of his own. Ozzy Trapilo is somehow well on his way back to the field after rupturing his Achilles in January.
We even thought Ben Johnson's comments about Coby Bryant's reported 8-10 week timeline were a good sign for his future. However, it turns out we were all duped in that regard. Those comments were interpreted incorrectly, as Johnson announced that Bryant would instead be on the shelf for the next 4-6 months earlier today.
It's a true worst-case scenario for a Bears defense already down one key starter in nickelback Kyler Gordon. The injury will not only strain the secondary, but it'll also put a lot more pressure on the defensive line.
Virtually everyone expected the team to make a deeper nvestment in the defensive line this offseason. It was widely considered one of their most glaring weaknesses entering the offseason after failing to get consistent pressure on opposing QBs and often getting gouged in the running game last season.
However, the fact that they already have the league's fifth-most expensive defensive line limited how much they could justify improving the room in free agency. They instead opted for bargain-bin free agent additions and the sixth-round selection of Georgia Tech's Jordan van den Berg. It was always a bold strategy.
Fortunately, it was a bold strategy that appears to be off to a brilliant start. It's still far too early to have the rookie's gold jacket fitted for Canton, but there's no denying the fact that he's made serious waves at training camp . That's a good thing, too, because they desperately need some juice in the pass-rush department with Grady Jarrett not getting any younger and hope increasingly fading in Gervon Dexter getting any better in his fourth season.
Montez Sweat and Austin Booker's hopeful progression at least instills some hope on the edges, and they might be able to unlock last year's biggest free agent disappointment , Dayo Odeyingbo, on the interior. However, Sweat is the only sure thing in that regard, as well.
The fact that the Bears signed Xavier Woods shortly after Bryant went down makes a lot more sense after Johnson's comments today. The veteran safety has 121 career starts under his belt, and he will at least provide some stability opposite rookie Dillon Thieneman.
Growing pains were always expected for Chicago's first-round selection, and that will especially be the case with Bryant out of action. While Woods has always been solid in coverage, Bryant is much more comfortable against the run than the veteran has been. That might be an area where they rely more on the rookie now, which could limit his upside and, in turn, remove the alignment flexibility that Dennis Allen was clearly vying for with the team's new safety duo.
It's also fair to question how well the new-look secondary will gel after losing one of their best players until (at least) December. The importance of getting Kyler Gordon back in the lineup has never been more paramount. Unfortunately, his health has always been far from reliable .
The loss the secondary suffered today cannot be understated, and it's going to have a wide-ranging impact on the entire defense.

title: Joe Burrow's Named Mentioned Amidst Jayden Daniels' Jersey Number Battle With LSU
full_text:
Joe Burrow's name is in the news this week with an LSU football tie-in.
ESPN's Mark Schlabach reported on Wednesday that former LSU quarterback Jayden Daniels is upset the team gave his old No. 5 jersey number to current sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett to wear this season.
Daniels posted a Heisman Trophy-winning season in 2023 and thinks his jersey should be treated like Burrow's No. 9. He doesn't want anyone else to wear it even though it hasn't been officially retired.
No one has worn Burrow's number since he entered the NFL in 2020.
"The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU's decision to give Jayden's number to another player," the statement from Daniels' spokesperson said in the story. "Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university."
Schlabach expanded more on the Burrow side.
"Sources told ESPN that Daniels believes he is being treated differently than Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, whose No. 9 jersey hasn't been worn at LSU since he won the Heisman Trophy and led LSU to a 15-0 record and College Football Playoff national championship in 2019," Schlabach wrote .
The duo represents two of LSU's three Heisman winners all time.
Head coach Lane Kiffin released a statement with his thoughts on the situation.
"DJ is in [No.] 5, and that was a situation that was promised to him in recruiting here, for him to sign here," Kiffin stated. "I've done a lot of research on that with the family and the representatives and the people, so really I didn't have a decision to make. It was promised to the kid; it wasn't done for whatever [reason]. I'm not going to get into that.
"I'm not going to judge something [that was done] when I wasn't here. But when a kid is promised something to come to a school, he should wear it. So, at that point, I don't think that's really my decision. We should honor what he was told."
Burrow is not directly tied to this and has not commented on the matter.

title: 5 Bengals Players To Watch in Preseason Opener Against Lions
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals open their 2026 preseason schedule Thursday night at Paycor against the Detroit Lions, and head coach Zac Taylor said the majority of the starters will see action .
That list includes quarterback Joe Burrow, wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins new defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence, who will be looking to knock down a quarterback other than Burrow.
“It won't be a ton of time, but for our fans to come out there, they're going to see Joe and Jamar and T, they're going to see Dexter,” Taylor said. “So they'll get a chance to enjoy some of our players there. But how long I keep him out there remains to be seen.”
Based on last year , which was the first time in the Burrow era he and the starters have seen significant action, you can expect it to be one series if it includes a couple of first downs. Or perhaps two if the opening drive ends quickly.
While the stars and other starters will be a big draw for many of those in attendance, there are several backups with intriguing storylines who will be worth following.
Let’s take a look at five of them:
Every year there is excitement and intrigue about how the top pick in the draft is going to look in his first live action.
Given how explosive Howell has looked coming off the edge in the first 10 training camp practices, he definitely follows the trend.
Though Howell sat out Tuesday’s light final tune-up for the game, he told reporters he expects to play against the Lions. And with Detroit not expected to play their starters, you should expect to see Howell challenging the visitor’s backup tackles.
But don’t blink. Howell is likely to have a workload similar to that of the starters, where you shouldn’t expect him to be in the game long.
The import from the Canadian Football League has consistently made plays in training camp, but his clearest path to cracking the 53-man roster is going to be showing explosion – and dependability – as a kick and punt returner.
Charlie Jones is the incumbent at both spots, but the Bengals know what they have in him (three returner touchdowns in the last three seasons). What they don’t know is if he can stay healthy.
Meyers and Ke’Shawn Williams, who averaged a team-best 10.5 yards per punt return last year and 25.4 per kickoff return on eight returns. Jones averaged 25.8 yards on 42 kick returns.
Unlike snaps for offensive and defensive players, return chances can’t be pre-planned by the coaching staff given the unpredictable nature of how many there will be. So it will be interesting to see how special teams coordinator Darrin Simmons allocates the opportunities as they arise.
The additions of Lawrence via trade and Jonathan Allen in free agency served as direct notice to Jenkins, who has struggled to make an impact since the Bengals drafted him in the second round in 2024.
There’s also the matter of B.J. Hill being close to returning from the Physically Unable to Perform list and the improved play of T.J Slaton, not to mention the addition of Landon Robinson in the draft.
The defensive tackle position is deep and competitive.
Jenkins has seen his opportunities with the first time increase as camp has gone along, with Allen and Lawrence taking multiple days off. Look for that to continue in earnest Thursday night as the Bengals for a couple of reasons.
Yes, the coaches want to see if Jenkins is more active and disruptive. They also want the other teams in the league to see it, as he could be a trade piece closer to the roster deadline. And a strong performance in the preseason will only help improve any potential trade value.
The team’s third-round pick, Davis has not looked like a rookie in camp in that there haven’t been any glaring gaffes. But there haven’t been many splash plays, although he did intercept third-string quarterback Josh Johnson in the end zone of Friday’s practice at the indoor facility.
DJ Ivey has earned his role as CB3 at the moment, but Davis is going to have a chance to push for that spot, and live action will be the best way to advance.
The one thing none of the rookies have been able to prove with no live periods in camp is how well they can tackle, which is of high importance given how the last two seasons have done, so Davis will be one to watch not just in coverage, but in run support.
He proved how strong his leg was last year as a rookie, but his touch left a lot to be desired as his 11 touchbacks were tied for the most in the league, and his 16.9 percentage of touchbacks led all punters.
Because of that, Rehkow’s gross punting average of 50.5, which was second best in the league, was overshadowed by his net of 42.9, which ranked 11th.
Punters and returners are the toughest positions to truly gauge in practice given that there are no live special teams.
Thursday’s game will give Rehkow a chance to show how much his touch has improved.
The Bengals clearly are expecting it because he is the lone punter in camp this summer.

title: Ted Karras Continues Stamping Major Praise on Dexter Lawrence With Top Talent Ranking
full_text:
Don't tell Ted Karras Dexter Lawrence isn't the best defensive tackle in football.
The 11-year veteran is battling daily with the Bengals' biggest 2026 star addition in the middle of the trenches. Lawrence has transformed the defense into what running back Chase Brown deemed a top-10 unit in the league over the past few months.
Karras described the battle to Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com .
"Yes. I'm playing Dexter Lawrence, the best defensive lineman in football," Karras said to Hobson. "I get him every day. I wouldn't call it fun, but it's a good test of mettle. I'm getting a lot better, and I think we are as a unit."
It echoes his comments to start the month in front of his locker.
Karras is getting sharper and sharper going up against truly elite talent in practice for the first time as a Bengal.
"He's the best in the league, so I mean our Week 1 opponent's right there with him (Vita Vea), so that's good practice for him," Karras stated to begin the month. "You've got to be ready to go every day. It's a little bit stressful in August for me, but at least I get to pass it off to our opponent's center come September."
Head coach Zac Taylor has loved Lawrence's "relentlessness" so far.
“A relentlessness to him,” Taylor said during a recent press conference. “Ted (Karras) has his hands full, and it’s making Ted better. Whatever year Ted’s in (11). I think it’s certainly a grind for both those guys. They’re two smart guys that are doing everything they can to win the rep and help their unit, but he’s tough.
“We ran a counter play that was really good the other day, and he just reached around and grabbed Chase Brown. And there’s nothing I would have told (right guard) Dalton (Risner) to do differently. Dalton did a great job 99% of the time against 99 of 100 tackles. That’s going to be a great block. And Dexter just made that play. That’s a rare play for a guy to make.”
The Bengals offense fought back with some big plays in a nice see-saw over the weekend. Sunday was reportedly the most physical day of camp so far, and Cincinnati got that great work in without suffering injuries anymore.
Lawrence's impact could only grow if his injured defensive line running mates come back soon and ready to roll. It looks likely as B.J. Hill could get lifted off the PUP list any day now, while Shemar Stewart is off crutches in his recovery from a knee hyperextension.

title: Dalton Risner Explains Long-Term Impact Desire With Cincinnati Bengals
full_text:
With NFL teams constantly chopping and changing their staff and players, it can quickly turn players into a “me-first” mindset, and it's hard to blame them. With this, it's becoming increasingly rare for teams to have their respective cult heroes, so when you find someone who looks towards the team rather than himself, you need to take good care of them, and for the Cincinnati Bengals, that player is guard Dalton Risner.
Heading into free agency following the 2024 season, Risner had already accumulated 87 games in the NFL with both the Denver Broncos and the Minnesota Vikings, yet he still had kinks in his game to iron out, so when the Bengals offered a one-year deal last offseason, there was no guarantee Risner was going to be there next season.
However, his 69.4 overall PFF grade in year one in the AFC North proved there was still loads of talent in Risner, causing the Bengals to extend his contract for another season worth up to $5 million .
While most players would be solely focused on clawing themselves back to the top of the depth chart, Risner’s team-first approach oozed through during his appearance on Dan Hoard’s “ Bengals Booth Podcast .”
“I want to make an impact on my teammates. I don't want to be a guy that is so caught up in myself and my own story that when guys look back on me, they say, ‘yeah, like good player,’ and that's all they have to say,” opened Risner earlier this month. Risner was originally selected in the second round of the 2019 NFL to the Broncos, where he spent 62 games before tacking on 25 more with the Vikings.
“I would hope some of these guys can look back and say, like, ‘man, I learned so much from that guy, the type of human being he was, the type of man he was. I look up to, and I admire.’ So I guess I just try to be fully me and what comes with that is trying to help some of these guys,” finished Risner.
The former Kansas State Wildcat brings eight years of experience with him, making him the most experienced guard by a country mile on the roster and the third-most experienced player across the offensive line, behind just Ted Karras (11) and Orlando Brown Jr. (9).

title: Bengals Franchise Valuation Rockets Up Following 2025-26 Season
full_text:
The Bengals franchise valuation got an update entering the 2026 season.
Sportico has been dialing into all 32 team valuations since 2020 and dropped its latest ranking from most to least valuable on Wednesday.
Cincinnati checked in at No. 32 with a valuation of $7.4 billion. A 35% increase from last year.
Don't think the Bengals are struggling in last place. The value has increased a ton this decade, and they just got a $453 million revenue-sharing check from the league before the season even starts.
"The Cincinnati Bengals have been parked at No. 32 for seven straight years in Sportico's annual NFL team valuations," Kurt Badenhausen stated . "The small-market club plays in an older stadium, ranks near the bottom on local revenue and lacks a national brand from its Super Bowl trophy-less history.
"Yet there are only six sports franchises on the planet outside the NFL that are worth more than the Bengals. The list includes three from the NBA, two in MLB and LaLiga's Real Madrid. The NFL's least valuable team is worth $7.4 billion, by Sportico's count, and all 32 teams land among the world's 40 most valuable sports franchises."
The Bengals are still one of the 40 most lucrative sports franchises on earth, and it's refreshing to see the team treat themselves that way this offseason.
Bengals executive Katie Blackburn and the front office pushed in plenty of financial chips to the center of the table for the most competitive roster possible. It led to their first major contract restructure in team history with Joe Burrow's current deal.
It was a massive 2025-26 for the league.
"The average team value rose 31% to $9.34 billion, based on conversations with more than 40 people involved in the league, including team owners, executives, investors, consultants and bankers," Badenhausen noted at the start of the piece. "It marks the biggest year-over-year value gain for the NFL since Sportico ’s valuations launched in 2020. The average value has increased 141% over the past five years.
"The 32 teams are collectively worth $299 billion, including real estate and related businesses, such as the Cowboys’ sports components of The Star mixed-use development in Frisco, Texas."
