title: Ja'Marr Chase Loves 'Pissed' Version of Bengals QB Joe Burrow
full_text:
Joe Burrow has made a deliberate effort to show a different side of himself as a leader this year, and superstar wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase is fully on board.
The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback talked earlier this offseason about becoming more vocal and even a little "mean" when teammates aren't meeting the standard. Burrow said in June that he wanted to bring more urgency to the locker room by calling things out immediately and with more intensity.
Chase has gotten an up-close look at that version of his longtime quarterback during training camp. He wouldn't mind seeing it more often.
“I like it when he's pissed,” Chase said in an interview with NFL Network on Sunday. “I like it when Joe's pissed. I'm not gonna lie. I like it when he's like that. I like the fire that he has.”
Chase said in the interview that Burrow hasn't displayed that side of his personality all too often since camp began, but added that it's surfaced once or twice. When it does, though, the difference is obvious.
“His demeanor is just more aggressive,” Chase said. “His face is more aggressive. The way he talks is more aggressive, and he got like a little mean mug on his face a little bit. So I kind of like when he's like that.”
The “aggressive” edge isn’t exclusive to everyone else either.
Burrow has gotten after Chase before, and it's something the All-Pro wide receiver doesn't take issue with. He views it as part of the accountability that has made their partnership so successful.
“I don't mind it, though, man. I'm not gonna lie. I don't mind it,” Chase said. “That's hard coaching. That's critical coaching. He's holding me accountable. I appreciate that. I would do the same to him.”
Burrow explained in June that becoming more vocal was outside his comfort zone, but that he viewed it as an area where he could grow as a leader. He's also stressed the urgency surrounding a Bengals team that has missed the playoffs in three consecutive seasons despite having championship expectations.
If "Mean Joe" is part of Burrow's effort to change that, his No. 1 wide receiver certainly isn't asking him to tone it down. The end goal is to be the only team holding the Lombardi Trophy in Inglewood, California, come February, and Burrow's leadership plays a significant role in that.

title: 'Pretty Big' - Cashius Howell Ready to Play in First NFL Game Opportunity
full_text:
Cashius Howell is eager to play in his first NFL game on Thursday night.
The rookie Bengals edge rusher is splashing in training camp all over the place but sat out the most recent practice with an unknown injury ding. Still, he plans on playing in the preseason game against Detroit and dove into the excitement with FOX 19's Jeremy Rauch.
Howell knows this is a chance to make a statement early in his career.
"Pretty big," Howell said about the game's importance for his growth. "Obviously, it's my first time getting live reps in the NFL. So it's obviously a big thing for me. So I just want to go out there and make sure that I'm playing to the best of my abilities and just playing the game that I was meant to play."
Zac Taylor addressed the media on Tuesday and gave his thoughts on players like Howell and fellow rookie Tacario Davis suiting up in the game.
Cincinnati plans to play a ton of starters early in the contest as they did for a preseason game last season.
"I think that's why I'm a little limited right now, just on some guys that we're kind of limiting day to day and making decisions for on Thursday," Taylor said on Tuesday . "So I'm not quick enough right now to say who's gonna be full go yet because there's just some guys that I just really want to manage through this week, and we'll make some decisions if they're playing tomorrow or not.
"But those guys, there's nothing long-term on them. It's just we kind of get out there some days, decide for that day if we're gonna put them out there."
Howell has put his head down and hit the grindstone all summer long.
There has been zero drama and only hard work from the Texas A&M product.
"I feel like I've done good given the circumstances, but obviously there's still room for improvement," Howell concluded. "Little things that I need to hone in on, but overall, I feel like I went out there and did the best that I could. Just got to continue to keep being consistent and keep stacking days."
If treatment goes well today and tomorrow, it seems like Howell will suit up during his first chance at NFL game action.

title: Ja’Marr Chase Names 3 Bengals Who Are Standing Out at Training Camp
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase knows what it takes for a receiver to stand out in the NFL.
He's done it himself — and now he says he's seeing it in two newcomers who have caught the 26-year-old superstar's attention. When Kay Adams recently asked Chase which teammates had impressed him at training camp, the All-Pro wideout named Colbie Young and former CFL standout Dohnte Meyers.
“Colbie’s been making big plays,” Chase told Adams. “Dohnte’s been making plays with the ones.”
The two receivers are taking different routes through a crowded WR room. Young is a fourth-round draft pick expected to develop behind Cincinnati's established stars, Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers is trying to turn a strong summer into a spot on the 53-man roster or the practice squad. Earning recognition from Chase is a promising sign for both.
Young, picked No. 140 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, gives the Bengals another big-bodied target behind Higgins. The six-foot-three, 215-pound Georgia product has used his size to make several contested catches during his first NFL training camp.
Meanwhile, Meyers has been given fewer opportunities on offense, but Chase has noticed how productive he's been when those chances arise.
“He gets in with the ones every couple — maybe he has like three or four plays out of the whole day with the ones — and he makes plays with the ones,” Chase said. “So that’s a big step.”
The 26-year-old Meyers spent the past two seasons with the Saskatchewan Roughriders before signing with the Bengals in January. He recorded 89 receptions for 1,405 yards and nine touchdowns in the CFL. He also has experience returning both kickoffs and punts, which could help his case in a roster battle.
Chase singled out DJ Turner II on the opposing side. The two have regularly competed against each other in practice, giving Chase a close look at the 2023 second-round pick's development.
“DJ’s been playing pretty good in camp. He’s been playing a little different,” Chase said. “I told him about himself earlier.”
Chase declined to disclose what he told Turner privately but said his teammate appears to be playing with more confidence and embracing his style. Turner is coming off a breakout season in which he recorded 18 pass deflections, one of the NFL's highest totals in just 16 starts.
Turner already has a starting role and is trying to build on a career year. Young and Mayers still have much more to prove. Their next opportunities will come in the preseason, when both receivers can show that the plays drawing Chase's attention in practice will translate to games.

title: Jordan Battle's Interception of Joe Burrow Adds Juice to Bengals D in Final Tune-up Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
Tuesday’s Cincinnati Bengals practice was light on participation, tight on space and slight on activity.
Numerous players dealing with tightness and tweaks took the day off for the final practice before Thursday night’s preseason opener against the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium.
It also was the second practice in five days forced inside due to weather, as storm clouds and rain rolled in about 30 minutes into the session.
Once inside the indoor facility, the Bengals only ran one period of 11-on-11. The first drive by the first-team offense ended with the defensive highlight of the day, with Jordan Battle ranging over from his single-high alignment to intercept a Joe Burrow deep ball intended for Ja’Marr Chase.
Jordan Battle reads the deep ball from Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase perfectly and makes the pick. pic.twitter.com/6yhIpCUTK0
It was the second time in Battle’s four-year career that he has intercepted Burrow in a training camp practice, with the first coming last year, also during an indoor session.
“Very rare,” Battle said. “I was more of a robber last year. This time I was out in the middle of the field.”
“It's all about knowing where Uno (Chase) is on the field," Battle said. "When you're playing middle of the field, you've just got to know certain things, see the quarterback's shoulder -- if it's high, it it's low -- so you can go from breaking down to breaking high.
“I was just reading his eyes and seeing the release of Uno,” he continued. “I saw him going deep, and just breaking before the throw allows you to make plays. I was happy he threw it because I knew I had a chance to make a play, and I did.”
Battle recorded a career-high four interceptions last year after snaring just one in each of his first two seasons in the league.
His four last year were tied for the fourth most in the league among safeties. They also are tied for the fourth most by a safety in Bengals history behind Reggie Nelson (eight, 2015), Kevin Kaseviharn (six, 2006) and Shawn Williams (five, 2018).
While practice picks don’t mean much in the overall picture, Battle said they do have value.
“They keep the energy up and gets us started,” he said. “After that, they fumbled a snap and we had a couple (tackles for loss). It’s just a spark for the defense. Obviously you don’t have momentum in practice, so we create momentum for ourselves.
“I feel like we’ve been doing a good job of that all training camp.”
Battling it out. pic.twitter.com/eNPiP8yIlh
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed the starters will play some Thursday against the Lions, although Battle's running mate at safety, Bryan Cook, will not be one of them. Nor will cornerback Dax Hill as both defensive backs deal with soft tissue tweaks.
Battle said he’s happy about Taylor's decision.
Obviously, you don’t want the first regular-season game to be the first time you’re tackling somebody. That can lead to bad things,” he said. “So I love the idea of playing in preseason games, being able to go out there and work on those things now so I don’t have to worry about them in Week 1.
“I’m ready to put my pads on and hit somebody else and take them to the ground,” he added. “It’s a long offseason. It feels like the time is finally here. I’m excited for this defense. I’m excited for myself. I’m excited to see what we do as a team. It’s been looking good. Let’s hope we continue on that path.”
Burrow, as he’s wont to do, got revenge on the defense on the next drive, marching the offense to the 2-yard line after hitting Andrei Iosivas on a slant to set up first and goal.
Burrow’s pass for Chase at the front pylon was broken up by Josh Newton. But Burrow went back to the same spot, only this time with Tee Higgins as the target, and the receiver made a one-handed snag and somehow tapped both feet as he was flying out of bounds at the pylon.

title: Joe Burrow Feeling 'Winning-Level Football' From Bengals Additions as Opening Preseason Game Approaches
full_text:
Joe Burrow seemingly can't stop gushing about the importance of Dexter Lawrence and all of the new additions for Cincinnati this offseason.
The Bengals' top star sat down with Kay Adams on Up & Adams this week, and he dove into all of the pieces fitting together in a championship puzzle.
"Yeah, of course, of course he's part of that," Burow noted on the show about Lawrence's championship impact. "But also, a lot of the guys that we've added this off-season: Boye (Mafe), Jonathan (Allen), Bryan Cook, getting DJ Turner back, Dax Hill back, Jalen Davis on the inside. We've got a lot of guys that we feel confident in that can go out and produce and play winning-level football."
Burrow is slated to suit up in the preseason opener on Thursday night for his first game action since closing the 2025 season in January.
Lawrence is firing out of the gates and playing alongside him as plenty of Bengals' starters get a taste of live ball against Detroit. The big fella has had fun prodding his new offensive leader in the early days of training camp.
On Day 1, Lawrence came at "the king" a little bit on and off the field. He's disrupting plenty of passing reps and had a little something to declare before that impact even started.
"I wanna see it today, Mr. Burrow," Dan Hoard noted Lawrence said on Day 1 before practice started.
"You can see it every day, brother," Burrow responded.
It's all in good fun as the chemistry and on-field execution grows throughout the rest of this month and beyond.
"Somebody has to challenge the King of the Jungle, as they say," said Lawrence after that practice. "Somebody has to keep him on edge for him to get better and grow. That competitive spirit won't stop. And with a guy like that, I know he's going to bring it. It's going to be fun."

title: Making Sense of How Browns Coach Todd Monken Is Starting Quarterbacks in Preseason
full_text:
The Browns' starting quarterback competition that has taken place throughout the summer and during training camp will continue into the preseason games.
Deshaun Watson will start the first preseason game against the Bears in Chicago on Saturday, while Shedeur Sanders will get the start in the second preseason game at home against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 22, Monken announced Wednesday .
Deshaun starting Saturday and Shedeur poised to start next week read more ➡️ https://t.co/thL2C3PiQ5 pic.twitter.com/B4FTBgGjum
"I have my reasons for how it's going to go, and it's still a competition," Monken said. "We're excited to watch guys practice today, let alone on Saturday, and then next week against Buffalo, and we'll get a chance to see them both. Every week we'll assess it. It'll be a little bit more difficult with the player who doesn't play as much this week or the other quarterbacks, right? We'll be able to assess the quarterback who started and how he played, and when the other quarterbacks came in and then the opposite will be next week against Buffalo."
Watson hasn't played in a game since 2024, when he tore his right Achilles in Week 7 of that season. He re-ruptured the same Achilles again on Jan. 6, 2025. Those two injuries came after he tore his rotator cuff and suffered a displaced fracture of the shoulder scapula, injuries that caused him to miss the final eight games of the 2023 season.
Now fully healthy , Watson is excited for the opportunity to get back on the field and believes the preseason would be a "great" opportunity for him, as he has played in only 19 games since 2020, all of which came with the Browns between 2021-24. In the three-year stretch, Watson's 33.1 Total QBR ranked last among qualified quarterbacks if he had enough starts to qualify.
"I'm super excited," Watson said before Wednesday's practice. "All the hard work that I put in with the training staff, with my team, my personal team, to get to this stage has been tremendous for me. So, I'm super excited for those opportunities and can't wait for it."
Sanders, meanwhile, started the final seven games of his rookie season after he was selected in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL draft. While completing only 56.6% of his passes and throwing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, Sanders' 18.9 QBR is the fifth-lowest among 696 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts since 2006.
But with one year of NFL experience under his belt, Sanders feels like he has something to prove ahead of his second season.
Shedeur Sanders throws a BEAUTIFUL deep pass that is dropped by Jerry Jeudy #Browns #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/cnvJmwL8EP
"We approach practice like a game," Sanders said Wednesday. "So it's the same amount of focus and experience. So that's why I'm excited: to feel how similar it feels to practice, honestly. Because it's a different type of intention and a mentality that we go out there every day with.
Watson and Sanders will likely each play a half in the first preseason game. The head coach also wants each quarterback to experience a two-minute drill on Saturday.
"I have my reasons for how it's going to go, and it's still a competition," Monken said. "We're excited to watch guys practice today, let alone on Saturday, and then next week against Buffalo, and we'll get a chance to see them both. Every week we'll assess it. It'll be a little bit more difficult with the player that doesn't play as much this week or the other quarterbacks, right? We'll be able to assess the quarterback that started and how he played and when the other quarterbacks came in and then the opposite will be next week against Buffalo."
Watson and Sanders have alternated reps with the first-team offense throughout the first eight practices of training camp. Despite Watson taking first-team reps on back-to-back days (Aug. 7-8) – the first of which was in helmets, while the second was in pads – it was simply to even out the reps each quarterback took with the starters. Cleveland once again alternated first-team reps between Watson and Sanders this week.
Both quarterbacks have had plenty of ups and downs throughout training camp . For Watson, it's becoming more consistent and accurate as a veteran quarterback. He threw nine interceptions in the Browns' first 12 practices of training camp but didn't turn the ball over on Wednesday.
But as the days go on, Watson admits that he feels more comfortable in Monken's offense each step of the way. Whether it's watching film or on-field practice, Watson understands how he must improve going forward.
the name's Bond. @isaiahbond_ 😎 @deshaunwatson | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/qR7vumwUBw
"My job every day is what I live by," Watson said. "I just keep trying to win the day, and every day I take it one day at a time. Can't rush anything and let the football that I've been doing my whole life kind of take care of itself. So again, I'm in a good spot, and I just keep trying to work and find ways to get better."
Quarterbacks coach Mike Bajakian also sees Watson's improvement as practices go on and the quarterback gains more confidence and becomes more comfortable in Monken's offense.
stretched down the sideline 🙌 @OfficialTylan2 | @deshaunwatson pic.twitter.com/ODu2RKLn2B
"He threw some interceptions early, and he's done a good job of protecting the football as of late. There was a string of three or four practices — the days run together — where there were zero picks from him. So, he's done a good job of that," quarterbacks coach Mike Bajakian said on Aug. 8. "On his good days, he's been decisive, his anticipation's been on point, and he's getting rid of the ball on time without having to move around in the pocket."
While Monken has seen improvement from both Watson and Sanders at times during training camp, he also realizes that preseason games will be much more telling than practices.
"I've seen a lot of really good things over the course of the four or five months I've been here," Monken said of Watson. "I think he's done a lot of really good things athletically, making plays that we're going to get a chance to see, because we're not live. We'll see if that comes to play when we get out there and go."
With the quarterback competition contuining into the preseason games, allowing both quarterbacks to start is a smart decision by Monken. It allows both Watson and Sanders to have live reps against anotehr opponent besides Cleveland's defense. But the smarter decision for the head coach is giving Watson the start in the first preseason game, which will be played in Chicago, while starting Sanders the second preseason game, which will be in Cleveland.
The last time Watson played in a game (in 2024), he was booed by Cleveland fans while down on the field due to a ruptured Achilles. Watson was also booed at times during training camp over the last two weeks.
Giving Sanders the start at home not only puts each quarterback in the best position to succeed and prove that they should earn the starting job, but it also makes things less awkward than they need to be.
With the Bills in town next week for joint practices with the Browns in Berea, each team will get plenty of live action against each other before the preseason game between the two on Aug. 22. With that, the playing time and amount of snaps Watson and Sanders receive in the actual preseason game could change from what Monken expects to happen on Wednesday.
But the current plan is for each quarterback to start – and play a half – in the first two preseason games, with Watson set to start on Saturday against the Bears and Sanders to start a week after against the Bills.

title: Todd Monken Finally Shares When Browns Will Learn Preseason Starting Quarterback
full_text:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken is keeping his quarterback plans very close to the chest.
But on Wednesday, the first-time head coach told reporters that he will inform Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders of which one of them is going to start Saturday’s preseason game against the Chicago Bears after practice.
Monken has already decided whether Watson or Sanders will start the preseason opener, but both quarterbacks will get the message from their head coach later Wednesday afternoon.
The preseason games will be significant for this competition. Throughout the first dozen training camp practices, Watson has more reps with the starting offense. But the 30-year-old veteran has also thrown more interceptions than Sanders, who has consistently developed over the course of the offseason.
Watson and Sanders will each start a preseason game for the Browns. It’s likely that a formal announcement of who won the competition could happen after Cleveland’s second preseason game.
Against the Bears, the starting offensive is likely to play the first drive. It’s possible that the starting quarterback could play the first half of each preseason game.
Monken’s decision will boil down to which quarterback he believes will give the Browns the best chance to win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.
Watson has more snaps with the starting offense so far because of Saturday’s switch in the rotation. Since spring practices, Monken has been alternating days between Watson and Sanders with the starters. But on Saturday, Watson was awarded a second-straight day of reps with the starting offense, snapping the cycle and giving him more reps than Sanders overall.
A big area of focus in this particular competition is which quarterback can efficiently run the entire operation. Monken’s offense puts a lot on the plate for quarterbacks, so Cleveland’s pre-snap operation needs to be flawless before the 60-year-old head coach names a starter.
Neither quarterback has run away with this competition, which makes the preseason even more intriguing for the Browns. There’s no telling how much Monken will honestly factor in preseason performance during the evaluation of these quarterbacks, but it’s certainly the next step in the process.
After this preseason opener in Chicago, Cleveland’s joint practice with the Buffalo Bills on Thursday August 20 will be the next big check-in on this competition. After that practice, the Browns will host the Bills for a preseason game. From there, it’s anyone’s guess as to when Monken could name his Week 1 starting quarterback.

title: Browns Host Another Free Agent Edge Rusher Knowing Defensive Line Is Thin
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns might have real depth issues on the defensive line heading into the preseason and are looking to add a player to help fill in that void.
With the injury bug making its way through training camp on defense for the Browns, they need to address the issue as soon as possible. One way the Browns are looking to address it is by adding a free agent edge rusher.
After Cleveland hosted Jadeveon Clowney a couple of weeks ago, it was clear that the Browns wanted to add a player to fix their depth issues. Now, free agent edge rusher Tyus Bowser is working out with the team on Wednesday.
Veteran edge Tyus Bowser, who last played for the Miami Dolphins in 2024, worked out today for the Cleveland Browns.
It’s clear that the Browns are interested in bringing in a veteran on the defensive line to fill in after recent injuries have limited their current players. Here’s what signing Bowser would mean in regard to Cleveland’s lack of depth.
There has been a plethora of training camp injuries that have led to the Browns defensive line being so thin, none that are threatening as of now, but it’s still an issue either way.
Over the last week of training camp, the Browns have had to mix some things up by upgrading some of their second and third team players to the first team defense. That was when it became glaringly obvious there was a depth issue.
Now, with Tyus Bowser visiting Cleveland and working out for the team, it seems like they’re more than willing to sign a player or two to help with that heading into the preseason. This will give their coaching staff a better idea of what they have to work with before the regular season.
Bowser hasn’t played a regular season game since the 2024 season when he was with the Miami Dolphins but has had a productive career even after being unsigned last season.
It’s been since 2021 that Bowser played a full season and hasn’t put up near the defensive numbers since his time with the Baltimore Ravens. In 2021, Bowser had 59 total tackles, 33 solo tackles, with seven sacks and two forced fumbles.
That was by far his best season of his eight-year career and had only mustered two sacks the following season before seeing a significant drop off in production and playing time.
Now at age 31, Bowser is still looking to make an impact in any given role with an NFL team, and his next may be the Cleveland Browns. If his workout goes well, he could wind up helping out on their thin defensive line that is still missing a few key players at training camp.
Bowser’s signing would allow for players like Adin Huntington and Elijah Chatman to continue seeing reps at defensive tackle while Mike Hall Jr. continues to work back from injury.
Maliek Collins is still on the PUP list, so this saga could continue into the regular season, but all eyes are on the preseason first. Cleveland’s first preseason game is this Saturday against the Chicago Bears, with kickoff scheduled for 1:00 p.m.

title: 7 Big Takeaways From Cleveland Browns' First Preseason Depth Chart
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 Preseason, and as expected, there were a few surprises.
As announced earlier by head coach Todd Monken, the quarterback position was going to show two co-starters, while a trio of rookies are slotted with the starting unit on offense.
Here are seven takeaways from the first installment of the Browns’ unofficial depth chart:
John Madden used to famously say, “if you have two quarterbacks, you have none.“
Nowhere has this proven to be more accurate than with these Browns, still undecided on who will be the starter come Week 1 of the regular season.
Head coach Todd Monken has promised Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders one start each in the preseason , but if Cleveland is really waiting until after August 22nd to make a call, how much preparation will the eventual starter get before the regular season opener, without having to look over his shoulder and being able to really focus on the task at hand?
The scales were always tipped towards the offense, after the team went offense-heavy in last April’s draft, including their top three picks. Now, said top three draftees are penciled in as starters -- Spencer Fano as left tackle, and KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston as wide receivers.
Fano’s inclusion among the starters is especially noteworthy, since it comes a few days after Monken shared that the team was considering staying with Dawand Jones, in case he wasn’t ready for the starting role. A training camp fight against Jared Verse helped change Monken’s mind about Fano’s readiness.
Even though Monken maintained from the very beginning that his preference was having Elgton Jenkins at guard, the team has him as the team’s starting center, with Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston battling it out for the right guard spot. Monken shared that Jenkins had the edge over Leveston thanks to experience, which would explain why he’s listed as the current starter, though there still might be some changes here.
Cleveland drafted two tight ends this year, and both of them are listed way on the deep end of the depth chart. It might be hard for the Browns to make room for both of them on the practice squad.
The starting foursome consisting of Verse and Alex Wright on the outside, paired with Mason Graham with Maliek Collins -- who’s on the PUP list -- on the inside, doesn’t really inspire awe. But things get more concerning once you get to the second and third stringers. Having the end positions manned by Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara and UDFAs Logan Fano and Khordae Sydnore, while the interior is handled by backups Mike Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Sam Kamara, Adin Huntington and UDFA Tyreak Sapp, just feels like a scream for help from the outside.
Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams were always going to be starters for Cleveland, and chances are they’ll be the two linebackers on the field when the Browns go to nickel alignment. But having Cleveland list Easton Mascarenas-Arnold as the third starter is a nice surprise, overtaking Nathaniel Watson, Winston Reid and rookie Justin Jefferson for that spot. That position battle has flown under the radar, understandably, but it does feel like a tight one.
With teams spending so much time in nickel and big nickel formations, it’s become increasingly popular to see depth charts listing five starting DBs instead of four.
Cleveland didn’t take this route, sticking with Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell at the corners, and Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman as safeties. This left second-round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren -- who’s expected to play a lot in three safety looks -- as a second stringer, along with presumptive nickel corner Myles Harden.
Like with the offensive backfield, expect the team to shed a lot of weight from their offseason 90-man roster here.

title: Cleveland Browns’ Offensive Line Picture Is Becoming Clearer
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns may be close to deciding who their best five offensive linemen are with the recent upgrade of one player to their starting offense at training camp.
After an offseason of rebuilding for the Browns on the offensive line specifically, not all of their linemen this season will be new faces.
Browns guard Teven Jenkins is one of a few returning players on the offensive line, and it appears he's been working all offseason to better position himself to start for Cleveland come week one.
During their training camp session on Tuesday, Jenkins started his second straight day at right guard with Cleveland’s starting offense. This may not mean anything concrete yet, but it does seem as though the Browns have an idea of the best way to form this offensive line.
Second straight day Teven Jenkins is at right guard with the 1s. I think we’re getting clarity. https://t.co/0EUJWMGVpa
Here’s what Jenkins earning first team reps during training camp could mean moving forward.
The biggest thing with Jenkins earning more reps at right guard is that there may be a bit of a decision to make regarding their starting center heading into the season. The expectation was that Luke Wypler would be in contention to start, but that doesn’t seem to be the case.
In reality, the chances that rookie center Parker Brailsford starts week one is slim, unless he shows out during the preseason that he can be counted on. As of now, it looks like Elgton Jenkins will be taking over the duties at center for Cleveland.
He was brought in as a free agent during the early stages of the offseason and was expected to slide back into his natural position at guard. With no clear-cut starter breaking out this summer, Elgton Jenkins is now listed as their starting center.
That works into Teven Jenkins favor, as he’ll now likely have the starting right guard job locked up with Zion Johnson on the other side at left guard. Jenkins was expected to be a backup, but he may have just found himself a starting job once again.
As of now, it appears that KT Leveston has also been seeing time at left and right guard, rotating in for Jenkins occasionally. Still, the Browns would likely feel more comfortable with Jenkins starting at guard than Leveston.
Jenkins started for the Chicago Bears before joining the Browns and starting for them last season at right guard, so he should have no issue remaining in his natural position. Jenkins was re-signed by the Browns back in early March.
Cleveland’s coaching staff has made it clear they want the best five starters on their offensive line on the field come the start of the regular season. If that includes Teven Jenkins, it’ll be nice to know that they have some familiarity with one of their starters at a key position.
The Browns will see their first taste of preseason action this Saturday against the Bears in Chicago, with kickoff set for 1:00 p.m.

title: Hanford Dixon Compares Shedeur Sanders to Bernie Kosar in New Interview
full_text:
With the Cleveland Browns still struggling to find an answer at the quarterback position after months of a seemingly endless position battle between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, one franchise legend has handed some lofty praise upon the second-year passer.
Hanford Dixon, a two-time first team All-Pro defensive back for Cleveland in the 1980s spoke up on the quarterback battle offering a huge compliment for Sanders by comparing him to none other than the club’s last true franchise quarterback, and a teammate of Dixon: Bernie Kosar.
“I see Bernie Kosar. And what I mean by that is, one thing we knew about Bernie, is that Bernie was very confident. I mean, he was a guy that believed in his ability, he knew that he could play, and knew that he could play quarterback,” said Dixon on the BIGPLAY Cleveland Show.
“Shedeur is the same way. He’s a very confident guy. Some people call him cocky. I don’t have a problem with him being cocky...” stated Dixon, who played alongside Kosar for five years, winning AFC Central crowns in 1985-1987 and 1989, the team’s last divisional titles to date. “But I think this guy is very, very confident. He knows that he can play, he believes that he can play. He’s the type of guy at the quarterback position that a team rallies themselves around him. They’ll get behind this guy if we give him the chance to prove himself.”
The quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson made front-page news again when head coach Todd Monken decided to ignore the strict rotation between the two passers leading the starting offense at practice on Saturday, giving Sanders’ reps for the day to Watson .
The sudden switch has many speculating that Monken may be leaning towards Watson, a notion that Dixon is not a big fan of.
“I don’t know why we would go back to Deshaun Watson. Here’s a guy that’s been with us for years now, at least four years with this football team and he has not shown us anything. We know what he did in Houston.”
Dixon, a three-time Pro Bowler during his NFL playing days, didn’t mince words when talking about the sudden change in the quarterback rotation on the weekend.
“I’m a little bit upset about the reps thing, because as we all know, Shedeur was supposed to get so many, and Deshaun was supposed to get so many reps. And I go back to last year, when Dillon [Gabriel] was taking most of the reps away from this kid, Shedeur. I know it’s still training camp obviously, we’re trying to figure out who the guy is, who the guy is going to be.”
Since Dixon has been lobbying for Shedeur to get a fair chance for some time, the recent turn of events has the Browns legend shaking his head at how the quarterback battle has been unfolding.
“Who knows what’s happening, what kind of pressure they're putting on Todd [Monken]. Hopefully none at all to play Watson because we all know Watson has made a lot of money. I mean we gave him $230 million and all that was pretty much guaranteed and I think this is pretty much the last year of that contract. But we still gotta find out what we have in Shedeur."
Dixon pointed to one specific factor why he thinks, given a fair shot, Shedeur Sanders can really thrive in Cleveland.
“The reason I think he can be [our starting quarterback], after your first year, the game starts to slow down for you. I don’t care what position you play, whether it’s quarterback, cornerback, defensive lineman, offensive lineman. Whatever it is, the game starts to slow down for you and it’ll be interesting to see what this kid can do if we give him a chance. And if he can’t, that’s fine, we gotta move on, but we still have to find out.”
Maybe from a physical standpoint, Sanders and Kosar aren't really that much alike. But if in fact Dixon is right about the confidence factor, then he should by all means have some edge over Watson . After all, it's hard to believe Watson's playing with any confidence right now in practice after almost two full years of surgeries and rehab, and leading the Browns QB tracker in thrown interceptions at training camp with nine after 12 sessions versus Sanders' four, according to reports.

title: 5 Cleveland Browns Players Who Need a Big Preseason and Why
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have finished their installations and are beginning to seriously prepare for their preseason games.
On Saturday, the Browns will travel to Chicago to face the Bears. They’ll return to Cleveland for a joint practice with the Buffalo Bills before hosting them at Huntington Bank Field in preseason Week 2. After that, the Browns round out their preseason with a dress rehearsal against the AFC Championship winning New England Patriots.
Browns coach Todd Monken has alluded to starters participating in the preseason, even though there isn’t any clarity yet on which players will play and when.
Regardless of that, let’s take a look at a handful of Browns players who need to have a big preseason.
As has been the case all training camp, Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will have all the attention during the preseason. Unless Monken changes his mind, each quarterback will have an opportunity to start a preseason game.
Recently, the Browns have given more starting reps to Watson, illustrating that he could potentially be the leader of this competition . If he starts against the Bears, he needs to be sharp. Throughout the team’s 11 training camp sessions, the quarterbacks have combined for 17 interceptions. So a strong showing from either quarterback would be a welcomed sight for the Browns.
The Browns have already handled Jamari Thrash, who will miss the entire season with an injury. That leaves Tillman as the lone Berry draft pick fighting for a roster spot in the wide receiver room.
Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and Isaiah Bond should be treated as locks to make this roster. If the Browns keep six wideouts, that leaves just two spots for free agent Tylan Wallace, who will be a core special teamer and Tillman, who is entering his fourth pro season.
Tillman will be competing against Malachi Corley and former preseason standouts Gage Larvadain, Luke Floriea for the final receiver spot, if the Browns decide to keep six.
Harold Fannin Jr. is the unquestioned starter at tight end after leading the Browns in receiving yards last year. But the room behind him? It’s unclear.
The Browns signed Stoll in free agency before adding tight ends Joe Royer and Carsen Ryan on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft. Royer has missed all of training camp with a personal matter.
That sets up Stoll to have plenty of opportunities in the preseason, especially if Fannin doesn’t play, as the 22-year-old has been banged up since the end of last season.
On Monday, Monken promoted No. 9 overall pick Spencer Fano to the starting offensive line at training camp. The rookie had been alternating for Dawand Jones, who should have an opportunity to prove to the Browns that he’s healthy and in shape ahead of Week 1.
Jones has an opportunity to be Cleveland’s backup swing tackle, as long as Fano and veteran right tackle Tytus Howard are both ready to go Week 1. A strong preseason from Jones would give Monken and offensive line coach George Warhop the confidence to keep him ready while continuing to develop rookie Austin Barber and transitioning KT Leveston to guard depth.

title: 3 Reasons Browns May be Forced to Start Deshaun Watson Week 1
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns remain in a quarterback battle that feels never-ending. Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been competing for months , with no one named the winner as August rolls along.
It's clear at this point that neither of the two have done anything to seize the job.
Yet this reality leads to several reasons why the job may ultimately go to Watson.
Todd Monken is a first-time head coach and wants to win . He knows he could be one-and-done if the team struggles and if he feels there is no clear winner in the competition, Watson does have the track record of someone with prior NFL success.
Browns fans would argue his success was a lifetime ago in Houston. That still does give him more of a resume than Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, who struggled in 2025 as rookies.
#Browns Deshaun Watson’s 9th pick in 12 practices: pic.twitter.com/dJ3kK793Qf
Watson winning by default would be a frustrating outcome for all involved. It may also point toward another one of the reasons why the Browns have to start him Week 1.
Watson is taking home $46 million in cash this year on the final season of his $230 million contract. Naming him the backup to start the year may have him and his agent asking for an immediate trade, or to be sent home to prepare for 2027.
The veteran needs to start and play well this season to have a shot at a decent contract in 2027 and beyond. If he is named the backup, he could argue the Browns were a terrible destination for him and ask to be sent home. Doing so would prevent him from putting any play on tape in 2026, using his past hype for next offseason.
Thus, the Browns may need to at least have Watson start the season to avoid blowing up the quarterback room right before the season begins.
Jimmy Haslam is a wealthy billionaire who can afford to waste $230 million from time to time. Yet it does make some sense to start Watson, at least to begin the season, because he is making $46 million this year. He is finally healthy and the team may just want to see what they have and try to extract any value out of him.
That could mean starting him, hoping he plays well, and trading him during the season to fully move on and start anew in 2027.
Sanders was a fifth-round pick, so starting him Week 1, especially if he can't separate himself in the competition, is much different than benching Watson and potentially having him demand to be out for the full season.

title: Browns Hopeful To Get Defensive Starter Back From Injury Ahead of Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are just a few days away from their first preseason game and are still hopeful for a few players to return to practice in order to see some in-game action over the next couple of weeks.
Among those players they hope will return soon is defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr., who is still working back from an injury plagued summer. Hall hasn’t practiced since August 3rd, but Cleveland’s coaching staff seems to think he’ll be back soon.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday regarding Hall Jr. and had some positive comments on his progress to get back on the field before their Saturday matchup against the Bears.
Here’s what Monken had to say, and what a return for Hall Jr. means for the Browns moving forward.
Having Hall Jr. back on the field will be great for the Browns heading into the preseason, but there really is no rush to get him back on the field right away based on his recent injuries this summer.
Monken commented on a return for Hall Jr., saying he’s hopeful to get him back at practice soon. “He got off to such a great start”, Monken said, and a return will really help the Browns plan for their 53-man roster with defensive tackle Maliek Collins still on the PUP list .
No date has been given for Collins to make his return to the team, but it will likely be closer to the regular season if not a few weeks into the season. This matters a lot when it comes to Hall, as he’ll likely be the starter alongside Mason Graham for a few weeks.
There’s no reason to get Hall Jr. back on the field as soon as possible, especially if they will need him to fill in starting time. Knowing that he was off to a good start before this recent injury is a positive sign for the coaching staff, which also plays into why they shouldn’t rush him back.
Through two seasons with the Browns, Hall Jr. has worked his way up to being one of their contending starters on a defense that has exceeded expectations in recent years and becoming one of the better units in the NFL.
While Hall Jr. has yet to play a full season for the Browns , he is still a serviceable player when he’s on the field. In his two seasons, Hall Jr. has 25 total tackles, 12 solo tackles, and 2.5 sacks as a rotational player.
Having a veteran like Maliek Collins on the defensive line helps the Browns feel more comfortable not relying a whole lot on Hall Jr. to produce. In his increasing role, he can surely learn from having one of the better defensive tackles in the room.
Hall Jr. will surely have a larger role on defense this season, even when Collins returns to the field. Being in a new defensive scheme under Mike Rutenberg should help him fight for more reps as well.
With Graham as their unanimous starter, Hall Jr. will have a good time playing alongside their first round pick from last year. Both should benefit from having Jared Verse on the outside, and if Alex Wright can take a step forward, the pressure applied should be similar to recent years.

title: Latest Reports From Browns Training Camp Proves QB Battle Remains a Mess
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have still not named a Week 1 starting quarterback. New head coach Todd Monken continues to insist both Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will get a shot to start their own preseason game before he comes to a decision.
Reports out of camp Monday may show why Monken is taking so long.
Beat reporter Ashley Bastock shared the ugly details from the end of Monday's practice.
End of #Browns practice.  One minute end of half situation.  Sanders up first and the drive ends with two false starts on the line.  Watson next and after two completions, a sack, an illegal formation and a false start.  Monken ended practice and looked like he threw something.
The offense was in an end-of-half situation and both Sanders and Watson got a shot to show off their clutch abilities. The former kept seeing his linemen jump and the latter had a solid start, followed by a sack and several penalties.
Mary Kay Cabot confirmed the scene shared by her colleague out of Berea.
A sloppy finish for the #Browns ' offense. Shedeur Sanders' 2-min drill ended with 3 straight procedural penalties, including a false start by Spencer Fano on the final snap; Deshaun Watson's 2-min ends with a sack and 2 procedurals.
Browns fans were ready to run Kevin Stefanski out of town for all the penalties in recent seasons, especially those by his offense. The Browns offense, under both Sanders and Watson, is now having trouble avoiding penalties in practice . That is the definition of a "total mess."
It is important to point out the offense will struggle in general because the defense is so talented. But it's inexcusable to have multiple pre-snap penalties in this type of drill in August. Such a thing happening in high school summer practice would lead to players running laps for it.
Monken was reportedly so mad he was throwing things, per Bastock. That is not quite where he wanted his offense to be to start the week of the first preseason game. Fans, meanwhile, may not be so surprised.
Monken has already gone away from his stated plans over the weekend, when Sanders saw reduced reps with the first-team offense. That seemingly meant Watson was the favorite, only for the veteran to struggle to even get snaps off on Monday.
This is a nightmare situation and one that will hopefully resolve itself when the preseason games actually begin. Even then, Week 1 will tell the true tale.
The fact a competition is taking place this late in training camp does indicate the team is still set on looking for a quarterback in the 2027 Draft . That is, the front office is viewing the plan that way. Monken and his coaches are doing their best to will the players to success, even if it may ultimately be a futile effort.

title: How a Maxx Crosby-Cowboys Trade Could Come to Fruition
full_text:
During the offseason, trade rumors circulated around the Dallas Cowboys as they reportedly had their sights set on Las Vegas Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby.
Dallas made a competitive offer , but were outbid by the Baltimore Ravens who agreed to send two first-round picks to Vegas in exchange for Crosby. The trade was nullified when Crosby failed his physical due to a knee injury, but the Cowboys already moved on and added Rashan Gary.
Las Vegas decided to patch things up with Crosby, who has since been cleared and is practicing. While they say they want Crosby to be part of their future, the speculation continues regarding his future. One analyst who still thinks Crosby could be traded is Mike Florio, although he doesn't think a trade will happen before the season.
Of course, in this scenario, the Cowboys would need to be a competent team in need of one playmaker to push them over the top. If they're not contending, such a move would make very little sense,
Florio believes the Raiders will go into the 2026 season with Crosby, but says they're a team to keep an eye on during the year. He believes they could decide to send Crosby to a contender if they struggle to start the season .
"Not necessarily before the season, but once the season starts, if the Raiders struggle. Because they've already stretched the rubber band to the point of trading him. And that was at a time when people were concerned about the health of his knee. He's cleared. He's back. Now, whether he's got five more years in that knee is a different issue. But, if they aren't playing well and they understand that Maxx Crosby isn't going to be part of the long-term solution and they could get value for him."
Florio said he's keeping an eye on the Tuesday after Week 9, which is the NFL trade deadline. That's where he sees the Cowboys making a move, especially after they expressed a desire to give up future assets to win now .
"I can see a team like the Cowboys. They've already talked about giving up future assets to improve their defense. And there was talk that they were thinking about making a play for Maxx Crosby back in March when the Ravens did. It would not surprise me if the Cowboys contend, the Raiders don't, Crosby gets traded to Dallas."
Crosby was in the news for another reason lately, as he and quarterback Kirk Cousins got into a "scuffle" during Raiders practice .
Cousins took exception to Crosby's physical play, which led to an altercation. While it was reported that no punches were thrown, both players were held out of practice for one day. Crosby plays with a relentless motor, which is part of what helps him succeed on game day, but in this instance, it drew the ire of the team's veteran quarterback.

title: Former NFL QB Says Cowboys’ D-Line Is Going to ‘Eat’ This Year
full_text:
Christian Parker is one of the biggest names in coaching right now. Whether he proves to be successful is still a question, but all eyes are on the Dallas Cowboys first-year defensive coordinator.
Parker takes over a defense that was atrocious in 2025 under Matt Eberflus, and will face plenty of pressure to improve that unit quickly in 2026. The Cowboys have an elite offense, with all 11 starters returning. The belief is that they will be a contender, as long as Parker makes them relevant on defense.
On Tuesday, Parker's star got quite the boost as his defense held its own against the Los Angeles Rams . It's a stretch to say they shut the high-flying Los Angeles offense down, which was never going to happen during a joint practice . Neither team had schemed anything up, so the players were very vanilla. What was important, however, is that the Cowboys weren't embarrassed. That wasn't the case in 2025, as the Rams made it look as though they were practicing against air.
That practice has once again given hope to Dallas, but others are seeing plenty of positives as well. That includes former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel, who said this defensive line is going to "eat" this year. Daniel claims the combination of the recently extended Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark is the best one-two punch on the interior that the Cowboys have had. He added that Parker will run a multiple defense in the same way his mentor Vic Fangio did, which will allow them to generate pressure without blitzing.
"And that is what a Vic Fangio defense does. They absolutely eat on that defensive line. Even going back to the 49ers years, they've always had beasts on that D-line," Daniel said on ESPN's NFL Live . "It's a system that's pretty simple at its core. But the first thing that Fangio would tell you is they do not want to blitz. And if you have a defensive lineman or defensive line in general that can get pressure on a quarterback without blitzing, it leaves more people in coverage, right?"
The one question Daniel seemed to have about this defense was just how fast Parker could get his scheme installed and allow the defense to find its rhythm.
That's a fair question not only because Parker is entering his first year as a defensive play-caller, but more than half of the defensive starters for the Cowboys will be new this season. Thankfully, their offense is good enough to win games even without an elite defense, but if they want to make a true run in the playoffs, this defense has to be firing on all cylinders.

title: 4 Dallas Cowboys Climbing the Depth Chart Following Joint Practice With Rams
full_text:
Tuesday was a big day for the Dallas Cowboys as they took on the Los Angeles Rams in a joint practice. It was a great opportunity for the coaching staff to see how their players performed against another team, and they came out of this one looking strong.
The big story was the defense , which was able to hold their own against the high-powered Rams. That's a major win considering how mismatched they were a year ago. Offensively, there were several standouts as well, which isn't surprising given how impressive they were on this side of the ball in 2025.
With the practice behind them, let's identify four Cowboys who are climbing up the depth chart.
Dee Winters was added in a trade with the San Francisco 49ers during the draft, and was penciled in as a starter next to DeMarvion Overshown. In recent weeks, Winters has been somewhat forgotten thanks to the explosion of rookie third-round pick Jaishawn Barham .
Against the Rams, Winters showed why Dallas made the move to bring him in this offseason. He was one of the better defenders on the field, making plays against the run and in pass coverage. Barham might be the future at the position, but Winters proved he might still be the more consistent starter right now.
Third-year tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford has made a name for himself as a blocker, but his pass-catching has been vastly improved during camp. Undrafted out of Syracuse in 2025, Justin Barron made waves as a converted safety who moved to linebacker. His coverage skills made him an intriguing option, but he became a forgotten man after playing just 30 snaps on special teams as a rookie.
On Tuesday, he reminded us all why we paid attention last year as he recorded three interceptions against the Rams . He also made several stops against the run, which could help him fight for a spot on the 53-man roster.
It's hard to find anyone on the roster, other than maybe Jaishawn Barham, who has seen their stock increase more during training camp than Marist Liufau.
When it was initially announced that Liufau would move to the edge, there was speculation that he wouldn't make the initial 53-man roster . He has been a standout during practices and his hard work carried over to their joint practice with the Rams. title: Quinnen Williams Extension Puts Finishing Touches on Cowboys' Micah Parsons Trade
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys signed defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to a massive three-year, $105.9 million contract extension on Monday, locking him in for the foreseeable future.
And in the process, the Cowboys put what could be viewed as the finishing touches on the blockbuster Micah Parsons trade that shook the NFL world last August. The New York Jets then got involved with pieces of the trade after sending Williams to the Cowboys before last season's deadline.
With the trade being a potential franchise-altering move for both Dallas and the Green Bay Packers, it's worth revisiting each part of the deal, including how things worked out for the Jets.
Let's look at the Cowboys-Packers Parsons trade as if it were a three-team deal with the Jets.
- DT Quinnen Williams - DT Kenny Clark - 2026 first-round pick (Dallas then traded this pick to move down and select Malachi Lawrence)
- DT Mazi Smith - 2027 first-round pick (from Green Bay via Dallas) - 2026 second-round pick (traded to Detroit)
The answer to that question remains up in the air. After all, the Jets could use their new 2027 first-round pick to select a franchise-altering player that brings multiple Super Bowls back to the franchise.
But until that unlikely scenario plays out, the clear winner so far is Dallas.
The Cowboys have one of the NFL's best interior duos on the defensive line with Clark and Williams. With seven combined Pro Bowl appearances and 79.5 career sacks between them, Dallas has the core of its defense in place for the next handful of years.
And with Parsons still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in November, it's unclear if he will ever get back to the form he was at during his first 14 games with Green Bay last year. The Packers may not end up getting the franchise-altering results out of Parsons that they anticipated when they traded for him.
One could argue that Clark, 30, will hit a wall soon and won't be as productive. That's a reasonable stance for most players, but Clark has missed just one game over the past five seasons and doesn't look to be slowing down anytime soon.
While Parsons will look to reprove himself coming off of injury, expect Clark and Williams to be the catalysts behind Dallas' defensive turnaround this upcoming season.

title: Dallas Cowboys Joint Practice Takeaways as Defense Dominates Rams
full_text:
Tuesday brought some welcome change for the Dallas Cowboys as they were able to take the field against a different team for the first time this offseason. Dallas headed to Woodland Hills to take on the Los Angeles Rams at their facility in a joint practice.
These joint practices have become very popular with NFL head coaches and players saying they get more from these sessions than they do any preseason game. That's why head coach Brian Schottenheimer hardly plays starters in the preseason, instead giving them their practice reps in controlled atmospheres such as the one they were in against L.A.
Cameras weren't allowed, so information was limited, but beat reporters on site were able to give us plenty of insight to the day's events. With their help, here's a roundup of the biggest takeaways from the day.
One thing that stood out to Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News was how much better the defense looked. While the starting offense had its issues, Hoyt said the defense held their own. He stated the Cowboys looked "shellshocked" by the Rams' offense in 2025 and despite giving up one big play to Puka Nacua, he said they " held up very well ."
He added that while Nacua beat Shavon Revel for a decent gain, the Dallas defensive back also made a great stop by catching up to Nacua on a deep route and forcing an incompletion. That's a huge win for new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is being tasked with fixing one of the league's worst defenses from a year ago.
Parker's solid work continued with the reserves taking over as the Dallas defense had multiple turnovers, stuffs in the run game, and pass deflections. Overall, it was a huge win for Parker and a momentum builder for the defense.
After moving from linebacker to EDGE this offseason, Marist Liufau is beginning to make some noise at his new position. His ascension continued on Tuesday as Liufau recorded an early sack while working with the backups.
He wasn't alone, however, with Isaiah Land also recording a sack while stuffing a run for no gain as well. Land was an undrafted free agent addition in 2023 but left in 2024 to join the Indianapolis Colts. He re-signed this offseason and while he's a longshot to make the roster, he's making sure he doesn't go down without a fight.
Dee Winters has been a forgotten man in Dallas with rookie Jaishawn Barham stealing all of the attention. Winters made sure to remind everyone he could play during the joint practice which included a great stop against Blake Corum in the run game. According to Patrik Walker, Winters showed excellent speed and recognition to shut down the play for a short loss.
Another linebacker who has been overlooked is Justin Barron, an UDFA from Syracuse in 2025. A converted safety, Barron showed off his coverage skills against Los Angeles while recording three interceptions . He was also active against the run, picking up a couple of stops.
Second-year running back Jaydon Blue has been turning heads throughout camp and seemingly had the inside track on the RB2 job. He might have hurt his chances against Los Angeles, however, as Blue had an early fumble. It's not the end of the world, but with Phil Mafah playing as well as he has, Blue has very limited room for error, making this a noticeable mistake.

title: Dallas Cowboys Salary Cap Implications From Quinnen Williams Contract Extension
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have wrapped up a key defensive player for the long haul after agreeing to a massive contract extension with Quinnen Williams — and we now have an idea of how that new contract could impact Dallas' cap space situation.
According to reports, Williams' new pact with the Cowboys is a three-year, $105.9 million contract that makes him one of the highest-paid defensive linemen in the NFL.
Now, Cowboys fans want to know how this impacts the salary cap, and while we don't have exact numbers until the official details are released, we do have an idea.
Patrik Walker of DallasCowboys.com says the deal could save the Cowboys close to $35 million in total over the next two years "depending on the contract structure."
That is broken down into roughly $15.5 million this season and $19.2 million next season.
According to Over The Cap , the Cowboys are sitting with about $5.4 million in cap space currently, so they could have nearly $20 million to work with after Williams' extension.
As far as next season is concerned, the Cowboys are projected to be $15.5 million over the cap, so Williams' extension could put them back in the black all by itself.
With that anticipated injection of cap space, the Cowboys are well-positioned to make at least another significant move.
And we know the Cowboys are open to doing so after both Jerry and Stephen Jones have made that quite clear in recent weeks.
"I'd give up the future to substitute where we are today," Jerry said to the media at the outset of training camp. "As to a player, to give you an idea about what I'd invest, something substantive, to get the right kind of deal and improve us for Opening Day? I would.
"Stephen Jones was talking on the Cowboys broadcast about tinkering with the roster and said that they are still actively talking to other NFL teams about options as well as veteran free agents," Blogging The Boys' RJ Ochoa relayed. "He said if he was a betting man the 90 man roster would look different in a couple of weeks."
Stephen noted that he was focused in on the linebacker and cornerback battles in training camp, so that may indicate which positions the Cowboys are thinking about adding at.
The first player who immediately comes to mind there is Bobby Wagner , who is still a free agent and would no doubt shore up Dallas' promising but uncertain linebacker spot.
When it comes to possible trades, we'd love to see Dallas make a play for either Maxx Crosby or Josh Sweat, although Crosby feels likely begin the season in Las Vegas after re-committing there following the nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens.
That said, a deadline deal remains possible if things go south for the Raiders once again in 2026.
Sweat was reportedly unhappy in Arizona earlier this offseason, so there's a legitimate chance he hits the trade block before Week 1.
If that happens, the Cowboys absolutely should make a play for him to bolster their edge rushers room, which, like the linebacker position, has some question marks.
Whether it's adding Crosby, Sweat, Wagner or a cornerback or another position, the Cowboys are in great shape to bolster the roster ahead of the season thanks to Williams' extension.

title: 6 Dallas Cowboys Who Need a Strong Preseason Debut vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys aren't expected to play their starters much, if at all, during the upcoming preseason. This should come as no surprise to anyone who watched the team a year ago as head coach Brian Schottenheimer was reluctant to expose any of their key players to unnecessary hits in the preseason.
That doesn't mean these games aren't important. They are still incredibly vital for players who are fighting for a spot on the roster and want to prove themselves in game situations.
Here we look at six such players who need to perform well in the Cowboys' preseason debut this Saturday against the Seattle Seahawks.
As an undrafted free agent a year ago, Traeshon Holden made a name for himself with a strong training camp. His performance wasn't enough to earn a spot on the 53-man roster as Holden spent the year on the practice squad.
Entering year two, Holden has been even better and is said to be higher on the depth chart than expected . Still, Dallas has had several players step up recently, including Camden Brown, which is putting plenty of pressure on Holden. That's why he needs to step up in the preseason to ensure no one surpasses him.
Cornerback was a weakness heading into camp but the competition has heated up. Shavon Revel and Cobie Durant have been excellent and are battling for the starting spot opposite DaRon Bland.
Behind them, Caelen Carson has also been playing well, but needs to fend off Devin Moore, Derion Kendrick, Reddy Steward, and Josh Butler. It's a tight race and Carson needs to do something to separate himself from the pack.
Earlier this offseason, Brian Schottenheimer said Nate Thomas would compete for the starting left tackle spot. That no longer appears to be the case as Thomas has been working with the second team at right tackle during camp. He's suddenly in danger of losing the swing tackle spot to rookie Drew Shelton and can use the preseason to remind the coaching staff why they liked him so much entering the offseason.
One of the changes Christian Parker made this offseason was moving Marist Liufau from linebacker to EDGE . It's a brand new position for Liufau, who has the physical tools to get the job done. He's also been stepping up his performance in practice lately, sending him into the preseason with rising stock . Liufau is firmly on the bubble but can lock up a spot with a strong preseason, which begins on Saturday.
Added in a trade with the New England Patriots last year, Joe Milton was the QB2 throughout the season for Dallas. When he was first added, there was plenty of excitement for the rocket-armed quarterback, but he had issues with consistency throughout the preseason. That's been the case again this year, as Milton is falling behind Sam Howell in the battle for the backup spot. Milton enters the preseason on the roster bubble and can't afford any lackluster performances.
Just as Milton can't afford to slip up, Sam Howell can't surrender any ground. He's been the more consistent signal-caller during camp but a poor performance against Seattle can erase a lot of the goodwill he's built up. On the other hand, if he comes out and impresses, he might be able to lock up his spot in a hurry.

title: Quinnen Williams' Agent Nicole Lynn Celebrates Blockbuster Cowboys Extension
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' defensive overhaul was in full swing during the offseason, with defensive coordinator Christian Parker bringing in a new batch of players to fit into his versatile scheme .
But even before Parker got his hands on the defense, the Cowboys were rebuilding the defense and culture, acquiring Quinnen Williams at the NFL trade deadline .
Williams brought All-Pro credentials to Dallas' defensive front, and now he is here long term.
On Monday, the Cowboys and Williams agreed to a blockbuster three-year, $105.9 million contract extension, with $101 million in guaranteed cash. Right before his deal was announced, Williams' agent, Nicole Lynn of Klutch Sports, foreshadowed and celebrated the deal.
In his seven games with the Cowboys last season, Williams recorded 20 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 33 quarterback pressures, and two tackles for a loss. It was clear that he was going to be the anchor for the Cowboys' defense, and he was rewarded.
Williams' agent, Nicole Lynn, celebrated the deal by shouting out Brinks.
Anyone have a Brinks truck? 👀
Not only does Williams' $105.9 million deal include $101 million guaranteed, but Williams also receives $63.35 million at signing. His $35.3 million annual average ranks second among defensive tackles across the league.
When speaking about Williams, Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones made it clear that Williams was a leader in the locker room, and someone the team values moving into the future.
"One, let's talk about what he does on the practice field," Jones said, via ESPN. "I mean he's a great player and he's one of the hardest practicing guys out there. Anytime he lines up, you feel him. He doesn't take anything for granted, doesn't say, 'Hey, I got this.' [It's,] 'Let my play do the talking when we play a game.' You see it. He's the best player on the field whenever he's out there. And so that was a big piece of it. And then the other thing is just what a man he is. He's a leader. We didn't have a lot of leadership on defense for the last couple of years. Now to have him and Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary, I think has really picked it up over there in terms of culture and the leadership ."
With an impressive offseason and high hopes for the defense, it was crucial to sign Williams to a big deal, and now the team can look to the future with an All-Pro talent in the center of its defense.

title: Broncos Camp Day 11: Good J.K. Dobbins News | Takeaways | Winners and Losers
full_text:
Denver Broncos training camp marched ahead on Wednesday.
With the first preseason game coming up on Friday vs. the Atlanta Falcons , Day 11 of Broncos camp was unique. The Broncos' practice format was an opponent-prep session with no pads.
It was also a shorter practice; just 90 minutes long, give or take. What did we learn?
Let's get to the key storylines from Day 11, what takeaways may be had, and the winners and losers.
After Wednesday's practice, head coach Sean Payton announced that Nix will not play on Friday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. However, Payton said that most starters will play "around 15 snaps" vs. the Falcons.
"Expecting our starters to play around 15 plays," Payton said after Wednesday's practice . "Bo won't play. He'll play next week."
Payton made it clear that Denver plans for Nix to get some preseason exposure, but the team is going to wait until Game 2 to debut its young franchise quarterback. Nix will also play in Game 3.
With Nix sitting out, the plan is for Stidham to play the first half and Ehlinger to play the second. Although Payton recently tried to walk back his offseason "we see a competition" comments about the No. 2 quarterback, this job is very much up for grabs.
Stidham has been the understood backup for the past three years — and he's paid like it. But after his performance in the AFC championship game, perhaps, the Broncos want to see if Ehlinger could be a better option.
Ehlinger has had a great camp, but it will take a lot to unseat Stidham as the QB2. The preseason games will play a major role in the Broncos' decision here.
Running back J.K. Dobbins practiced on Day 11, making it two days in a row after he got dinged up in Monday's session. The Broncos need him healthy in order for their revamped ground game to reach its full potential this season, so don't expect to see the veteran back in Atlanta.
Working on the side field during practice on Wednesday were wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr., centers Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth, offensive lineman Alex Palczewski, linebacker Jordan Turner, and rush linebacker Dasan McCullough, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel . Palczewski's presence on the side field is new; he practiced in full on Day 10.
Adkins got hurt last Friday, but recently returned to practice after missing a couple of days, so he may have reaggravated his injury. Turner was just activated off the Non-Football Injury list on Day 9 , so missing more live reps isn't good for his roster outlook.
Not seen at practice were tight end Caleb Lohner, wide receiver Michael Bandy, and center Michael Deiter. We learned from Payton after practice that Deiter suffered a serious quad injury on Tuesday that will end his season.
With all three of Denver's top centers injured, Calvin Throckmorton has run with the first-team, despite being listed as the No. 2 left guard on the first unofficial depth chart .
The Broncos worked out the veteran safety on Wednesday, per Gabriel , which comes with some curious implications for how the depth competition is shaping up at the position. Beyond Talanoa Hufanga, Brandon Jones, and Devon Key, the Broncos have been hoping to see great competition at safety.
If the Broncos keep four safeties, there's only one open roster spot. Key is an assumed lock because of his special teams prowess (first-team All-Pro last year), and he's also getting the first bite at the apple in replacing P.J. Locke as the No. 3 safety.
If the Broncos sign Rapp, it will be a poor reflection of how the Broncos see the depth safeties. However, with all three preseason games left to be played, there's plenty of time yet for one or two of these safeties to make a case for themselves.
Again, it was a lighter practice, so there wasn't as much to see from an individual performance perspective, but Dobbins makes the winner's column for practicing two days in a row.
Key makes it for returning to practice after missing many days with a soft-tissue injury.
Deiter's injury puts him on this list. He's the second player injured in camp whose season is already over.
Palczewski and Adkins make the list for not practicing in full. It'll be interesting to see if they travel with the team to Atlanta, as Payton said the Broncos plan to leave the injured players behind.
Skinner, Anderson, Scott, and Robertson make the list simply because of the implications of Rapp working out. It's a little unfair to paint them all with such broad strokes, but if the Broncos sign a safety, it means they're not happy with what they're seeing on the depth side.
