title: Sean Payton Made the Right Call on Bo Nix Ahead of Broncos' Preseason Opener
full_text:
With the preseason opener coming on Friday, the Denver Broncos have made their decision.
Third-year quarterback Bo Nix won't play in Game 1 on the road vs. the Atlanta Falcons , Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced on Wednesday.
"Expecting our starters to play around 15 plays," Payton said after Wednesday's practice. "Bo won't play. He'll play next week."
The Broncos are acting accordingly with their young franchise quarterback. All of this team's 2026 ambitions are tied to Nix being on the field.
With Nix returning from a fractured ankle that required corrective surgery in January and a clean-up procedure in the spring, there's no reason to play him in the first preseason game. That's doubly true when you consider the artificial surface of Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Better safe than sorry.
Keep in mind, this isn't a reflection of Nix's performance in training camp thus far or of his overall health/recovery. He's been a full participant at camp with zero limits or strictures on his participation. Through 11 practices, he's looked as mobile and athletic as ever, like he's as good as new.
Nix's throwing motion looks more polished , and his deep-ball accuracy has been impressive. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said recently that Nix's deep accuracy has been " off the charts " in camp.
Nix looks more comfortable, more poised, and maybe even a bit more vocal. These practices have been physical and competitive, and the first-team offense and defense have butted heads at times.
Now in his third year in Payton's system, Nix recently told Kay Adams of the Up & Adams Show that he and the offense feel more on the level with the Broncos' elite defense, which has raised the competitive bar. These practices have been intense.
Another big reason not to play Nix in Game 1 is the absence of a healthy center. Starter Luke Wattenberg has been out since suffering an injury on Day 3 of camp, while Alex Forsyth has missed the past three days.
Even third-team center Michael Deiter went down on Tuesday, forcing the Broncos to turn to Calvin Throckmorton to snap with the starters. Payton announced on Wednesday that Deiter suffered a major quad injury that will require surgery, which means he's likely headed for injured reserve.
The Broncos are concerningly thin at center with Wattenberg and Forsyth still sidelined. I wonder if it we were in the regular season whether Wattenberg would be able to push through the injury report to play on game day, but with no such pressure existing in August, the Broncos aren't rushing their starter back onto the field.
As for Nix, if this were a regular-season game, he would be playing. But it's an exhibition contest, and the Broncos made this decision weeks ago.
"He wants to play. He'll play the next two weeks," Payton said of Nix. "I think that was probably something that was already decided like a month ago. But if we were playing a game, I would say he would play—you'd have to ask him—but I would say 100%."
In all honesty, I think most Broncos fans would be fine if Nix didn't step on the field of play until Week 1 of the regular season. But he's champing at the bit to play, and Payton believes in playing his starters in the preseason to help build a football callus and re-acclimate them to NFL game speed, but there's always a fine line.
Nix obviously wants to play in the preseason, but with Game 2 (Green Bay Packers) and Game 3 (Minnesota Vikings) being at Empower Field at Mile High on a playing surface he and the Broncos know well, the team is going to bide its time.
“I think preseason’s always a great time to get back out there and get your feet wet a little bit and see defenses in a live situation before the first game," Nix said on Monday, Day 9 of Broncos camp.
By this point, all the players on the Broncos' roster are dying to go against an outside opponent. That's especially true this summer, since Payton opted to skip the opportunity to hold a joint practice with any of Denver's preseason opponents.
Fans will have to wait at least another week before seeing Nix suit up again. When he returns to the field at Mile High, it'll be the first time since he suffered that heartbreaking fractured ankle on the third-to-last play of the divisional round of the playoffs in January.
Nix led the Broncos to a 33-30 overtime win, then had to watch from the booth the next week when the New England Patriots came to town for the AFC championship game. We all know how that game turned out.
Suffice it to say, Nix is hungry. He's looking to make up for lost time after leading his team to the doorstep of the Super Bowl. But good things come to those who wait.

title: Sean Payton 'Feels Bad For' Michael Deiter After Major Injury
full_text:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced backup center Michael Deiter, who was carted off the practice field on Tuesday, suffered a quad injury that will end his 2026 season before it even began.
Deiter will undergo corrective surgery and likely head to the injured reserve list.
"Feel bad for him," Payton told reporters following Wednesday's practice.
A former Dolphins third-round pick, Deiter is in his second season with the Broncos after joining the club's practice squad in January and subsequently landing a futures deal . The soon-to-be 30-year-old found his way to the Mile High City following stops in Miami, Houston, and Washington.
Deiter had been temporarily handling first-string center responsibilities with starter Luke Wattenberg and direct backup Alex Forsyth both battling injuries . Neither Wattenberg nor Forsyth participated in drills on Wednesday.
Veteran guard-by-trade Calvin Throckmorton was forced into the pivot with the aforementioned sidelined. It's possible, if not probable, that Throckmorton remains there for Friday's preseason opener at Atlanta before giving way to undrafted rookie C Gavin Ortega.
“We’ll work through it. We have guys that are flexible. We’ll be fine," Payton said Tuesday.
With Denver's starters set to play only 15 snaps against the Falcons, it's unlikely that All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz will be asked to man the center position in what's ultimately a meaningless game.
However, should this issue linger into the regular season, Meinerz acknowledged he's willing to pinch-hit if needed. Moreover, he stressed the importance of the starting front five (read: Wattenberg) getting back on the field together as soon as possible to form necessary chemistry — especially when the proverbial bullets start flying for real.
“We’re able to get into the level 400 of our offense a lot quicker because we already have a base foundation and fundamentals of how we want to do things," Meinerz told reporters Tuesday. "Now we’re looking at efficiencies, now we’re looking at not only winning the block, but being dominant with that block and understanding that there’s an emphasis in the rushing game this year for us. So just constantly grinding in our individual period to make sure that those reps are feeling good, ‘Hey, are my hands good here? Hey, was my hat... Did I give you enough help here?’ There’s always constant little feedback here, and I think what’s most fun is how much smaller the communication’s going to get on the line of scrimmage because when an offensive line’s able to communicate so little, there’s a lot less tells for the defense to be able to pick up on.”

title: Broncos' Release First Unofficial Depth Chart—Analyzing the Clues
full_text:
Let the overreactions begin! The Denver Broncos' first unofficial depth chart is here.
The Broncos are set to face the Atlanta Falcons in their first preseason game of the year on Friday, giving us our first look at the unofficial depth chart.
With two weeks or so of training camp in the books, let's take a look at the Broncos' first depth chart, with an emphasis on unofficial , and see if we can uncover any clues relative to the roster battles taking place this summer.
Analysis : Nothing has changed here, for now. Ehlinger has turned in an impressive camp performance, though, while Stidham seems to be pressing. This depth chart could change, depending on how these preseason games unfold.
Analysis : This is our first big reminder not to read deeply into this unofficial depth chart. As per Sean Payton's tradition, the rookie, Coleman, starts at the bottom of the depth chart, but based on what we've seen in camp, he's the No. 3 running back behind Dobbins and Harvey.
Analysis : That's that. Just one player listed and we all know who it is.
Analysis : Again, we have the rookies at the bottom. It's a matter of course with Payton, though in this case, it also happens to be an accurate reflection of where things stand. It'l be a surprise if the fifth-rounder Joly doesn't make the 53-man roster, but he has a long way to go in his development as an NFL-caliber tight end.
Analysis : Key, Manjack, and Duplessis are undrafted rookies, while Butler is a 30-year-old veteran in his second NFL season, officially. Butler, a two-time UFL Offensive Player of the Year, is interesting, based on how he's performed in camp, but nobody, and I mean nobody, has looked better than "Patty Ice" in camp thus far .
Analysis : The X and Z in Payton's offense is often nominal. He interchanges much, but as it stands, Mims tops the depth chart over Franklin, which is interesting, considering how Franklin was Denver's No. 2 receiver last year. Rowan recently returned to the Broncos after spending much of his rookie year on the practice squad, while Ross and Katsis are undrafted rookies who've shined thus far in camp.
Analysis : This is another example of the relative meaninglessness of the X, Z, and slot. Waddle is the 1a or 1b receiver in the ultimate pecking order, and will be moved around the formation at all the different spots. For now, though, only Waddle and Humphrey are listed in the slot.
Analysis : This one is based on NFL experience, once you get past Bolles. Peart is a veteran, while Crum is in Year 3. Peart missed most of last season after tearing his ACL in Week 6, so Crum served as the primary swing tackle. Miller is an undrafted rookie.
Analysis : Powers is the starter, while Throckmorton is a tenured vet. Ortega is an undrafted rookie. Both Throckmorton and Ortega have been called to play center snaps this week with all the injuries the Broncos have dealt with at the position.
Analysis : All three men are currently injured. Wattenberg has missed the past week, going down on the first day of pads, while Forsyth has missed the past couple of days. Deiter was running as the first-team center on Day 9 and Day 10 before going down himself on Tuesday, and being carted off. It's unlikely that any of these three will play in Atlanta.
Analysis : This is interesting. We all know the All-Pro, Meinerz, but Casey is a fourth-round rookie who's spent his entire career playing on the left side of the line. Casey's future is at left guard; another reminder not to read into these depth charts.
Analysis : McGlinchey is the locked-in starter, while Palczewski is still the primary backup at right tackle. However, after filling in for Powers at left guard for much of last season, Palczewski has right-to-left-side and inside/outside versatility. When Powers has been given any rest days or reps in camp this summer, Palczewski has gotten some first-team reps at left guard, and at right tackle in place of McGlinchey.
Analysis : It's interesting to see Jackson listed ahead of Jones here, but again, this unofficial depth chart doesn't carry much meaning. Jones is a 2025 third-rounder while Jackson is in his third year with the Broncos.
Analysis : There's a conspicuous name missing from the nose tackle depth chart, but we'll address that with the next position. Miller and Williams are the last two guys in the D-line room, so they'll need to shine in the preseason to stand a chance at making the roster.
Analysis : This may be the first depth chart to provide any true inkling into what the coaches are thinking. With John Franklin-Myers gone, Roach is in the driver's seat to win that starting job, instead of living as the backup nose tackle behind Jones. And Uwazurike is giving Roach a run for his money in camp. Onyedim is a rookie third-rounder who is a lock for the roster.
Analysis : Bonitto is a Pro Bowler, but Elliss has been one of the defensive stars of camp. I'm really looking forward to seeing Elliss in action this year. Robinson has also had a great camp as a 2025 fourth-rounder, while Walker is trying to make up for lost time after missing his entire rookie season with an injury.
Analysis : Cooper is the starter, while Tillman will be hard to beat out for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Sanders, a 2023 third-rounder, will certainly try, but unless the Broncos keep five outside linebackers this year, it'll be tough for him to make the roster. McCullough is an undrafted rookie who's dealt with an injury that has sidelined him for nearly a week.
Analysis : These linebacker spots are interchangeable. Singleton is the starter, while Reid made the roster last year as an undrafted rookie. Turner just got activated from the Non-Football Injury list, and has some catching up to do.
Analysis : Strnad returns as a starter, with Bailey doing everything he can to win one of the two linebacker roster spots. Murdock is a seventh-rounder and York is undrafted. Both are rookies and have impressed thus far in camp.
Analysis : Surtain needs no explanation. Abrams-Draine has had a great camp in Year 3, while Fresch was signed from the UFL in June, though he's dealt with an injury in camp that cost him a couple of days. Hallman was signed late last week after the Broncos waived the injured Jaden Robinson.
Analysis : Moss has been a super-stud in camp, leaving absolutely no daylight for Barron to win the No. 2 cornerback job. Barron, a 2025 first-rounder, has played a lot of nickel and dime in camp. Austin is an undrafted rookie who's shown some fight in camp.
Analysis : McMillian will remain at the top here, with Barron as the first defensive back onto the field in most sub-packages. The Broncos like Taylor, but they're super strong at nickel corner.
Analysis : Behind Hufanga, this depth chart is still up for grabs, though Skinner has the edge due to his sixth-round draft pedigree (2023) and special teams acumen. Anderson was a free-agent signing, who also brings some third-phase production to the table, while Robertson is an undrafted rookie.
Analysis : Jones is the starter, while Key is also a lock for the roster as a first-team All-Pro special teams ace. Scott is a seventh-round rookie battling with Skinner, Anderson, and Robertson for the fourth, and likely final, safety spot on the roster.
Analysis : No explanation needed.
Analysis : Again, self-explanatory.
Analysis : Who will serve as Mims's kickoff partner? Don't discount Coleman as a contender, even though he's unlisted here. Coleman returned some kicks during the Broncos' planned scrimmage on Day 8. Katis was signed for his returner upside.
Analysis : Mims is a two-time All-Pro returner, but if he's going to feature more in the offense, the Broncos need another good option. Bandy is at least reliable (though he muffed a punt last year), while Ross is a rookie with some juice. Katsis is unlisted here but may also be in the running.

title: Broncos Unveil 2026 Uniform Schedule: What They'll Wear for Every Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have unveiled their uniform schedule for the 2026 regular season.
Once again, the Broncos will use various combinations of their Sunset Orange, Summit White, and Midnight Navy jerseys throughout the season, with two games featuring the iconic '77 Throwbacks.
The combination of pants and socks will be announced each week. Once again, the Broncos are poised to win double-digit games and look good doing it.
The Broncos unveiled their Mile High Collection of new uniform designs in 2024. It just so happened to coincide with the arrival of Bo Nix, but it's another example of the Walton-Penner ownership group's influence on the Broncos.
Sports Illustrated ranked the Broncos' Mile High Collection in the top 10 of NFL uniforms for a reason. They're a great look that balances the late-'90s era uniform design with the vintage Throwbacks.
Here's how the game-by-game uniforms will shake out in 2026.
Our 2026 uniform schedule is here! Full uniform combos with pants + socks will be announced the week of each game. pic.twitter.com/3vAIh4FopJ
The Broncos don't have it easy this year. Not only do they get to play a first-place schedule, but it is also the AFC West's turn to face the AFC East and the NFC West.
Five playoff teams came out of those two divisions last year, and the Broncos will face every NFC West team within the first seven weeks. The Broncos will also have to face the Chiefs twice in the first eight weeks, along with the Chargers on the road and the Jaguars at home.
It's a gauntlet, but if the Broncos can weather it, their second-half schedule is one of the easiest in the NFL . Things do tighten up late in the season, with a Week 16 home game against the Bills on Christmas Day, a trip to Foxboro to take on the Patriots in Week 17, and a homestand vs. the Chargers for the season finale.
Suffice it to say, there's a reason the Broncos' training camp has been so physical and competitive. If they don't form that callus now, the Broncos risk being eviscerated early in the season.
It's also no wonder why Sean Payton and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have focused so heavily on the run game in camp. The Broncos are gearing up to out-physical their opponents in 2026.
Let's just hope the injuries in camp begin to slow down somewhat. I suppose there is a price to be paid for building any callus, and that includes the figurative variety as a collective.

title: Broncos vs. Falcons: 5 Things to Watch for in the Preseason Opener
full_text:
Football is back. The Denver Broncos are getting ready for their first preseason game by traveling to take on the Atlanta Falcons on Friday.
With this being the Broncos' first football contest since losing the AFC championship game, there are five things to watch for, especially given the changes the team has made since January.
Let's get into Broncos-Falcons.
The biggest change the Broncos made is with their offensive play-caller, which means there is a lot to watch for here. It might take some time for Davis Webb to get up to speed, and the first step to watch for is how long it takes to get the plays in .
It was a clear issue for Bo Nix last year, and in multiple games you could see his frustration with how long the play calls took coming in from Sean Payton on the sideline. We don't yet know whether Nix will play in preseason Game 1, but we will still be able to monitor whether Webb can get the calls in on time and give the quarterbacks time to make adjustments before the snap.
Throughout the camp practices, there has been a lot of harping on the Broncos' safeties for their poor play. There have been a lot of downfield passes that have gotten over the safeties' heads.
This game will be a chance to see whether they step it up in a game setting or if the Broncos need to start looking outside for additional safety help. The Broncos know they have quality special teams play from their depth safeties, but they need someone to step it up on the defensive side of the ball.
The linebackers have a similar situation before them, as Payton mentioned how he is looking for a linebacker to step up for the third spot on the roster. There have been some plays made by the depth linebackers, especially Karene Reid and Red Murdock , but this game offers them all a better chance to ply their wares, and for them to stand out, especially with special teams being a factor.
Denver’s run game was inconsistent last year whenever J.K. Dobbins wasn’t carrying the ball, both before and after his injury. The offensive line did well, though it wasn’t perfect, while the Broncos' tight ends were extremely poor in run-blocking execution.
Denver needs more from both its offensive line and tight ends, but more pressure is on the latter group. Part of the issue with the tight ends in particular is the lack of blockers in the room.
The Broncos have some potential blockers if Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley can develop, but until then, they only have Adam Trautman and Nate Adkins, and the latter has been dealing with an injury.
Can the unit step up and be a boost to the run game instead of the detriment it was last season?
On the opposite side of things, the Broncos' defensive front had some inconsistencies against power running teams last year. While the Falcons may not have some of their starters playing, including their star and recently paid running back Bijan Robinson, this can still be a good test for the Broncos' defensive front.
Not only is it about how the unit executes as a collective, but also how individual players handle the run game. Players like Sai’vion Jones and Que Robinson both have some concerns about their run defense, so can they show improvement in that aspect of their game, or will they look like pass rushers only?
Robinson showed promise in limited playing time in 2025, and what he's displayed in camp thus far shows there's plenty to build on. It's time to really make it clear in the preseason.
The Broncos have an All-Pro returner in Marvin Mims Jr., but they need someone to step up to help on kick returns and provide value as a backup returner. They have some options to look toward, but do any of them actually step up?
Keep an eye on rookies Jonah Coleman, Kolbe Katsis, and Cameron Ross in the return game. With Mims nursing an injury, it's unlikely he plays, so this group should get plenty of action.

title: Bo Nix Extension Timeline: Greg Penner Makes Broncos' Stance Clear
full_text:
Bo Nix is back on the field, which makes everything happening at Denver Broncos HQ right now feel right as rain.
Two weeks into training camp, Nix has looked very, very good. His mobility is not in question, seven months after fracturing his right ankle in the playoffs. He seems to be unencumbered by the ankle, and fully back to his pre-injury form.
As a passer, Nix's throwing motion looks even more polished , like he spent time working on it during the offseason. And as Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said on Day 8 of camp, Nix's deep-ball accuracy has been " off the charts ."
With an upgraded arsenal around him, there's every reason to hope for a big year-three leap from Nix, just as offensive coordinator Davis Webb forecasted earlier this summer . Sean Payton has insisted that this year's squad is just as fierce a Super Bowl contender as he predicted the 2025 Broncos would be.
After 2026, though, the Broncos have a big decision to make because Nix will be eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. With the rapidity of the quarterback market's growth each year — heck, each month — the Broncos are incentivized to get a Nix extension done as soon as possible.
The question is, have the Broncos begun to look at Nix's future contract? Co-owner and CEO Greg Penner was asked that very question on Tuesday.
“Not much at this point," Penner said. "Obviously, we want Bo here long-term, but we’re really focused on getting ready for this season, putting a competitive team on the field."
The Broncos would be forgiven for not having already locked in a detailed plan, as they're about the business of preparing for the 2026 season, and, frankly, the team can't take action on a Nix extension until the NFL's next new league year opens in March of 2027.
At some point, the Nix conversations will be had, and Penner will leave those initial explorations of the topic to GM George Paton and head coach Sean Payton.
"I’ll leave that to George [Paton] and Sean [Payton], [they] will have conversations about it, but I’ll leave that up to them to lead," Penner said.
The Broncos extended both Paton and Payton during this past offseason. Both men's fingerprints are on the Broncos' 24 wins over the past two years, but without Nix, as we learned in January, the music stops.
They say a franchise quarterback is the tide that raises all ships. If we hold Nix to that standard, does he measure up?
The answer is a resounding yes. Nix deserves a ton of credit for his influence on the Broncos' remarkable turnaround over the past two years. This team went from being an AFC doormat for most of the preceding eight years to immediately making the playoffs with Nix as a rookie.
In Year 2, Nix led the Broncos to a 14-3 record — tying the franchise's single-season wins record — dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West, and earned the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. From there, all of Denver's Super Bowl aspirations were on the table, but Nix would have to out-duel Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills as the first order of business.
Nix did just that, but suffered that heartbreaking ankle fracture on the third-to-last play of overtime. Wil Lutz's game-winning field goal gave Denver the 33-30 win, but it echoed hollowly in retrospect, as soon as Payton announced Nix's injury and that he was done for the season.
Payton and the Broncos put on a brave face, pushing Jarrett Stidham to the fore as the Broncos had no choice but to march ahead to host the New England Patriots in the AFC championship game. But without Nix, the Broncos were dead in the water.
Payton is an excellent coach, but overcoming the loss of a young franchise quarterback on the doorstep of the Super Bowl was a bridge too far for almost any team in NFL history. If nothing else, though, the AFC title game clearly illustrated just how important Nix is to the Broncos.
The Broncos will only go as far as Nix can lead them. And there's every reason to believe the third-year quarterback can rally the Broncos once again, make another postseason run, and perhaps get over the Super Bowl hump.
After the 2026 season, though, the Broncos will want to jump on getting Nix extended. Right now, the going rate for a proven franchise quarterback is somewhere between $44 million and $65 million per year.
The Broncos probably won't even start trying to crack that nut until the 2026 season is in the books. But the sooner they can get Nix re-signed, the better it'll be for the bottom line, because the mind-boggling cost of a franchise quarterback will continue to grow between now and March of 2027, especially if Nix fulfills expectations, and leads the Broncos back to the playoffs.

title: The Biggest Mistake Broncos Can't Afford to Make This Training Camp
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' front office has assembled a strong roster that should keep them among the favorites in the AFC.
Two weeks into training camp, the Broncos are shaping up well. The early signs are more than encouraging, but there are a couple of things I'm concerned about.
As camp marches on, there's one big mistake the Broncos can't afford to make. Let's talk about it.
The Broncos should play the trade market, but in a very specific way. Despite calls on social media for them to trade away a wide receiver or cornerback, they can’t afford to.
That being said, the Broncos would also be remiss if they ignored the opportunity to trade for a tight end. This would keep the team's strengths strong, while bolstering a clear weakness, depending on the tight end Denver traded for.
The reason the Broncos need another tight end really boils down to how weak the position is. Evan Engram built some early hype in camp, and while he and the Broncos are striving to involve him more in the run game as a blocker , it's certainly not his strong suit.
Meanwhile, there has been very little positive about the tight end room as a whole. Tight end has been a roster weakness for three years in a row ; the Broncos need to take greater measures to strengthen it.
Fifth-rounder Justin Joly is displaying his rawness as a rookie; rookie seventh-rounder Dallen Bentley is at the bottom of the depth chart; Nate Adkins has already dealt with a camp injury , and Adam Trautman is yet to make one of our camp notebooks for any reason through two weeks.
Lucas Krull has made a positive play or two as a receiver , but they're few and far between. Caleb Lohner has yet to practice after undergoing a "routine" clean-up procedure in June that wasn't supposed to cost him any days in camp.
It isn’t clear which tight ends might be currently available for a trade, but there isn’t anyone left in free agency who could make enough impact to change the direction of the position in Denver. The Broncos can’t accept just rolling it back with what they have, and no, the solution isn’t Taysom Hill either.
As for why it would be unwise to trade a player away, there are two very different reasons at wide receiver and cornerback. At wide receiver, it's about the medicals, and at cornerback, it's about the depth.
At wide receiver, Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr. are both banged up, and Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin both dealt with injuries last year. This is an offense looking for more explosive plays and a more consistent passing attack throughout the season, so they'll need as many of their weapons in the arsenal as they can get.
Run it back at wide receiver this season, especially with the Broncos' clear Super Bowl aspirations, and then re-evaluate after in 2027 based on who steps up and, of course, contract situations. The Broncos shouldn’t look to disrupt the room right now, and potentially their passing game, which has shown some encouraging signs of taking flight already despite facing a tough defense in practice every day.
As for cornerback, Jahdae Barron has been unable to force his way into the starting lineup. Riley Moss has been on fire, and the Broncos just gave Ja'Quan McMillian a one-year raise on a restricted free-agent tender, so it's not as if Barron has had it easy, despite being a 2025 first-round pick.
However, Barron seems to be behind Kris Abrams-Draine in the boundary cornerback competition. Moss is the starting boundary corner opposite Patrick Surtain II, and he looks like he's made a leap with his play. Trading Moss away would make the room significantly weaker.
If Barron had stepped up by now, this could be a different discussion, but he seems to be falling behind and is trending in the wrong direction. The Broncos can’t afford to make the mistake of trading Moss and putting too much trust in Barron at this point.
It isn’t just one misstep the Broncos can’t afford to make, but three mistakes that are all closely related. This is a good roster, and the Broncos don’t want to disrupt it too much, but they have to see the glaring weakness at tight end and address it.

title: Broncos Camp Day 10: Broncos Thin at Center | Takeaways | Winners and Losers
full_text:
Denver Broncos training camp marches on, with the team back at it on Tuesday.
Day 10 of Broncos camp featured a 2:10-minute practice in the weltering Colorado heat. The players were in pads once again, slugging it out at Broncos Park.
The hope was that a day would pass without a player injury, but alas, it wasn't meant to be. Since the pads went on eight days ago, the Broncos haven't completed a practice without at least one injury.
With that said, let's get to the unfortunate injury that occured on Day 10, as well as the takeaways, and winners and losers.
The Broncos are suddenly extremely thin at center. Deiter went down during a 9-on-7 team drill and had to be carted off by trainers .
With Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth already sidelined by injuries, Deiter had been running with the first-team. The Broncos' center depth is being tested, but head coach Sean Payton dismissed it as a concern moving forward.
“We’ll work through it," Payton said after practice. "We have guys that are flexible. We’ll be fine."
Following Deiter's injury, Calvin Throckmorton took over as the first-team center, a young veteran who's been with the Broncos organization for a couple of years. Undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega saw a bump-up, too, running with the second-team offense, per The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson .
The Broncos still list All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz as a guard/center on their roster, and on cue, he was seen practicing his snapping skills on Tuesday, though not during any team drills. After practice, Meinerz said that he tries to stay sharp at snapping, just in case of emergency.
With the first preseason game coming up on Friday on the road against the Atlanta Falcons, that emergency may be at hand, despite Payton's remarks.
Not in pads on Tuesday were Forsyth, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, outside linebacker Dasan McCullough, wide receiver Michael Bandy, and tight end Caleb Lohner. Meanwhile, running back J.K. Dobbins, wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr., and Wattenberg were in pads but didn't fully participate, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel .
That's a step in the right direction for Dobbins ( injured on Monday ), Mims, and Wattenberg. The Broncos have really struggled to avoid the injury bug in this camp.
It is football, after all, so there's no avoiding injuries completely, but this camp has to be the most eventful injury-wise since Payton took over as head coach in 2023. Again, it's been every single day.
I do wonder whether the Broncos' strong emphasis on the run game in this camp has anything to do with the injuries, especially to the centers and front-seven players on defense. It'll build that callus, to be sure, but it's coming at a cost.
Dobbins was in pads, but he also participated in individual drills ( Tomasson ). Dobbins had fun with the media, conveying that he's doing just fine, as captured by CBS Colorado 's Romi Bean.
J.K. Dobbins running hard and letting everyone know he is good and healthy 👍😏 pic.twitter.com/D9O9O4VEav
Dobbins had to let everyone know he's good after the " pinky promise " he delivered early in camp, vowing to the media and fans that he'd stay healthy for all 17 games. He has a long injury history since entering the league as a Baltimore Ravens second-round pick in 2020, and missed the final seven regular-season games and the playoffs in his first year with the Broncos.
Despite the injury, the Broncos re-signed Dobbins on a two-year, $16 million deal in March, which amounted to a 4x raise. The Broncos believe they can keep him on the field, and not only view him as one of the NFL's premier running backs, but also as a "force multiplier" in terms of the many ways he makes the team better.
It's good to see Dobbins at least practicing individual drills.
"Patty Ice" continued his breakout camp performance on Day 10, catching multiple touchdown passes. He's been a force to be reckoned with, especially in the red zone.
Throckmorton is a big winner on Day 10 because he got to run with the first-team offense. He may be the fourth center option, but it's a great opportunity to showcase his versatility and value to the Broncos, especially with how much depth the team now has on the interior offensive line.
Moss and Bryant are the two biggest standouts of camp thus far. Moss once again had multiple pass break-ups on Day 10, including a deep Bo Nix pass to Courtland Sutton, per KOA 's Ryan Edwards .
Coleman may be a rookie, but he doesn't look or talk like one. He's already displayed his prowess as a between-the-tackles rusher in camp and his receiving skills out of the backfield, but on Day 10, he had a couple of impressive reps in pass protection, too, per Denver7 's Troy Renck . Coleman is a complete back.
Toward the end of practice, when the Broncos were running their situational drills — like two-minute and red-zone — Katsis made an impressive catch in the back of the end zone, skying up to catch a 25-yard Sam Ehlinger "dime" on 4th-&-10, per 9NEWS ' Mike Klis . Katsis has had a great camp thus far, and as an undrafted rookie, he also brings returner ability to the table, which I'm sure fans will get to see in the preseason games.
Krull caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jarrett Stidham to end practice ( Klis ). It was another nice red-zone play made by the veteran tight end, who's feeling the pressure with the Broncos' two rookie tight ends, both of whom were draft picks (Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley), pushing from the bottom of the depth chart.
Deiter makes this list simply because of his unfortunate injury. Otherwise, though, he's been solid and reliable this summer as the Broncos' third center behind Wattenberg and Forsyth. Fingers crossed for the seventh-year Deiter.
Sutton makes this list simply because he's yet to really shine since returning to practice late last week following three straight veteran rest days . On Day 10, Nix looked Sutton's way a couple of times during team period, but couldn't connect; both were broken up by Moss.
With Bryant making plays left and right, it would be good for Sutton to remind everyone of his Pro Bowl pedigree in practice, but the absence of big plays of late is far from an indictment on his status and place with the Broncos. When the regular season rolls around, odds are, Sutton will continue to be Nix's first look and security blanket.
It's worth mentioning, though, how Bryant has capitalized on the time missed by veterans like Sutton and Waddle. Nix has been looking Bryant's way first in practice; how much that has to do with the absences of Sutton and Waddle is unclear, but at the very least, it's safe to say that "Patty Ice" has established some strong chemistry and trust with his quarterback.

title: Ramifications of Backup C Michael Deiter Being Carted Off at Broncos Camp
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were already stretched at the center position. They ended Tuesday even thinner.
That's because backup C Michael Deiter was carted off during training camp practice with an apparent injury suffered in 9-on-7 drills. He did not return to practice and was replaced by veteran lineman Calvin Throckmorton.
Head coach Sean Payton failed to provide an update on Deiter's immediate status, suggesting he's undergoing an evaluation to determine the severity.
A former Dolphins third-round pick, Deiter is entering his second season with the Broncos after joining the club's practice squad in January and subsequently inking a reserve/future deal. The 30-year-old (in September) arrived to Denver following stops in Miami, Houston, and Washington.
Deiter had been assuming primary center responsibilities with starter Luke Wattenberg and direct backup Alex Forsyth both battling injuries and working off to the side amid Tuesday's session.
Deiter is the latest in a long line of Broncos players to go down since camp opened. The list also includes the aforementioned Wattenberg and Forsyth, wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims, and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen, who suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon last week.
"I don’t think it’s heat-related as much as you always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration, obviously. It’s incumbent on the player," Payton said of the injury epidemic on Monday. "It’s hard for anyone to know your soft tissue. So I’m always looking at, all right, what did we do leading up to maybe a period where someone had a strain? We had a warm-down after practice, and we’ll continue to focus on it, though."
As mentioned, Deiter was Denver's third option at center with Wattenberg and Forsyth unavailable. Throckmorton, a more natural guard by trade, was forced into the pivot for the remainder of Tuesday. The latter will likely continue operating as such on Wednesday.
Other in-house options include undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega, who sailed an errant snap on Monday, and perennial All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz, who holds some previous center experience (some last preseason) — and would be up to filling in temporarily if called upon.
"I gotta have it in the back pocket," Meinerz told reporters. "I know that it's important I add that value to the offensive line room, in an emergency situation."

title: Lions Believe Wide Receivers Room Is Best Since Dan Campbell Hired
full_text:
Throughout training camp, multiple Detroit Lions wide receivers have stepped up and made plays.
Head coach Dan Campbell indicated before the final practice leading up to the preseason opener that the receivers room was the best he had observed since he became the Lions coach back in 2021.
Each day, a new player has emerged to contribute and help the offense. For the former NFL tight end, performance on special teams could also be a deciding factor for a wideout battling for a roster spot.
“An all-out battle. That receiver room, this is the best receiver room we've had since I've been here in camp, top to bottom," Campbell said. "I mean, those guys are gifted. It's a really good crew, man. And they're all pretty tough, they're all a little bit different the way they're built. And every one of those guys has flashed on one day or another, has done something pretty damn good. So man, honestly, this thing's up for grabs.
"After you get to the ones you just talked about that we know are up there, there is no telling," Campbell added further. "And special teams is going to have a huge factor. That's the other thing, man, I'll just give you an example. Tay Martin, man, makes plays every day. And he's intriguing on offense, but he makes special teams plays every day. And that's important to us. And he's not the only one.”
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Can Defense Finish in Top 10 in 2026?
It is presumed that second-year wideout Isaac TeSlaa is going to be the Lions third wideout on the depth chart behind offensive staples Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.
Behind the former third-round pick are Greg Dortch, Tom Kennedy, Cedrick Wilson, Tay Martin, Malik Cunningham, Dominic Lovett, Lucky Jackson and Tarik Black.
Wilson, 30, has also made an impression in his first camp with the Lions. A journeyman wideout, Wilson has 126 career receptions for1,524 yards and 12 touchdowns in his career.
After a stint with the Dolphins, the veteran is making plays and was called a "headsy" player last week by Campbell.
"They come in here, they compete. They're not entitled, they just go work, man and that's what he does. And by the way, his special teams reps are pretty good too," said Campbell. "I mean, for a receiver, he can do some stuff. And his tape says that too.”

title: How To Watch Detroit Lions First Preseason Game Against Bengals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions, led by sixth-year head man Dan Campbell, are set to take the field for the first time this preseason Thursday night against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. EST at Paycor Stadium, providing Lions fans with their first chance to see the 2026 roster in game action.
Detroit and Cincinnati last squared off with one another in Week 5 of the 2025 season. The Lions prevailed, 37-24, in a game that saw Jake Browning start in place of the injured Joe Burrow.
This exhibition contest Thursday will be televised across multiple local stations in Michigan (detailed below).
The television broadcast will feature play-by-play voice Jack Kizer (subbing for Jason Benetti), former Lions offensive lineman T.J. Lang and sideline reporter Patti Cesarini. For fans who would rather tune in on the radio, the game will also be broadcast on the Lions Radio Network , with 97.1 The Ticket serving as the flagship station. Dan Miller and Lomas Brown will handle the radio call.
On Thursday, most of Detroit’s first-stringers will not see the field, including signal-caller Jared Goff. It makes the Lions’ preseason tilt with Cincinnati all the more meaningful for the organization’s younger players and those competing for roster spots.
First-round pick Blake Miller, for one, will get his first taste of game action as he competes for the starting right tackle job along with veteran Larry Borom.
Additionally, the backup quarterback position will be another storyline to watch.
Undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer has received a healthy dose of second-and-third-team reps so far in training camp, and is likely to garner a significant number of snaps against the Bengals. Meanwhile, veteran backup Josh Dobbs, who was recently signed by Detroit, is also expected to see some time under center.
All in all, Thursday night's matchup will provide the Lions faithful with its first real look at the team's first-year pros, roster hopefuls and ongoing position battles.
The Lions' contest with Cincinnati marks the first of three exhibition games for Campbell’s squad, with its first and only preseason home game taking place August 22 vs. Washington.

title: Former Detroit Lions OL Joins Scouting Department
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have offiicially announced promotions to a few members of their pro player personnel staff and added a former National Football League player to the scouting department.
Offensive tackle Jamarco Jones, who had a stint in Motown (2024-2025), has been added to the scouting team.
Rob Lohman is now the Vice Preseident of roster operations, while Dwayne Joseph is now in the role of Vice President of Player Personnel. Joe Kelleher has been promoted to Director of Pro Scouting.
Mark Olsen is in the role of assistant Director of College Scouting.
Detroit also made the hiring of Chris Grier official, as he is now serving the role of Personnel Advisor.
Prior to practice on Wednesday, Dan Campbell was asked how fluid the conversations are with general manager Brad Holmes at this point in training camp.
"I mean, we see players very much the same way. We respect what players do, how they play pretty much the same way, what they put on tape and so those happen. It doesn't happen every day, but it does happen. But I think we're going to kind of stay away from a total eval. That's what we're going to do a little different, a total eval until late," said Campbell. "Let's just get all the way through this almost, and then let's really sit down and deep dive.
"And let's get a really good perspective, certainly from the coaches, myself, but he and his staff, personnel department, man, what are they seeing? And then Brad and I will come together at the end of all this. But yeah, I mean, we certainly communicate .”

title: Most Important Players to Watch in Lions First Preseason Game
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will take the field for the first time in 2026 Thursday night.
In their preseason opener, the Lions will take on the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. Fans won't get to see the Lions' stars, as head coach Dan Campbell doesn't expect to play many of his starters. However, there are several noteworthy players who will hit the field against a Bengals team that will trot out its starters.
Here are 12 players to watch in the Lions' preseason opener against the Bengals.
Campbell stated that he plans to play his first-round pick from this year's draft, so Miller will get his introduction to the NFL on Thursday night. It's been an up and down training camp full of learning moments for Miller up to this point, as he's been getting reps against Aidan Hutchinson throughout.
Now, Miller will get a chance to take aim at a Bengals defense that will feature its starters for a fixed amount of time. It's uncertain exactly how long Miller will play, but there will be plenty of eyes on his every move throughout Thursday's game given his status as a first-round pick.
Hassanein has been one of the biggest standouts from this year's camp. He's changed positions, shifting from the EDGE to the big end, and as a result has seen a boost in his performance throughout camp.
Last year, Hassanein flashed before having his season ended with a preseason injury. Now, he gets a shot to prove his worthiness of not only a roster spot, but a significant role on this year's team. He should get plenty of opportunities to make an impact, and could have a statement performance if his performance in practice translates to the game.
Jared Goff is not expected to play, and the abrupt retirement of Teddy Bridgewater left the Lions scrambling. Detroit added Josh Dobbs to the quarterback room, but it's expected that Altmyer will get a hefty workload in his first taste of game action.
Altmyer is an intriguing undrafted free agent addition for Detroit. He's had his moments in camp thus far, and reviews from coaches and teammates have been positive. He'll have the opportunity to prove them right in his first preseason showing.
After Jimmy Rolder suffered an injury, the Lions quickly added White to the roster. While there were concerns about White's performance in recent years and whether he was capable of playing at a high level, he has reportedly had a phenomenal start to camp.
White will play in Thursday's game, and as a result fans will get their first look at the former All-Pro in a Lions uniform. He has the upside to start and play a huge role in Detroit's defense, and could offer a glimpse of that against the Bengals.
With Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco and even Sione Vaki not expected to play, Thursday's game will be a showcase of depth. Reports indicate that Jabari Small missed practice Tuesday and may have an injury he's dealing with, so expect Saylors to be the first option.
Saylors was on the Lions' active roster throughout the regular season last year primarily as a kick returner. Now, Thursday gives him the chance to prove he's worthy of having a bigger role. He could shrink the gap between he and Vaki, who is currently the third running back, with a good performance.
Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp's intuition will be tested Thursday, as he projected Hunter to have "a million" tackles throughout Detroit's preseason slate. While that projection may have been exaggerated, Hunter is expected to be a big contributor defensively.
The Lions are deep with veterans at the linebacker position, especially with the recent additions of White and Amen Ogbongbemiga. However, there could be a path to a roster for Hunter on special teams. He should get plenty of work in all phases on Thursday.
Wilson has stood out on a few highlight plays throughout camp, and as a veteran could surprise some in what is a deep wide receiver room. He does have plenty of experience, and for a young quarterback like Altmyer, Wilson could be a reliable target.
Looking to revitalize his career after going around the league throughout his career, Wilson has a chance to make a statement in his first preseason game with the Lions. Detroit has several talented options at the position, and as a result they're looking for players to take advantage of the opportunity.
Lucas was one of the top undrafted players in this year's class, and landed in Detroit looking for a shot to prove himself. He has plenty of upside as a former five-star recruit, and his size and athleticism gives him all the necessary tools.
The USC product could be utilized either as a big end or a speed rusher, and as a result could be a presence in the Bengals' backfield. With Derrick Moore expected to be out dealing with a groin injury, Lucas could get a heavy workload.
Cade Mays is expected to be out for a significant amount of time with a wrist injury, and as a result McLaughlin has his shot. Signed to a futures contract this offseason, McLaughlin assumed first team duties earlier in the week and presumably will be the first guy at the pivot in Thursday's game.
Juice Scruggs is currently sidelined dealing with a soft-tissue injury, and when he gets back he's expected to enter the center competition. As a result, McLaughlin could have his biggest opportunity to make a statement that he belongs on the final roster in Thursday's game.
After injuries have derailed the first two seasons of his career, Rakestraw is looking to prove he belongs on Detroit's defense. He may not be at starter level at this point, as Rock Ya-Sin appears to be pulling away in the competition for the second starting cornerback spot.
As a result, Rakestraw could see snaps in Thursday's game. With the Bengals playing their starters, he could draw a matchup against Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins. This would be a great test for him, and could provide clarity for fans about where he stands.
Meeks is one of the most intriguing players on the roster bubble offensively for Detroit. The Syracuse product is a converted wide receiver, and added bulk this offseason to get ready for the position change.
Like Wilson, Meeks could be a consistent target for Altmyer and Dobbs. He flashed plenty of potential in the preseason last year as a UDFA, and though it wasn't enough to make the team, he showed enough to remain with the organization for the entire year.
Whiteside is another player who has stood out the most in camp, as he has gone from afterthought to legitimate contender for a role in the secondary. He has been getting his hands on the ball seemingly every day in practice, and shown good coverage skills throughout camp.
Now, Whiteside has the opportunity to do it in a game. The Bengals playing their starters is a huge test for him, as he could have a good test awaiting him across the line of scrimmage. Thursday is an opportunity for him to add validity to the claims that he's been among the best in camp.

title: Sheila Hamp: 9-8 Season Wasn't Good Enough, Expects Team To Be Contender
full_text:
The Detroit Lions organization is one that has been associated with misfortune for a majority of its history.
Though the team enjoyed some success prior to the start of the Super Bowl era, it has been through its share of misfortune. The Lions are one of just four teams to have never appeared in a Super Bowl.
However, they've enjoyed a resurgence in recent years, and three seasons ago held a lead at halftime of the NFC Championship game. Under Principal Owner and Chair Sheila Ford Hamp, the Lions have had plenty of success in recent years thanks to an influx of talent and an identity change spurred by a cultural shift.
That's why the Lions are operating with a renewed hunger in 2026. Even after finishing last season with a winning 9-8 record, the Lions quickly hit the ground and got back to work after that record found them in last place in the NFC North division.
With the recent success, Hamp admitted that the team's standard is set above the 9-8 finish they had a season ago. There has been unity established within the organization, headlined by the relationship shared by Hamp, head coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes.
Hamp explained to FOX-2 that the team is motivated by the performance last year, and that the bar is set high for the upcoming campaign.
“9-8 is a winning season, but that wasn’t good enough for us. It’s not what we expected, it’s not where our standards are. So we, top to bottom, we went through everything about last year and what could we have done differently, what went wrong, what went right," Hamp said. "We really have done a thorough self-searching exercise, and I think we’ve identified several things we could’ve done better and hopefully we’ve corrected them. The entire organization is aligned, aligned in the fact that what we want to do is bring a winner to the city of Detroit.”
Additional Lions Insider Analysis: Dan Campbell Makes Decision Regarding Blake Miller Playing in Preseason
Speaking with Lions play-by-play broadcaster Dan Miller, Hamp shared her optimism for the team's upcoming campaign after observing several training camp practices. She noted that the offensive line has the necessary depth to withstand injuries, and expects the team to be in contention once again in 2026.
“Of course everything looks rosy right now. I think it truly is. We’re all excited," Hamp stated. "Camp has gone really well. We’ve had some injuries, but I have to say that for the first time, I think we have more depth than we’ve ever had, especially on our o-line. I think we’re gonna be definitely a contender, so excited. We’re all excited.”
Hamp and the Lions recently made a big addition to their front office, hiring Rich Haddad as the new team president.
The Lions conducted a national search using the firm Russell Reynolds Associates to find a replacement for the retiring Rod Wood, and wound up finding Haddad just down the road. Prior to coming to the Lions, Haddad had spent the last 14 years working with the Detroit Pistons and Pistons Sports and Entertainment.
Hamp explained what stood out about the new president, noting his leadership ability and familiarity with the city of Detroit.
“We’ve been working on this since February, and the thing about Rich that stood out, this huge search and we ended up with someone in our backyard which was incredible," Hamp said. "He rose to the top because of his leadership, as well as his knowledge of the city and all the things he’s done here. And his experience with the Pistons and the players. He was the right cultural fit.”

title: Winners and Losers From Day 11 of 2026 Detroit Lions Training Camp
full_text:
The Detroit Lions held a shortened, non-contact practice Tuesday ahead of their preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Coach Dan Campbell doesn't plan to play many of the team's starters in Thursday's game, and with Wednesday being a travel day the Lions used Tuesday to get some reps for players not playing in the exhibition game.
The head coach expressed his excitement for the preseason opener, particularly for the young players who will have a chance to show off their development in terms of technique after being coached for the first three weeks.
"I think always with these is, as a coach, you want to see some of these guys, you've been coaching them on technique, fundamentals," Campbell said. "The scheme is not as big of an issue right now, I'm not concerned with that because with what we're giving them they're gonna be able to play fast, but how do they handle competition? Cincinnati, I think (Bengals coach) Zac (Taylor) is gonna play those guys a couple of drives, their starters. So it'll be a great look for our guys."
Here are winners and losers, as well as what we're learning from day 11 of Lions training camp, with some insights provided by the team website .
Avonte Maddox returned after missing practice Monday. With the latest update on Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch being that they're expected to return after the start of the season, Maddox is believed to be part of the team's starting safety tandem for the start of the regular season along with Chuck Clark.
Derrick Moore (groin), Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) and Sione Vaki (eye/broken nose) were all getting work in with trainers. Running back Jabari Small, cornerback Khalil Dorsey and offensive lineman Devin Cochran were all out for undisclosed reasons.
The Lions remain without center Cade Mays (wrist), linebacker Jimmy Rolder (hamstring), offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (undsiclosed soft-tissue), Isiah Pacheco (MCL) and defensive end Payton Turner (back). Campbell noted that Kerby Joseph is away dealing with a personal issue.
After a slight lull in productivity over the recent stretch of practices, cornerback Ennis Rakestraw appeared to bounce back for a strong day on Tuesday. He was matched up with Jameson Williams three separate times in one-on-one drills, and Rakestraw had a good showing.
On the first rep, Rakestraw was in phase from the snap against Williams and forced an overthrow. He was also in good coverage on a throw in the end zone to force an incompletion. The third rep went to Williams, who brought in a slant route that Rakestraw initially deflected.
Another defensive back that had a bounce back day is Roger McCreary, who reportedly won two of his three reps against Greg Dortch.
Sam LaPorta has been somewhat quiet to start camp, but reviews indicate he is rounding into season shape. When the Lions began a team rep, the Iowa product showed up in a big way.
LaPorta had two big catches with the first team offense, beating a linebacker for a big gain on an out-and-up. Then, he burnt Thomas Harper for a touchdown grab in the red-zone.
After missing the last seven games of the year with a herniated disk in his back, LaPorta continues to incrementally improve as he gets reacclimated. This is a positive development, as his absence was felt heavily throughout the offense after his injury.
Additional Lions Insight: Analyzing First Unofficial Depth Chart
With the Lions not playing quarterback Jared Goff in the preseason opener, Josh Dobbs could be thrust into action shortly into his tenure with the team. Dobbs took team reps for the first time on Tuesday, running one drive.
He started strong, firing a completion to Cedrick Wilson between a linebacker and a safety to move inside the 10-yard line.
A penalty derailed the drive, as Miles Frazier jumped early. Dobbs wouldn't finish the drive, as he was relieved by Luke Altmyer before third-down. According to reports, Dobbs stated he came out because he is still learning the team's red-zone plays after arriving Sunday.
Altmyer was unable to lead the offense into the end zone, as his pass to Greg Dortch was stopped short to force a field goal.
The Lions finished practice with a situation for the offense. They were down 10 with all three timeouts with under four yards to go. After an early completion, the offense took a step back as Aidan Hutchinson sacked Goff after he beat Blake Miller.
Detroit's offense got the yardage back after a defensive holding, then ultimately couldn't move the chains as Goff overthrew Brock Wright. They were in range for a field goal, so they were able to get within a score.
After notching the needed stop to get the ball back to the ofense, who took over at their own 20-yard line with 1:38 left. It ended poorly, as a sack by Avonte Maddox set the offense back. The Lions got yardage back with short completions from Goff to Gibbs and St. Brown, but a last-ditch attempt from Goff to Williams was ruled incomplete as he came down with the ball out of bounds.
Coaches overruled the incompletion, instead opting to get the offense some extra work. Yet, their fortunes stayed the same as Goff was intercepted by Thomas Harper to end practice.
1.) Cornerback Keith Abney had a tough day, getting beat by Dominic Lovett on a slant and also being whistled for penalties working against Tom Kennedy and Wilson. Kennedy also got the best of him near the goal line, making a leaping catch on a fade route.
2.) Nick Whiteside had an interception for the third straight day, picking off a pass working against Isaac TeSlaa during one-on-ones.
3.) Offensive tackle Blake Miller had a big block during team drills, taking care of Avonte Maddox on a screen pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown.

title: Analyzing Detroit Lions First 2026 Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their first unofficial depth chart ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
Detroit has its first preseason game on Thursday, so the unofficial depth chart adds some clarity to how the organization may be thinking heading into the opener. However, this depth chart is compiled by the communication staff and as a result may not be entirely indicative of how the coaching staff is thinking at this stage of training camp.
Here are four takeaways from the team's first released depth chart of the 2026 season.
Detroit Lions first unofficial depth chart @DetroitPodcast @CBooher_ pic.twitter.com/QUjirKWf4Q
The Lions currently have three position battles going on for spots along their offensive line. They entered camp with competitions for right tackle and left guard, and another wrench was thrown into their plans with the injury to center Cade Mays .
Currently, the Lions have veteran Larry Borom listed ahead of rookie Blake Miller at right tackle. Miller has taken his fair share of first team reps at the position, and is being viewed with a very realistic chance at starting the opener at the position after the team drafted him 17th overall.
At left guard, Juice Scruggs is currently listed ahead of Christian Mahogany. However, Mahogany has drawn strong reviews for his performance early in camp and is right in the mix to win the position.
Additionally, Scruggs is expected to get reps at center when he returns from a soft tissue injury, and as a result Mahogany may still be the favorite to win his job back and start at left guard.
When Scruggs returns, the Lions will have him competing to start at center with Seth McLaughlin and Michael Niese. The depth chart lists Niese ahead of McLaughlin, but it was McLaughlin taking first team reps at the position in Monday's practice.
The Lions have an established top four at the wide receiver position, but there is plenty of competition for the fifth spot. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Greg Dortch are all roster locks, but there are several players in the mix for the final one or two roster spots at the position.
The starters are St. Brown, Williams and TeSlaa. With this pairing, which would be 11 personnel, it would likely be St. Brown in the slot with Williams and TeSlaa out wide. Dortch, meanwhile, is behind St. Brown which checks out with him being expected to be a slot-exclusive presence.
Dominic Lovett is listed as the backup behind Williams, while Tom Kennedy is the third-string in the slot. Those two players are expected to be competing for the fifth spot, so the Lions could make the choice dpending on which player offers more versatility.
Cedrick Wilson Jr. is the backup behind TeSlaa. Another wide receiver with a big physical profile, Wilson has flashed with several strong moments in camp.
The Lions' depth chart lists two linebackers and a nickel cornerback, which could be an indication of coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's intent to play more nickel defense as opposed to base in 2026. The Lions have had different players playing the position throughout camp, with Roger McCreary currently holding top billing on the depth chart.
McCreary's performance throughout camp has been up and down , with the consensus being that he has work to do to become a starter within the unit. Head coach Dan Campbell stated that Christian Izien would also get some work at the spot, and Izien is currently listed second behind McCreary.
At linebacker, the Lions currently have Devin White and Malcolm Rodriguez listed as the top two backups behind starters Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes. White, a former All-Pro, seems to have the leg up in the competition to be the top option in Detroit's three-linebacker packages.
Several standouts have emerged amidst the Lions' roster through the first 10 days of training camp. Among them are defensive linemen Ahmed Hassanein and Tyler Lacy, who have both been showing up in a big way throughout camp.
Detroit has deployed a big end traditionally in their defense, and both Lacy and Hassanein have played well in this role throughout camp. On the first depth chart, they are listed second and third, respectively, behind presumed veteran starter D.J. Wonnum opposite of Aidan Hutchinson.
Another development on the defensive line is the fact that undrafted free agent Anthony Lucas has been listed ahead of veteran Payton Turner. A former first-round pick who has had his career interrupted by injuries, Turner has been absent from practice since completing the first day and could be in danger of not making the roster if he remains sidelined.
Another rising defender is cornerback Nick Whiteside. Viewed as a potential afterthought not long ago in Detroit's secondary, Whiteside has generated a ton of positive momentum behind a strong camp.
On the first depth chart, Whiteside is listed as the backup behind D.J. Reed. This puts him ahead of Khalil Dorsey and rookie Keith Abney, which would be a very positive development for his hopes of making the roster.
Both Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are listed as starters on this depth chart, but neither is currently expected to play in Week 1. Instead, their backups are listed as Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox, and that pairing is anticipated to be the starting duo against the New Orleans Saints.

title: Lions Kerby Joseph Health Update, Is Away Dealing With 'Personal Issue'
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided an update on All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph ahead of Tuesday’s training camp practice.
Joseph has been sidelined due to a nagging knee injury that held him out of the final 11 games of the 2025 season. He has yet to participate in practice in training camp, but has been observed putting in work with trainers on the side at points throughout camp.
On Tuesday, Campbell said that Joseph is dealing with a personal matter, and noted that he remains on roughly the same trajectory to return to action as fellow safety Brian Branch. Branch is currently out while rehabbing a torn Achilles suffered in December.
“Kerby right now, first of all, he’s dealing with a personal issue right now. But his rehab is coming along very well,” Campbell said. “That is still, I still see him on the Branch plan if that makes sense. And Branch is doing well too. Those guys, we’re talking about on down the road, the season’s already begun. But I like where Kerby’s at.”
At the start of training camp, Campbell stated that getting Joseph back for the regular season opener against the New Orleans Saints would be a "bonus."
Joseph was coming off an All-Pro season after leading the NFL in interceptions in 2024. He signed a four-year contract extension prior to last year, but began dealing with swelling in his knee during training camp.
He initially tried to play through the injury through the start of the regular season, and recorded three interceptions in his first five games. However, the pain became too much in Week 6 against the Kansas City Chiefs, and that would be the final game he played in last season.
The specific details of Joseph’s injury remain relatively uncertain, with speculation being that it could be a chronic injury dealing with cartilage in his knee.
When healthy, Joseph and Branch have formed one of the NFL's top safety duos. Joseph has earned a reputation as a ballhawk, with 20 career interceptions in his first four seasons. He spoke to the media earlier in training camp, and stated that he's confident he'll be able to contribute at some point in 2026.

title: Before Packers-Steelers, Love for Green Bay Will Never Leave Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After the 2022 season fell short of the playoffs, the Green Bay Packers traded Aaron Rodgers. At the time, it probably was in the best interests of everyone. It certainly was for the Packers, who had Jordan Love waiting in the wings.
Rodgers might not have always seen eye to eye with Mike McCarthy or Matt LaFleur. He might not have appreciated Ted Thompson’s ignore-free-agency-at-all-costs approach to roster building or Brian Gutekunst’s decision to draft Love on the heels of a trip to the NFC Championship Game.
But one thing never wavered, and that was Rodgers’ love for Green Bay.
A day before the Packers play at Pittsburgh in the preseason opener, the Steelers put together a Zoom call between Rodgers and Packers beat reporters on Wednesday.
The final question went to WBAY-TV’s Dave Schreoder. It was a simple one: What was he most thankful for in his career.
“Definitely the people I got to do it with, you know? That’s what makes it so much fun. You know even here [in Pittsburgh], being 42 and not having the extended time with these guys, you just really love those moments when you’re off and when you’re joking and playing cards and hanging out and just shooting the sh**.
“That’s what this game’s all about. It’s about the relationships, and I’m just most thankful for all the men and women who’ve been in my life through this game over the years. So many great people in Green Bay, in the entire organization, top to bottom. You know, just salt-of-the-earth type of people.
“And I think a lot about the kind of the unsung heroes, the unknown people, the Larry Van Alstines of the world, who was our whitecap referee for so long at practice. We went hunting, actually pheasant hunting, a couple times together (and became) close. He’s like a fabric of the team.
“I think about Larry McCarren, ‘The Rock,’ just what a great dude he is, and how many hundreds of games he called of mine and just always loved the interaction with him. The guys in the equipment room – Kevin Nelson and Tom Bakken and Red Batty and Brian Nehring and Tim Odea and all the other understudies and, obviously, Andy (Gruber). Just so many great people that I got to meet over the years that I never would have met without this game and that I still consider friends.
“And then, obviously, all the teammates I’ve had over the years who had such a big impact on my life, and still talk to a lot of them. A lot of the quarterbacks I’ve been able to be around and help mentor, and who’ve mentored me, and I’ve learned stuff from them.
“But if you miss out on the relationships in this game, you’re kind of missing the whole gist of what we’re actually doing. Obviously, we’re judged on our wins and losses and paid based off our production. But the thing that actually lasts the longest is those people that impact your life, and there’s been a lot of those, a lot of especially in Green Bay, it had a huge impact on my life. So, I think about those people a lot.”
The NFL, in its infinite wisdom, scheduled this game in Pittsburgh. After last year’s regular-season game was played in Pittsburgh, a return to Green Bay would have made a lowly preseason game must-see TV. Instead, the game will only be aired locally.
Rodgers said he “100 percent” wishes this game would be played at Lambeau.
“When I heard it was possible to play both my former teams, I was really hoping this one was going to be in Green Bay, not just to get back at Lambeau one more time, but to head out to Chives for a dinner and maybe head out to Green Bay Country Club for a quick nine or something,” Rodgers said.
“I was really hoping it was going to be in Green Bay, for a lot of reasons. It would have been strange being in that locker room and stuff, but I would have found my way over, like many former players have over the years. Found my way over to Flea’s office [Flea, aka Brian Engel, is the team’s vice president of player health and performance] and hang out back there and see some of the guys and see some of the trainers and equipment staff and all the people I really care about that still work there. Yeah, I was definitely bummed out that we weren’t in Lambeau for this one.”
So, with this being Rodgers’ final season in the NFL – subject to change, of course – his big return will have to wait until he is inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame five years after his final game. At that point, the Packers presumably will retire his No. 12 jersey.
“There first has to be an invite back,” Rodgers said.
Of course that will happen.
“We’ll see about that,” Rodgers replied, “but, yeah, I’m always going to have such a strong tie to Green Bay and the organization. If that comes to fruition, that could be a cool deal.”
Rodgers said he misses his house and gave a couple more plugs to Chives, the restaurant located in nearby Suamico.
But then, he brought it back home to the people – those who work at Lambeau Field and those who fill the metal bleachers.
“The falls there are just awesome, when the weather gets that cool little nip,” he said. “I loved the night games at Lambeau, especially the Sunday nights, Monday nights and occasional Thursday nights. Just so much fun. There’s nothing like that crowd. Been other places, but there’s nothing like that fan base and the way they travel and the crowds at home.
“Players around the league they talk about how special it is to play at Lambeau, and sometimes you might miss that or forget about that when you’re playing because it becomes so normal to have such an amazing crowd and they’re tailgating and they’re loud and they rarely sell their tickets to other teams fans.
“There’s a lot of great things about Wisconsin. I grew up there, really, and became a little more mature as an adult over the years there and had a great time and still have a lot of close friends there, a lot of fond memories.”
