title: Chargers Injury Tracker: Every Injury Update From Training Camp
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have some high-profile injuries to track as training camp continues.
Granted, the Chargers don’t have many injuries. But when one of the guys dealing with an issue is a top-10 player at his spot after missing all of last season due to injury, it becomes a much bigger deal than most training camps around the NFL.
The other guy battling injury , too, happens to be a player who is likely about to reset the entire NFL market at his position with a contract extension.
Tack on the usual wear and tear of training camp for other guys as things progress, and it can be tough to track all of the updates. Here’s a live-updating list of injury items to know for the Chargers.
This is the big one for the Chargers.
Rashawn Slater inked a big contract extension last year and suffered a torn patellar tendon in early August, ending his season before it started. Since, he’s been described loosely as ahead of schedule for most of the offseason before showing up for training camp work.
Last week when the Chargers put on pads in San Diego, though, his surgically repaired knee went through what he called a "minor flare-up" when asked by reporters. He’s been missing practice since.
Chargers fans, understandably, are worried. But considering the team made Slater available for a media session and he was pretty open about the whole thing, it doesn’t seem like a major concern.
That said, Slater’s practice participation is going to be something to closely watch until Week 1.
When Tuli Tuipulotu worked off to the side, if at all, to start camp, it seemed related to the mentioned contract extension talks.
Turns out it might have been something else.
According to Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, Tuipulotu has been “working through” an issue “ramping up” on his way to a return. The star edge rusher himself has said that he won’t comment on the contract and that working on the side away from teammates has been tough.
Like Slater, it’ll be interesting to see how and when Tuipulotu takes part in full practices before the season, but there’s the contract stuff in the background to watch, too.
A possible No. 1 wideout in Mike McDaniel’s scheme, Quentin Johnston has been held out of practice recently while he deals with some minor undisclosed setback.
The steal of a mid-round find for the Chargers defense a few years ago, Tarheeb Still has also been out with a minor undisclosed setback.

title: Jim Harbaugh Brought the Hammer Down after Chargers Practice Skirmish
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers training camp, by most accounts, has been pretty tame.
Granted, there are some important things happening. Rashawn Slater and Tuli Tuipulotu are battling injuries . The offense continues to figure out Mike McDaniel’s new offense while Justin Herbert leads the way, new stance in certain formations included.
But that almost casual nature of it all got broken up this week by, well, a fight.
Let a variety of onlookers tell it, linebacker Daiyan Henley got into it with the likes of edge rusher Bud Dupree and offensive lineman Cole Strange, which led to consequences from head coach Jim Harbaugh himself.
Cole Strange, a newcomer to the Chargers via free agency, was right in the thick of it with two Chargers defensive leaders, it seems.
According to Fernando Ramirez of The Sporting Tribune, the “skirmish” was possibly the first one under Jim Harbaugh at all.
The punishment? All three players going with Executive Director of Player Performance Ben Herbert to a side field for "focus exercises" for the remainder of practice.
And yes, fans at practice apparently captured footage of the dust-up that led to punishments, with Strange removing his helmet at the end of it all:
For those of you asking, here’s the video of the tiny skirmish today. Pretty much nothing but the 3 “involved” still had to go work out, away from the team with Ben Herbert. https://t.co/1ERFHg184O
Kris Rhim of ESPN classified the situation as so: "Daiyan Henley, Bud Dupree and Cole Strange left the team period early and worked off to the side with strength coach Ben Herbert."
This is pretty standard training camp stuff for most NFL teams around the league. But as Ramirez hinted, it’s extremely rare for a Harbaugh team, hence the punishments, even for a veteran like Dupree and one of the core team leaders in Henley.
Is it a bad thing? Probably not. A little fire in training camp during 11-on-11 work is hard to complain about, especially when the rest of camp so far has seemed pretty timid to onlookers.
Obviously, onlookers will want to keep track of whether anything else like this happens during camp. But most Chargers fans probably won’t complain about a new starting offensive lineman like Strange coming over and showing some aggression in front of the star quarterback after how the last few years have gone in the trenches.
They also happen to know what a leader Henley is, so it's not shocking to see a little tone-setting on that front from the heart of the defense.

title: Injury Updates, 1 on 1 Battles and Highlights From Chargers' Last Pregame Practice
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers held their second practice of Week 3 of 2026 training camp. Los Angeles is just two days away from their first preseason game against the Houston Texans and will have an off day for travel on Wednesday. The Chargers started their week on Monday with a light walkthrough but turned up the intensity on Tuesday with pads on.
Overall, the defense was dominant on Tuesday and several players fighting for roles flashed dominant plays. Several bubble players who are battling for roster spots also stood out heading into their first chance to prove themselves in live action. Let's dive into everything noteworthy from Tuesday's practice and press conferences.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh mentioned during his pre-practice press conference on Tuesday that aside from Rashawn Slater, two additional starting players are out of practice "working through something minor." Wide receiver Quentin Johnston and cornerback Tarheeb Still are both out of practice right now.
Rashawn Slater missed his fourth practice in a row and Harbaugh tried to avoid mentioning the specifics of what Slater was dealing with but Slater himself addressed the media and clarified the situation. It was apparent after he had missed his third practice in a row, that Slater had suffered a setback.
Slater did clarify that he felt something around his surgically repaired knee back at the first practice at the University of San Diego last Tuesday. The training staff is holding Slater back to make sure the discomfort he felt doesn't progress to something worse.
"We haven't seen anything that's really concerning. Obviously, it's not always the smoothest process coming back from a big injury," Slater said. "Nothing to be concerned about. Just being smart, being thoughtful with the way we progress.
The Chargers released their first unofficial depth chart following Sunday's practice to wrap u the second week of training camp. The depth chart is not made by the coaching staff and is made by the Chargers media team and PR staff and is therefore not truly indicative of where players stand. However, there were a handful of notable takeaways on the depth chart.
The unofficial depth chart had Tarheeb Still as the starter opposite veteran Donte Jackson or Cam Hart which was a bit of a surprise. Still was sidelined at practice and Jackson and Hart, who may be battling for a top role, put on a show. Jackson walked away with two interceptions on the day and Hart went toe to toe with Ladd McConkey showing off his physicality in press-man coverage.
Undrafted free agent edge rusher Nadame Tucker, who notably was the only UDFA not listed last in his position group on the unofficial depth chart, put on a show in one-on-ones against the offensive line. He even went straight through the chest of veteran offensive tackle Trey Pipkins, as he has been flashing his power.
Tucker is likely in a competition with Kyle Kennard for a role and potentially a roster spot. Meanwhile, Kennard had himself a day as well, showcasing an improved pass rush arsenal. The preseason games will be major for both players.
Defensive linemen Teair Tart, Jamaree Caldwell and Justin Eboigbe continue to be wrecking balls in the middle of the defensive line. Caldwell and Eboigbe both seem to be poised for and embracing the opportunity for larger roles heading into the season.
Wide receiver Keandre Lambert-Smith has stacked together multiple good practices and had a very good winning route in one-on-ones on Tuesday. Wide receiver Tre Harris channeled his inner Mike Williams with a phenomenal adjustment on a back-shoulder throw with Donte Jackson glued to him in coverage to haul in a spectacular catch.
okayyyyyyy tre' 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/jKFqEwO5gH
Edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu has appeared to have fully ended his hold-in and returned to full activities with the team. He spoke to the media for the first time since camp began after practice. Both he and coach Harbaugh danced around the wording of what was going on behind the scenes with the negotiations.
Tuipulotu clearly stated in regards to his contract heading into the final year of his rookie deal, "I'll let my agents and the guys upstairs handle that," Tuipulotu said. "Let the business handle business. I'm a football player. That's all I do. That's all I know."

title: 1 Quote and a National Spotlight at Chargers Training Camp Hint at Big Things in 2026
full_text:
It didn’t take long for Los Angeles Chargers fans to see all the positives of the Mike McDaniel hiring, which paired him with head coach Jim Harbaugh and elite quarterback Justin Herbert.
Free from the likes of Greg Roman and a long, long, exhausting list of other coaching names to roll through Los Angeles over the years, watching Herbert finally get a modern offensive mind like McDaniel sort of felt like an offseason Super Bowl.
Now that preseason games are almost here, the national side has started to catch up with these ideas a bit. That’s especially the case when seeing how things have worked out on the field, plus more quotes from McDaniel and Harbaugh , too.
The result? Even more hype for Chargers fans, too.
Offseason moves hinted that the Chargers gave McDaniel pretty much free rein over what he wants to do with the offense.
McDaniel's moves included adding fullback Alec Ingold, tight ends Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, running back Keaton Mitchell, an entirely new interior offensive line and even drafting wideout Brenen Thompson.
So, every layer of the depth chart while revamping the scheme and fits.
Oh, and McDaniel forced Herbert to rework his footwork and approach in certain packages while installing an entirely new offense.
Fast forward to camp, the results look good and for some, like Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer , the quotes kick things into overdrive. That’s especially true when McDaniel talks about the freedom he’s been given by Harbaugh.
“And he really fosters the maximum out of me because he gives me responsibility and doesn’t micromanage things I earned, in his opinion, that he’s comfortable with me taking ownership of,” McDaniel said. “ He’s just an elite leader that way. … Our relationship couldn’t be stronger.”
Look no further than the running back room. McDaniel just told onlookers that he’s going to ride the hot hand regardless of whether it’s Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell or Kimani Vidal.
The modernized unpredictability of it all might fluster fantasy football managers, but from a national perspective, the Chargers feel more dangerous than ever.
Good thing McDaniel gets the all-clear from Harbaugh, too: This might be his only year with the Chargers. If they match the hype, there’s little doubt he will instantly become one of the top names on the head-coach hiring cycle again.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: Genesis Smith, a Rookie Ball Hawk Who Can Make Big Plays
full_text:
Genesis Smith, born on November 5, 2004, in Chandler, Arizona, played his high school ball at Hamilton High School, where he had 16 interceptions during his football career with the program, earning three-star recruiting status, according to 247Sports .
Smith decided to stay close to home, committing to the University of Arizona, where he would instantly see the field in 2023 as a true freshman. He recorded an interception and 24 tackles during this season.
Going into his sophomore season, he had his breakout season with 63 tackles (3.5 for loss), three interceptions, six pass deflections and two forced fumbles. After this successful year, Smith looked to transfer away from Arizona, but eventually found himself back with the program for his third and final year with the Wildcats.
This final season saw Smith help the Wildcats to the seventh-best passing defense across college football, becoming a stalwart roaming safety striking fear into opposing Big 12 offenses.
This elite season, coupled with his first attempt to have draft eligibility, led Smith to decide to enter the 2026 NFL Draft, with NFL Scout Lance Zierlein describing him as a player who: "...offers ballhawking coverage qualities but has alarming issues as an open-field tackler. He’s instinctive, with the eyes to digest route development while reading the quarterback like a poker player looking for tells. He has average top-end speed but good route recognition and premium ball skills. Smith is a low-impact run defender and open-field tackler, though...His run defense won’t appeal to some teams, but his ability to read the field and make plays on the football will entice other squads looking for a safety on Day 3."
The Los Angeles Chargers selected Genesis Smith in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft , with hopes of him improving his tackling while continuing his dominance as a free-ranging safety who can create turnovers in a defense that is now under new leadership.

Going into 2026, Smith will find himself in a Safety battle, with himself, Tony Jefferson and RJ Mickens all fighting to be the third Safety on the Chargers' roster. This role will allow Derwin James Jr. to play the slot and create mismatches in favor of the Bolts' defense.
If Smith can clean up his tackling woes, he could very well turn into an elite safety in the NFL. If he does not, he may be buried on the depth chart for his first NFL season.

title: Chargers Underdog Story: Branson Taylor's Rise and Jim Harbaugh's Culture Shift
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are starting their third week of fall 2026 training camp. One of the most anticipated position battles at the left guard spot along the offensive line is heating up with at least three players battling for the job heading into the first preseason game.
One of the biggest surprises in the position battle is second-year player Branson Taylor. Taylor has received praise from nearly every corner of the team for the improvements he has made from year one until present day.
Taylor was a sixth-round pick out of Pitt in the 2025 draft. The coaching staff experimented with him throughout training camp in different roles last season but he ultimately failed to make the 53-man roster out of training camp. He spent the entirety of the 2025 season on the practice squad before being elevated to face the division champion Denver Broncos and start in place of starters who were resting heading into the playoffs.
Entering the 2026 offseason, Taylor was largely written off with the additions in free agency and the 2026 draft that the Chargers had brought on to the roster with the new scheme from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. I did not have him on the initial 53-man roster in my first post-OTAs prediction.
What has changed? How do we explain how Taylor is firmly a contender to take the starting left guard job and also showing tackle flexibility? The short answer is simple: he worked his tail off.
Jim Harbaugh was asked about Branson Taylor getting reps with the first team at his pre-practice press conference before Saturday's padded practice and the growth he has seen from year heading into Year 2. "This offseason, just been a really incredible offseason," Harbaugh said in reference to Taylor's growth, "In the training environment, saw it there first and then on the field in OTAs and in minicamp."
Harbaugh also specifically mentioned the reports he was getting from the training staff and executive director of player performance Ben Herbert regarding Taylor's work in the offseason. "I mean, the reports coming back from Ben Herbert and staff were like, Branson, wow! Leveling up."
Quarterback Justin Hebert was also asked about Taylor getting work with the first team in his post-practice press conference after Monday's walkthrough. Herbert's response to the question was indicative of how much Taylor has changed from last season. "Branson's put in a lot of great work this offseason, he showed up a different man," Herbert said, "It's been fun to see and it's been cool for him to get the opportunities to run with the ones."
A sixth-round pick spending a year on the practice squad and one year later possibly pushing for a starting role, if not at least a roster spot, is a great story. The fact that Taylor is in a true battle for the job is a testament to the work that he put in this offseason and his dedication to becoming a professional.
Taylor's current resurgence is also a testament to the culture Jim Harbaugh has brought the Chargers, now in his third year with the franchise. Taylor's hard work got him the opportunity, but the coaching staff, starting with Ben Herbert noticed and rewarded that hard work.
Just before Justin Herbert, Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said at his press conference, "I really want the starter to earn it. I think the player will tell us. I think his teammates will tell us by the collective group execution," McDaniel said. "The best player for that position will be helping the whole group operate with great communication and decisiveness and style of play."
The collective mindset and culture from every corner of the Chargers' staff and roster appears to be something that Harbaugh has brought to Los Angeles.

title: What Recent Chargers Training Camp Practices Mean for Week 1
full_text:
Day 11 of Los Angeles Chargers training camp is in the books. While Monday's practice wasn't anything special, due to it being a walkthrough day, it still gave us another look at the direction the team is heading.
The first preseason game against the Houston Texans is less than a week away and the Chargers are getting a clearer picture of what they will possibly look like when the season starts.
Even with it being a slow practice, there are a few developments that Chargers fans should pay attention to.
During the first padded practice of the year, Rashawn Slater went to the medical tent on 11-on-11 drills. He returned briefly and was seen after practice doing routine activities, but he has now missed three consecutive practices.
The Chargers haven't disclosed what exactly went wrong, however you have to think how serious it could have been. Slater missed all of the 2025 season with a torn left patellar tendon, which hurt the Chargers offensive line immensely.
It seems like they are taking precautionary measures as of recent, making sure no further damage is done. Trying to ease the Pro Bowl tackle back into action. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh mentioned to reporters that Slater was taking a rest day on Saturday, but have not been told what the reason for the last two days is.
The Chargers have plenty to figure out when it comes to the left guard position with the first game of the season lurking around the corner. As of Monday's practice, the position is still wide open for anybody to take.
Second-year Branson Taylor and former Detroit Lion Kayode Awosika appear to be the frontrunners of the competition. Splitting the first-team reps almost every practice, these two have impressed the coaching staff early on. Despite neither being viewed as the obvious favorite when the competition began, these guys have really shown what they are capable of in 2026.
Honorable mentions in the race for the starting position are Jake Slaughter, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins, who have also impressed at times during camp, and are still in the race for that number one spot at left guard.
On Monday courtesy of Chargers.com , the Bolts' offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel stated, "No one's eliminated themselves from the tournament". To me, it's their position to lose or win. Meaning, making no mistakes and being as sharp as possible on a regular basis
At this point in preseason, the Chargers will have to start making decisions in all aspects of the team. As each day passes, new situations occur that can affect the whole season, starting with Week 1.

title: Rashawn Slater Setback, Chargers' Fantasy Dilemmas and Joe Alt Shines to Start Week 3
full_text:
Week 3 of 2026 training camp has started for the Los Angeles Chargers with their first game on the horizon. The Chargers will face the Houston Texans at 5 p.m. on Thursday night to kick off the preseason games.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh said about 15 of the veterans will warm up with the team but will not play in the first game. None of the regular starters are expected to play in the first preseason matchup.
The Chargers released their first unofficial depth chart following their Sunday practice to wrap up week two which had a few interesting takeaways but overall serves as what to expect for Thursday night's lineup and position rotations.
Los Angeles started their third week of camp with a light walkthrough after a weekend of padded practices. Since it was a walkthrough on Monday, there are no significant highlights from the practice. Let's take a look at noteworthy news from the Mike McDaniel's press conference as well as some lineup questions from practice plus a pair of roster moves to start the week.
Chargers left tackle Rashawn Slater is returning from a devastating ruptured patellar tendon which he suffered just days into his return to the field in training camp of 2025. The timing of his return was always subject to some management by the coaching and training staff.
Slater gave everyone a scare last week during the first padded practice of training camp. He left practice and headed to the injury tent and the NFL world breathed a sigh of relief when he was spotted back on the sidelines and participating in conditioning drills.
Slater participated is practice in the days following the scare but has now missed three practices in a row. Slater did not participate in padded practices over the weekend and he did not participate in walk-throughs on Monday. The team will stay tight-lipped about his health but it is clear that he is experiencing something that is causing to to take a step back at let it rest.
At the moment, Slater's absence can simply be chalked up to soreness in his surgically repaired knee which missing two padded practices makes sense including the start of game week for walk-throughs in a game there is not way he will play in. It is obvious Slater suffered some sort of setback that is being managed and the situation is worth monitoring going forward. At the very least, this gives the Chargers a chance to rotate through multiple options at left tackle to be better prepared if Slater has to miss any time or even if he is not ready to start the season.
Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel took the podium after practice today and gave massive praise to right tackle Joe Alt for successfully setting up and blocking Khalil Mack on a screen play. Mack apparently has been making it impossible for the offense to run a screen to his side so far in camp.
McDaniel also faced a question regarding the running backs and how the roles will be handled. He jokingly responded that he felt the question was rooted in fantasy football.
" Bad news, fantasy owners. Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level," McDaniel said, "Bad news is I can’t tell you which games those are.” He went on to say, "I'll use all three of those guys probably every game. The relative ratio, that will be based on opponent."
Omarion Hampton is widely considered a fantasy breakout in waiting and has been going very high in redraft leagues. Figuring out where to draft Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal will be much more difficult to value.
The Chargers have made a roster move to start the week.
we've signed OLB andre carter + waived WR mante’ morrow pic.twitter.com/HvP5FBOdEl
The Chargers released wide receiver Mante Morrow, who was signed as an undrafted free agent after a rookie minicamp tryout but has been unable to practice. In his place, Los Angeles signed former Army star edge rusher Andre Carter. Carter was a highly productive player at West Point who was once considered a potential early-round draft pick but ultimately went undrafted after a poor pre-draft process.
Carter has had several years in the NFL bouncing around practice squads but also plenty of time to build up his size and strength. He had a stint with Mike McDaniel and the Miami Dolphins last season and is likely depth to bolster the edge room for preseason.

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From the Rams’ Initial 2026 Depth Chart
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams released their initial depth chart ahead of the first preseason game. While the initial depth chart doesn't mean a lot, it can still provide some clarity at certain positions. Here are seven takeaways from the Rams’ initial depth chart.
It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that Stetson Bennett is the backup quarterback . Bennett took all of the backup reps throughout training camp and the Rams were very impressed with his overall growth and confidence in the offense. AIt’s not a knock on Ty Simpson, as he remains on his own development path. The Rams seem to be pleased with both guys. Right now, Bennett’s experience in the offense gives him the edge.
It seems harsh to call Jarquez Hunter a bust after one season. However, he didn’t play any offensive snaps as a rookie and is listed behind Ronnie Rivers and alongside Dean Connors and Jordan Waters as he goes into year two. Hunter could certainly be a special teams contributor, but after being drafted in the fourth round, more was expected from him coming out of Auburn.
When the Rams drafted Trost, it was unclear where they would play him. Some projected him inside. However, the Rams seemingly see him as a tackle. To see him behind McClendon as the backup is a positive. Trost should get plenty of work during the preseason, which will be good to see.
Looking at the offensive line, seeing Dylan McMahon at center behind Coleman Shelton was certainly a surprise. Back in 2024, Beaux Limmer started the majority of the season at center with Jonah Jackson injured and played admirably. The Rams played Limmer at guard last year and he struggled. McMahon at center is certainly something to watch going forward.
At the beginning of training camp, Xavier Smith and Kyren Williams were both returning punts and were both returning punts and competing for the job. Smith was listed as the starting punt returner on the team’s depth chart with Konata Mumpfield behind him. That could be a positive sign for Smith when it comes to making the roster.
While it was odd that the Rams listed their top four tight ends as starters , it shouldn’t be too surprising. It’s clear that the Rams see all four as being interchangeable.
“I don't expect anyone in particular to come out on top,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase last week. “I think those guys push each other and challenge each other and are so versatile that you're just excited to see who ends up coming to life based on what the defense wants to do…They all can do so much, both in the run game and the pass game, that you're excited just based on a game plan.”
The Rams may have their internal hierarchy, and some guys will play more than others. However, the Rams see those four players as being able to do similar things. Who starts or plays more will likely depend on the matchup or who’s hot at the time.
Late last season, the Rams moved Desjuan Johnson from the interior defensive line to the edge and had success. The Rams liked what they saw, as that’s where he’s played all offseason and where he’s listed on the depth chart. Johnson was listed as the backup edge to Myles Garrett and could be part of the rotation.

title: 5 Things to Watch When Rams Release Initial Depth Chart
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams get ready for their first preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs, they will release their initial depth chart of the preseason. The Rams likely won’t give up a lot when it comes to the initial depth chart, butit still provides a good look at how the team views certain players. Here are five things to watch for when the Rams release their initial depth chart.
When the Rams release their initial depth chart, it seems almost inevitable that Stetson Bennett will end up ahead of Ty Simpson . Multiple things can be true here. Bennett has certainly earned the backup quarterback role and the Rams appear to trust him there. He has taken all of the backup reps throughout the entirety of the offseason.
At the same time, it shouldn’t be taken as a knock on Simpson. The Rams are bringing him along at his own pace. Additionally, the Rams typically list rookies behind established veterans on the depth chart. In 2023, Puka Nacua was listed behind Tutu Atwell. Terrance Ferguson was listed as the fourth tight end last year behind Davis Allen. The Rams know where each player stands and they aren’t going to reveal a lot on the Week 1 preseason depth chart.
With all of that said, it will be interesting to see where the Rams list CJ Daniels. Daniels has been a standout throughout training camp and the offseason program. The Rams may not have a true WR3, but where Daniels ends up will be something to watch.
Given how the Rams handle rookies, it wouldn’t be surprising, and probably should be expected for Daniels to be behind Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith, and Konata Mumpfield. At the same time, he’s shown a lot throughout training camp to potentially get listed alongside Whittington.
Not a lot has been said about Keagan Trost throughout the offseason. Early in training camp, Kevin Dotson mentioned that Trost had taken some snaps with the ones.
“He has gotten in there and competed, which is what you want,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “You want guys to go look like they belong. He definitely does that.”
When the Rams drafted Trost, it was unclear where they would play him. While he played tackle at Mizzou, he projected better as a guard at the next level. It’ll be eye-opening to see if the Rams list Trost behind Warren McClendon at right tackle or behind one of the guards.
The Rams are set at the top of the cornerback depth chart with Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Behind them is where it gets interesting. Emmanuel Forbes is likely the CB3 behind Watson. However, it’s unclear where the Rams could list Josh Wallace and Cam Lampkin.
Wallace is more of a slot player, but Lampkin has had a strong training camp. Additionally, Quentin Lake is technically a safety, but the Rams played him as their nickel most of last year. With how Chris Shula uses his defensive backs, there are several ways the Rams could structure the depth chart at this position.
Heading into the offseason, a competition at punt returner didn’t seem to be in the cards . However, that’s exactly what’s taken place as Kyren Williams and Xavier Smith split reps as the team’s punt returner during training camp.
It wouldn’t be surprising to see Smith listed as the starter, but how the Rams list it on the depth chart will be very telling. If Williams is listed as the team’s punt returner, it could make for some difficult decisions come roster cutdowns.

title: What Rams’ Joint Practice With Cowboys Revealed About Week 1
full_text:
On Tuesday, the Los Angeles Rams had their first of two joint practices of the summer. The Rams faced a good Dallas Cowboys team and m uch of the reaction coming out of the practice was mixed . According to reports, the Rams’ offense wasn’t as sharp against the Cowboys’ defense.
Much of the discussion after the joint practice was how the Cowboys’ defense got torched by the Rams’ offense last summer when the two teams practiced against each other. However, the Cowboys’ defense fared much better against Matthew Stafford and co. on Tuesday.
“Christian Parker and the Cowboys’ defense passed their first test against an opposing team at the Rams’ practice facility on Tuesday,” wrote Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News. “The starting defense limited the Rams and quarterback Matthew Stafford to a few big plays.”
According to Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star Telegram, Stafford went 22-for-33 on the day with an interception, and most of the Rams’ passing attack focused on the short game.
It would be concerning if the Rams had played terribly or lacked the overall energy and execution that frustrated head coach Sean McVay toward the end of training camp. However, that wasn’t the case on Tuesday. McVay seemed overall pleased with what the Rams were able to accomplish.
The Rams didn’t game plan or run anything specific to the Cowboys. Tuesday’s practice was simply about going up against a defense that wasn’t their own and continuing to work on fundamentals.
“We exchange personnel groupings and predetermine the down and distances with the exception of the two-minute situation, but I'm looking for the fundamentals,” said McVay. “I'm looking for some of the style of play within the framework of the rules of engagement that we established. I felt like a lot of that stuff seemed like it was there and that was a positive for us.”
We’re at a point in the NFL offseason where fans are craving any football and everything matters too much. Even if the Rams weren’t sharp on Tuesday or ‘lost’ the joint practice, they have a month to get ready for Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers . There were still some positive things to take away.
Terrance Ferguson got involved in the pass game, creating two big plays. Davante Adams got involved as well. While only 10 of the Rams’ passes may have traveled more than 10 yards down the field according to Harris, there’s still plenty to take away. Without a specific game plan, the focus was more on execution and how the Rams’ rules held up against another team.
“We don't game plan for any of this. We just go out there and play our rules, see how they hold up,” echoed Stafford. “There are going to be things to learn, things to correct but it's a good chance to go compete to see what else is out there.”
Over the last few weeks, the Rams’ defense has been showing signs of dominance and has started to come together. While wide receiver George Pickens had a strong day, Quentin Lake had an interception and the pass rush got after Dak Prescott without Myles Garrett in the lineup. It’s possible that right now, the defense is further along than some may have expected.
However, Tuesday also showed that the overall health of the team is one of the biggest variables in winning the Super Bowl. The Rams may have been erring on the side of caution, but being without Nacua for the final 45 minutes of practice and without Garrett completely would have had a huge impact during an actual game.
Tuesday was a good barometer for the Rams to see where they stand against a good Cowboys team. On August 20, the Rams will have their second joint practice of the summer against the New Orleans Saints. At that time, it will be another test before the focus shifts completely to Week 1. The joint practice against the Cowboys showed where the Rams stand and where they still have work to do.

title: Rams Face Interesting Decision With Stetson Bennett in Preseason
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play their first preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs. However, one of the biggest questions heading into that game is how head coach Sean McVay will handle the quarterback position .
There is no doubt that Ty Simpson will play. That has been confirmed by McVay and it’s the correct call given that it is the only live-game experience he’ll get as a rookie. Simpson only had one year of starting experience at Alabama. Playing during the preseason will be key for his overall development.
However, McVay wasn’t sure whether Bennett would play or rest like other key depth. McVay only noted on Tuesday that he had discussions with quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone and that he would have a clearer answer on Thursday.
Over the past few years, the Rams have rested their backup quarterback while Bennett has played the entirety of the game. With that said, the Rams’ backup at the time was Jimmy Garoppolo, who didn’t need preseason reps. This may be Bennett’s fourth preseason, but he still doesn’t have the same experience as Garoppolo.
The preseason could still be beneficial for Bennett. He’s certainly gotten more comfortable in the offense and looked good last year during the preseason. Bennett also had a lot more college experience than Simpson had coming out of Georgia.
Still, unlike Garoppolo, Bennett doesn’t have the experience of starting regular season games. In two years with the team, he hasn’t taken a real regular season snap outside of a kneel-down. The snaps during the preseason are the only live-game reps he’s gotten as well.
That’s not to say that Bennett and Simpson should evenly split the preseason reps with one playing the first half and the other playing the second. However, it would make sense for Bennett to play the first quarter or at least the first drive or two simply to get those live-game reps even if that’s just for the first two preseason games.
While Bennett has shown improvement, he still has things that he needs to work on in games. His interception numbers were down last year, but he has a tendency to overlook coverage in the middle of the field or put the ball in harm’s way. That was seen during the joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys.
3️⃣ INTs Have yourself a day, @justinbarron22 👏 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/Dfv4SLCtmK
The priority for the preseason s hould be to get Simpson as many reps as possible . If the Rams chose to play him the entire game, it would make sense. At the same time, those are reps that are still valuable for Bennett. He’s not the seasoned veteran that Garoppolo was the last two years.
It’s clear that the Rams trust Bennett as he’s taken every backup quarterback rep throughout training camp. However, the live-game reps are still valuable for Bennett given his lack of regular season experience.
McVay has typically prioritized keeping starters and key depth healthy during the preseason. If Bennett is the backup quarterback, he would likely be included in that. However, there wouldn’t be a significant drop-off if something happened to Bennett given that the Rams drafted Simpson. They have two very capable backup options behind Stafford. Getting both players live-game experience during the preseason would benefit the Rams more than keeping Bennett on the sideline.

title: Puka Nacua Injury Scare Highlights Rams’ Biggest Roster Concern
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have one of the best rosters in the NFL as they head into the 2026 season. However, if there is one major question on the roster, it’s the wide receiver depth behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Given Nacua’s injury history and Adams’ age, the Rams will likely need to rely on that depth at some point this season. That was already the case when Nacua left Tuesday’s joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys early.
It’s very possible that the Rams lean into more 13 personnel this season. Colby Parkinson showed some reliability last season, but Terrance Ferguson is unproven in his second year. Additionally, Tyler Higbee hasn’t been the same since tearing his ACL and is getting older.
The Rams also aren’t going to completely move away from using three wide receivers . They are going to need a reliable third wide receiver at some point. While Jordan Whittington has spent three years in the system and CJ Daniels has impressed during training camp, it would be hard to rely on either of them in big moments. The same can be said about Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield.
Last season, the Rams lacked a third wide receiver. With the season on the line, they were forced to go to Mumpfield, who was a seventh-round rookie. That’s not to blame the NFC Championship loss on Mumpfield. However, it does show how their lack of wide receiver depth left them vulnerable in a big moment.
There’s no doubt that Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. The Rams were likely being cautious when he left Tuesday’s joint practice with an injury. Nacua likely continues to play during an actual game. At the same time, Nacua’s physical play style makes him more susceptible to injuries. That also doesn’t account for the possibility that Nacua is suspended to start the season .
During the draft, the Rams had the opportunity to draft players like Makai Lemon or Denzel Boston. Instead, they took a quarterback in Ty Simpson with the 13th overall pick. The Rams didn’t necessarily make the wrong choice by taking Simpson. It made sense that they took Simpson, given that Lemon or Boston would have been the third wide receiver in the offense at best. The Rams also don’t want to be relying on young, inexperienced players in a Super Bowl season.
However, that’s exactly where the Rams would be if Nacua or Adams were to go down with an injury. The 2026 season is too big for the Rams to rely on inexperienced depth.
This is a team that already missed out on signing Stefon Diggs. While Diggs may have been a fit for what the Rams need, it’s possible they learned from the DeSean Jackson situation in 2021. Jackson was sold a bigger role in free agency than he got, and the two sides ended up going their separate ways midseason.
Even if the Rams don’t see Tyreek Hill as a fit, Brandin Cooks and Keenan Allen are both free agents . Cooks has played in a complementary role over the last few years of his career. Allen was basically the third wide receiver for the Los Angeles Chargers last year as both Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey each had a higher snap count than Allen.
It’s possible that the Rams are waiting to see what Aaron Donald does before making any other additions to the roster. The Rams have around $15.3 million and will need that when they begin working out Donald’s contract. However, once that is settled, taking another look at the roster before the regular season begins would be beneficial.
The Rams offense has the ability to scheme players open. However, the biggest question mark on the roster remains the wide receiver depth. It’s one thing that could cost them and the Rams got a glimpse of that on Tuesday when Nacua left the joint practice against the Cowboys. The Rams don’t need to make a splashy trade or bring in someone who expects a significant role. However, adding a veteran would give the offense another reliable option and address one of the biggest needs on the roster.

title: Rams Get Mixed Reviews in Joint Practice Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams had their first of two joint practices this summer. On Tuesday, the Rams practiced against the Dallas Cowboys as they prepare for their first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Historically, head coach Sean McVay has found more value in joint practices rather than preseason games as it’s a more controlled environment.
Given that the practice was in Woodland Hills and not Oxnard at the Cowboys’ facility, media reporting was limited. The Rams don’t allow the media to comment on specific personnel or report certain details from practice.
Reviews of the Rams’ performance were pretty mixed. Still, McVay seemed pleased with the overall takeaway from the practice.
“There was a lot of good work that we got today against an excellent opponent, just bouncing back and forth. I thought the team periods were competitive and most importantly, we can learn,” said McVay. “These are opportunities for us to grow even though we don't game plan it. We're just testing our rules. There was a lot of good stuff really from both sides and I look forward to looking at the film and diving into how we can learn from it.”
According to team reporter Stu Jackson , quarterback Matthew Stafford threw one interception, but was flawless otherwise. Jackson noted an interception from Quentin Lake and the pass rush getting to Dak Prescott without Myles Garrett. After practice, Stafford made sure to compliment the offensive line, especially in the run game.
The Athletic’s Nate Atkins noted that the Rams’ secondary won the day. Said Atkins, “The Rams’ secondary mostly won the day, thanks to some help from the pass rush. And what stood out was the versatility in their approach.”
Lake on lock. 🔒 pic.twitter.com/IybGv21Lq5
However, given some of the reporting limitations, it was mostly Cowboys media commenting on the practice as it was happening. According to many Cowboys media members , the Rams’ offense struggled at times against Christian Parker’s defense.
The Cowboys’ linebackers reportedly stole the show, especially Dee Winters and Justin Barron. Barron had a pair of interceptions on Stafford and Stetson Bennett. Wide receiver George Pickens also made some plays against the Rams’ secondary.
3️⃣ INTs Have yourself a day, @justinbarron22 👏 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/Dfv4SLCtmK
Reading the Rams’ coverage, it’s easy to come away with the takeaway that they had a very strong joint practice. On the other hand, Cowboys media would have you believing that they dominated the afternoon.
At the end of the day, the answer is likely somewhere in the middle, and it doesn’t matter as much as many want it to. That’s not to say that joint practices don’t matter. McVay clearly finds value in them. With that said, there’s no game planning involved, and winning a joint practice doesn’t equate to winning games in the regular season. It matters in the same way that the preseason doesn’t matter.
This is simply a chance for the Rams to compete against a different defense and test out some things that they’ve been working on. Since the start of training camp , the Rams have been going up against the same group of players on the other side. Tuesday was an opportunity to compete against another set of players and go against a team that feels different. The Rams aren’t going to show their entire hand against a team that they are set to play in December.
While the Rams may not have been their sharpest, there were still strong moments and McVay seemed pleased with the work they got in. That’s the important part. The Rams will have nearly a month to make adjustments based on what they learned and continue building toward Week 1.

title: Rams Get Positive Puka Nacua Injury Update, Remain Cautious With Myles Garrett
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams wrapped up their joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday, but it didn’t come without its share of injuries . Wide receiver Puka Nacua left practice about 45 minutes early and did not return while edge rusher Myles Garrett sat out practice completely.
Head coach Sean McVay said that he wasn’t sure exactly what happened to Nacua.
“He was not able to finish practice so something happened. I'll have an update on it. I'm not sure exactly what that was,” said McVay. Added quarterback Matthew Stafford, “I'm not really sure what the issue was but nobody ran up to me in a panic, so I don’t think it was anything too major.”
NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport confirmed that it was nothing major for Nacua. Rapoport reported that Nacua is dealing with some minor soreness in his groin and that the team was just being cautious.
#Rams WR Puka Nacua, who left practice while walking with a trainer, is dealing with minor soreness in his groin, I'm told. The team is just being cautious.
Nacua wasn’t the only player the Rams were cautious with on Tuesday. After missing three consecutive practices during training camp , Garrett returned to the field for the final two days. He also practiced when the team got back to Woodland Hills. However, Garrett was held out once again for the joint practice with the Cowboys due to some swelling in his knee. McVay said that Garrett felt 85 percent, but the team erred on the side of caution.
“We just erred on the side of caution,” said McVay. “He wanted to be able to be out there, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he's able to return to full performance and feel like himself. There's nothing to be concerned about. It was just us erring on the side of caution.”
The Rams have been cautious all offseason with key players on both sides of the ball. Stafford has been practicing every other day while the Rams have held out wide receiver Davante Adams with rest days. Left tackle Alaric Jackson has missed some time as he manages blood clot medication and edge rusher Byron Young has missed practice with some knee soreness.
It shouldn’t be surprising that the Rams are being cautious with injuries and their star players. It does the Rams no good if Myles Garrett hurts his knee in August when they’re going to need him in November. The focus remains staying as healthy as possible for the start of the regular season. The goal is winning Week 1, not a joint practice against the Cowboys.
The Rams will start preparing for their preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs. As in past years, no starters or key depth players are expected to play during the preseason, with health being the priority.

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua Facing Potential Suspension for Week 1 vs. 49ers
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams wrap up training camp and get ready for the regular season, they could be without their star wide receiver when they play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. On his podcast on Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter said that Nacua’s case is one of several that are under review and being investigated by the NFL.
“Right now, there are some things going on behind closed doors that we don’t have full access to that are going to have a significant impact on the season,” said Schefter. “Cases I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams’ wide receiver Puka Nacua…it’s possible when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game.”
Potential discipline looms over a group of NFL players, including Rams WR Puka Nacua and Packers RB Josh Jacobs. Cc: @tyschmit 🎧 https://t.co/mTwS98lcWO pic.twitter.com/e5fW2ZoQwV
Following the Rams’ loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game, Nacua was seen out on New Year’s Eve and made headlines. Nacua allegedly bit a woman on the shoulder, leaving a mark. The victim has filed a civil lawsuit against Nacua. While no court date is currently set, Nacua's attorneys recently requested to push back a key witness deposition after September 7.
Nacua spent time in rehab this summer as he worked to grow as a person . He has been on his best behavior throughout training camp and didn’t hold out despite being in the final year of his rookie contract.
It’s unclear how long Nacua’s suspension would be and if one occurs before the regular season. The NFL still needs to go through its own independent investigation. The league also tends to let the legal process play out before making a decision. If Nacua is suspended for Week 1, it would be a significant loss against a division rival.
Schefter also noted that Alaric Jackson’s case from the offseason is under review. Jackson was arrested on felony domestic battery. However, the charges were dropped . While the charges were dropped, that doesn’t mean that the NFL can’t still hand out a suspension. This would be Jackson’s second offense against the personal conduct policy.
The cases remain under review and are still being investigated, according to Schefter. However, discipline is still a potential option. “By the time the regular season opens, we’ll have more clarity as it pertains to Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackson,” said Schefter.
This is certainly going to be something to monitor over the next few weeks. The league typically announces its disciplinary actions after law enforcement and independent league investigations conclude.
The Rams are heading into a season with Super Bowl expectations. Suspensions and injuries are among the few things that could derail those expectations. These situations were completely avoidable, and the Rams may now have to face the consequences. The Rams have a difficult schedule to open the season with their first four games against the 49ers, New York Giants, Denver Broncos, and Philadelphia Eagles. They will certainly want to be at full strength for those games and get off to a strong start.

title: 5 Key Things to Watch During Rams-Cowboys Joint Practice
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to practice against the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday in Woodland Hills before they start preparing for the preseason. Head coach Sean McVay typically rests all of his starters and key depth during the preseason, opting for the more controlled environment of joint practices.
These reps during joint practices will be the only ones against a different defense for the Rams’ starters before Week 1. It’s a chance for the Rams to see if what they’ve been installing is working and if adjustments are needed. Here are five things to watch as the Rams get ready to practice against the Cowboys.
The Rams put a lot of focus on improving their secondary this offseason . They signed Jaylen Watson and traded for Trent McDuffie. Against the Cowboys, the Rams’ secondary will get an immediate test as they go up against a good quarterback in Dak Prescott as well as one of the best wide receiver duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Watson and McDuffie go up against Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on a daily basis. However, it will be interesting to see how they do against another good wide receiver pairing. The Rams likely won’t show a ton, but we will get a first look at how the Rams deploy their secondary and how they envision McDuffie, Watson and Quentin Lake fitting together.
While the Cowboys no longer have Micah Parsons, this is still a defense with a strong front. Quinnen Williams can be dominant and Kenny Clark is one of the better nose tackles in the NFL. Rashan Gary brings good speed off of the edge and presents some challenges. Donavan Ezeiruaku was ejected from a Cowboys practice last week and was seen throwing a punch. If the two sides get heated, he’s one to watch.
That group will be a good test for the Rams’ offensive line. Williams and Clark give the Cowboys a strong interior, which should present a challenge for Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila and Kevin Dotson. Gary’s speed will be a good test for Warren McClendon on the right side. In these settings, it’s always interesting to see how the offensive line performs.
Throughout the entirety of training camp, CJ Daniels was someone who consistently impressed . The Rams may not have a true WR3, but if Daniels can continue performing at that level against another defense, the rookie could carve out a role in the offense.
It will be interesting to see how much work the second-team offense gets. If they do get some work, Daniels will likely be part of the rotation. The next couple of weeks will be important for Daniels as he looks to carry what he did during training camp into joint practices and the preseason.
The biggest trade of the offseason was undoubtedly the Rams trading for Myles Garrett. While Garrett spent some of training camp dealing with lower-body soreness, the defense finished training camp on a high note . The Rams have had to focus on Garrett when going up against him in practice. Now the Rams will get to see how he impacts another team’s offensive operation.
Garrett has the ability to take over games, which is why the Rams traded for him. While this isn’t a game, they will still get to see him go up against an offensive line other than their own. Tyler Guyton has shown some positive moments, but Garrett could make things very difficult for the Cowboys on Tuesday.
When Sean McVay was asked how he would deploy the quarterbacks in the preseason , he wasn’t sure if Stetson Bennett would play, but said that Ty Simpson certainly would. If Bennett performs well during the joint practices, it wouldn’t be surprising for McVay to make the decision to rest him through the preseason. Bennett performed better than expected during training camp and the Rams seem to feel comfortable with him as the backup.
With Stafford practicing, it’s unlikely that Simpson gets too much of a look against the Cowboys’ defense. Most of the reps will be split between Matthew Stafford and Bennett. Still, it would be nice to see Simpson get a few reps against another defense, especially as the Rams prepare for the preseason.

title: One Raiders’ Position Battle Isn’t As Close as Some Think
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders made wholesale roster changes across the board this offseason. Those changes led to increased competition at training camp, which will continue into the preseason and the 2026 season. Las Vegas' coaching staff has insisted that competition has taken place at every position.
The Raiders' front office added talent to essentially every position group on the roster, except tight end and punter, where they have two of the best players in the league at both positions. The roster additions have improved the Raiders, but there is still plenty to figure out.
Las Vegas recently released its depth chart ahead of its first preseason game. Thursday's exhibition matchup against the Arizona Cardinals will be the best look at Klint Kubiak's Raiders . They have a long way to go. They hope a new approach will lead to even more improvement.
Las Vegas plans to handle their wide receiver position by committee. The position will be handled largely by Jalen Nailor, Tre Tucker, and Jack Bech. Kubiak noted earlier this offseason that Bech is in competition with Dont'e Thornton and others, but Bech appears to be solidified on the depth chart.
Despite Kubiak's words, there is a decent gap between Bech and Thornton that was not there last season. While there is increased competition at the position, that competition comes from the group as a whole, more than from Thornton specifically.
Rookie wide receiver Malik Benson was drafted in the seventh round of this year's NFL Draft. He has already begun making more of an impact at receiver than many expected on draft night. He is also making that impact sooner than most would have expected.
Many players have had a strong training camp, only to fall by the wayside during the regular season, but Las Vegas' need at receiver and more productive practices will lead to more opportunities for Benson. Raiders wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni recently gave insight into Benson's development.
"Malik’s doing a good job. I'm pleased with his improvement, his progress. Long way to go. He's still a rookie, makes those rookie mistakes. But I'm pleased with his effort, his attitude. He's extremely coachable,” Azzanni said following training camp.
“He's tough. You do that, you got a chance. And he's improving every day, which is what I want to see. Slight improvement, steady, a little bit every day, and he's been doing that. So, I'm pleased with where he's currently at."
Las Vegas' group of wide receivers features several players who could push for playing time at some point this season. The Raiders will handle the position by committee, giving any and every receiver on the roster a chance to secure a roster spot and playing time.
If Benson can shoot up the depth chart, any of the other wide receivers can too. This should encourage and motivate the likes of Thornton and any other receiver moving forward. Azzanni believes Thornton has responded well to his ups and downs on the field.
"Same thing with Dont'e. I always tell our room that the tape is our resume, let the tape be our guide. So, all of those guys, if they have a down day, they got to come back and have a better day. We just press play. We evaluate it every day. He's had a couple rough days and he's bounced back and had some good plays here and there,” Azzanni said.
"And that's what we're looking for in training camp, we're installing all this stuff. Everything's not going to be perfect, but I am pleased he's got a great attitude. He's working his tail off. I saw some improvement today, which was good. We go day by day in training camp, so he's coming along like the rest of them."
With the Raiders aiming to supply their offense with as many capable pass catchers as possible, they will likely hold on to as many receivers as make sense. This should buy time for Thornton and others who hope to progress to develop further.
However, Las Vegas is sure to continue revamping the position group over the next few seasons. Time will tell how patient the front office and coaching staff will be with a group of receivers that is largely replaceable. The receivers currently on the roster must make the most of their opportunity.

title: Raiders Training Camp Report 16: Evolving Expectations Emerge
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—Today marks Day 16 of the Las Vegas Raiders' full-team training camp, and expectations are high as the team prepares for its first preseason game of the year tomorrow night at Allegiant Stadium.
Klint Kubiak, while a rookie head coach, has shown none of the rookie head coaching mistakes so far by running a considerably efficient and tight camp, with enormous credit going to his staff, young and old, and the fact that he has been born into the NFL and it has been the totality of his life.
Today will be my final update before the preseason game, and I want to do a deep dive into what is setting this camp apart and what you can really learn from the first preseason game.
On a team with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, with NFL executives swooning over Fernando Mendoza, you would not have expected so much attention to go to so many other rookies.
Perception would be wrong. While Mendoza has looked terrific, credit John Spytek and his staff of Brian Stark, Brandon Hunt, and Brandon Yeargan, and their respective staffs, for assembling a fantastic rookie class.
The youngster Hezekiah Masses, CB, appears to be a fifth-round steal as he makes plays every single day all over the field. The biggest criticism of his game coming into the NFL was his lack of physicality on tape. It was a fair criticism, but it didn’t mean he couldn’t do it. He wasn’t asked to. He is now making those criticisms look foolish. I asked him about his impressive physical nature and that criticism.
"Oh, yeah, I'm trying to take their head off. Yeah, that was a big issue, they said I can't tackle, so I'm going to show them. I'm going to show them very physical. I can do everything."
Once, while interviewing Michael Jordan, I asked him about when he performed at his highest level, about being in the zone, and what that was like. He told me, “Like the rim is 10 feet around, not high.” I have never forgotten that, and right now, Masses is playing in that proverbial zone, in my perception. I asked him.
“I'm in that zone for sure, just 100%. I'm just out there just making plays and just being myself. They calling great calls, and I'm just out there executing."
Masses has been terrific and will clearly have an impact on the Raiders' 2026 season. But don’t say that too loud; he still thinks he is on the bubble and said he has his focus on making the 53-man roster. Hey, Hezekiah, you have.
“A goal for me is just make the 53-man roster, and then just be the best version of myself, be the best teammate I could be, and then just whatever I can do to contribute to help us win. That's what I'm going to do."
When Hezekiah speaks, the appreciation of being an NFL player exudes from him. You can see it every moment, every rep; he wants more, he will do more, and he loves the moments. While fans and many veterans even bemoan preseason games, Masses isn’t one of them.
He knows that it is special to play in the NFL, and since he was little, being in this league has been his dream. When you listen to him talk about Thursday night’s preseason tilt with Arizona, he makes it sound like a Super Bowl. It most certainly is for the young man who dreamed of being an NFL player. It was refreshing.
"Yeah, I'm just super excited, man. It feels so unreal, man. My first preseason game. I'm just happy for the opportunity. I'm just ready to play on Thursday."
Coming into the 2026 NFL Draft, Jermod McCoy was considered by most as the best CB in the draft. Concerns about a potential issue with a knee plug saw him plunge to the top of the fourth round. That plunge conceivably cost him $40 million. But he isn’t bitter; he is motivated, and credits the Raiders staff for having him in tip-top shape.
“I think it's been a great process with them. From the day I came in to now, the way I feel is so much better. AG [Alex Guerrero], all the guys in there, I feel like they just really been pouring into me. I mean, they got me right."
Malik Benson, the WR the Raiders somehow managed to snare in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has not been good; he has been sensational in his first NFL training camp. The coaches love him, and McCoy loves the chance to compete with him.
"Oh, it's been good. Me and Malik [Benson], man, every time I'm up against Malik, I love it because they love throwing to Malik. So, I know when I'm against Malik, the ball's probably coming there. So, I'm going to try to make a play."
The Raiders have been terrible on defense, creating and getting turnovers. But in adding new players, they have brought in ball hawks. Men who see the ball and get it. Something Jermod McCoy is known for, and he thinks he and the “Leonard Doctrine” are tailor-made for each other.
"I'm always trying to get the ball back, make plays on the ball. I mean, we want the offense on the field as much as possible to put points on the board. So, whatever we can do to get the ball back and help the team do that, that's what we're going to do."
McCoy missed his entire 2025 season after his preseason knee injury. While incredibly gifted, he doesn’t take the game for granted. This is a game he loves. Like Masses earlier, getting back on the field Thursday night is going to be emotional for him. Not only achieving his dream of playing in the NFL, but also being back on the football field for a game, something he loves.
"For sure, there's definitely going to be some emotions."
McCoy has seen the success of fellow rookie CB Masses and thinks the two are helping each other, which is exactly what Spytek wanted in selecting four DBs in the 2026 NFL Draft. A decision that appears to be paying off, per McCoy.
“Me and Zeke [Hezekiah Masses], we talk a lot about stuff that we see, try to coach each other up on things. I feel like we're really similar with our mindsets. We both want to be the best. So, I mean, I think two rookies coming in and doing that, it's something. It's hard to find that for real, I think."
No matter who you talk to on this team, the appreciation for Klint Kubiak’s commitment to detail has them raving about the Silver and Black first-year head coach. Something rookie Trey Zuhn III echoes.
"I love working with him. He's extremely detailed. He expects the most out of us every single day, day in, day out. So, he's definitely taking this team where it needs to go."
Zuhn, the top OL in the SEC last year, dug into the adjustment from the country's second-best conference (SEC) to the NFL and why he loves the challenge.
"Yeah, it's just more detailed. The competition's so much better; it's the best of the best. So, you can't be half a step wrong. You have to know the playbook like the back of your hand, and you have to study your teammates like they're an opponent every single day so you have a step on them. So, I've enjoyed it."
In the MLB, a five-tool player has mastery-level ability in the five core critical skills of playing baseball. Zuhn can play all five offensive line positions in the NFL, and does so seamlessly from one rep to the next. His football IQ is enormous, and when he does get a break, I often see him talking to Tyler Linderbaum, the Raiders' C and a generational talent, and Kolton Miller, one of the top-five LTs in the NFL. So what is it like as a young rookie having those two resources to draw from? I asked him.
"Right, those are amazing resources. So, I want to talk to them all I can. I just want to learn from them because they've been in the league, they know how it goes, they know football. So, whatever I can learn from them to help the team, I want to learn."
Switching from one play to another, or one series to another at a different position, wouldn’t be easy for anyone. Zuhn’s football acumen is off the charts, and he let us into his mental process for dealing with and playing so many different spots.
"Whenever I'm going in for a series and I'm at a certain position, I just have to lock in and be at that position. Because I've learned the playbook from a whole, so I know what everybody's…

title: Spytek, Raiders Add Offensive Lineman: What It Means
full_text:
With their first preseason game of the season quickly approaching on Thursday, the Las Vegas Raiders made another addition to their offensive line Wednesday. The Raiders made the addition while they are still in the process of solidifying the depth chart along their offensive line.
Las Vegas completed training camp on Tuesday evening at Allegiant Stadium, then signed offensive lineman Braeden Daniels. The fourth-year offensive lineman has spent time with several practice squads around the league, including the Dallas Cowboys and, most recently, the Miami Dolphins.
Daniels will be a depth piece on Las Vegas' offensive line, as their front office continues to make changes to the unit. The Raiders will take the next few weeks of preseason practices and games to sort things out.
In a corresponding move, the Raiders waived/injured offensive guard Justin Pickett. The Raiders' front office continues to make moves they believe will improve the roster overall, regardless of how big or small those moves may be.
The addition of Daniels to a position group that Las Vegas is still figuring out shows they are serious about revamping every level of their depth chart. Daniels' addition is likely not a big move, but it should send somewhat of a message to the players that the front office notices everything.
The addition of Daniels should also be a reminder that it will take longer than just this offseason to truly fix Las Vegas' most pressing issue. When healthy, the Raiders' offensive line is better than it was last season, but the starters need further development in a new system, and the unit still needs depth.
Raiders offensive line coach Rick Dennison recently explained where the Raiders' offensive line stands, noting that although some positions have been solidified, players on each level of the offensive line's depth chart are still competing.
“They're all trying to be the best they can be for the team, whatever role they are. I think that's the big thing. It's a big 'we' in our meeting room,” Dennison said following training camp.
“They all talk about we watch individual, we watch team, I correct them, they talk to each other, and the leaders like Kolton [Miller], he'll say, 'This is what I would have done. You should think about this.' So, those guys have shared information. I think they're just trying to get the best team out there."
After an offseason filled with big swings that added much-needed talent, there is not much more the Raiders' front office can do to improve the roster this offseason. Still, they continue to look for ways to improve at every turn, as they look to establish a firm offensive identity under Klint Kubiak.
The Raiders have improved the coaching along their offensive line and look to continue adding talent when possible this offseason and beyond. Dennison elaborated, noting that he and the coaching staff are doing all they can to help build a cohesive offensive line.
“I don't think we have anybody in the room that doesn't want to be pushed. That's why they're here. If they were that way, they probably wouldn't be here, right? So I don't know if I'm tough or not, I'm just me. I tell them all the time, I'm going to be mad at you if you make a mistake. If you make it twice, I'm really going to be mad,” Dennison said.
“But it's important that they know that their jobs are essential for all 11 to do right. It's not just one guy. All 11 got to do something right. So, we can't just say we're successful because one guy did it right. We've all got to work together, that's why the five of them have got to work hard."

title: Raiders Round Out Training Camp, Prepare To Move Forward
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders held their final training camp practice of the 2026 season at Allegiant Stadium on Tuesday night. The Raiders opened the stadium to fans to showcase the progress made on the field after a number of solid roster moves.
The Raiders hope to be consistently competitive sooner rather than later. Below are a few notes from Las Vegas' 11th and final training camp practice of the season. The Raiders are two days away from their first exhibition game under head coach Klint Kubiak.
The Raiders took the field at Allegiant Tuesday evening in front of Raiders fans. It was an affordable opportunity for fans to connect with a largely new-look roster that the Raiders will debut this season. Tuesday was another step closer to a season that has begun garnering cautious optimism.
It was an unpadded practice for Las Vegas, yet they showed enough to give an idea of what to expect moving forward. It also gave the Raiders a chance to get some work done on their home field, which differs from the practice fields at the team's headquarters.
“Tonight's really important. Really excited about going and being in front of our fans, being on the grass that we're going to play on. Coaches communicating with the headsets; really important for the whole operation,” Kubiak said earlier on Tuesday before practice.
“Obviously, it's my first game in there. Played a few games on the other side of the stadium, but it'll be really important for players and coaches to get familiar with our surroundings so that we can play our best football on Thursday night."
With Tuesday's practice out of the way, Las Vegas will take Wednesday off before returning to Allegiant Stadium for their first preseason game on Thursday to face the Arizona Cardinals.
Las Vegas is implementing a whole new offensive and defensive scheme, with a new head coach, coordinators, and players at critical positions. They have practiced against each other enough. They need additional work against a different team to truly improve. Kubiak explained his plan for Thursday.
"We do have a plan for those guys and how many snaps or series we'd like to see them go. No need for everyone else to know it, but we're going to have a lot of guys playing this game. We need to evaluate the whole roster,” Kubiak said ahead of Tuesday night's open practice.
"I think it's really important that our guys have the same attitude we've asked them to have all camp – have a team-first attitude and have shocking effort. That's what we're looking for, looking for competitive guys. And one thing that we've really stressed is, especially for our young guys, of using special teams as their avenue to make the team. So, we're going to be evaluating those reps very critically."
Kubiak has made it clear that Las Vegas' starters will play against the Cardinals. Regardless of how much they do or do not play, it is fair to assume that progress will be made. The Raiders have about another month's worth of practices and preseason games before the first regular-season game.
The Raiders will now enter the preseason looking to take the next step in their progression under Kubiak ahead of his first regular season as a head coach. Progress has been made, but even Kubiak would agree that much more must be done in the next few weeks before they face the Miami Dolphins.
It must be remembered that much of the progress the Raiders and other teams hope to make cannot be made until everything is going at full speed. That means it will likely take a few weeks into the regular season to get an idea of what the Raiders will be this season.
Based on what they showed during training camp, it is fair to expect they will be better than in the past two seasons. That is, assuming they stay relatively healthy. Kubiak's coaching staff has begun changing the culture in Las Vegas. They hope additional wins will follow.

title: Kubiak Discusses Mendoza, Starters Snaps in Raiders' First Preseason Game
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders kick off their 2026 preseason on Thursday night against the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium at 5 pm PST.
While speaking with the media on Tuesday, head coach Klint Kubiak revealed the plan for the starters and rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
Because Kirk Cousins has 15 years of NFL experience, I don't expect the 37-year-old quarterback to play much, if at all, on Thursday night. That should open up plenty of runway for Mendoza, who will be the player everyone will be keeping tabs on as the contest progresses.
Kubiak stated that the No. 1 overall pick will get "plenty of experience" against the Cardinals, which could mean multiple quarters. If Cousins were to sit entirely, I would expect Mendoza to play two quarters. Kubiak was reluctant to reveal how many snaps certain players would receive on Thursday night, but this is a great opportunity for Mendoza to show what he has demonstrated throughout camp.
As everyone knows, training camp is physical , but quarterbacks are not to be hit. In the preseason, it is free game for a defensive lineman to hit the quarterback. Mendoza's timing, pre-snap recognition, and command of the offense will be under the lights in live snaps. It is a nationally televised game, as Mendoza was the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft.
Nevertheless, this is an exciting time for Raiders fans, as they will have the chance to watch their future franchise quarterback play against an opposing NFL defense for the first time.
