title: McCarthy vs. Wentz: Debating Who Vikings Should Name as Kyler Murray's Backup
full_text:
It's no longer news that Kyler Murray is the Vikings' starting quarterback for the 2026 NFL season, as there's been more than enough time to digest the new reality. Without much surprise, Murray becoming the QB1 has left Vikings fans wondering what to make of J.J. McCarthy's outlook with the franchise .
For now, head coach Kevin O'Connell has made it crystal clear that the 23-year-old QB is "ready to go" when it comes to taking on backup duties , per Bring Me The News ' Will Ragatz. Even though that's another vote of confidence from his head coach, it doesn't exactly sound like O'Connell confirmed that McCarthy would be the de facto QB2—which is especially curious with Carson Wentz lurking in the shadows.
That said, it's time to examine whether McCarthy or Wentz is the better backup option for the Vikings.
Although he started 10 times last season, it's fair to doubt whether McCarthy is the right man for the job given that the results were... less than stellar.
He completed 57.6% of passes for 1,632 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a 72.6 passer rating. McCarthy's 61.8 overall grade ranked 35th among 43 qualified quarterbacks on Pro Football Focus , giving a clearer picture of where he ranked around the league.
Couple that performance with an underwhelming training camp for the most part , and no one would blame the Vikings for wanting McCarthy to further prove himself. In fact, that's exactly what he should be doing. He's given the doubters too much material—between last season and this summer—to doubt his capabilities, and it's time to use the upcoming preseason slate to silence them.
As for his case, McCarthy's 10 starts indicate he should slot in seamlessly should he need to step in for Murray at any point. He'll have had another training camp and preseason to work with O'Connell, so there's no excuse not to be better than what we've already seen. Especially if McCarthy is fighting for his future at that point.
The fact that there are two years plus a fifth-year option remaining on his contract only adds to why the Vikings might want to keep McCarthy rather than expose him to waivers.
Bringing in Murray wasn't the only QB-related move the Vikings made this offseason, as they also re-signed Carson Wentz back in March.
The former Pro Bowler competed with McCarthy for the QB1 job, and while he initially lost, he made five starts as his younger counterpart faltered early on. Unfortunately, injuries—including a season-ending shoulder issue—limited his availability. Wentz finished the 2025 campaign with 1,216 yards, six TDs to five INTs and an 85.8 passer rating with a 65.1% completion rate.
Despite the injury-plagued year, all signs point to Wentz having a strong training camp so far.
On Saturday, Vikings OnSI 's Jason Harmon mentioned how the former NFL MVP finalist stood out among the rest and " flashed what remained of his mobility at age 33 by taking off for a scramble ." The preseason will reveal if the throwback performances in practice are a sign of what he can still do against an actual opponent, but it's safe to say that the early signs are encouraging.
Of course, the fact that Wentz has 99 regular-season starts and a Super Bowl ring in his collection helps strengthen his QB2 case. On the flip side, his recent injury history gives reason for pause.
Yes, last season was a frustrating experience. Yes, he's made some mistakes in training camp and will likely mess up a few more times in the preseason. Still, McCarthy is who the Vikings should roll with behind Murray, rather than choose Wentz.
Experience and results are on Wentz's side, but McCarthy's age and contract can't be ignored. He also still has O'Connell's trust, and that, regardless of what you think about it, means something. Whether McCarthy repays that trust by taking that next step remains to be seen, though.
At the end of the day, the Vikings could end up looking foolish by letting McCarthy go (either via cut or trade) and watching him develop into a legitimate starter elsewhere. He might even be ready to overtake Murray next season. Meanwhile, veterans like Wentz—as solid as he's been—can be found throughout the season.
For now, No. 9 should be QB2.

title: J.J. McCarthy Could Still Start After Losing Vikings' QB Battle (and Here's When)
full_text:
The Vikings are still a few weeks away from finalizing their 53-man roster , meaning there's plenty of time for the ongoing position battles to develop. That said, the team's competition under center is officially over . Head coach Kevin O'Connell named Kyler Murray as the Vikings' QB1 on Tuesday, leaving no doubt who'll lead the offense into Week 1 of the regular season and beyond.
Although he had his fair share of believers, it's fair to say that the writing was on the wall for J.J. McCarthy for a while now. Although not every shortcoming so far is his fault, McCarthy rarely looked like a legitimate QB1 in the 10 starts he saw last season, and a drastically inaccurate start to training camp left O'Connell & Co. with no other option but to roll with Murray as their top arm.
But just because one battle was lost doesn't mean that all hope is gone, as the Vikings' coaching staff still believes in the former Michigan signal-caller's potential .
"(J.J. is) still a guy that's only played 10 games. He's shown improvement off of last year," O'Connell said on Tuesday. "Even in this training camp with the work he's put in and his comfort level, just growing a little bit day in and day out. Very excited to continue to get to work with him every single day, coach him."
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on JJ McCarthy’s future in Minnesota: “He’s still a guy that’s only played 10 games. He’s shown improvement off of last year… as he knows, he’s holding the pen on his story. We’re going to support him and try to help him continue to improve as a… pic.twitter.com/GdKql9mGsh
With his head coach still standing firmly behind him, there's a chance that McCarthy could wind up starting for the Vikings at some point this fall.
Murray might be the best pick to lead the Vikings' offense starting in Week 1, but that doesn't mean that he can rest on his laurels. The former Cardinals QB is still playing on a one-year contract, meaning his future is far from secure. He'll need to leave no room for questions as soon as the regular-season action begins.
Otherwise, the door will be open for a change.
The Vikings will open the season with back-to-back NFC North clashes against the Packers and Bears at home and on the road, respectively. It will be important for Murray to prove himself in these matchups, showing that the Vikings can compete with the two teams that finished first and second in last year's divisional race.
After that, he'll head into a Week 3 matchup against the Buccaneers, looking to out-duel Baker Mayfield, who's been floated as a potential QB option for Minnesota in 2027.
Games against the lowly Dolphins (Week 4) and Saints (Week 5) should be layups for Murray and company; however, they also have the potential to be trap games. If he struggles against either or both of those foes leading into the Week 6 bye, that could be the perfect excuse for the Vikings to switch things up under center.
Bye weeks are the perfect opportunity for coaches to make major lineup adjustments, including a quarterback change. Considering how the Vikings will have 14 days between their road game against the Saints and a home meeting with the Colts, McCarthy is likely looking at Week 7 as his best chance to take the reins back from Murray.
Hosting the Colts will start a tough five-game stretch that also features the Lions, Bills, Packers and 49ers. In other words, the Vikings will want the best man under center for that. If Murray proves that he can't be that guy, there won't be much to lose by throwing McCarthy back into the mix. It might be a one-game experience or last much longer.
Either way, the week leading up to Sunday, Oct. 25 is worth keeping track of.
Assuming that's McCarthy's likeliest date to return to starting duties, the 23-year-old QB has about two months to keep O'Connell and the rest of the Vikings' staff believing in him. Otherwise, regardless of how Murray performs, No. 9's time with the franchise could end sooner rather than later .

title: 6 Most Important Non-QB Positions to Watch in Vikings' Preseason Opener
full_text:
Ladies and gentlemen, we’ve made it. The Vikings are only days away from playing a real football game, kind of.
I get it, though; August football isn’t everyone’s cup of tea. While the preseason can seem like a snoozefest for some fans, the implications these games carry for players, coaches, and front office staff cannot be overstated. Each NFL team has just a few weeks left to finalize their 53-man roster , and these preseason games are the biggest stage many of these players will have to make their case.
The Vikings are currently working through decisions for several position groups, with the quarterback situation already solved . On Tuesday, head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that Kyler Murray will be the team's QB1 moving forward .
Head Coach Kevin O'Connell on naming Kyler Murray the starting QB pic.twitter.com/YSUhnuem7J
With head coach Kevin O’Connell’s preseason plan for the position a mystery and eyes already fixated on the quarterback battle, I want to highlight other key positions I’ll be watching closely when the Vikings visit the Giants on Saturday afternoon.
The Vikings are taking a… less-than-traditional approach at the center position so far this year. After injuries decimated their offensive line last season, utility offensive lineman Blake Brandel moved in as the team’s starting center for six games. The most impressive part? Brandel had never played center once in a football game before this, and he wasn’t bad. In fact, he impressed the team enough to give him the fast track to the C1 role after Ryan Kelly’s retirement.
So far through training camp, the results have been less than perfect. Brandel has had multiple botched exchanges, mainly with Kyler Murray. Backup center Michael Jurgens and rookie Gavin Gerhardt haven’t looked much better either. Center has been a noticeable weak point in both pass and run protection regardless of which unit is on the field.
While O’Connell typically avoids giving much playing time to his starters in the preseason, Brandel needs every rep he can get, especially if the Vikings are going to bet so much on his sustained success at center in 2026. If the answers don’t look promising, general manager Nolan Teasley will need to find an alternative before the season.
The Vikings' running game has been a consistent point of contention in the O'Connell era. The team enters 2026 with the returning duo of Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason, now in a revamped run scheme courtesy of assistant head coach Frank Smith. Neither Jones nor Mason is likely to get many opportunities Saturday or for the remaining preseason games, but the three backs behind them will have their opportunities to shine.
Zavier Scott, Demond Claiborne and Jordan Mims should all see significant action this week.
The depth chart scuffle between Scott and Claiborne is of particular interest. Scott has several fans within the building and was able to blend in to the room seamlessly when called upon in 2025. He is a safe, relatively dependable depth piece for a room that has dealt with its share of past injuries.
Claiborne, on the other hand, is a low-risk, high-reward gamble from the sixth round of April’s draft. The team took a flyer on Claiborne’s unique home-run speed , and Saturday would be a great time for him to put it on tape. Mims has quite the climb if he is going to make a case for the roster, as his recent addition to the team seems to fit the very definition of adding depth for camp.
I do not expect to see much, if anything, from Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison or Jauan Jennings on Saturday. Luckily for all of us, the Vikings have some fun storylines in the remainder of the WR room.
Tai Felton has been the dominant name on the offensive side of the ball through camp, and he looks to benefit from a default placement at the top of the depth chart this weekend. Felton has shown a refined ability to run routes and track the football, two things that limited his impact last season.
Myles Price has made the most of his opportunities as well. The special teams playmaker has brought in several impressive catches so far this summer. Dontae Fleming and Jeshaun Jones appear to be battling it out for the last spot in the WR room, alternating impressive moments daily between practices. Undrafted free agent Dillon Bell will need to show out in a major way to reclaim the hype he garnered all spring.
Byron Murphy Jr and Isaiah Rodgers are unlikely to see action on Saturday, but I would expect a bit of work from new addition James Pierre. The real fun, though, comes further down the depth chart.
Chuck Demmings has dominated Vikings camp discourse , and for good reason. The fifth-round corner via FCS  Stephen F. Austin has broken up passes almost daily, frustrated the team’s star wideouts, and even shown the ability to blitz during the team’s night practice. All of this hype could solidify or break apart depending on what we see on Saturday.
Dwight McGlothern and Zemaiah Vaughn will be fighting for roster spots, as both have been inconsistent to kick off camp. The team saw potential in both corners as developmental projects but will be looking to see improvement over their camp performances once preseason games kick off.
Second-round pick Jake Golday is going to be a big name to track on Saturday. While he was initially paired with Blake Cashman and other MLBs, he’s already made appearances on the outside through camp, coming in for Andrew Van Ginkel. How Flores utilizes Golday on Saturday may give us a slight hint of how he could be used once Flo’s full stash of secret plans is available in September.
Ivan Pace has had a strong performance through camp so far and will look to carry that over against the Giants. While Pace’s benching last season and the recent addition of Jamal Adams to the room had some thinking he was destined to be cut , his performance and recent developments for Adams may have created an opportunity to stick around.
Vikings fans may need to mentally prepare for the very real chance they’ve seen the last of Harrison Smith. While a post-camp return is certainly on the table, the team needs to plan for life without Hitman just to be safe.
Adams's recent number change allows him to play both linebacker and safety, giving him the chance to step in as a veteran voice and presence in the room if Smith’s absence is indeed permanent. We’ll see if he continues to get work at both spots at MetLife Stadium.
Rookie Jakobe Thonas is a key name to keep an eye on as well. The 98th overall pick from Miami is a hard-hitting missile, but he’ll need to show he can play with the poise and fundamentals needed to avoid giving up big plays in the NFL.

title: Max Brosmer Is a Surprise Winner From Kyler Murray Earning Vikings QB1 Job
full_text:
The Vikings' training camp isn't close to being over , but one position battle is. Hours before Tuesday's practice, ESPN' s Adam Schefter reported that the Vikings have ended their quarterback competition , naming Kyler Murray as the QB1 with less than a month to go before the regular season. As such, J.J. McCarthy's bid to be the No. 1 sign-caller is over.
ESPN sources: the Vikings have named Kyler Murray their starting QB. pic.twitter.com/VBE4azfGoF
Despite having yet to play a game in a Vikings jersey, Murray's strong training camp performance made it abundantly clear that the QB1 job was his to lose early in training camp. More often than not, each passing practice solidified that fact, leaving McCarthy with an uncertain future in Eagan.
Of course, Murray being named the starting signal-caller doesn't only impact McCarthy. The Vikings' decision also means that Max Brosmer's outlook with the franchise could look much different than it did at the start of training camp.
Vikings fans had high hopes for Brosmer after joining the Vikings as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Minnesota last offseason. He showed promise with 364 passing yards and two touchdowns (with an interception) in three preseason appearances, leaving fans with hope that he and McCarthy could be a solid QB tandem for years to come.
Most of that goodwill was stripped away when Brosmer was forced to make his first NFL start against the Seahawks in Week 13.
Although there's nothing wrong with losing to the eventual Super Bowl Champions, Brosmer did little to provide optimism , going 19-for-30 (63.3%) in the pocket with 126 yards and four interceptions in the 26-0 loss. He looked more poised in the three appearances that followed (including a start), but it wasn't enough to avoid being a huge question mark this offseason.
Fast forward to Murray being named the Vikings' starting arm, and the conversation will shift to who will be the QB2 and QB3.
Given that McCarthy has left much to be desired (both in his early career and this offseason), head coach Kevin O'Connell might be more comfortable giving the backup job to Carson Wentz, who's a former NFL MVP finalist with 99 career starts and a Super Bowl ring under his belt. It's also worth mentioning that Wentz has looked solid in training camp, with Vikings OnSI' s Jason Harmon remarking about his mechanics last week .
In a world where Wentz is named the QB2, it's hard to imagine McCarthy sticking around as the third-stringer—whether he wants to or not. Having him in the QB3 spot would be a distraction, and the Vikings would be better off cutting their losses and trading him elsewhere, with a potential deal leading to dead cap hits of $3.1 million in 2026 and 2027 , as well as $2.7 million in savings this year, per Spotrac .
Besides, having a former first-round pick as the QB3 isn't exactly great for optics.
Having Wentz as the backup quarterback with Brosmer learning under him as the QB3 isn't a bad idea at all. Yes, the former Golden Gopher left much to be desired in Year 1; however, Brosmer is only 25 years old and could look more at home with another season in O'Connell's scheme. If it works out, great. If not, it wouldn't be a huge loss, as the majority of his cap hit—just over $1 million—will come off the books with a cut at any point.
Other than Murray being at the top, the QB room's pecking order is still malleable. Brosmer's outlook might not be glistening at the moment, but it's brighter than it was as recently as a few days ago. If he can string together some strong practices, as well as capitalize on any preseason opportunities he gets, there's a good chance that Brosmer could be the Vikings' QB3 once Week 1 of the regular season arrives.

title: Inside Mitch Van Vooren's 'Tremendous' Journey From D1 Track Star to Patriots
full_text:
Mitch Van Vooren told his roommates. Most of his other teammates weren't aware, at least not to his knowledge.
But the senior had plans after Marquette. The 6-foot-5 track star, one who had been named an All-Big East outdoor hurdler, was transferring. He recalled being asked about what he wanted to do in the workforce after his time at Marquette. Van Vooren had other ideas.
Thanks to an extra year of eligibility granted during the COVID-19 pandemic, Van Vooren decided to pursue a dream that most people thought was crazy.
He wanted to play professional football.
"My family and friends, they always believed in me," the New England Patriots tight end told Patriots On SI last week at training camp. "I believed in my athletic ability, so it got me here to where I'm today."
Before his time in college, Van Vooren was a star for the Peshtigo High School football program in Wisconsin. But track, especially at a Big East program like Marquette, was hard to pass up. Bert Rogers, the director of track & field and cross country, remembers recruiting Van Vooren, a player who earned a scholarship after lettering four times.
As a freshman, Van Vooren finished first at the UW-Parkside Classic in the 55m hurdles (7.96 seconds), good for a personal best. In the three years that followed, Van Vooren blossomed into one of the best hurdlers in the entire Big East -- "Mitch really learned how to tactically race," Rogers told Patriots On SI.
"Over his time at Marquette, he did fine-tune his hurdling form, which certainly helped," Rogers said. "Mitch had a strong aerobic engine for a sprinter, which made him so good at the longer sprints like the 400 meters and the 400 hurdles."
By the time Van Vooren graduated from Marquette, he was a three-time Big East All-Academic and broke the university record in the 400m hurdles in the NCAA Tournament.
But he had an itch he couldn't scratch. He wanted to play in the NFL.
A hurdler at a university where the football team folded in 1960 wants to go to the NFL?
"I know there was routes to like get there," Van Vooren said. "If COVID never happened, I was gonna try out somehow and somehow get there. But with COVID, that extra year gave me the opportunity to play football. ... Everything happens for a reason, so it worked out a good way."
So Van Vooren, now in the transfer portal, looked for a new home. Sure, he had offers from Wisconsin and Miami to run track. But he wanted to stay close to home and play football. That's how he landed at St. Norbert, a Division III school in De Pere, Wisconsin -- a town with a population of about 25,000.
That doesn't scream NFL all that much. Still, Van Vooren knew what he wanted to do.
"That whole summer before I went to St. Norbert, I had a lot of good help and a lot of people around me (who) helped me make that transition," said Van Vooren, who admitted it took a lot of hard work behind the scenes.
The first year at St. Norbert was a grind, according to head coach Dan McCarty. Van Vooren came in wanting to play receiver. His body type might have screamed more of a tight end, but the transfer knew where he wanted to line up. Plus, his track background could translate to the route running needed.
"I think the whole first year was a learning curve, going from a track athlete, track mentality to a football player mentality," McCarty told Patriots On SI. "He'd been out of football for so long ... It was a lot of adjustment."
While he was at St. Norbert, Van Vooren didn't completely give up track. He ran for the Golden Knights' track program, setting a personal-best in the 400m outdoor hurdles (52.02 seconds). He would qualify for the NCAA Division III Outdoor National Championship in the category and was named a First Team All-American.
"It was a chance for him to be able to continue doing track, but also play football," McCarty said.
In his first season with St. Norbert, he caught 32 passes for 535 yards and three touchdowns. "Decent," as Van Vooren put in.
In 2024, his final year of college eligibility is when he came into his own. He caught 33 passes for 510 yards and 10 touchdowns. He was named to the All-NACC First Team and started to look like he belonged on the field. After the season, he had earned an invite to the College Gridiron Showcase in front of scouts.
He was getting onto the radars of a few NFL teams.
"He's just got that tremendous work ethic," McCarty said. "I can't say enough good things about just the character of Mitch and the type of person he is."
Van Vooren went undrafted, later signing a free agent contract with the Seattle Seahawks. His time in the Pacific Northwest was short lived, as he was released just nine days later. He'd land on his feet and join the Cleveland Browns -- only to be released after 20 days. Van Vooren remained a free agent since.
"This last year, I took a lot of effort just to make sure that I was in the correct shape," Van Vooren said, "so when I did get another shot, I'd have a chance to make that more of an opportunity than last time."
The 25-year-old arrived in New England on July 22, thrown into the training camp fire without getting reps in OTAs or mandatory minicamp. Still, he's held his own and has made several plays with the third-string offense .
The Patriots offense is historically tough for tight ends to learn , especially for those who are still trying to play catch up with their peers who didn't take a four-year hiatus to run track. So other than making the 53-man roster, what does a successful summer look like for Van Vooren?
"You never know when's the last snap," Van Vooren said. "When I get in there, just showcase my ability and I know what I can do. So hopefully I can show the team and the general public what I believe myself."
"He obviously had the physical gift, but a lot of people do," Rogers said. "What separated Mitch was that attention to detail and the drive to become better."
Not many people expect to see St. Norbert next to an NFL player's name. Even less would expect to see Marquette. And yet, Van Vooren has cleared both those hurdles with ease.
"I like to say I'm keeping that football tradition alive," Van Vooren laughed. "It kind of gives me some some pride when people ask me where I went to my undergrad. It's like, 'Oh, I went to Marquette.' They're like, 'I didn't know they had a football team.'
"They don't," he said with a smile.

title: Everything Inside Patriots' New Multi-Million Dollar Practice Facility
full_text:
FOXBORO — Even though they’ve been working out of the building for the last six months, the New England Patriots officially cut the ribbon for their New Balance Athletics Center Wednesday afternoon.
The 160,000 square foot facility, overlooking the team’s trio of practice fields, dwarfs the size of the operations that had been used inside Gillette Stadium. According to Sports Business Journal , the cost of the project was $95 million dollars.
Executives from New Balance and Suffolk Construction, along with Patriots owner Robert Kraft , head coach Mike Vrabel and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf were in attendance.
"When our family purchased the Patriots in ‘94, we made a commitment to all our fans to do everything we could to build a first-class organization and give the team the right resources to compete at the highest level," Kraft said. "This building is the latest example of that commitment."
🎗️✂️ pic.twitter.com/CMzzMZ689S
"You built such a wonderful building and practice facility and athletic performance facility that if we were to ever lose, I don't think we're going to be able to use facilities as a reason for our loss," Vrabel said to Kraft. "We spend more time here than we do at our own families, at our own homes, and we’re proud to call this home."
Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola were part of the guided tour throughout the facility. From a new-look locker room to plenty of decorations lining the walls, here’s a rundown of what stood out.
The Patriots' new cafeteria, which combined with the kitchen totals 11,000 square feet, is formatted more similarly to a restaurant’s dining room than a traditional cafeteria. It provides players and staff with food made to order, a salad and fruit bar, and buffet-style proteins.
Wednesday afternoon’s buffet included t-bone steak, mac and cheese, waffle fries, miso mirin sea bass, barbecue chicken thighs and grilled chicken breast.
A quick look at the Patriots cafeteria, where several players (Behren Morton, Nick DeGennaro, Will Campbell, Morgan Moses) were spotted eating during our tour. pic.twitter.com/LNcsO7jJkH
Right by the room’s main doorway sits a coffee station, along with to-go bars equipped with five refrigerators of drinks and shelves full of snacks. The cafeteria is on the building’s second of three levels, right at the top of the primary staircase. Vice president of football operations and strategy John Streicher called it the first and last place in the building players visit on a daily basis.
The weight room has two levels, with the bottom floor housing the majority of equipment. The primary area houses numerous machines, a Patriots -branded turf strip for sled workouts, monitors for workouts to be displayed and a large Pat Patriot emblem squatting a barbell in front of word art in the shape of New England.
The top floor contains cardio machines such as treadmills, ellipticals and stationary bikes, plus an area which Streicher referred to as “the violence room.”
That room, which includes different types of punching bags, was championed by Vrabel and his staff as a necessity. Streicher said players often end their workouts in the area, at times finishing by hitting the spring-loaded blocking pads.
The Patriots’ weight room. Not pictured: What John Streicher referred to as the “violence room,” where players can work on hand placement with punching bags. pic.twitter.com/mLlMaN6OxJ
The team’s new locker room contains 92 permanent “Longhorn Lockers,” with state-of-the-art airflow for players’ equipment to stay dry.
The top of each locker has a screen with the player’s name, number, college and position. Lifting the screen reveals shelving where helmets, pads and shells can be placed to dry off. At the bottom of the shelf, which can be pulled down to hang from the top of the locker, has Kraft’s “We Are All Patriots” mantra.
Underneath that is an open shelf and an additional closed compartment for personal items. The largest portion of the locker is dedicated to player uniforms and other clothing, next to another area for personal items.
The bottom has a cushioned seat, which has a pull-out drawer for shoes. Below the left armrest is another compartment with air-flow for gloves, towels and other gear.
Connected to the locker room is a player’s lounge complete with sofas, massage chairs, four televisions, a ping-pong table and a two-seat barber setup.
The Patriots also installed a new aquatics recovery and training room. The hydrotherapy space alone is 3,700 square feet.
The pool room contains two cold tubs, two hot tubs, five ice water plunge tubs, a rehab pool and an underwater treadmill. The area dedicated to underwater recovery has four times as much pool space as the team had in its previous facilities.
Although the media was not shown the trainer’s room on Wednesday, we did see “The Best Ability Is Availability” above several tables.
Streicher calls it the virtual room. Vrabel calls it the remote classroom. Regardless of name, it’s 10,500 square feet of turf spanning the width of an entire football field. There’s a divider in the middle, allowing it to be split into two separate rooms.
Ultimately, it’s used for players to be able to get meaningful reps “on the field” without having to step on the field. Lined with hash marks and yard markers, players can easily see their splits and work on formations in a smaller environment.
A look at the virtual classroom, where players can get reps before even coming out to the practice field. pic.twitter.com/oqqO4bCuzT
Several positional rooms connect directly to the virtual room, and massive screens are also available to let players visually see what’s being taught by the coaching staff.
Each position group has their own meeting room all along one long hallway. Some, like the safeties and cornerbacks room, have a connecting door to create one larger defensive back room. In each of the rooms, the desks work as dry-erase boards, allowing players and coaches to draw and erase information right in front of them. Each room had its own personality, as the quarterback room had Drake Maye’s now-famous orange juicer while the defensive line room had a Trojan horse in the front.
The main team meeting room seats 160 people. At the front of the room was a larger-than-life video board. Streicher explained that the center part of the board would show film, while the outer screens on either side would show additional information like coaching points or formations.
Both walls also had the team’s identity on it, which read: “Effort & Finish”, “Ball Security & Ball Disruption”, “Details, Technique & Fundamentals,” and “Make Great Decisions.”
During April’s soft-launch tour, media members weren’t able to get a look inside the war room. They were today, as they were met with a massive video board on the left-hand side. That’s the board the team used for their completed draft board , as well as a screen to FaceTime drafted prospects. On the left side of the room, the Patriots keep tallies on the rest of the NFL’s draft picks with another screen.
When it’s not draft season, the room is used for other purposes. Streicher shared that a meeting with the team’s analytics staff was recently held, as was a meeting with the scouting department to watch recent film.
Inside the walls of the Patriots’ new facility: pic.twitter.com/Le5Zw3tcHX
There were not many blank spaces along the hallway walls throughout the building. When you first enter, right above the doorway is each of the Patriots ’ six Super Bowl championships (and space for more). Go up the front stairs and on your right, you’re greeted by a wall honoring all of the team’s captains since 2000.
Through the cafeteria hallway, plaques honoring the Patriots Hall of Fame and Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees lined the walls. Go up a flight of stairs and a mural with each of the Patriots’ Ron Burton Community Service Award winners was on the left.

title: Biggest Surprises Spotted on Patriots' First Preseason Depth Chart
full_text:
Ahead of their first preseason game this week, the New England Patriots -- like every team -- released their first unofficial depth chart of the year.
A lot will be made of these depth chart placements, including this story. But nothing here is set in stone. Except for maybe Drake Maye as QB1, Christian Gonzalez as CB1 and A.J. Brown as WR1. Those feel like safe bets to me right now.
There were a few names, however, that did jump out as surprises. Whether they were ranked higher than they've been working in training camp or the complete inverse, there are several Patriots who stand out to me.
With the preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colt s slated for tomorrow, here's what caught my eye (and what to expect from these players come game action).
Here’s a look at the #Patriots first unofficial depth chart of 2026: pic.twitter.com/0fHWufMEwN
Jennings was absent to open up the summer while he nursed an ailment on the non-football injury list. In his place was second-year Lan Larison, who's currently named the RB3 on the Patriots. Larison might have gotten reps as the third back earlier in camp, but since Jennings has returned, it's been all him.
There's a clear drop-off between Jennings' skillset and the rest of the running back room (Larison, and rookies Jam Miller and Myles Montgomery). It's safe to say that Jennings will earn that RB3 spot, although the depth chart doesn't reflect that just yet.
Maybe it's because he's a veteran and Eli Raridon is a rookie, but Dippre is certainly not the Patriots' second tight end right now. The second-year player missed most of training camp to this point while on the physically unable to perform list, and since he's returned, he's been repping mostly with the backups as a blocker.
On the other hand, Raridon has become one of the stars of camp . It doesn't matter if he's with the starting offense or with the backups, the Notre Dame rookie has become a reliable target in the passing game. Additionally, rookie Tanner Arkin has gotten a lot more reps than his "TE5" status suggests.
It hasn't been the strongest start to Lomu's first training camp, but the tackle has gotten plenty of reps to learn. Whether it's been on the left side or the right, the Utah rookie has been moved around a lot throughout the offense.
Despite that, he's consistently repped as the second right tackle behind Morgan Moses in team drills. Sure, second-year Marcus Bryant got a few more of those reps this week, but Lomu has been a constant name etched into the second-string offense. Having him as the RT3 doesn't match how much playing time he's been getting to this point in time.
The Patriots struggled at the kick returner position last year, and it's led to plenty of competition this summer. Jennings, Miller, Larison, Efton Chism III, Kobe Prentice and Channing Canada have all gotten time returning kicks. So has Williams (who returned some last season), who was up first in Tuesday's joint practice.
Right now, if it was up to me, I'd assign the top kick returning duties to both Jennings and Chism III. Both of those players have lived up to expectations on both offense and special teams, and have popped when given the chance to run with the ball in their hands. Williams' speed is a plus, but Jennings has looked smoother returning kicks.

title: Five Bold Predictions for Patriots Preseason: Does Drake Maye Struggle?
full_text:
The New England Patriots have just one day left before their 2026 preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday. They won't have a padded practice, but will have one final walkthrough ahead of their first organized football game since Super Bowl LX.
Of course, the final scores won't matter, and most fans in attendance will forget about which players stood out 10 years from now. But now is a better time than ever to make some bold predictions about how the Patriots' three-game preseason will go.
So what do I think might happen over the next month? Here's a few things that could potentially happen in Patriots land, including a major contract that finally -- finally -- gets settled.
This one feels far-fetched, especially when you consider the fact that he might not play more than a drive or two total. But Maye has looked solid in training camp that it can't be this good, right?
Here are Maye's numbers in the five preseason games he's played in: 28-for-46, 250 passing yards, one passing touchdown, nine rush attempts, 48 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns, two sacks, four fumbles, one fumble lost. Overall, not the worst set of stats.
Really, the bar of "struggling" for Maye is very low. He's locked into the starting job and if he maybe sails a few easy throws, that could fit the description of struggling. For me, it feels like these next few games will give the 23-year-old a chance to try some things out.
Maybe test a throw you wouldn't make in the regular season. Try to evade pressure a bit longer. Be a bit dramatic. Maye's abilities on the field aren't a question, but maybe he'll be risky in what he wants to work on in his brief time on the field (again, if he even plays).
Every year, there's always a player or two on the offensive side of the ball that makes a lasting summer memory. That player can easily be wide receiver Cameron Dorner, the North Texas rookie who has come along as one of the top UDFAs on the roster this summer.
He's been a consistent target for rookie quarterback Behren Morton on the third-string offense and could easily play himself into a practice squad spot by the end of the month. Dorner has looked smooth in his route running in practice and it wouldn't be a shock if that translates to the game field.
Patriots fans have fallen in love with the underdog that pops in the preseason. Austin Carr, Ralph Webb, Danny Etling, Gunner Olszewski, Efton Chism III. The list goes on and on. A touchdown (or two) could etch Dorner's name into that illustrious list.
Jacas' training camp debut as the Illinois rookie was sidelined without a contract. Now that he's been on the field and working with the starting defense, his talents have shown New England why he was selected in the second round.
In a room with depth issues off the edge, Jacas could easily be a player the Patriots decide to limit in the preseason -- especially when you want to consider the knee procedure he had over the offseason. But the speed that he's shown is exactly what you'd want in a pass rusher.
He knocked down outside linebackers coach Mike Smith in a positional rep earlier in the summer with a lot of force. Once he straps the pads on and hits someone else, he could be putting opposing quarterbacks into the ground instead of his coach.
The Patriots' secondary is in a bit of a tight spot right now, considering Christian Gonzalez's contract negotiations and Carlton Davis' nagging hamstring ailment. Obviously, both of those players wouldn't be playing in the preseason anyway, but it's going to put more pressure on some of the younger defensive backs in that room.
And it feels like that pressure could create a diamond moment. The Patriots secondary, after starting the summer slow in the turnover department, has slowly turned that around. I see that transferring onto the field in the next three weeks, and the Patriots end up snagging an interception before taking it to the house.
It might be rookie Channing Canada. It might be rookie Kenneth Harris. It might be rookie Peter Manuma. It might be second-year John Saunders Jr. (who has two picks in camp so far). Regardless, I see the Patriots taking an interception the other way for the first time since Jamie Collins took one 43 yards against the New Orleans Saints in 2016.
Finally. At some point this summer, the cornerback will agree to terms with his long-awaited contract extension. To this point, he's been a full participant in every padded practice. But once the Colts came along for joint practices , he was absent.
It was reported that he missed the day to deal with a minor ankle injury suffered the day before, but it's certainly nice timing that another team came to town. Ultimately, the Patriots can't go into the regular season without a happy Gonzalez and a contract will need to get hammered out at some point.
Maybe it happens this week. Maybe right before the final preseason game against the Cleveland Browns. Regardless, I predict that Gonzalez heads into Week 1 with some heavier pockets.

title: The Biggest Decision the Patriots Must Make Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
FOXBORO --- In less than two days, the New England Patriots will have to play their first preseason game of the summer. They just finished their joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts and will now have a closed walkthrough before the game.
But now the Patriots' coaching staff has an important decision to make, and it's one that coaches across the league can sometimes struggle with around this time in the NFL schedule. How much, if at all, should they play their starters?
We know with certainty not to expect Drake Maye out there. Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke to reporters before the joint practice , and all, but confirmed it.
"I wouldn’t anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday, but that’s all subject to change," Vrabel said before Tuesday's practice. "That’s where my mindset is right now, standing here today. It’s important that we get the work in and get things accomplished that we are looking to get accomplished. That can always change, but I wouldn’t anticipate that happening right now."
So we know that against Indianapolis, the quarterbacks will likely be a mix of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Who'll start that game is unclear, even to the players. DeVito told reporters that he doesn't have a clue what the plan is right now.
"I think about my rookie year, I was told that morning how much I was playing in the game," DeVito said. "I'll just prepare like I'm gonna play the whole game and then whenever they tell you whatever you do, that's how it is."
But the quarterback position isn't really the one in dire need of confirmation. The Patriots have to figure out what to do with the rest of their roster . Most teams will try to get their starters, at least most of them, some snaps during the summer to get them back into the swing of things.
Veterans, like tight end Hunter Henry, defensive tackle Milton Williams and wide receiver A.J. Brown, should get some time on the field at some point in the next three weeks. But how many snaps is the question.
Other times, the Patriots have let their youngsters play for quite a long time. Last year, undrafted wideout Efton Chism III fought his way onto the roster because he wasn't able to be taken off the field. He scored touchdowns in each of the first two games he played in, and was given that long leash as a rookie.
It's just knowing what buttons to push at the right time. For Vrabel, it's looking like this week's battle against the Colts will be more about the depth pieces than trying to get the veterans adjusted to game speed.
"That’s really the only reason that we do these joint practices," Vrabel said when asked about using joint practices to evaluate players who won't play in games. "It will be a lot of the frontline players and whoever’s available. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work today will get extensive work in the game on Thursday.
"That’s just how it goes. So, let’s see how today goes, and we can always adjust and plan accordingly."
In New England's practice, some longer-tenured guys got heavy workloads. Brown led the team with five catches . Henry had four and worked with both the first and second offensive units. Linebacker Robert Spillane was on the field for quite a while.
However, there are some players that fall right into the middle of the depth chart that could be interesting choices. Does Kindle Vildor, the free agent cornerback who replaced Christian Gonzalez Tuesday, get rest because of a lack of depth or playing time because he's not promised a spot. The same goes for the depth offensive linemen who might be in roster limbo right now (Dametrious Crownover, Andrew Rupcich, James Hudson).
That's not to say that the Patriots won't give their stars some reps during the preseason (keep an eye on next week's joint practice/game with the Philadelphia Eagles).
But the team needs to figure out the line between resting valuable players in non-valuable games, and keeping their players ready for the regular season.

title: Winners From Patriots Joint Practice vs. Colts: A.J. Brown Remains Top Target
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots walked off the practice fields in lock step with the Indianapolis Colts after their joint practice. Both sides looked solid moving the ball, and some Patriots made their mark known during 1-on-1 and team drills.
But which Patriots stood out among the rest?
For the first time all training camp, the Patriots were able to line up and hit another team. Here's the players that rose to the challenge Tuesday.
The Patriots certainly don't need a new starting quarterback, but DeVito has been making strides as the second-in-command. He's taken full control of the second-string offense and continued to look the part against the Colts.
He went 2-for-6 in 7s and 11-for-16 in 11s, with several long throws being the highlights of the day. His 50-yard touchdown to Mack Hollins on the first play of his two-minute drill was just the cherry on top for an already-impressive summer.
"He continues to learn, and with it being a new system, I think it got his attention a little bit better, as opposed to saying, 'Hey, I know what this is,' and kind of taking it for granted," head coach Mike Vrabel said pre-practice. "I think he’s really done a nice job."
Brown remained the No. 1 option for the Patriots' passing attack . It started off with a win over Sauce Gardner in 1-on-1s, a play that led Sauce Gardner to hop on social media and write about it in a now-deleted post .
Once the teams began full squad reps, Brown was finding the ball early and often. Working in tandem with Drake Maye, Brown led the Patriots with five receptions. One of those would have been good for a 10-yard touchdown, an in-breaking route where he slipped through two defenders near the goal line.
Just one day removed from signing a two-year extension to stay with the Patriots , Henry was a constant factor on the field. Not just with the starters -- where he'll be all season -- but with the second unit as well.
Maye's first two completions of the day were to Henry, one of them a 25-yard catch and run down the right seam. Later in the practice, he spent time with the backups, catching two passes (and a touchdown) from DeVito. It was a fantastic joint practice for the player who was excited about facing a new team.
"It’s the first time we’re a full team. We’re all going to wear the same color and cheer on each other in a way instead of going against each other," Henry said Monday. "It’s always fun to have those battles throughout camp and all of a sudden just kind of come together as a team and try to build that."
Ponder remained with the top defense, and it's starting to stick that the second-year edge rusher belongs in the NFL . He recorded an impressive batted down ball at the line of scrimmage, leaping in the air to make contact, before eventually recording a would-be strip sack later in the practice.
Vrabel said before practice that veteran Harold Landry is still working his way back from a knee injury suffered last year, so until he returns to the field, it's looking like Ponder has played his way into the starting lineup for Week 1.
But how could Gonzalez be a winner? He didn't even appear at practice! Considering how depleted the Patriots' secondary was without Gonzalez and Carlton Davis (limited, hamstring) on the field, it just was more evidence that the 24-year-old deserves a new extension .
The Patriots rolled out Kindle Vildor, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada with the first-string defense -- who have each looked good at points in camp -- but it just wasn't a good fit. The Colts' offensive weapons, including Josh Downs and Tyler Warren, were running wild during team drills.
"Everybody's expected to be able to come in and compete at the highest level that they're able to compete against," safety Dell Pettus said after practice on missing Gonzalez. "We love having Gonzo out here, and if he's just not able to go for whatever reason it is that day, whoever comes in next is supposed to come in and be held at the same as level as he is."
The final play of practice helped leave a good taste in the mouths of Patriots fans. With Riley Leonard and the Colts driving on a two-minute drill, the pass across the middle got deflected near the 10-yard line. Saunders, the second-year safety fighting for a spot on the team, was in the right place at the right time to nab the interception (his second of training camp).
"John, he keeps getting better," Pettus said on Saunders. "He's always been a playmaker when it comes to getting his hands on the football. He just continues to grow."

title: Everything We Know About Patriots' QB Plan for Preseason Opener
full_text:
FOXBORO --- We now have a better idea of who to expect to see at quarterback when the New England Patriots host the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday evening.
After working against the Colts' starting defense throughout Tuesday's joint practice, Drake Maye is not expected to play in the Patriots' preseason opener.
“I wouldn’t anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday, but that’s all subject to change," Mike Vrabel said prior to practice on Tuesday. "That’s where my mindset is right now, standing here today. It’s important that we get the work in and get things accomplished that we are looking to get accomplished.
"That can always change, but I wouldn’t anticipate that happening right now.”
Vrabel also mentioned the importance of the work from joint practices, as each team's starters get to face each other for an extended period of time. In a preseason matchup, the reps would be more limited.
Maye being out on Thursday would open the door for Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton to split time on Thursday. However, DeVito has yet to be told what his workload will be.
"I have no clue," DeVito said when asked about his role against the Colts. "I think about my rookie year, I was told that morning how much I was playing in the game, I'll just prepare like I'm gonna play the whole game and then whenever they tell you whatever you do, that's how it is."
Maye not playing on Thursday would be a shift from the Patriots' preseason plan a year ago, but would closely resemble Vrabel's preseason tendencies from when he was the head coach of the Tennessee Titans.
Last year, Maye started in the preseason opener against the Commanders and stayed in through two drives. Backup Joshua Dobbs played the next four drives, up until the end of the first half. Undrafted free agent Ben Wooldridge came in after halftime and finished the game.
However, last year's preseason opener was also the first-ever opportunity for Vrabel's coaching staff to work with Maye in a game setting. Now, with a year under their belts working with each other, Maye's expected inactivity on Thursday would follow a trend set by Vrabel in Tennessee.
Starting quarterback Ryan Tannehill did not play in the preseason opener during any of Vrabel's final three years with the Titans -- after the NFL shifted to a three-game preseason slate. As Maye continued to grow in the Patriots' system, Vrabel anticipates him getting that same treatment as Tannehill this Thursday.

title: Patriots, Colts Joint Practice Notebook: Backup QB Goes Deep, Nearly a Fight
full_text:
FOXBORO --- For the last few practices, it's clear that the New England Patriots were getting tired of hitting each other . They finally got the opportunity to hit another team Tuesday, as the Indianapolis Colts came to town for a one-day joint practice.
It was a good day of work, with both sides getting plenty of reps on each of the two fields next to Gillette Stadium. It also gave us highlights for both sides on offense. The passing attacks looked good and it gave the fans in attendance a lot to cheer about.
Here's what stood out from the Patriots' 14th training camp session of the summer, including how one backup quarterback continues to launch the football through the stars.
The Patriots got some good news on the defensive front, seeing defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Charles Woods return to the field. Barmore, who had missed the last two practices, was a limited participant and didn't partake in any team drills. Neither did cornerback Carlton Davis, who was working his way back from a hamstring injury.
Wide receiver Kyle Dixon, cornerback Christian Gonzalez, safety Mike Brown and long snapper Julian Ashby were all absent, as were edge rusher Harold Landry (PUP) and safety Brenden Schooler (NFI).
Gonzalez's absence was not surprising. As he continues to work his way through contract negotiations, the player so willing to play in pads with his teammates was not spotted during today.
There were some really good moments from New England's two quarterbacks (Behren Morton didn't take a team snap). Drake Maye went 4-for-6 in 7s and 15-for-23 in 11s. He looked sharp across the middle, and did have a nice scramble out of pressure, but his day ended with a tough interception to Colts safety Camryn Bynum. He was looking in the direction of DeMario Douglas in the end zone, but an underthrown ball allowed Bynum to leap up and pick it off.
Backup Tommy DeVito aired the ball out all morning. He finished the day going 2-for-6 in 7s and 11-for-16 in 11s. DeVito had the confidence to launch some passes, including touchdowns to Mack Hollins and Eli Raridon. He's continued to be one of the biggest risers throughout camp.
For the receivers, A.J. Brown (five catches), Hunter Henry (four), Raridon (four) and Hollins (three) all had nice days. Hollins was on the receiving end of a 50-yard touchdown from DeVito -- where he pretended to spike the ball through the goalposts after burning the Colts secondary. It looked like DeVito connected with Raridon on the ensuing two-point conversion.
The practice began with 1-on-1s between New England's receivers and Indianapolis' defensive backs. Everyone's favorite drill of training camp started off with a bang: Brown vs. Sauce Gardner. The route, a quick comeback on the outside, was won by Brown after the cornerback slipped and the Patriots fans erupted.
Here you go (via @PatriotsCLNS ): pic.twitter.com/aDNGYx0IcF https://t.co/0sLZqMd8h8
It was the only rep between the two stars, with Garner taking to social media after practice to write "all this from a 1on1 rep? & a 8 yard sit route at that? its a reason that's the only one yall saw."
Other winners including wide receivers Kobe Prentice, Efton Chism III and Cameron Dorner, each with a pair of wins. For the Colts, Josh Downs beat Marcus Jones (who was flagged for holding) and began jawing at the Patriots cornerback after the play.
Henry's four catches were the second-most on the entire team , and those came with both the first- and second-string offenses. Henry caught his first two passes of the day in 11s, connecting with Maye down the seam for the practice's first chunk play.
He also got several snaps with the backups, hooking up with DeVito for a pair of grabs, including a touchdown in the back of the end zone.
For both sides, it felt like the offenses had the better results. Yes, there were two interceptions thrown (Bynum's on Maye, and Patriots safety John Saunders Jr. picked off Riley Leonard on the day's final snap), but overall, the offenses won the day.
New England's run defense and pass defense had cracks, both for different reasons. The Colts ran behind Jonathan Taylor for a lot of their 11s plays, putting pressure on a Barmore-less defensive front. In the passing game, Kindle Vildor, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada got extended look as starters, which didn't go too well for the Patriots.
There was some nice plays, including pass breakups from Bradyn Swinson, Elijah Ponder and Marcellas Dial . Ponder also added a strip-sack during 11s, one of the biggest plays of the day for the Patriots.
The Patriots have been very disciplined during the start of camp, but there was a clear message drilled into them from the coaching staff.
"Obviously, there’s going to be some pushing and shoving," head coach Mike Vrabel said prior to practice. "If you throw a punch, you just have to head over and run hills or do something with Frank (Piraino) and his crew because that’s what is going to happen in the football game, and I don’t anticipate that happening."
There was almost a fight, however. On a special teams drill, Colts defensive end Durell Nchami was in the middle of a little skirmish. It didn't seem like any Patriots players were escorted off the field, but edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins and Dre'Mont Jones both appeared in the middle of the pile. Nchami spent the rest of practice walking with a member of the Colts staff witih his helmet off.
"It's different, but it all goes back to how we want to play as a team, man, and how we want to do things. We can't worry about how they practice or how they run their plays or whatever. We gotta stick to our details." - defensive tackle Milton Williams on maintaining structure in a less-structured practice.
The Patriots will have a walkthrough tomorrow that is closed to both the public and the media. In the meantime, the team will host an official ribbon-cutting event for the recently-built New Balance Athletics Center at 2 p.m.
On Thursday, the Patriots will host the Colts for their first preseason game of the summer. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. from Gillette Stadium.

title: Patriots Keeping Their Options Open When It Comes To Caleb Lomu
full_text:
FOXBORO --- Caleb Lomu played left tackle in college . He's been asked to play both left and right tackle with the New England Patriots. He's also been mentioned as a player who could play guard.
The Patriots have kept their options open when it comes to their first round pick.
Lomu was at right tackle for most of training camp to this point , working with the second-string offense and sometimes replacing Morgan Moses in the starting offense. For the Patriots' scrimmage on Friday and practice on Monday, he was back on the left side. It was clear he's more comfortable on that side, but it's still a work in progress to nail down both positions.
"It's been good being able to learn both sides of the line just to understand the playbook a little bit more," Lomu told reporters after the team's 13th practice of the summer. "It's a little bit difficult at first. It's different footwork, different hand placement, going the opposite way on plays and from one side, but it's been helping me a lot.
"Being able to get more playing time and just understanding the playbook a lot more."
It's been an up-and-down summer for the Utah rookie . Sometimes, he's struggled in 1-on-1s and got beat almost immediately. Other times, like Monday, he was a perfect 3-0 against some of the Patriots' quickest edge rushers.
The Patriots haven't officially penciled him in to either side for the preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts this week, but it wouldn't come as a surprise to see him get snaps at both spots.
"It's throwing with a different hand, kicking with a different foot," Lomu continued. "But then, it's just, you know, playing tackle - the position I've played my whole life. So a few kicks, few practices after that starts to feel a little bit more comfortable."
So Lomu is getting comfortable at the tackle position, but what about guard? The Patriots' depth at guard is thinning out, as the team recently traded away Caedan Wallace and might need to rely on veterans Ben Brown/Andrew Rupcich to hold down the fort as backups.
The Patriots haven't ruled out the possibility of moving Lomu to guard, maybe not full time, but for a brief time to get his feet wet there.
"I mean, I think that there's — whether we have injuries or things, but I think that guys are working in there," Mike Vrabel said on Aug. 4. "James (Hudson) is getting some reps inside there, and there will be a time where you guys will see Caleb work in there. So, we're just looking to find the best combination of guys for the season."
Lomu's start to his rookie season hasn't been ideal from a pure win/loss standpoint. Sure, he's getting his reps, but it's not always the best result. According to Lomu, that's actually the best kind of beginning .
"Everyone that is out on this field belongs to be here. And so, I’m not going to win every rep, and I know that," Lomu said. "I’m either winning, or I’m learning. And so those reps that I don’t win all the time. I’m learning from that. What did I do to lose that rep?
"And whatever I did, just don’t do that again. But I know I’m not going to win every rep. And so especially in the one-on-ones, it’s a place to try different things and to try different techniques that you use."

title: Three Things To Watch When Patriots Host Colts For Joint Practice
full_text:
On Tuesday morning, the New England Patriots welcome the Indianapolis Colts to town for a joint practice. With the two team's starters likely to get more work against each other than they will in Thursday evening's preseason matchup, here are the four biggest things to watch during practice.
The Patriots made two splash moves at the receiver position this offseason, signing former Packer Romeo Doubs to a four-year $68 million contract and trading for A.J. Brown from the Eagles.
While Maye and Brown struggled to connect on the first few days of camp prior to full pads coming on, their chemistry has taken a significant leap since then. While Doubs' camp has not been at the same level as Brown's, he has shown some flashes, including an over-the-head catch on Christian Gonzalez on Monday.
. @DrakeMaye2 to Romeo art 🎨🖼️ pic.twitter.com/cabmp7sAeW
In a competitive practice with a new team coming into town, can Maye's momentum with Brown and Doubs continue to build, or will the Colts' defensive backs give the Patriots' newest offensive weapons a reality check?
Indianapolis has one of the league's best running backs in Jonathan Taylor, whom was recently rewarded with a two-year $44 million contract extension. The three-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in rushing touchdowns (18) last season, while tacking on just under 2,000 all purpose yards.
Throughout training camp, New England has experimented with three linebacker sets which puts Chad Muma in with starters Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss. While Muma was a key defensive contributor at the beginning of his career with the Jaguars, he spent last year primarily as a specialist with the Colts and Patriots.
Now slated to have a significant role in Zak Kuhr's defense, how comfortable will Muma look on Tuesday against one of the NFL's best rushing offenses?
On a similar note, undrafted free agent Khalil Jacobs seems to currently control the Patriots' fourth linebacker spot. If he plays any snaps against Indianapolis' starters, keep an eye out on how comfortable the 22-year-old looks out on the field.
While the Patriots' defensive line has gotten the better of the offense in camp, Tuesday will provide a true benchmark of where the two sides stand.
The Colts' offensive line, headlined by six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, tied for the seventh-fewest sacks allowed in the NFL last season with 29. For perspective, the Patriots' 48 sacks allowed was tied for the ninth-most.
With Indianapolis coming to town, New England's front four -- headlined by Milton Williams and Christian Barmore -- get a worthy challenger to compete in a good-on-good matchup.
On the other side, the Colts' defensive line should provide a similar challenge for the Patriots' offense. Veterans DeForest Buckner, Arden Key and Grover Stewart, plus 2024 first-round pick Laiatu Latu, have each solidified themselves as key contributors in the NFL.
On both sides of the ball, if the Patriots are able to hold their own in the trenches against an impressive Colts team, it could be a sign of a bright 2026 season in New England.

title: Saints Make Final Preparations Before Jaguars Joint Practice
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had their final light day of practice before the Jacksonville Jaguars duke it out with the Saints on Airline Drive Thursday in a joint practice ahead of Saturday’s session.
The Saints had a light practice, as they were just in helmets. It was not a walkthrough, as there were two 11-on-11 periods and a goal-line period as well, but there was hardly any physicality. It was essentially two-hand touch and the play was over.
That is in part because of the joint practice happening tomorrow with the Jaguars. A lot of the starters will be participating in those collaborative sessions. Due to that, head coach Kellen Moore said to expect mostly the twos and threes to play on Saturday.
Here are some notes from everything I observed.
Nothing has changed since yesterday, but Devaughn Vele was the most notable absentee. However, Moore stated that Vele was healthy and was only taking a rest day. Vele was a starter in the slot for the Saints in the first unofficial depth chart they released next season.
Davon Godchaux (ankle) and Rejzohn Wright (hip) remained out after leaving practice early with trainers Tuesday. Kendre Miller (back), Devin Neal (hamstring), Cam Jordan (hamstring), defensive lineman John Ridgeway (back) and linebacker Chris Rumph (ankle) also were not seen.
These are in addition to defensive end Bryan Breese and offensive lineman Dillon Radunz being placed on the Injured/Reserved (IR) list. Both are out for the year .
The Saints added free agent defensive lineman Kahlil Saunders in the wake of placing Radunz on IR.
Saints sign DT Kahlil Saunders #Saints | @Shift4 https://t.co/hQ4ViGFrCz
In Vele’s absence, Kevin Austin Jr. took reps with the first team and Barion Brown rotated in as well.
William Sherman and rookie Jeremiah Wright played left guard and right guard for one team series with the first-team offense.
On defense, defensive tackle Khristian Boyd took reps with the first team while Godchaux took a break.
Linebacker Pete Werner was back as the starter alongside Kaden Elliss after missing yesterday. Werner was suited up, but he was on the sideline resting a groin injury. How much he will participate in the joint practice with the Jaguars is to be determined.
If Werner is a no-go, Danny Stutsman will take his place. Stutsman has been one of the breakout stars of training camp and has been pushing Werner for the starting position.
Jaylan Ford also took a few reps with the first team linebackers as well.
Despite a shorter practice than usual, there were still some highlights.
Cornerback I saac Yiadom made a great play in the first 11-on-11 session. Spencer Rattler threw a deep ball to Bryce Lance , and it looked like he was about to make the catch of the day, but Yiadom forced the ball out for an incomplete pass.
However, Lance made up for it when he hauled in a deep touchdown pass from Rattler in double coverage in the end zone. Lance has been better than expected throughout training camp and should be a lock on the 53-man roster.

title: 4 Major Takeaways from the Saints Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints dropped its unofficial depth chart for the 2026 season, giving Saints fans a look of how the roster is taking part.
There were few notable surprises given that most of the starters returned from last season and the fact that most anticipated what the depth chart looks like right now. However, depth charts change all the time, and some players currently listed may not even be on the team by the end of the month, given that NFL teams are mandated to select 53 players on their final roster by 6 p.m. ET Aug. 30.
Without further ado, here are four notable things from the Saints’ unofficial depth chart for the 2026 preseason.
With Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson locking up the starting spots on the outside, there were a lot of questions surrounding who was going to be the third receiver in the starting rotation. With the depth chart being released, that question has been answered as Devaughn Vele was listed as the No. 3 wide receiver in the rotation.
Vele had modest numbers last season with 25 catches for 293 yards and two touchdowns. However, he was a reliable target for Shough in the second half of the season, catching 26 passes for 238 yards and a touchdown in his final four games before missing the last three due to injury.
While Barion Brown did not make the starting rotation, he will definitely be a factor in the offense as well as special teams.
His performance in training camp so far likely has him as the fourth wide receiver in the rotation after Olave, Tyson and Vele. An All-American return specialist at both Kentucky and LSU, Brown is the No. 1 returner for both kickoffs and punts.
As expected, Travis Etienne and Alvin Kamara are listed as the first team backs. While it does have an “OR” in between the two tailbacks, expect Etienne to get a few more carries than Kamara. While the latter still has some of the things that made him a five-time Pro Bowler, Etienne is a little bit younger and is still in his prime as he is coming off his third 1,00 -yard season in four years.
Another interesting development from the depth chart in the running back room is Kendre Miller and Devin Neal being above Audric Estime.
Estime took first team reps alongside Etienne and Kamara while Miller (back) and Neal (hamstring) were out with day-to-day injuries. Estime took a majority of the snaps in the final two games rushing 35 times for 157 yards (4.5 yards per carry) for 157 yards and a touchdown.
While it was a given, everyone knows that Cam Jordan’s time is coming to an end and everyone who is part of Who Dat Nation wants to enjoy it while it lasts. But it is surprising that there is an “OR” next to his name in the same way that Chase Young, who is coming off a 10-sack season. So did Jordan, but Young is significantly younger than he and is on a longer and heftier contract.
Jordan is limping through a hamstring injury right now that will sideline him. For how long? Read our story here .
Vernon Broughton , Davon Godchaux and Nathan Shepherd are the starters on the inside. Broughton has shot up the depth chart after playing only one game last season.
One of the more noteworthy position battles has been for the starting kicker job between Charlie Smyth and Tanner Brown. Both kicked during Tuesday’s practice.
Smyth finished 5 of 6, with his one miss wide as he pushed it left from 55 yards on his last attempt. Meanwhile, Brown made all seven of his attempts, including the 55-yard attempt Smyth failed to convert.
According to NewOrleans.Football , Smyth is 27 of 35 (77.1%) throughout training camp, while Brown is 28 of 32 (87.5%).

title: Could the Saints be without Cam Jordan to Start the Season?
full_text:
New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan may not suit up for the beginning of the season due to a lingering hamstring issue.
Jordan's injury occurred during Thursday's practice, and he has missed the past three practice sessions. He did not attend Saturday's practice because he attended Drew Brees' Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement .
Head coach Kellen Moore said "he's going to miss a little bit of time," noting that regular assessments will dictate the recovery process. Moore did not say when the eight-time Pro Bowler would return, but the injury was serious enough to have Moore admit that Jordan could remain sidelined beyond the preseason slate.
"It could possibly get into the season, but you never know," Moore said. "[You need] to have some patience with it, let it take its course and we'll collect more information as we go."
Jordan, who has been in the league since 2011, has played in all but two games oin his career. In 2022, he sat out for a Week 11 matchup following an orbital fracture, and previously, he was sidelined for a single game in 2021 after testing positive for COVID-19.
The 37-year-old edge rusher signed a one-year contract to return to New Orleans for a 16th season on June 16th.  Jordan's deal has a base value of $7.5 million ($6.15 million signing bonus, $1.35 million base) and is worth up to $11 million with sack incentives.
Replacing a veteran like Jordan is difficult; he is the roster's most tenured player and led the team with 10.5 sacks last season. However, they do have options on the edge, and great ones at that.
The Saints feature veteran pass rushers in Chase Young (10 sacks) and Carl Granderson (6 sacks) on the defensive line. New Orleans also bolstered its roster by trading for Tyree Wilson during the draft and signing former New England Patriots defensive end Anfernee Jennings in April.
"We certainly feel good about our depth in that position. We got some really talented players on the edge. We view it as a strength of our football team," Moore said. "We're going to need multiple guys to play throughout the season no matter what. ... So we'll take time to kind of evaluate while Cam's out and see where it looks here through training camp and then these other guys will be ready to go."

title: Saints Defense Dominates Again as Offensive Mistakes Pile Up Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints were back on Airline Drive on Tuesday as they continued preparing for their first preseason game of the season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday.
The defense continued to dominate the offense, which is commonplace at any level during the preseason. However, the situational mistakes have continued and, to make matters worse, most of the day focused on late-game situations.
Here are some of the takeaways from today’s practice.
On the first team offense, nothing necessarily changed.
Tyler Shough was the starter at quarterback, a position he had held since the second half of last season. Spencer Rattler took reps with the second team while Zach Wilson took snaps with the third.
At running back, Trevor Etienne and Alvin Kamara both took reps with the first team. Audric Estime also took reps with the first team as Moore wanted him take reps there as well.
In the receiving corps, Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson were the starters on the outside while Devaughn Vele was the starter in the slot. The second team consisted of the rookie duo of Barrion Brown and Bryce Lance , along with veteran Kevin Austin Jr.
At tight end, both Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant both rotated with the first team. Rookie Oscar Delp took reps with the second.
On the offensive line, it was the usual with Kelvin Banks and Taliese Fuaga starting at left and right tackle, David Edwards and Cesar Ruiz at left and right guard with Erik McCoy at center.
On the defensive line, Carl Granderson and Chase Young were the starters on the edge while Vernon Broughton and Nathan Shepherd were the No. 1 guys on the interior.
At linebacker, veteran Kaden Elliss was starting alongside Danny Stutsman . The latter has been slowly but surely locking up the starting role over longtime mainstay Peter Werner.
In the defensive backfield, nothing changed. Just like in the past couple of practices, Quincy Riley and Kool-Aid McKinstry were on the outside while Justin Reid and Jonas Sanker manned the safety positions.
Defensive tackle Davon Godchaux was off to the side after rolling an ankle, and Rezjohn Wright hurt his hip during Tuesday's practice.
Other than that , defensive end Cam Jordan was not available again at practice today because of a hamstring injury.
Defensive lineman John Ridgeway III i s dealing with a back issue and remains day to day.
Second-year running back Devin Neal was still off to the side doing rehab work for a hamstring issue and is day to day as well.
Pete Werner (groin) was back in uniform but did not appear to participate in any full-team drills.
The Saints’ strongest position group may be the defensive backfield with the amount of depth it has.
We saw that today with Martin Emerson Jr. The fifth-year cornerback out of Mississippi State had three pass breakups and an interception on the day. He should have had two if he had hauled one in during the second 11-on-11 session.
Carl Granderson made several big plays as he gave right tackle Taliese Fuaga all he could handle off the edge. Granderson was constantly forced pressure off the edge. He also had a presence in the passing game as he had an interception and nearly had another as well on the play right before it.
There were several plays stood out throughout the day.
Austin made several catches throughout the day, including a 25-yard touchdown catch on a nice ball from Rattler.
While it might of been a mixed day for him, Shough made some nice throws as well.
One that stood out was when he spiraled a touchdown throw on 4th down in the red zone to Johnson on a fade route in the back of the end zone over tight coverage from McKinstry to end the second session of 11-on-11 in a quasi two-minute drill.
He also made a nice play later in practice where he used his feet to escape pressure and found Tyson in the middle for a first down.
Riley snagged an interception from Shough to end the main practice session.
Shough was 15-for-27 and threw two interceptions on the day. Despite a rough start to practice, Rattler was 7-for-9, but he also threw an interception. Wilson was 9-for-15 (60%) and did not turn the ball over, but also did not necessarily do anything to separate himself from Rattler.
However, the most concerning thing about the offensive struggles is the lack of situational awareness, something that has been a recurring issue.
The most egregious one came when the offense faced third-and-2 with 14 seconds remaining during a full-field hurry-up drive and committed a costly false start. Shough bailed his offensive line out by converting a fourth-and-1 with a touchdown to Johnson.
However, Johnson committed another false start on the first play with just under 45 seconds on the clock in another 11-on-11 session.
The good thing for the Saints is that its just the preseason and these things can be ironed out before the season starts.
