title: Jets Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times and TV Channels
full_text:
The New York Jets are just days away from beginning their preseason slate, meaning it will only be a matter of time before head coach Aaron Glenn and his staff finalize the 53-man roster. Until then, every player on the roster bubble must capitalize on each chance given to them between now and the Aug. 30 deadline, with the preseason being the biggest opportunity to garner goodwill.
The upcoming exhibition slate will be the first crack for Jets rookies and veterans alike to give the fan base a sense of optimism ahead of the regular season. For those wanting to get in on the action, here's everything to know about the Jets' preseason, including the dates and how to watch each game.
After engaging in back-to-back joint practices on Tuesday and Wednesday, the Jets will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the preseason opener at MetLife Stadium. Things will be even more interesting after multiple fights broke out at the first co-practice.
Glenn & Co. will be out for revenge after falling 29-27 to the Bucs in Week 3 last season. New York made a strong comeback effort despite trailing by as many as 17 points; however, a 36-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin as time expired crushed a lot of dreams that afternoon.
It remains to be seen who will be suiting up here, as well as how much they'll play, but Friday's clash will be a good chance for the Jets to test their offseason additions. Whether that's David Bailey— who's been crushing it throughout training camp —or a new veteran arrival like Minkah Fitzpatrick, New York fans will have plenty of reasons to tune in, regardless of the outcome.
The Jets' lone road preseason game will take place in the Steel City. All eyes will be on Mike McCarthy as he prepares for his first year as the Steelers' head coach, giving the Jets every reason to play spoiler on the road and sow some seeds of doubt. Considering how New York is 3-3 in its last six matchups against Pittsburgh, anything is possible.
The Jets also have added motivation stemming from a 34-32 loss to the Steelers in the 2025 season opener. It was a back-and-forth contest that ended on a low note. Much like the loss to the Bucs, the Jets saw their lead over the Steelers evaporate when Chris Boswell connected on a massive 60-yard field goal , giving Pittsburgh the lead with 1:03 remaining on the clock.
Glenn & Co. will also be closer to finalizing the 53-man roster at this point, meaning we'll likely see fewer lineup regulars and more bubble players in the mix. Either way, a win over the Steelers would provide some much-needed confidence ahead of the preseason finale.
As is a preseason tradition, the Jets and Giants will duke it out at MetLife Stadium at the end of the month. The Jets lost by 19 points when they collided last summer, but also notched a 10-6 win over the Giants in their last instance as the "home team" back in 2024.
Nevertheless, given that the two New York teams combined for seven wins last year, it's safe to say that both will want to end the preseason on a high note.
The 53-man roster deadline is only two days after this collision, adding to the pressure that all the players involved will feel. Most roster spots will be decided by then, meaning it'll be crucial for each active Jet to give it their all. Otherwise, they might quickly find themselves on the unemployment line, with it not being guaranteed that another team will come calling.

title: Early Geno Smith Concerns Could Leave the Door Wide Open for Jets QB Controversy
full_text:
As training camp moves along and the start of the preseason quickly inches closer , the quarterback room remains a major focal point for the Jets ahead of the 2026 season.
While projected starter Geno Smith spoke out about the multiple speeding violations and a domestic dispute with an ex-girlfriend that was ultimately closed, that does not change the distraction-filled offseason he has endured. Now, the focus has shifted to his up-and-down performance on the field and the confidence that he needs to instill as QB1.
Smith started off training camp showing why he is a massive upgrade under center for the Jets with his accurate passing and smart decision-making, but it didn't last long. His turnover-prone history has always been a cause for concern and a risk the Jets knew they were taking when they acquired him in a trade with the Raiders earlier in the offseason.
On Tuesday, there was some good and bad from Smith as the team took part in a joint practice with the Buccaneers. According to ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini, Smith " was sharper toward the end, in the red zone , but still not a great practice." He finished 10-of-16 with two interceptions, two touchdowns and a couple of sacks.
Geno Smith was sharper toward the end, in the red zone, but still not a great practice. Had him at 10-for-16, with two INTs, two TDs and a couple of sacks. Offense a little of sync. Good day, though, for TEs Ruckert and Taylor. Isaiah Williams making his move. https://t.co/cTN1BX98yL
Despite the history of turnovers and Tuesday's uneven showing, coaches have made it clear how confident they are in their veteran signal-caller. That said, rookie QB Cade Klubnik has played well over the offseason and could lead to Jets fans wanting a switch early in the season, especially if the turnover woes persist for Smith.
While the offense has struggled to get on the same page at points during training camp, Smith brings his leadership and gives the Jets the experience they have been lacking under center. After all, this was an offense that scored the fourth-fewest points per game (17.6 ppg) and one that has utilized at least three different starting QBs in four of the last five seasons, so his return to the organization was welcomed by coaches and teammates.
Throw in his early statement at training camp under new offensive coordinator Frank Reich's scheme and a plethora of weapons down the field, and it is hard to see him not being the starter under center for at least the majority of the season, if not the entire 2026 campaign. With that said, Smith has thrown nearly as many interceptions (32) as TDs (40) the last two seasons, so there is at least an opening for someone with the upside that Klubnik brings to pose a challenge.
Klubnik has certainly looked like a rookie QB at times throughout the offseason, but the joint practices with the Buccaneers will provide an excellent test for him to show that the flashes can continue to outweigh the mistakes. For the most part, though, Klubnik has been one of the biggest winners of training camp so far with his decision-making, arm talent and accuracy.
In other words, Klubnik has outshined Bailey Zappe and Brady Cook for the QB2 role and should be in the driver's seat to serve as Smith's backup. Now into the third week of training camp, the Jets have to feel better about their backup QB role as Klubnik continues to live up to the hype and put himself in position to learn from the veteran Smith as he develops more confidence and familiarity with the offense.
While the coaches continue to support Smith and put the offense's trust in his control, the turnover-prone history is still hard to ignore, and it would not be the worst thing for a talented rookie like Klubnik to earn some more trust from fans for the starting position.
This appears to be Smith's job to lose for the 2026 season. Rightfully so for a team that could really use some stability at QB, but fans could easily run out of patience with him in the early going if the turnovers become an issue and the option is there to turn to Klubnik.
As much trust as Smith has earned so far with the Jets, this is a team that still needs to take that next step and show that it can win more games with the talent it has put together. If Smith does not make a statement out of the gate and the Jets are back in a familiar position, it may not take long for fans to lose trust and want a switch under center.

title: 4 Winners & 3 Losers From Jets' 1st Joint Practice with Buccaneers: David Bailey Keeps Shining
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. — It's time to separate the men from the boys. The Jets, after weeks of competing against themselves , got the opportunity this week to battle against another NFL foe. While the Buccaneers are not on the 2026 schedule, their pedigree gave the Jets a chance to show just how much they have improved .
Joint practices are always a delicate balance. Fans want their team to play well during the week of buildup, but understand that it's normally not a clear indicator of future success.
Jets fans will be hoping that remains the case, as the Buccaneers appeared to "win" the day with a fiery start to practice that included four separate fights on different fields. While New York did manage to make things competitive later on, it felt like a day Tampa Bay will be confident in winning as opposed to the latter.
As always, there were plenty of winners and losers throughout the day. Let's go to each one now.
It was obvious from the first snap. David Bailey was the Jets' best player on either side of the field today. In one-on-ones, he completely embarrassed Buccaneers tackle Luke Goedeke to the point where the young tackle false-started on the final two plays of the drill. After getting an early jump on the last rep, Goedeke tried to smack talk Bailey, who promptly threw a punch and started a brawl.
Excellent fire and speed, but the Jets would like to see more discipline from their second overall pick (more on that later).
In team drills, Bailey was just as dominant, picking up multiple sacks, including one against Tampa's starters where he orchestrated an excellent rip move and would have tackled Baker Mayfield within two seconds of the snap coming to him.
David Bailey would have just recorded a sack in team drills. Oh man what a move 👀👀 #Jets
Jets fans have never seen a player show this much of an impact in his first-ever training camp. If Bailey can put this together come Week 1, we could be looking at the next great superstar edge rusher.
Let's start with the positives. First, Geno Smith's red-zone period remains his strength, as he threw two touchdowns in the period. Cade Klubnik was also quite solid, albeit with some missed throws as well. New York's quarterback room salvaged the day at the end.
But it doesn't take away from the poor start.
Isaiah Williams finds himself wide open for a deep completion. Geno found him despite pressure. Next play is picked off with Geno going across his body. Just ugly day for Geno #Jets
In a two-drill sequence, Smith failed to complete any pass beyond five yards and was picked off twice, including one that would have gone for a touchdown. Much of New York's offensive struggles stemmed from the defensive blitz disguises that Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles used throughout practice. It was a good lesson to learn from in that case.
But it does not take away from the fact that the Jets' offense stumbled through most of practice. And a big reason for that was Smith's inaccurate throws and poor decision-making.
Tuesday was the best day of training camp for second-year tight end Mason Taylor. He also came through with his best catch. On the first play of a red zone drill, Taylor lept up into the air and caught a deep pass across his body. It was a difficult catch for any receiver to make. But Taylor made it.
That's the kind of play the Jets will need from Taylor going forward, especially with Kenyon Sadiq in workout clothes as he recovers from hernia surgery .
More importantly, Taylor lived over the middle of the field and caught several passes on the day with large completions. Without any drops, the LSU product showed why he is a key cog in the Jets' passing offense today.
Over the last few seasons, it appeared that the Jets struggled mightily with discipline. This year might be the same, and the several fights showed why. Whether it was Armand Membou checking a Buccaneers edge rusher after a play, or Bailey throwing a punch after winning a rep, the Jets need their best players on the field at all times if they are going to be better than last year.
Yet another fight: Membou and A’Shawn Robinson. Membou had his helmet ripped off and took umbrage. And that triggered a melee. #Jets
Fighting won't help anyone. In Membou's case, he watched from the sidelines at the end of practice due to his last fight. New York cannot afford to lose him, and today was a good reminder of that.
Add in several false start penalties and holding calls and the Jets still have a long way to go here.
Mayfield found plenty of wins on the day while attacking zone coverage. What he struggled with was throwing one-on-one, especially against Brandon Stephens. In his second year as the starting corner in New York's secondary, Stephens made multiple good plays in coverage throughout the day.
His best came in a team session and a one-on-one deep shot to Chris Godwin. Mayfield's pass was on the money, but Stephens stepped up in a major way to come through with an excellent deflection. It was the kind of play that showed his improvement from last year.
The Jets are going to have two main problems this season on defense if Tuesday's practice is any indicator of the future. First, New York's aggressive nature with their edge rushers will leave them susceptible to screen passes. Tampa Bay saw plenty of big offensive plays thanks to that very concept.
Second is their four-man front. The Jets built their defense with the unofficial goal of turning more to a 3-4 alignment. In doing so, though, the team also showed its desire to run with four-man fronts. Throughout the last week, the four-man fronts have been gashed against the run, just as they were today.
New York's defensive line is going to be better than last year. But it will be a challenge if they can't win with four down linemen and need five to do so. It's something to look out for going forward.
Before practice, Jets receiver coach Shawn Jefferson turned heads when he called Isaiah Williams the "heartbeat" of the offense. Normally, that title should befall the likes of Garrett Wilson or Smith. Instead, Williams showed exactly why today.
He wasn't perfect. Williams dropped a touchdown pass in the red zone late. But throughout the day, he seemed to be the only one willing to mix things up against the Buccaneers' defense, which had toyed with the Jets' offense.
In one run play, Williams decked a Buccaneers linebacker while blocking. On the next play, Williams made a catch and came up jawing at the opposition.
It's good to have those types of players on the roster. It's even better that Williams continues to show his mettle every time he touches the ball.

title: 3 Most Important Jets to Watch in Friday's Preseason Opener: Cade Klubnik's NFL Debut
full_text:
It’s been over seven months since we’ve seen the Jets, and that streak ends on Friday with the team taking on the Buccaneers at MetLife Stadium after a week of joint practices .
Although it’ll be exciting to see Gang Green finally play a somewhat meaningful game, fans shouldn’t expect to see any of the star or marquee players suit up. If they do, it’ll only be for a drive or two.
Instead, we should expect the Jets' coaching staff to use this game to deploy players in a position battle or at the back end of the depth chart. These additional reps provide the coaching staff with an opportunity to evaluate the players and the strengths of each position group.
With that being said, here are three Jets’ players to keep an eye on against the Bucs.
Cade Klubnik is coming off an impressive week in training camp, which he capped off with a 60-yard completion to Isaiah Williams in last Saturday’s scrimmage . Overall, the 2026 fourth-round pick has had a solid camp and is in a strong position to obtain the QB2 role, especially as his success continued against the Buccaneers on Tuesday , per Jets OnSI 's Nick Faria.
Taking a look across the field, #Jets secondary has held their own as Cade Klubnik delivered a nice throw to Ruckert for a deep completion. Good stuff from the rookie.
However, camp play alone won’t secure him the job. Klubnik must stand out in preseason play to increase his chances of earning the backup spot and convince the organization not to add another quarterback to the group.
Although general manager Darren Mougey didn’t indicate that he’s bringing in another quarterback, he was asked about potentially adding a veteran to the room before the start of training camp. Mougey responded that he’s always checking the market for players at all positions.
If Klubnik wants to shut down talks about potentially bolstering the quarterback room, he must protect the football and prove he's capable of moving the offense downfield.
Entering training camp, Chip Trayanum wasn’t considered a candidate to earn a roster spot. Despite this, the Jets’ unofficial depth chart lists him as the RB3 alongside Isaiah Davis and ahead of Kene Nwangwu.
Of course, this list should be taken with a grain of salt given that it was compiled by the team’s communication staff rather than the coaching staff. But with Davis sidelined for the next couple of weeks with a knee injury, Traynaum has a chance to make a strong impression .
Traynaum’s bruising, down-hill running style makes him an intriguing player to watch against Tampa Bay. If he can pick up tough yards after contact and secure the football, he could put himself in a position to earn a spot on the practice squad.
Another surprise from New York’s unofficial depth chart list is Tyler Baron being on the fourth team behind Kingsley Jonathan and Nathan Voorhis.
Baron is already considered a long shot to make the final 53-man roster, but his listing on the depth chart shows that he has a lot of ground to make up. Despite this, he displayed some potential last season, recording four pressures in 48 pass-rush snaps , per Pro Football Focus.
Against the Buccaneers, Baron must showcase his development as both a pass-rusher and run-defender as he competes for a roster spot in a crowded edge rush room. New York ranked amongst the worst teams in both categories last year, and if Baron can prove to be an effective contributor in either area, it could significantly improve his chances of making the roster.
But if he fails to capitalize, don’t be surprised if Baron ends up being a cut candidate by the end of August.

title: One Jet Whose Offseason Struggles Shouldn't Worry Fans
full_text:
As the Jets head into the third week of training camp and prepare for their first preseason game against the Buccaneers on Friday, the 2026 roster will begin to take shape even more as players get a chance to impress on the field against some different competition.
Someone who impressed last season and is one of the most important players on this team is defensive end Will McDonald IV, who led the Jets with eight sacks in 2025 and excels as a pass rusher. He acknowledged that he needs to improve against the run, an area the Jets were the fourth-worst group in last season, but there have been some causes for concern regarding his quiet offseason play so far.
That said, there are a few reasons why concerns regarding McDonald's offseason are overblown.
McDonald has since bulked up as he tries to improve against the run and is athletic for his position. He still needs to show more at training camp after what has been a silent performance so far, but the 15th overall selection in 2023 is the only player on the team the last two seasons to record more than six sacks, and his explosiveness has made him difficult for opposing teams to slow down.
Additionally, second overall draft pick David Bailey has been one of the biggest winners of training camp so far, and the early buzz surrounding him is certainly warranted as the hype continues to explode . That alone has created some additional pressure and only amplified the silent showing that McDonald has had thus far.
Both Bailey and McDonald have similar strengths and weaknesses, excelling against the pass while still trying to improve and make some gains against the run. Of the eight sacks that McDonald registered last season, four of them came against the Cleveland Browns, so it is imperative that he becomes more of an every-down player and not just someone who can come in and have a big performance before taking a step back.
With that said, McDonald is credited with 18.5 of the Jets' 68 sacks the last two seasons, so there is a good chance he replicates that success once again . For a team that had the second-fewest sacks (26) in the league in 2025, that level of pressure from McDonald cannot be ignored, even if he has not boasted Pro Bowl-caliber numbers and is lacking some of the big plays you would expect from a former first-rounder.
After all, Pro Football Focus gave McDonald the 37th-ranked pass-rush grade (71.0) out of 115 qualified edge defenders last season. Granted, his overall grade (59.2) was just 85th, and his run-defense grade (41.6) was a dismal 112th, but he still brings some explosiveness and athleticism to a unit that has depended on him to be a constant disruptor on the edge.
At the same time, the 2026 season will be a critical one for McDonald as the Jets decide if he is worth keeping around in the long haul . The Jets brought in free-agent acquisitions Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare, with both possessing better skills as run defenders. Enagbare, specifically, is already making a strong impact against the pass.
Throw in the fact that McDonald only played 57.48% of the Jets' total defensive snaps in 2025, and it is even clearer that he needs to step up as a more reliable down-to-down defender—especially with the increased competition he is facing at the position now.
Even with that in mind, McDonald has shown to be the type of sack artist the Jets have lacked as a whole recently. Sure, he still needs to develop into more of an all-around edge defender the team can feel comfortable with alongside Bailey, but he has become one of the most valuable components of the Jets' pass rush and should not be doubted yet despite a silent outing in training camp.

title: Eagles Training Camp Notebook: How Jalen Carter Lost 10 Pounds this Summer
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Jalen Carter stood smiling after going through a nearly two-hour practice in the South Philly heat and humidity on Tuesday. The Eagles defensive tackle was asked a few times about his weight, which he said, his down 10 pounds from last year.
As he answered questions, he patted his stomach, saying, “I like juice. I might drink some juice, but I had to slow down. Mostly it’s all water and juice in here. I just slowed down. Mostly being just once a day, twice. But small portions, not Big Daddy meals.”
Having a weight clause in his recently signed contract extension has helped. It a clause that will allow him to make another $250,000 each year by staying at or below his mandated weight, with Spotrac data indicating Carter will have five weigh-ins a year with a $50,000 bonus each time he passes them.
It’s not so much about the money, though. It’s more about defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.
“Me and Vic had a little thing going where he wanted me to come in at a certain amount of weight, and I made that weight,” said Carter. We had a little bet. It was all fun and games. All principles and stuff like that. It was just coming in with a mindset.
“That also shows that the contract wasn’t my biggest focus. My biggest focus was putting a smile on Coach Vic’s face coming in at my weight. He was happy. We dapped up. We hugged. We’re doing good. We’re just working every day.”
A handful of days after Lane Johnson announced that this would “probably” be his final season, reaction inside the building is trickling in.
Landon Dickerson: “I've been very fortunate to play a lot of years with Lane, and I hate to see him go. I mean, it's honestly been a pleasure to play with a guy like that. You learn a ton on and off the field from somebody that's been in this game and just at the level he's played and super excited to watch him go in the Eagles Hall of Fame and then in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.”
Jalen Hurts: “Lane is a special player. He’s had a very special career and to get to know him and for him to immerse himself into my career and me developing ever since I walked into Philly, working out together, the time we spent together, I take pride in those things. I want to make sure it’s a special year for him. I know it takes great courage to say this is the last dance going into it, so I’m hoping he gets everything he desires out of this year.”
Nick Sirianni: “We want to support Lane in that, and he's a phenomenal football player. One of the best guys I've ever been around and, in my opinion, the best offensive lineman in the NFL. So glad he's here and just thinking about every day. I can't say enough good things about Lane, but you don't think about those things until - I don't think about those things until later on and just happy he's here and out at practice and contributing to our football team.”
Cam Jurgens’ surgically repaired back from last offseason passed a major test when he went one-on-one with the powerful Jordan Davis earlier this week and won both reps. That’s a good sign.
Drew Kendall looks like the top backup on the interior of the offensive line. A solid center at Boston College for four years, the second-year fourth-round pick is getting the hang of playing guard and looks like he will be the No. 1 backup option at either guard or center should disaster strike one of the starters.
Fangio isn’t known to sugarcoat anything, so it was interesting to hear his answer when asked about what he has seen from Riq Woolen since the pads have come on.
“At times he can get a little lazy or sloppy with his technique and have a bad down or two, but he's still showing everything that I think he can do,” said the DC. “He's just got to get in such great shape and calloused to football that those don't happen.”

title: Four Moves I Would Make If I Was Eagles GM Howie Roseman: WR Becomes Top Priority
full_text:
Ten practices are in for the Philadelphia Eagles, enough of a sample size to learn what areas where the team needs to be addressed.
Those answers aren't as obvious as they were prior to training camp. The Eagles actually have good interior offensive line depth, which didn't appear to be the case heading into camp. This is the cause and effect of drafting and developing.
Other areas of the roster need to be addressed , which is what we're going to do if we were Howie Roseman. This is the blueprint for Roseman for the rest of camp (not like he needs one), but more of a guideline.
What is Roseman thinking -- and how will he fix it?
Some Eagles fans are trying to convince themselves the wide receiver group is better than it was last seaosn. That was never going to be the case .
A team doesn't trade a top-5 wide receiver in A.J. Brown and improves at the position. That's crazy talk.
Don't be fooled. The Eagles aren't better at wide receiver.
The Eagles were banking on Makai Lemon to be an immediate contributor. That isn't going to happen since hamstring injuries have kept Lemon off the field. He just hasn't gotten the reps needed in this offense to be the WR3, although Lemon could significantly contribute later this year.
What the Eagles should do is add veteran receiver help to ease Lemon in, allowing him more time to catch up. DeVonta Smith is the WR1 and Dontayvion Wicks is the WR2, but it remains to be seen who will be the WR3.
Darius Cooper is making his case to play, but going from a WR5 to starter is a tall task. Perhaps Hollywood Brown gets out of his funk and becomes a contributor (instead of a cut candidate) or Elijah Moore can fill the void for a few weeks (assuming he makes the team).
If I told you Wicks was going to be the WR2 and Cooper the WR3 in June, many would be on red alert for a wide receiver. This is a move -- free agent or trade -- the Eagles may need to make.
Find a WR3 or WR4 to help out this team until Lemon is ready. The Eagles definitely aren't better at wide receiver. You're lying to yourself if you believe that.
The Eagles could improve in a few areas on their roster. They don't have to weaken depth at one position to strengthen another -- so no player-for-player swaps.
This includes Byron Young, who is one of a few players that has had a strong camp and should have more playing time this year (even as the No. 4 defensive tackle). The Eagles have tremendous depth at the position with Young and should keep him around -- instead of pulling a Thomas Booker and trading a starting-caliber player for a position they could improve upon.
The same goes for any of the wide receivers the Eagles don't keep. They need depth at that position, even if the wide receiver doesn't play much. Basically, don't trade Elijah Moore for a late round pick.
Fred Johnson is a cut candidate, but it would be hard to trade him too. There's just no depth behind him at tackle -- even if Johnson loses the No. 3 tackle job to Markel Bell.
Bryon Young and Michael Carter are on the "do not trade" list. For the record, I don't think the Eagles will trade either. I wouldn't trade Nolan Smith either -- at least this year.
I don't care how old Brandon Graham is. He should be back on this team for one final season -- even at 38.
The Eagles aren't asking Graham to be a major contributor to the pass rush. They have Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa at pass rusher currently.
Here's why Graham should be back. Jonathan Greenard is on the PUP list and the Eagles aren't likely to see him for a few weeks. There are questions whether Greenard will be ready for Week 1 , which is a month away.
Why rush Greenard back when you don't have to? An easy way to accomplish this is to bring Graham back next week, as Graham wanted to come back sometime in camp to get in football shape. Graham can get ready for the year and provide added insurance as a No. 5 pass rusher.
The Eagles can also move Graham inside as added depth at defensive tackle behind the top four. Why not bring him back for one more year?
This isn't a desperation move, but a move to buy Greenard more time and carry Graham as an extra defensive lineman the entire year. If Graham wants to come back, why not let him go one more season.
I'm perfectly fine if the Eagles decided to roll with Marcus Epps or Michael Carter at safety. Both players have been fine this training camp and can get the job done on the back end.
If Epps or Carter win the job, the Eagles can survive. With that being said, there's room to improve.
The Eagles spend just over $8 million on the safety position, the lowest amount in the NFL. There isn't depth behind Epps or Carter, even with either starting next to Andrew Mukuba.
Could the Eagles use a No. 4 safety? Absolutely, but I wouldn't mind giving Andre Sam or Maximus Pulley a chance. I don't think they go that route.
A starting safety could still be in play here, and the Eagles shouldn't have too much troble finding one if they get creative. Perhaps converting a cornerback into a safety again -- or maybe that player is Carter?
This isn't a priority by any stretch, but it helps on the back end with the pass rush the Eagles are going to have.

title: Six Eagles With Soaring Stock Who Flipped Depth Charts At Training Camp
full_text:
Ten practices and two weeks of training camp have been completed for the Philadelphia Eagles. Several players have gotten off to hot starts this summer , enough where they are becoming the breakout stars for the Eagles.
These players are taking over the depth chart conversation , and earning their way onto the 53-man roster. While some of these players may not make it, they have definitely made it difficult for the Eagles to cut.
Behold, the Eagles who have soared their stock over the last two weeks. All these players are worth paying extra attention to this preseason.
Cooper has been the story of camp. All the former undrafted free agent from Tarleton State has done is make plays, becoming the most trusted receiver in camp when he's on the field.
Not only is Cooper making tough catches over the middle, he's becoming a threat in the red zone. That may be Cooper's role in the offense this season, as he's elevating into the WR4 on this team -- and maybe even a bigger role .
The Eagles found a gem in Cooper last summer, and took a shot on him with a 53-man roster spot. That gamble has clearly paid off. Not bad for a player that was signed for $90,000 with a $15,000 signing bonus just 16 months ago.
Moore was a known name in NFL circles, but struggled to find his footing in recent years. He only had nine catches for 118 yards last season, one year after having 61 catches (only averaging 8.8 yards per catch).
A change of scenery and fresh start was what Moore needed, even if he was a roster long shot. That's not the case after 10 practices, as Moore has flashed with his crisp route running and creating yards after the catch.
Moore is in contention with Hollywood Brown for the fifth wide receiver spot, and he deserves it based on his play. This preseason will be a big one.
The Eagles were looking for one of these young linemen to emerge into the No. 3 guard spot. That player is Kendall, who is the top backup option behind Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen.
Kendall has performed well with the first team offense and continues to improve in 1-on-1s. He's also the top option to back up Cam Jurgens at center too, offering position versatility on the interior of the offensive line.
There's still competition for that job, but the top option is most likely Kendall.
One of the camp darlings this summer, Lampkin played his way from a roster unknown into prime position to land a 53-man roster spot. The Eagles deserve a lot of credit for developing Lampkin, whose blocking and punishing defensive tackles stands out on film .
Lampkin is in the mix for the spot on the second team at guard, and can also play center. If Lampkin makes the team, he won't play much this season -- but adds much needed depth on the interior of the offensive line.
This is the player to watch this preseason.
Carter went from batting for a roster spot to a roster lock, based on how the safety competition is going. He's a legitimate threat to Marcus Epps for the starting safety job, and can win the spot next to Andrew Mukuba.
Not only is Carter transitioning to safety well, he also can play slot cornerback and basically occupies two roster spots in the secondary. That's important in Vic Fangio's defense.
Wouldn't be surprising if Carter starts come Week 1. He may rethink the Eagles looking to add a safety this summer.
The cornerback position is basically set, but McWilliams is challenging Kelee Ringo for that final spot. Philadelphia basically has six cornerbacks if Carter is included in that mix (since he can move down from safety if needed), so McWilliams would have to beat out Ringo for a job.
McWilliams has shown flashes in camp and has held his own against receivers. He had a slow start to camp, but has picked up his coverage as of late.
This preseason will be massive for McWilliams. Eli Ricks once made the Eagles based on one strong preseason game, so maybe McWilliams can do the same.

title: Why Eagles Are Leaning Heavily Into Ground Game This Training Camp
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles leaned heavily into the ground game during Tuesday’s training camp practice at the Jefferson Health Training Complex, an impactful session that featured plenty of pistol looks and under-center work.
Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley all looked effective to the naked eye in the running game, with Barkley and Bigsby, particularly, breaking off several nice runs.
Without live tackling to the ground, though, evaluating those gains presents a unique challenge—one the offensive line approaches with precision through extensive daily film study.
Left guard Landon Dickerson explained exactly how the unit assesses the running game in that non-contact environment.
“I mean, we watch the film,” Dickerson said. “We evaluate every play. We do that every single day. And we go through, and it’s really making sure that is your alignment, assignment, technique correct? Do you have good hat placement? Is everybody blocked up? Did we point it right?"
If all that aligns the rep is generally going to be graded well, according to Dickerson.
“From there it’s it’s kind of easy to tell, right? If we have guys all doing their assignment, everybody’s got, the right alignment, their hat placement in the right place, and there’s a gap for the running back, then it was probably a good play,” Dickerson explained.
In a practice setting where plays are often blown dead early and defenders aren't wrapping up, yards gained on the field provide limited insight.
Instead, coaches and players have to break down each rep for the fundamentals: proper pre-snap alignment, correct individual assignments, sound technique, and especially the hat placement Dickerson spoke of. The angle and positioning of a lineman’s helmet helps control the defender and create or seal a running lane.
When those details become checked boxes and a clear gap appears for the back, the play is deemed a success regardless of how far the runner actually travels before the whistle.
Conversely, missed assignments, poor leverage, or clogged lanes stand out just as clearly on film and become teaching points for the next practice.
Tuesday’s emphasis on the run game fits the broader installation of the new offense under offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, which has featured more under-center and outside zone elements.
Barkley and Bigsby’s explosiveness continues to generate positive buzz as a potential one-two punch for the Eagles, while the offensive line works to refine the details that make those runs possible once live tackling begins in earnest.
The Eagles continue camp on Thursday this week ahead of their preseason opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday, a live environment where success or failure in the running game will be easier to see.

title: Why Joshua Weru Is Still 'Light Years Away' From Helping Eagles
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Vic Fangio is done talking about the two Eagles from the African continent . At least for now. As they develop, if they ever get to the point where they can be contributing pieces on his defense, he will. Right now, no.
“It's going to take a long while,” said the Eagles’ defensive coordinator. “You guys can get off that topic, they're light-years away.”
The topic? Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru.
Bernard is from Nigeria; Weru from Kenya. The two countries are not close, with Kenya on the east coast and Nigeria on the west coast, with a driving distance of 3,290 miles separating them.
They are in Philly now, trying to be football players. Weru was a rugby player. Bernard played basketball.
They got to know one another in October when they both turned up at the Loughborough Combine at Loughborough University in England to try to earn the right to be picked for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. They were, and they both landed in Philly after the draft.
Bernard has talked to reporters already.  Day 10 of training camp on Tuesday was Wehru’s first time in front of a phalanx of reporters and TV cameras.
So, Philly, meet Weru. Wehru meet Philly.
It’s a relationship that will take time to build and Wehru and Bernard are building it together.
“I knew he was a crazy athlete from that time (in England), so seeing how he’s developed and I’m sure him seeing how I’ve developed has been crazy,” said Wehru about Bernard. “And then also just having someone in the locker room who you know is going through the same things that you’re going through is just good to have.”
Weru, who is 22, has Jalyx Hunt in his corner, and that’s a good thing since Hunt is an outside linebacker, the position that Weru is learning to play. In Fangio’s scheme, that means he must learn how to rush the passer and cover when called on.
“That’s my guy,” said Hunt. “Josh is so cool. He’s really accepted his role as the guy who doesn’t know how to play football yet. He’s learning each day because this is his first time playing. So, it’s been real cool to be able to explain things that I might have learned when I started out earlier because he’s never been in these situations to know what it is, or what it’s not supposed to look like, or what you’re not supposed to be – like unspoken football rules, things like that.
“To be able to explain that has been cool. And he’s so humble, he’s confident in his abilities regardless of him not knowing the right moves to make all of the time. You can tell his effort and his detail and his want-to is always there … I really admire how he’s approaching it.”
Weru was attracted to football when he was 16 while attending boarding school in England and playing rugby. One of his favorite rugby players was Christian Wade, who was ultimately signed by the Buffalo Bills through the IPP.
“It was crazy because he played in the preseason and scored a touchdown, I think on his first or second drive, so I kind of watched that story and always knew I was athletic,” he said. “I kind of had it in the back of my mind, but I had rugby as an option.”
Weru and Bernard may see some playing time on Saturday night when the Eagles open the preseason against the Baltimore Ravens, though Fangio is being cautious with them.
“It's hard because there's a health part of that, too, where you don't want them in there against, say, your number one offense or even with your number one defense because you're never quite sure what's going to happen,” said the DC.
“I just feel really supported because I’ve talked to some other guys who I mean I’ve gone through the program with and just hearing stories about how training camp is for rookies for people who maybe aren’t in the first and second team and I’ve been lucky to get so many reps,” he said.
“And every rep I get, the more I see; I feel like the better I’m getting. So, I've been given that opportunity to actually develop, which I feel like many other places wouldn’t give me that opportunity.”

title: Eight Surprises Spotted On Eagles First Unofficial Depth Chart: Shocker at Backup RG
full_text:
The first unofficial depth chart by the Philadelphia Eagles is out.
The Eagles typically release their depth chart ahead of the each preseason and regular season game. The preseason depth chart is noteworthy given the position battles that are taking place in training camp.
This depth chart is compiled by the communications department, so take some things with a grain of salt. This isn't how the depth chart has looked throughout training camp practices, but it's an indicator of how things stand so far.
What takeaways can we examine from this depth chart? What are the surprises?
Take a look at the depth chart before it's broken down.
The #Eagles depth chart. pic.twitter.com/UXAbtXuuJQ
The surprise: Andy Dalton AND Tanner McKee
Evaluating Eagles depth charts for 10+ years, this isn't a surprise. List both competitors in alphabetical order and not list a leader.
McKee and Dalton have split second team reps all of training camp, but Dalton has the slight lead right now. Nick Sirianni won't reveal if the starters will play in the preseason opener, but who gets the first crack at QB2 is the storyline.
At this point, it could be McKee or Dalton. While Dalton is the leader in the clubhouse in the battle, who starts Saturday won't be known until pregame warmups.
Lemon has missed the past week of practice with a hamstring injury. He's been the sixth best wide receiver in camp and really didn't do much when he was healthy.
Darius Cooper has been better, and so has Elijah Moore. There's a case to be made Cooper is set for an elevated role in the offense, perhaps as a WR3. Moore is pushing for a roster spot too.
When Lemon gets back, he's expected to slide right in with the first team -- so this does make sense. Lemon may not be the instant contributor the Eagles thought, but he'll get the first crack in the slot (which is where he'll likely have the most success right away).
Bell and Fred Johnson have been battling for the No. 3 tackle spot all summer. Johnson got the first crack at right tackle, but quickly ceded to Bell -- who played well at right tackle.
The Eagles moved Johnson back to right tackle this week and Bell over to left tackle. The No. 3 tackle spot doesn't have to be revealed on the depth chart, but it's noticeable Bell is listed as the second team right tackle.
Bell may have the edge over Johnson.
The Eagles have been rotating at right guard throughout camp, with Micah Morris getting the early looks there before he suffered an injury last week. Morris is back, but he's listed on the third team.
Willie Lampkin is on the third team too, which is a surprise given how well he's played this summer. Wouldn't have been surprising to see Lampkin on the second team.
Drew Kendall is listed as the second team center, which has merit. Kendall is likely the No. 3 guard too, getting the first call to fill in for Landon Dickerson (LG) and Tyler Steen (RG). Michael Jordan is the second team LG.
Majors is still a surprise, even though he's had a good summer.
The surprise: Cooper DeJean
DeJean is listed as the starting safety on the Eagles defense . Not Marcus Epps nor Michael Carter.
There is soome truth to this, as DeJean is the starting safety in base defense. The Eagles only run base defense 20% of the time (at most), in which DeJean will be there.
Notice DeJean is the first team starting slot cornerback too, signaling how he'll be on the field at all times. When the Eagles are in base defense, DeJean is at safety. When the Eagles are in nickel, DeJean will be in the slot.
So who's the starting safety.
The surprise: Michael Carter AND Marcus Epps
Been evaluating Eagles' depth charts for over 10 years and this is a typical move (so this isn't a surprise to me).
The Eagles listed both Carter and Epps as the safeties, as there isn't a winner in the position battle yet. Epps has been getting more first team reps than Carter, but Carter is coming on strong in recent practices.
The Eagles can get by at safety with either Epps or Carter at starting safety in nickel packages. The depth behind them is troublesome, but the starters appear to be fine for a position the Eagles spend the fewest money in the NFL on.
The surprise: Michael Carter AND Mac McWilliams
Carter has been learning safety and cross raining in the slot. This is why he makes the roster outside of performance, as position versatility is crucial in Vic Fangio's scheme.
McWilliams has gotten first team opportunities with Jonathan Jones hurt (Jones is the top cornerback on the outside and in the slot behind the starters). he's held his own after a slow start to camp, and will get a long look this preseason.
There may be a roster spot for McWilliams, but he is a long shot.
Perhaps this isn't a surprise, given the safeties behind Epps and Carter haven't done much. Sam has bene the best of the bunch, but Maximus Pulley has made plays (the Eagles aren't going to have a rookie UDFA on the second team).
Sam is listed next to Carter AND Epps on the secodn team and has been around the Eagles for a few years. This is Sam's best chance to make the active roster.
Not a surprise Ojomo is listed as a first team defensive tackle, but more of a surprise the Eagles listed three firts team defensive tackle (Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter with Ojomo).
This shows how highly the Eagles think of Ojomo, a player who is going to be in the rotation with Carter and Davis. Ojomo isn't even listed on the second team, and the Eagles listed three defensive tackles on the second team (Ty Robinson, Byron Young, and Gabe Hall).
There's the puzzle that needs to be solved. Who is getting the No. 5 DT spot? Robinson or Hall?

title: Why Jalen Hurts Is Faster This Year -- And How Eagles QB Is Confusing His Defense
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Several times during training camp, Jalyx Hunt has chased after Jalen Hurts, forcing him out of the pocket and sending the Eagles quarterback fleeing to whatever open green grass he can find while continuing to scan the field.
It’s hard to tell if Hunt could have caught him because the quarterback wears a red jersey and can’t be touched. The outside linebacker is having a great camp, but Hunt may have had to find an extra gear to catch his QB because Hurts looks faster.
Maybe he is faster, though he denied it after Day 10 of camp on Tuesday.
“No, nothing specifically," Hurts said when asked if there was something he did this offseason differently to regain the explosion he seemed to lose last year when he appeared more bulked up. “I just went on my regimen as normal. … I feel good. I’ve always felt good. I don’t feel any different than I have in the past.”
Vic Fangio begs to differ. In fact, it was the defensive coordinator who volunteered that information about Hurts looking faster when asked before practice what he had noticed about the QB in the new offense.
“Jalen's having a good camp,” said the DC. “He looks faster. Obviously, we can't touch him during practice. There's always that debate whether you had him or not. There have been a few times where our guys think they had him and they really didn't. He's moving good and I think he's doing a nice job with the new offense.”
Ah, the new offense. It’s different, that’s for sure. It’s noticeable to all who have watched practices. More under center, more motion.
“A lot's been made about (Hurts), all these coordinators he's been with, but it's basically been the same offense every year,” said Fangio. “This is different. He's done a great job with it.”
And the man doing the chasing throughout camp, Hunt? What does he think?
“Yeah (he’s faster),” said Hunt. “The attention he pays to his body, and just his preparation for the season is second to none. He’s always trying to figure out the next thing, and the best things that he can do for himself. He looks fresh. He looks good moving. He looks confident back there, so I’m confident in him.”
Head coach Nick Sirianni has liked what he has seen from Hurts in the new offense, and each day it appears better.
“You're seeing it out there,” said Sirianni. “He's just doing a really good job. You can see how quickly he's getting through progressions and onto the next read with great footwork. Jalen's a very accurate passer, and you're seeing that continue to shine.
"Some of the new things [that he has to do] with different footwork, particularly under center. You're just seeing the growth of him daily within this offense and getting more and more comfortable, and you're seeing that on the field. Jalen's having a great camp, and look forward to continuing that.”

title: 5 Winners And 4 Losers from Day 10 of Eagles Training Camp: Jake Elliott Has Been Near Perfect
full_text:
Another day of Philadelphia Eagles training camp has passed. Another day some players shined and some disappointed.
There's starting to become a clearer picture of how this roster as shaped out, and who will be the players to watch this preseason. Tuesday's evaluations of practice and the overreactions said it al l.
With the Eagles having a walkthrough on Wednesday, who are the winners and losers from Day 10 of practice. This is a good indicator how how things are going for some players this summer.
Elijah Moore: The wins keep coming for Moore, and the stacking up of good practices. Moore is starting to show his deep-ball ability, as he connected on a 47-yard touchdown pass from Jalen Hurts that was arguably the play of the day in practice. Moore is making a push for a roster spot, and deserves the nod over Holywood Brown right now. Let's see how Moore plays this preseason, but there's a lot to like when it comes to his roster chances.
Jake Elliott: On a windy morning, Elliott shined when it was his turn to kick field goals. Elliott went 6-for-6 in practice, and improved to 25-of-26 this camp. That's why the Eagles didn't bring in competition for Elliott this summer, as they believed he would fix whatever physical and psychological issues he had. Elliott has been excellent kicking in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and needs to transfer that to NFL stadiums -- including his own this fall.
Micah Morris: Getting back on the field has been a plus for Morris, as the sixth-round rookie is starting to show his physicality. Hurts when a player misses time, especially when that unavailability allowed Willie Lampkin to pass Morris on the depth chart. The Eagles have been working Morris at left and right guard, and he's played well at both spots. There may be a roster spot for Morris after all.
Tyler Steen: The breakout player this year may be Steen, who had a solid year at right guard last season considering Cam Jurgens and Lane Johnson were injured. Steen has been consistent in 1-on-1s and had a victory over Jalen Carter on Tuesday (which isn't easy to do). The Eagles will go as far as the offensive line can take them and if Steen continues to improve, they may be the best unit in the league again.
Byron Young: Another good practice for Young, as he beat Drew Kendall and sacked Andy Dalton when the second team offense was out there. Kendall has had a good camp (and a good day on Tuesday), so this was a massive win for Young. There's a case to be made Young deserves more snaps this year, and he's earning them -- even as the No. 4 defensive tackle in a loaded position.
Cameron Williams: There isn't much depth at tackle behind Fred Johnson, and Williams proved it on Tuesday. Tarron Jackson was signed two days ago and easily beat Williams in 1-on-1s for a sack. No matter how you slice it, not a good look. Is Williams even going to be on the 53-man roster? Someone may have to be that fifth tackle, but Williams has not helped his chances. This is why it's hard to envision Johnson getting cut.
Will Shipley: The hits keep coming for Shipley, who hasn't been good through 10 practices . Running backs were working on blitz pickup on Tuesday, and Shipley was struggling in that department. Whether Shipley earns the RB3 job or not is up in the air, but he has to show something this preseason to prove he's worth keeping around. Elijah Mitchell is out of the competition after he was waived with an injury settlement and Dameon Pierce has been solid -- if not spectacular -- in camp. The job is still Shipley's to lose.
Tariq Woolen: The best player in Eagles minicamp this spring has been okay this summer. Woolen hasn't been great, but also hasn't impressed. He gets beat on a lot of moves in 1-on-1s and hasn't flashed in coverage. Woolen is still a starter and his evaluation will come starting Week 1. He just hasn't been as dominant as he was in the spring. Woolen will need to work on defending out routes through the rest of camp.
Hollywood Brown: Feels like every day Brown shows up here. He had a drop in 1-on-1s on Tuesday and the bad practices are stacking up. Darius Cooper has been great and Elijah Moore has been racking up good practices, which puts Brown on the bubble for a roster spot. Again, how did we get to his point? Brown needs a sharp preseason -- probably more than any player on this roster.

title: Overreactions From Day 10 of Eagles Training Camp: Eli Stowers Set For TE2 Role?
full_text:
Hard to believe, but the Philadelphia Eagles are through 10 training camp practices.
There have been plenty of developments over the first 10 practices open to the media, and practice 10 had no shortage of storylines. preparation and game tape come into play, a sthe Eagles get set to fac ethe Baltimore Ravens in Week 1 of the preseaosn Saturday night.
With this practice, a few observations came into play. Thanks to observations, we have overreactions.
Which overreactions are overreactions and which are reality?
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Stowers had a good practice on Tuesday, making a few strong catches and becoming a valuable red zone target in this offense. He's had a string of a few good practices , which is a massive improvement over the poor start to this camp.
Stowers isn't under the "losers" section of camp anymore . He has bene improving over the past week, enough where there should be some consideration for the TE2 role over Johnny Mundt. Is Stowers ready for that job?
If Stowers continues to improve and makes plays in the preseason, he'll get out of the disappointing rookie class. Stowers has shown a lot of positive gains in the past few practices, a very encouraging sign for the Eagles.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Moore had the highlight play of Tuesday's practice, catching a long touchdown pass from Jalen Hurts. This is the type of deep ball prowess the Eagles are seeking from one of the wideouts in their offense.
Every day, Moore is making a case to be on this roster. He should be on the 53 over Hollywood Brown if we stopped the count after 10 practices. Moore just keeps getting better and better as the practices wear on, even now he's catching deep passes in these sessions.
There's a lot to like about Moore, who runs smooth routes and has been making good catches when Hurts targets him. He could be the WR5 on this team, and he's also a veteran (like Brown).
If the choice right now is between Moore and Brown, Moore gets the nod.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Robinson has been another player that has had his fair share of criticism. He's had a slow start to this training camp and also found himself into the cut candidates section , but that may be changing.
Not only did Robinson have a sack on Tuesday, but he's been getting into the backfield of late. This is a positive development from a player who was stuck on the third team the majority of camp. Robinson still has a ways to go, but has this in his back pocket.
Being a fourth-round draft pick form last season buys you some time. Robinson is getting the benefit of the doubt here, and he'll likely make the roster if he shows enough improvements. Right now, that seems to be the case.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Boy did this blow up for no reason. DeJean was listed as the starting safety on the Eagles depth chart (which is complied by the communications department), but that is partially true.
DeJean is the starting safety in the base defense, which the Eagles run less than 20% of the time. He goes to the nickel defense, which the Eagles run over 80% of the time. When DeJena is in nickel, either Marcus Epps or Michael Carter are the starting safeties -- a battle that is still going on.
The depth chart is the depth chart, but the Eagles have DeJean in the slot for a reason. No need to overreact here.

title: Ranking Eagles WRs After 10 Training Camp Practices: How Close Is Elijah Moore To Bubble
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver battle has been one of the most intriguing ones of training camp. The WR2 battle was settled early, but so was the WR5.
There is another battle that emerged as a result of Darius Cooper playing well. Who is going to be the WR4? This battle will be settled over the preseason an din the next couple weeks.
After a week of practice, all the wide receivers on the roster were graded -- based on how they performed in training camp practice. This time, let's do wide receiver rankings with two weeks and 10 training camp practices in the books
Where does each wide receiver stand with Week 1 of the preseason this weekend?
The Eagles aren't going to rush DeVonta Smith back from a hamstring injury, and nor should they. They can Smith in bubble wrap until Week 1 at this rate, since he will be the WR1.
This passing game can't flow without Smith, and they need him in order to win football games. Smith is set to take his game to the next level, but the Eagles have to make sure he's 100% on September 13.
Wicks has taken the reins as the WR2, having a strong first week of practice. While Wicks has played well, Makai Lemon has been inured and Hollywood Brown has been underwhelming.
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is a fan of Wicks, comparing him to Keenan Allen on multiple occasions. All Wicks has done is run routes well and catch the football, becoming a trusted weapon in the offense.
The Eagles just have to see Wicks play in a game. That will come Week 1.
There's a argument that Cooper could be ranked higher than Wicks . Every practice Cooper has shined, emerging from a bubble player to essentially a roster lock.
Cooper is more than a WR5 in this offense. He could be the WR4 and maybe even a WR3. Thanks to Wicks and Cooer, the Eagles can take this slowly with Makai Lemon (which isn't the most ideal scenario).
If the Eagles are looking for a red zone target, Cooper may be the guy.
Moore has played his way to a roster afterthought on the roster bubble , maybe even a roster spot (pending on if he can beat out Hollywood Brown). The Eagles could use a slot receiver with makai Lemon on the mend, which is where Moore enters the picture.
Moore has typically been a good route runner, and a fresh start with the Eagles may have been what he needed. He's making it difficult for the Eagles to cut him.
Brown has been underwhelming in camp, getting outplayed by Cooper and Moore. He was a dark horse for the No. 2 spot in camp, but has fallen to competing for a roster spot . The Eagles have $5 million reasons to stick with Brown, and he'll get every opportunity this preseason.
The final roster spot may be between Brown and Moore. This preseason will be important for both wideouts.
Lemon has missed a week of practice, but even when he was practicing the rookie first-round pick wasn't standing out. Fair to state Lemon has been a disappointment so far .
Every practice Lemon misses, he does't get the opportunity to work with Jalen Hurts and the offense. The timing hasn't been there with Hurts because Lemon hasn't practiced and he has a lot of catching up to do.
Don't expect Lemon to be a major contributor in this offense come Week 1 at this rate.
Watkins still has the speed to make plays, but he's a long shot to make this roster. He has gotten open on some deep balls this camp, even if the results haven't been there.
Perhaps Watkins ends up on the practice squad again. He's adapted to the new offense.
The success in the spring hasn't translated in the summer. Cooper took the WR5 job from Wilson early, and Wilson hasn't been a threat for the job. He's unlikely to make the roster at this point, no matter how well he blocks.
Covey had a good start to training camp prior to a hamstring injury keeping him out for around a week. The best chance Covey has of making this roster is punt returner, but even that is a long shot.
Another player who could find a way onto this team as kick returner, Ezukanma has made a few nice plays in training camp. He's still considered a roster long shot.
The former seventh-round pick has made some nice catches in camp, even getting some looks with the second team due to all the injuries at wide receiver. Toure will get a lot of reps this preseason.
The former minicamp standout -- and third-round pick of the 49ers -- hasn't been noticeable this summer. He's another one that could improve his stock this preseason.

title: Steelers Reunite With Veteran LB Elandon Roberts
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are bolstering their inside linebacker room, signing free agent Elandon Roberts to a one-year deal, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
Roberts returns to Pittsburgh after a year away when he played for the Las Vegas Raiders. His return to the Steelers marks his third season with the team, playing in 33 games and 29 starts during his first two-year stretch. He recorded 147 tackles, 3.5 sacks, 15 tackles for loss and a forced fumble during those two seasons.
Reunion: veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts, who played in Pittsburgh during the 2023-2024 seasons, reached agreement today with the Steelers on a one-year deal, per source. pic.twitter.com/Zpg0I72ghQ
Roberts, 32, is entering his 11th season in the NFL. He played four with the New England Patriots and three with the Miami Dolphins before joining the Steelers for two years and spending the 2025 season with the Raiders.
For the Steelers, they add another run-stuffing linebacker to their room as they prepare for the regular season. Roberts now joins the mix with Patrick Queen, Payton Wilson, Cole Holcomb, Carson Bruener and Malik Harrison as players who could make the 53-man roster.
It may mean that one of those players gets cut, but right now, the Steelers have not yet announced a move alongside Roberts.
The Steelers are the perfect landing spot for Roberts, and he's the perfect addition for them. A true thumper who excels in the run game and can bring a ton of leadership back to Pittsburgh, Roberts fits a hole this team has carried all offseason.
There also shouldn't be much of a learning curve. Roberts spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons with the Steelers, working with players like Payton Wilson, Cam Heyward, T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and others. Then, in 2025, he worked in Patrick Graham's defense with the Raiders. So, he should already know the playbook and be able to aclimate well with the players around him.
There have been concerns about Pittsburgh's depth at the position since last season when Wilson and Queen struggled at times. Holcomb can hopefully fill more of a role this season, now being a full season back from his knee injury, but that's still unknown. And Harrison has seemingly fallen off from the defense.
Roberts should be working himself into the rotation pretty immediately, whether that be as a backup or starter. Right now, either is an option. And he'll almost certainly add a boost to a defense that has already looked good this training camp.

title: 5 Players With Most Riding On Steelers Preseason Opener
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers begin their preseason schedule with a familiar opponent. New head coach Mike McCarthy began his head coaching career with the Green Bay Packers, so it's only fitting that they face the Packers in his coaching debut with the Steelers.
It's a new chapter for the Steelers. They have a new man in charge, along with a brand new staff. They also have a brand new set of roster competitions and challenges to overcome.
Which leads us to five players who have the most to prove for the Steelers.
Everyone wants to see what the third-round pick can do, and Drew Allar is eager to get his first taste of NFL action. Coach McCarthy indicated that two quarterbacks would receive the bulk of the snaps, and the logical conclusion from that is that Allar will play the entirety of the second half.
If he impresses, the quarterback depth chart is instantly shaken up. If he struggles mightily, what will the response be?
Just like Allar, Will Howard should see significant time in the preseason opener. He's trying desperately to knock Mason Rudolph out of the backup quarterback role, and he needs to be excellent against the Packers to make his case.
The fact that Broderick Jones reported to training camp healthy and has been a full participant is one of the best surprises of the preseason. The neck injury he suffered in 2025 could have ended his career, but here he is, fighting for a roster spot.
Jones still has that positional versatility, something coach McCarthy has stressed as essential for any backup on the 53-man roster. He has to show that he's put in the work on his technique. Are his hands and feet working in tandem, or is he still a player who has unsteady hands to go along with an athletic lower-body? That will be put to the test in his first taste of preseason action.
The Steelers have a new defensive approach to the upcoming season, and that's thanks to new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. Part of that new approach, at least from their work in camp, is relying more on three outside linebackers. It's a smart move, as the team has T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig at the ready.
Where does that leave second-year edge rusher Jack Sawyer? He played well in short spells as a rookie, but does this year's team have the same plans for him? He can force his way into those plans with a dominating effort against the Packers.
For a seventh-round pick, Robert Spears-Jennings has been overly impressive from the start of training camp. With multiple starters receiving days off and working through various injuries, the former Oklahoma defender has risen to the occasion. Right now, he's slated to be the team's third safety, but that's a huge ask of a seventh-round rookie.
It won't feel like a huge risk, however, if Spears-Jennings can show how ready he is against Green Bay.

title: Aaron Rodgers Starts Prank War at Steelers Training Camp
full_text:
During the Pittsburgh Steelers' three-week stay in Latrobe for training camp this summer, it appears a prank war of sorts have broken out in the dorms.
While speaking with reporters a few days before the Steelers ' first game of the preseason against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium, Aaron Rodgers confirmed that pranks have occurred and that he was tagged as a potential culprit.
"There might've been a prank that happened in the dorms," Rodgers said. "I got the finger pointed at me immediately for some reason. Can't confirm or deny whether I was involved or not. Gotta keep guys on their toes for sure, it's part of the fun being out here in Latrobe."
Rodgers also issued a warning to his teammates, stating that he has unlimited resources at his disposal to go out and get back at someone if they decide to target him in a prank.
"People gotta be careful, because I do have unlimited resources to spend on pranks," Rodgers said. "We can have pranks back and forth, but just know that whatever you do to me, I'm gonna do something worse back to you."
Rodgers has previously spoken about his affinity for spending training camp at Saint Vincent College, which isn't necessarily a popular opinion amongst Steelers players.
“Mike [Tomlin] used to talk about a lot capturing that cannot be kind of quantified, and that’s what Latrobe gives,” Rodgers said. “The opportunity to spend time with each other at nighttime on the breaks, and you’re staying in a dorm, you know, sharing a bathroom and a shower with a teammate, and there’s some great team bonding opportunities for that and I just think it’s invaluable.”
With Rodgers speaking about the presence of pranks in the dorms a few days after Cam Heyward stated, "that's all he wants to do," it's clear the four-time MVP is enjoying himself as his last rodeo in the NFL is still in its beginning stages.
Coupled with the fact that Rodgers has reunited with his former Green Bay Packers head coach, Mike McCarthy, for one final run at a Lombardi Trophy after the pair won Super Bowl XLV over the Steelers in 2010, everything is lining up for a potentially happy ending to his illustrious career.
Rodgers has looked rather good throughout camp as well, and the 42-year-old holds the keys to the team's season as a whole. If he can come out and be just a little bit better than he was for Pittsburgh in 2025, there's a good chance the organization could finally snap its seven-game losing streak in the playoffs.
On the flip side, if Rodgers regresses and looks like a shell of himself, it won't matter how the rest of the team performs.
Everything on that front will sort itself out once the regular season arrives. For now, though, Rodgers is savoring his time in Latrobe.

title: Steelers Likely Lose First-Round Rookie in Preseason Opener
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One of the most exciting battles occurring at Pittsburgh Steelers training camp was the one between linemen Dylan Cook and Max Iheanachor to determine the starting right tackle.
That battle was quickly derailed when the Steelers' most recent first-round draft pick sustained an injury during the second week of camp. After a few days off, Iheanachor returned to the practice field at St. Vincent College wearing full pads and a helmet. He participated in a few reps of individual drills, but watched the rest of practice from the side.
Despite the positive sign, head coach Mike McCarthy cautioned that Iheanachor is not quite ready to make his team debut. Speaking to the media ahead of a recent practice, McCarthy clarified the injury situation. He's making progress, but he is likely out for the team's preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers.
"He's making progress," he said. "I do not see him playing Thursday night, but he's getting close."
Unlike the previous update from McCarthy, where he provided seemingly no new information, this one contained a bit more. He acknowledged that Iheanachor's participation in individual drills marks a progression in his rehab, but he's not cleared for full participation.
"He's just working his way back," McCarthy said. "Just like any return from injury, there's a strength component that we're trying to get over and there's some things we wanted to see with some pads and a helmet on."
It's not much, but it sheds a bit more light on the injury and where he's at. He's not 100%, but the stud tackle is very close. The fact that they were testing him in pads shows that he's closer to returning than not. The team has been cautious all training camp regarding injuries, and this seems to be another case of the organization protecting their players.
The team is hoping that the youngster can get some preseason reps as soon as possible. The competition between Cook and Iheanachor was one of the toughest and closest battles happening at Latrobe. Iheanachor had the edge before his injury, but Cook has taken hold of the starting job and he's not keen on letting it go.
Iheanachor can re-take the lead, however, if he can get back on the field. The team will try to get him on the field for their next game, but his status remains unclear and uncertain.

title: Steelers 53-Man Roster Projection: Three QBs, New Rookies
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are about to play actual football.
Their preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers is here, putting over two weeks of training camp practices to the test and giving plenty of players an opportunity to showcase themselves in live-game action for the first time this summer.
The preseason opener can certainly put players on the map, and change some decisions the team makes about their 53-man roster.
Heading into the game, though, there's a clear direction this team is going to go. Unless there are big surprises, here's what the Steelers' final roster should look like at the end of the month.
Maybe the biggest question and biggest surprise on the roster is at quarterback. Right now, Mason Rudolph holds a strong lead as QB2. Does that last? Well, the preseason may decide that. If it doesn't, Will Howard likely won't stick around.
Mike McCarthy has never been into keeping four quarterbacks, and it's hard to imagine he'll start now. Howard ends up on the practice squad where we sit today.
As much fun as Eli Heidenreich is for local Steelers fans , his chances of making the roster as a rookie are slim. Kaleb Johnson still holds the RB3 job and Travis Homer and Lew Nichols are fighting for a spot ahead of Heidenreich.
When it's all said and done, the guess is that Heidenreich and Nichols end up on the practice squad, Homer finds a new home and Rico Dowdle, Jaylen Warren and Johnson are the three running backs left standing.
The fifth-round rookie out of Indiana has impressed during training camp. He's the only fullback on the roster and is making a name for himself as the lead man for Dowdle and Warren. Mike McCarthy has been impressed, and there's no hiding he's going to make the team.
Robert Tonyan was named by Aaron Rodgers as one of the more impressive players at training camp. Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are givens. Really, it's about if the team plans to keep two or three tight ends.
They have the extra space and therefore, keep Tonyan around for Rodgers' final season.
No big surprises here. Brandon Smith is fighting as hard as possible for a roster spot, but it's going to be easier to put him on the practice squad and call him up when needed instead of trying to find a place for him on the team.
So far, Wetjen has shown very little as a wide receiver, and Skowronek is mostly a special teamer as well. So expect Smith to get opportunities, but the final group will be what many thought it would be before training camp.
Mike McCarthy said he's open to keeping up to 10 offensive linemen, and he's going to have to. Because Gennings Dunker has struggled so much during training camp, keeping Ryan McCollum is almost a necessity. Hoffman is an easy keep as well, meaning Pittsburgh needs to find an alternative somewhere.
Broderick Jones is the big "if" here, but with Max Iheanachor being hurt, his chances of sticking around are increasing. The Steelers typically keep at least one swing tackle and then a player who can play multiple positions. They don't really have that this season. So, Jones needs to stay to add more depth, making him the ninth or tenth o-linemen, depending on how you rank them.
This is where things get difficult. The Steelers defense is loaded, but who do they keep around? Dean Lowry was not someone I had on my 53-man roster going into training camp, but he's played his way into the rotation, for sure. Sebastian Joseph-Day and Yahya Blacks are locks.
Then, there's Gabe Rubio. Can the Steelers sneak him onto the practice squad? Do they want to take the risk? Truthfully, he's played so well at training camp that it's going to be very hard to cut him at the end of the month. Chances are he stays.
The second big cut of the year is Malik Harrison. The Steelers have clear plans for Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson, and Cole Holcomb is the clear third behind them. Carson Bruener is the special teams ace who's building a role for himself as a role player on defense.
Harrison doesn't have a place. And it's pretty easy to see him being pushed out of the roster. Add over a $4 million cap savings and it feels like an easy prediction that he'll be gone.
No surprises here. No, the Steelers aren't trading Alex Highsmith or T.J. Watt. They want all four of their edge rushers and are going to keep them, at least in 2026.
This may be the most loaded room on the Steelers' roster. Asante Samuel Jr.'s emergence at training camp has been fun to watch, but he's not the only one making plays. Jamel Dean has looked great the last week, and before his injury, Brandin Echols was making plays in the slot.
Jalen Ramsey (knee) and Joey Porter Jr. (back) should be back for the start of the regular season. No one really knows if they need to slowly work themselves into the defense, but if the do, Pittsburgh has options. And they're keeping all of them.
In order to keep 10 offensive linemen, the Steelers need to cut at least one surprising name. That name is probably Rayshawn Jenkins.
The Steelers want a veteran safety behind DeShon Elliott and Jaquan Brisker. Mike McCarthy has made it known that they are searching for someone, but that may not mean they keep them.
Robert Spears-Jennings has gotten more first-team opportunities than any other rookie on the roster, and he hasn't looked bad running with the ones. With Ramsey's versatility, the Steelers have options to keep Elliott and Brisker fresh, but it also means they only keep three traditional safeties on the roster.
No surprises here. Laith Marjan is here for the summer, but he's not beating out Chris Boswell.
