title: Steelers Linked to Ridiculous QB Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't even played a single preseason game, but talks regarding their trade deadline plans have already developed.
Of course, the only trade deadline moves that matter to the Steelers are the ones surrounding Aaron Rodgers. The team's starting quarterback is in his final NFL season, according to the man himself, and the organization understandably wants to do anything it can to deliver him another Super Bowl victory.
But some believe it's more likely to go completely off the rails. That's what Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio proposed on a recent appearance on Pardon My Take. After 19 years of avoiding losing seasons, the Steelers might be staring down their first one in two decades under new head coach Mike McCarthy. If that happens, Florio believes the Steelers might try to move Rodgers to give him one more postseason run.
"There's a chance this thing goes sideways," he warned. "You get to the trade deadline, you can have Aaron Rodgers maybe asking to go somewhere that may need a quarterback. Some contender that may need a quarterback because 'Get me the hell outta here, this is my last year. I want to have a chance to play into the postseason.'"
Could we see Aaron Rodgers be traded at the deadline if the Steelers season tanks? pic.twitter.com/txneoKW1RR
The Steelers are undoubtedly focused on the Vince Lombardi Trophy. The way they are preparing for the year and moving through training camp, it's clear that the belief within the organization is that they are a legitimate contender.
That belief isn't shared around the NFL, however. And that's what Florio points out during his appearance on PMT. He outlines the timeline he imagines the Steelers are working with, around Thanksgiving. By then, the team might be out of contention, and their hands might be tied.
"If we're (the Steelers) not contending by Thanksgiving," he stated. "Why do we want to play out the string with Aaron Rodgers?"
That's all fair and good, but does it align with the organization's goals and plans? The obvious answer is no, as the Steelers have no plans to deal the future Hall of Fame quarterback. Instead, the team believes they can help get back to the Promised Land once more.
If Rodgers does become available, what teams would have any interest? Florio proposes that a team that is in contention but in need of a quarterback would be the most likely option.
Realistically, what team fits that description? No team does, because no NFL team can contend without a competent starting quarterback. Injuries can change things, but right now there is no possible landing spot for Rodgers outside of Pittsburgh.

title: Germie Bernard Has Huge Opportunity After Steelers WR Injuries
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have been very impressed with the work of rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard. The team's recent second-round draft pick arrived at camp ready to compete, and it didn't take long for him to cut into the first-team snaps.
The Steelers may be calling upon the rookie receiver to play a pivotal role in the team's preseason opener. Top wideout Michael Pittman Jr. suffered an upper-body injury during a recent practice, and he's been limited in the team's final practices before taking on the Green Bay Packers. In addition, top receiver DK Metcalf was a spectator as the team took things inside for a recent practice.
For Bernard, it's another opportunity. Of course, this one comes with just a bit more pressure, as he gets acquainted with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers and the rest of the first-team offense.
"It's a great opportunity to get in there with A-Rod and kind of just learn everything about him. Learn his signals and everything," he said. "I'm still asking questions from DK (Metcalf) and Pitt (Pittman Jr.), so those guys are doing a great job of teaching everybody in the room and making sure that everybody is falling in line."
Based on how the practice reps have gone so far, the Steelers are ready to give Bernard a huge opportunity against the Packers. The young receiver has been playing plenty with the first-team offense, and if both DK and MPJ are not active, that leaves him and Roman Wilson as the top options.
Luckily for Bernard, he thrives on being available in any and all situations. It's something he believes he has always brought to the football field, and versatility remains a top priority as he establishes himself as a professional.
"Just being versatile," he stated. "That's something I hold dearly to my heart just because it presents me with a alot of opportunities."
Bernard does not lack confidence, but can he match that with production on the field? That will be the toughest challenge for the rookie receiver, who will have to create chemistry with more than one quarterback against the Packers.
Asked what he tries to do when filling in for players like DK and Pittman Jr., Bernard kept it simple. Sure, he can't replicate the size those two hulking pass-catchers inherently provide, but he can bring something even better: himself.
"I'll be myself," he said.
And the Steelers are planning to let Germie be himself in the preseason opener. Now, let's see where that takes him.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Has Preseason Plans
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't announced if Aaron Rodgers will play in the preseason or not, but it sure doesn't sound like the 42-year-old wants to.
Speaking with the media, Rodgers made it very clear that he doesn't see the benefit of preseason games for himself or many other veterans.
"It's preseason. It's not real football," Rodgers said. "So if I do great. If not, great. Preseason's a lot different. Teams don't run anything anymore, they just really don't. It's good to see guys with pads on, under the lights, how they react to the nerves. But it's not real, regular season football."
So, it's hard to imagine he'll be out there. If he's not, he still has intentions to improve the Steelers during the three exhibition games.
"I like to be on the headset and calm everybody down," Rodgers told Steelers On SI. "Usually, the first game, it's a little hectic on the headset. So I like to be the voice of reason, occasional dad joke or one-liner. Just keep everybody settled in a little bit."
"Well, their age, really. They're young kids. They're excited about learning, open to some extra coaching from me," Rodgers added about Howard and Allar. "They ask questions. They want to do it right. They watch what I do and try and mimic that. Or if I do something they don't understand, they ask a question. And the best part of it is Tom [Arth] gives me a lot of latitude in the room to speak up and to talk about things or stop the film and say, 'What are you thinking here?' And quarterback, just like all things, can be over-complicated to make it seem more difficult than it might be sometimes. It's not easy, but you can simplify things and that's what I'm trying to help them with."
The ears he'll be speaking into on the headset will be Mason Rudolph's, Will Howard's and Drew Allar. For Howard and Allar, this will be their first NFL game ever, meaning the nerves will certainly be high for the young quarterbacks.
Rodgers will be able to be a calming presence while offering advice as they navigate a game for the first time.
For Rudolph, it's likely more of a "how can I help you" situation. The 31-year-old is in the midst of a quarterback battle with Howard and could create maybe an uncloseable gap if he plays well against the Packers. Rodgers will be a helping hand in doing so while watching from the sideline.
The Steelers will be without a number of players in their preseason opener. Rookie tackle Max Iheanachor (shoulder/neck) will likely be out after missing the last week of practice. Wide receivers DK Metcalf (unknown) and Michael Pittman Jr. (leg) will also miss the game after not practicing.
Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson will start in their places. Dylan Cook will start at right tackle, as he's been throughout training camp.
Defensive tackles Sebastian Joseph-Day (unknown) and Logan Lee (unknown) and offensive guard Steven Jones (unknown) have also missed practice time and are not expected to play. Defensive backs Jaquan Brisker and Brandin Echols (ankle) likely won't either as they work through injuries. Echols remains in a walking boot since injuring his ankle.
Rookie running back Eli Heidenreich is expected to play after missing time with a hamstring/groin injury. Heidenreich told Steelers On SI that he feels much better and is ready to go out there on Thursday night against the Packers.

title: Steelers Get Good Injury News on Rookie Eli Heidenreich
full_text:
It appears Eli Heidenreich is set to return and will play in the Pittsburgh Steelers ' first game of the preseason.
After missing a handful of practices in recent days as the second week of training camp transitioned into the third, Heidenreich told reporters that he feels good from a health perspective after taking some time off and is trending in the right direction.
"Health-wise, I feel great," Heidenreich said. "I took a few days off, I'm sure you guys saw that, but I'm healing up."
When asked if he'll be a full-go in the preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, Heidenreich stated that's the plan.
"The plan today was to practice," Heidenreich said. "It got changed up a little bit today, but yea as far as I'm concerned."
With Heidenreich back on the field and ready to go heading into Pittsburgh's bout against the Packers, it won't come as a surprise if his number is called a ton at Acrisure Stadium later this week.
Coming into training camp, Heidenreich was lumped in with the likes of Kaleb Johnson and Travis Homer as the top candidates to snag the last spot or two on the 53-man roster at running back.
With Johnson handling a steady workload behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle while Lew Nichols has emerged as one of the stars of camp, however, Heidenreich is in a precarious position next to Homer.
It doesn't help that Heidenreich missed multiple practices, as previously mentioned, especially as a rookie who is still acclimating himself to the NFL.
The seventh-round pick's versatility provides a nice boost to his stock and the overall intrigue surrounding him, though. Whether it's at running back, on special teams or perhaps a snap here and there at wide receiver, the fact that Mike McCarthy and his staff can get creative in how they deploy Heidenreich means he has several avenues through which he can make the roster.
Because he's buried so far down the depth chart at this point, it more or less feels like his fate as a likely cut candidate is well on its way to being cemented. There just isn't room on the roster for him.
Heidenreich could still make up for lost time by catching a few passes out of the backfield and holding up in pass protection while thriving in whatever role(s) he handles on special teams, but it's hard to imagine it being enough to snag an initial 53-man when it's all said and done.

title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Steelers QB Plan in Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't yet made a concrete decision on who will start at quarterback in the team's preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, but they at least have an outline.
Head coach Mike McCarthy told the media that while the team is still drawing up their plan and will have more to report back on once additional meetings are conducted, his likely intention is to go with three groups - one that will go through a series or two, a second that will finish out the first half from there and a third that will stay on the field for the second half.
Regardless of which quarterback falls into those respective categories, it'll be an opportunity for the backup battle to take center stage between Mason Rudolph and Will Howard, the latter of whom will play in the first game of his professional career next to Drew Allar , even if it's not technically an official contest.
Ahead of his Steelers debut after a hand injury kept him out of the preseason and on the reserve/injured list through Week 11 as a rookie last year, Howard couldn't contain excitement to finally get out on the field against Green Bay while speaking with reporters on August 10.
“I’m so fired up,” Howard said. “I can’t wait for the game, but obviously I’m trying to take it day by day. It’s still camp. But, you know, sometimes you can’t help but look forward a little bit and start getting excited just to be out there in live game reps.”
Howard has the most to both gain and lose among all of Pittsburgh's signal callers. The 2025 sixth-rounder has been up-and-down during training camp, with a good start to his time in Latrobe this summer before a rather poor finish to his second week there.
Rudolph entered camp as the No. 2 quarterback behind Aaron Rodgers, and nothing has changed on that front thus far. The 31-year-old has been as steady as expected, and while it's not always exciting with him, he's the type of stabilizing veteran presence that any team would covet as their backup.
As a result, Howard must go above and beyond both against the Packers and in each of Pittsburgh's following two preseason bouts in order to make up enough ground in the race for the No. 2 job to hold any sort of suspense leading into final roster cuts at the end of the month.
Allar, on the other hand, just has to show progress week-over-week and prove that he has taken steps forward when it comes to his mechanics, footwork and processing.
The third-round pick is a lock to make the 53-man roster as the No. 3 quarterback, meaning he isn't facing the same type of pressure that Howard or even Rudolph are at the moment.
Still, some conclusions are going to be drawn about Allar based on he performs this preseason whether it's right or wrong, and jumping out to a strong start against the Packers would provide a good foundation for the rookie to work off of.

title: 4 Seahawks That Could Raise or Hurt Their Stock vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will inch closer to building their 53-man roster when they take on the Dallas Cowboys in their first preseason game of the year.
Roster battles will be taking place, and some players could gain an edge while others could falter. Here's a look at four players to keep an eye on for the team's game against the Cowboys.
Lock is expected to be the backup quarterback for the Seahawks going into this game against the Cowboys. There's a good chance he only sees a quarter or so of action, but his performance could dictate how the backup quarterback competition goes.
Lock is the favorite for the QB2 role, but if he underperforms, second-year pro Jalen Milroe could take over.
Lock may be the favorite for the backup spot, but Milroe has a chance to overtake him. In order to do that, however, Milroe needs to play at the level he's been at since the start of training camp. Coaches have been impressed with Milroe's growth from his rookie year to now, but he has to showcase that in a game in order for the team to truly believe in his abilities as a backup quarterback.
I'm also curious to see if the Seahawks build any other role for him outside of the quarterback position, just to get him involved as a 2025 third-round pick. The Seahawks should try to extract some value out of him if it is available.
The Seahawks value versatility in their players, even at the quarterback position. This is the time to experiment with subpackages and new plays with specific players, so the Seahawks should take advantage.
Many fans might have been surprised to see Holani as the team's RB1 in the first unofficial depth chart. The pro from Boise State isn't likely to be the starter during the season, but his experience with the team, coupled with an injury to Zach Charbonnet, has thrust Holani into the starting spot.
Last year, Holani made quite the impact in the preseason, racking up 61 yards on seven carries and a 24-yard touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders. In that game, the No. 6 overall pick, Ashton Jeanty, only had three carries for 10 yards.
Holani should be given the most carries out of any Seahawks running back, but Emanuel Wilson, Jacardia Wright, and Velus Jones Jr. should also get some opportunities while Jadarian Price and Charbonnet deal with injuries.
Pritchett is competing for the third cornerback slot on the roster. The third-year pro from Auburn has a couple of teammates fighting for his spot, but he is hoping to showcase his growth and earn a larger role within the defense. That all starts with performing well against the Cowboys.
Pritchett is off to a good start in camp, but he can maximize his potential by showing out in his preseason debut.
"I've grown a lot," Pritchett told reporters via the team's website. "As a rookie, you're coming in, you really don't have a routine, you're trying to see what vets you can get close to to just get an idea of what you need to do as far as taking care of your body.
"As far as the playbook, Mike is a defensive minded coach, so you know his playbook is going to be super complex, so you're trying to learn all this new terminology, so I've grown a lot being more comfortable in the defense. Everything has slowed down a lot."
Pritchett will get a chance to showcase how much he has grown when the Cowboys visit the Seahawks at Lumen Field on Saturday at 5 p.m. PT. Fans can watch the game locally on KING 5 or stream it on the Seahawks mobile app.

title: Seahawks' CB3 Battle in Training Camp Could Have a Favorite Emerging
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are figuring out what their depth chart will look like going into the season as training camp continues to roll into the first preseason game.
Riq Woolen is no longer with the team after signing with the Philadelphia Eagles, so his spot in the depth chart is up for grabs. The Seahawks could sign a free agent like Terrion Arnold, who worked out with the team earlier this week, but they could also promote someone from within. Nehemiah Pritchett is making a strong impression and could make a case for that spot in the secondary rotation.
"He's really competing and really excited for the opportunity he has," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said via the team's website. "He's making the most of it. He's making a heck of a case for carving himself a role."
Pritchett and former first-round pick Noah Igbinoghene are listed as the second-string cornerbacks in the Seahawks' first unofficial depth chart, which was released earlier this week ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys.
Pritchett is hungry for more going into his third season, which could fuel his attempt at earning that third spot on the depth chart.
"I definitely want the bigger role, I'm embracing the competition," Pritchett told reporters. "I'm just trying to take it day by day and take the steps I need to take to keep getting better each and every day, so if I'm put into that role, it'll be smooth."
Igbinoghene has the NFL experience as he enters his seventh NFL season with his fourth different franchise. Pritchett has the experience of playing in Aden Derde's defensive scheme for the past two years. That's part of what makes this decision very difficult. It doesn't make the Seahawks' job any easier knowing that both of them have performed well in training camp.
55 tackles, 7 passes defensed (17 games, 10 starts for WAS)
12 tackles, 1 pass defensed (10 games, 1 start for SEA)
35 tackles, 1.0 sacks, 5 passes defensed (15 games, 2 starts for WAS)
14 tackles, 2 passes defensed (17 games, 0 starts for SEA)
"Whoever wins the job, it's not like they're the ones getting all those snaps. It's about how we want to deploy and how many DBs do we give time? Do we want to be able to play more three linebacker sets? Do we want to play more five down sets? It's everybody right now," Macdonald told reporters.
"The front guys are battling to say, 'Hey, look, we need to be on the field more.' That trickles into the linebacker room, which affects the DB room and vice versa. That's where we're at right now. Both those two guys you mentioned (Pritchett and Noah Igbinoghene) are having really good camps, and they're definitely putting their best foot forward."
The Seahawks' defense doesn't work the same as many other units across the league. Their ability to utilize different positions in other ways makes them build their team very differently than others. That could make things easier or harder to do, depending on what position they play.
Ultimately, the team is looking for effort and competitiveness, so it only makes for a very challenging decision for the team.

title: Top 25 Seattle Seahawks Going into 2026 NFL Season: #8 Charles Cross
full_text:
There were several reasons why the Russell Wilson era was over after the 2021 NFL Season. One of the biggest was that the Seahawks couldn't build a sustainable offensive line with him taking up so much of the salary cap. They started over by trading him for a collection of picks, including offensive tackle Charles Cross, who has become one of the top blindside tackles in the NFC West .
After helping lead the Seahawks’ young, but talented, offensive line to a stable performance going to the Super Bowl, Cross is capable of achieving more than team success. He is capable of a couple of individual achievements, like a Pro Bowl bid, as long as he remains healthy. Cross is under a new contract and the right new offensive coordinator to help more recognized as the tenacious blocker he is.
Cross had a big task ahead of him last season to protect the blindside of new quarterback Sam Darnold, maintain a dynamic backfield and be a leader on the offensive line. He was solid in the first 14 regular-season games, but missed three games in the regular season due to a hamstring injury .
He finished the regular season with a 73.2 overall grade from Pro Football Focus (30th of 89 offensive tackles in the league), 76.9 in pass-block grade (18 of 89) and a run-block grade of 66.7 (43 of 89). Cross committed only five penalties, while allowing two sacks and four pressures. He did, however, allow 24 pressures.
The Seahawks will keep much of their offense, including multiple running backs and multiple tight ends. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury will have more unique spread looks and get more pass-catchers involved. It will also be a more offensive line-favored format with zone-blocking schemes. This will be an offense where Cross can really thrive with the Seahawks’ dynamic schemes and show how consistent he can be.
Cross had a stellar season in pass-protection, but he is coming off a considerably down year in run-blocking. This is a concern as the Seahawks remain a serious rushing offense with a rookie as a first-string running back. He has some tendencies to adjust slowly in run-blocking, which could cause disruption at the line of scrimmage.
Despite the fact that he got his contract extension this offseason , there is still a lot of development for him to be done. He hasn't hit the elite threshold that most top-ten selected offensive tackles fall under.
This season is a good opportunity for him to earn that Pro-Bowl level of recognition. He has been good enough to be a top-tier player, but he needs to be great for the Seahawks' offense to thrive from start to finish of the season.

title: What Makes Seahawks OC Brian Fleury Different From Klint Kubiak
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were heavily criticized this offseason for letting some of their key components from their Super Bowl-winning team walk out the door. The biggest loss was from offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, who left to become the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders .
All of the praise of the offense's production and quarterback Sam Darnold turned into questions again. Those doubts continued as the Seahawks hired Brian Fleury as the new offensive coordinator.
After a few weeks of training camp, it feels like national media outlets are starting to believe in Fleury. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler appeared at one of the Seahawks' practices to feel the vibe and to answer any questions about the team's ability to compete. After just one practice, Fleury is respected. There are still some attributes that the national media still don’t understand, but will when the season kicks off.
The Seahawks will utilize considerable similarities from last season. Among them is the multiple tight ends being utilized, often on the field at the same time. Fowler believes A.J Barner is an ascending tight end going into his third year in the league.
That could be said for second-year Elijah Arroyo, who could be utilized as a fast, deep-route pass-catcher. He found himself in big moments before his injury.
Arroyo has been one of the biggest risers in this training camp . He has been a constant efficient target throughout the field as he could be a player for quarterback Sam Darnold after wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Kubiak utilized multiple tight ends on the field, but mostly in the run game. This made the offense more predictable, but with the way that Fleury is a tight end developer and how he wants to make the offense more unique, Barner and Arroyo could be a significant boost for the Seahawks.
Kubiak was regarded as one of the best offensive minds last season. What many experts didn't understand was that he was more efficient at utilizing a player's best attributes. With JSN, it was incredible route-running and separation skills . What Fleury has shown to do just in these training camp practices alone is to utilize multiple unique offensive schemes.
This is going to be a big factor for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed , who had his first full offseason with the Seahawks. He looked to develop great chemistry with Darnold. This dynamic has Shaheed all over the field, including the backfield. The new offensive schemes allow receivers like JSN, Shaheed, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton to run multiple different routes.​
Darnold is going to be the player who benefits the most with Fleury as the offensive coordinator . The offense is going to be unique and dynamic enough to open the field to many playmakers. JSN has the potential to have another explosive season, but he doesn't need to be to ensure the offense is among the top scoring units for another season.

title: 4 Seattle Seahawks Who Need a Strong Preseason Debut vs. Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
Football is back. The Seattle Seahawks will kick off their preseason this weekend as they host the Dallas Cowboys on Saturday night .
It would be surprising to see either team play their starters much, if at all, in the first exhibition game. Coaches and players have often stated they get more from joint practices and the Seahawks have one scheduled later this month against the Tennessee Titans .
As for this weekend, there will still be plenty to keep an eye on as players on the roster bubble fight for a spot. That being the case, here is a look at four Seahawks who need to stand out vs. Dallas.
The Seahawks have a strong defensive line, which is where their defensive dominance begins. They have star players such as Byron Murphy, Leonard Williams, and Jarran Reed who have their spots locked in. There's also Rylie Mills, who has had a strong camp and rookie Deven Eastern has promise as well. That has Brandon Pili fighting for a roster spot, and he can use a good showing on Saturday to put himself on the right side of the bubble.
With Zach Charbonnet out, rookie Jadarian Price is set for the RB1 role. Behind him, George Holani has made a strong case for the RB2 spot but Emanuel Wilson shouldn't be overlooked. The former Green Bay Packer averages 4.5 yards per attempt for his career and could be a key piece of the offensive puzzle, but first he has to earn his spot behind Price.
Nehemiah Pritchett has a chance to earn a significant role in what Michael Hanich called a " boom-or-bust " season for the third-year pro. Before worrying about the "boom," Pritchett first has to secure a spot on the roster. Saturday will give him a great chance to prove himself against a Dallas team that's rather deep at wide receiver (even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens not expected to play).
A third-round pick out of Alabama last year, Jalen Milroe was a camp star. His athleticism had fans excited and there was talk of Seattle creating packages to get him involved in the offense. Not much came of this as Milroe appeared in just three games and had four yards on three rushing attempts .
This year, Milroe is again battling for the QB2 spot, but Seahawks On SI's Jeremy Brener says Drew Lock is currently leading the way . Milroe has time to catch up and can gain plenty of ground by showing out against the Cowboys.

full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will have uniform nerds geeking out during their Thursday Night Football meeting with the Denver Broncos during the 2026 season.
The Seahawks and Broncos announced that they would be donning throwback uniforms in Empower Field at Mile High when the two teams meet to open Week 6 on primetime television.

"The Thursday Night Football matchup will mark the eighth time the Seahawks have worn their throwback uniforms since making their debut in the 2023 season," Seahawks.com contributor Colin Gunther wrote.
"Seattle's won four of the seven games where they have worn these uniforms, including a Week 1 victory over the Broncos to open the 2024 season. The team wore these uniforms three times during the 2025 Super Bowl-winning season with one game being played in primetime; a 38-14 road win over the Commanders in Week 9."
There was a mixed response to the reintroduction of the jersey, but most of them were relatively positive.
Update the logo and make these the primary. Please & thank you!
Some fans questioned if the Seahawks would wear their white throwback uniform because they are going to be the road team for the matchup. Fans are hoping this is the direction they will take, especially with the Broncos wearing orange for the game.
Bruh we just want the white throwbacks man….
Let’s make it authentic and do the white throwbacks please and thank you 🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/G5ity3TDJg
One fan is even considering bringing out an old shirt of his specifically for the game, as the Seahawks and Broncos used to be AFC rivals.
I’m ready to bring this out of storage.   Let’s go Seahawks.   It may not fit as well …. pic.twitter.com/Cohlm810W5
While most of the reaction to the jersey announcement was positive, there were some that weren't as thrilled about the decision.
As a proud Seattle Seahawks fan I will always prefer the current logo over the old one that looks mentally handicapped.
throwback jerseys always look better on tv than they do irl though, curious if these hold up
Would have been better if we had some away throwbacks
Before the Seahawks made the move to the NFC in 2002, they were big rivals with the Broncos, and they have played them 58 times in NFL history, which is tied for the most games against any other opponent, along with the Los Angeles Rams.
The Seahawks are 35-23 against the Broncos all time, including a 43-8 win in Super Bowl XLVIII back in 2014.
This could potentially be a Super Bowl preview for this season, as both teams finished the 2025 campaign as the number one overall seed in their respective conference. The Seahawks went on to win the Super Bowl, while the Broncos finished one game short, losing to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship game.
The Seahawks will face the Broncos inside Empower Field at Mile High on Oct. 15.

title: How Bears' Coby Bryant Injury Affects Seahawks
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks fans are disappointed after learning of some news coming out of Chicago Bears training camp .
Former Seahawks defensive back Coby Bryant , who signed with the Bears during the offseason on a three-year, $40 million deal, underwent surgery on his knee that will likely keep him out for the entire season.
Bears S Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and now will miss 4-6 months. Bears are hoping he can return for the playoffs.
Initial signs show that Bryant would likely only miss 8-10 weeks, keeping him with a chance to play against the Seahawks on Monday Night Football on Nov. 2. This news should keep him out for that game and beyond.
Bryant spent the last four seasons with the Seahawks after being selected in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Cincinnati. He worked hard during his tenure in Seattle, which awarded him with a Super Bowl ring this past season and an expensive three-year, $40 million contract with Chicago.
Bryant was one of the top defensive backs in free agency, and the Seahawks wanted to keep him, but they felt they could not match the money the Bears were willing to give. Once he left for the Bears, he stated how excited he was to play against the Seahawks in his first season with Chicago.
“We actually play Seattle this year, in Seattle, so they better be ready for me, for sure,” Bryant told Kay Adams back in March on the Up & Adams show.
Even though Bryant no longer wears the Seahawks uniform, his absence for the 2026 campaign will affect Seattle's future. The Seahawks were projected to get a compensatory draft pick for losing Bryant in free agency, and it was projected to be around a sixth-round pick, according to Over the Cap.
Bryant's injury, which will keep him out for the season, likely means that his value will slip into the seventh round or possibly be erased altogether.
That being said, the team still has seven selections for the 2027 NFL draft, and they will likely have other compensatory picks from their other free agents who moved on. They also will be awarded an additional third-round pick for assistant general manager Nolan Teasley's hiring by the Minnesota Vikings. Boye Mafe, who signed with the Cincinnati Bengals, will likely fetch a fourth-round pick, while Kenneth Walker III and Riq Woolen could help the Seahawks land a pair of fifth-round picks.

title: Five Observations From Episode Two of Seahawks Hard Knocks
full_text:
Hard Knocks Episode Two is officially a go. It was another phenomenal showcase of what’s going on at the VMac as the Seahawks prepare to defend their title. As always, the production is a mixture of entertainment and information, fluff and substance. It remains a must-see for any Seahawks fan. But what were the major themes of this week’s episode?
The early seconds of the episode picked up where the first episode left off, in a manner of speaking. Derick Hall, the edge rusher who was rewarded with a $42 million dollar contract extension in the offseason, was getting just a little too excited during practice, hitting too hard and getting too close to the quarterback. Quickly, Mike had seen enough.
He sent Derick off the field, amid protests, in response to his refusal to amp things down. When this event happened, and how soon it happened after the brawl depicted in episode one, isn’t clear, but it does seem to establish a trend. Hall is one of the instigators in camp so far, and he’ll need to find a way to crank it down now and bring it back up for the season.
We had an expanded look at the scene later in the episode as well, making it one of the biggest emphasis points of the episode. Mike Macdonald wants to protect his quarterbacks, especially this early in camp, so his frustration is understandable. And while there was some anger, ultimately, it was a learning moment for Derick.
One of the highlights of the episode was the cameo by Mitch Johnson , coach of the San Antonio Spurs. He and Brian Wright (San Antonio’s General Manager) had a short conversation with Macdonald in Mike’s office. They exchanged notes, with Mike talking about how his training camp process has changed from last year to this year.
It was a cool moment, two successful professional coaches in different leagues trying to find ways in which they could help the other. Mike has spoken about how he feels like you can learn things from experts in other sports, and it speaks to his focus on chasing edges. And perhaps Mitch picked up something that will help him on his quest to his first title.
One extended sequence in the episode focused on Sam Darnold’s spin rate, of all things. Darnold, apparently, puts more spin on the ball when he throws it than any other quarterback in the league. The average rate is around 570, and Darnold is around 100 more than that. According to Jake Peetz, this creates a more catchable and accurate ball.
I can’t say I’ve ever heard of spin rate when looking at and scouting quarterbacks, and I don’t know about the science behind it actually being easier to catch a fast-spinning ball. But for whatever it’s worth, Cooper Kupp expressed his belief that the faster spin is superior, so I suppose it’s another thing that Darnold is getting right so far in Seattle.
One of the recurring recreational activities the players partake in during camp, going back to last year, is shadowboxing. I can’t say I came out of the episode with a great understanding of exactly how the game worked, but to make a long story short, it’s a way for the players to bond and remain in competition with each other, as a sort of rock-paper-scissors game.
It gets players who typically don’t work with each other to interact, and it sure seems like they’re having plenty of fun doing it. If nothing else, it’s a non-violent way for the players to settle disputes, which is always appreciated. I don’t think I’d be very good at it, but they’re having a good time, and that’s all that matters.
The episode included a brief discussion of the Terrion Arnold conundrum , as the Seahawks have an opportunity to make a play for him in free agency. Obviously, the issue is complicated, with his legal issues and felony charges making it unclear if he’ll even be allowed to play. But Schneider makes it clear he believes he can help the team.
I can understand why the squad would be tempted to allow Mike Macdonald to get an opportunity to coach someone as talented as Terrion Arnold. Furthermore, one scene involved a discussion about how they had inquired with Jalen Milroe, who developed a relationship with Arnold in college. We even got to see some of the workout Arnold had in the VMac.
There was plenty of fun content as well, like Leonard Williams’s affinity for gardening and Derick Hall’s truck hobby. Nick Emmanwori’s pool rehab got a couple minutes. A sledgehammer-based competition of strength between Mason Richman and Rylie Mills was used to settle a particularly physical moment on the field. The mock game got some focus as well.
All in all, it was another great look into the team. It gave fans just about everything they could want. Three more episodes left. We will be seated.

title: Seahawks Rookie Jadarian Price Gets Huge Comparison to Pro Bowl RB
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are expected to feature first-round pick Jadarian Price heavily in their run game this season.
While Price will have a role in the team's running back committee, he has the potential to break out and be a true lead back. Per a report from ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler , Seahawks defensive back Julian Love compared Price to a prime Dalvin Cook, which is a massive compliment.
It's a bold statement for Love to compare Price to Cook before the rookie from Notre Dame even takes an NFL snap, but the vision is there.
Cook, in his prime, had a violent running style. When he saw an opening, he would attack it with force. That's similar to what we saw Price do in his limited action at Notre Dame behind Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick in this year's draft.
The two also have similar builds. Cook stood 5-10 and weighed 210 pounds, while Price is 5-11 weighing 209 pounds. Cook has a bit more muscle than Price, but the latter is still just 22 years old and has plenty of room for growth. If Price can reach Cook's prime, the Seahawks should have something very valuable.
In Cook's six seasons with the Minnesota Vikings from 2017-22, he was one of the top running backs in the league.
Cook averaged just under 1,000 yards per season with the Vikings, and that came even with him missing 17 games across his first two seasons due to injury. That's a good baseline for Price, but there will be some struggles for him to hit that number with the Seahawks.
Cook was far and away the best running back with the Vikings while he was there. Nobody was really challenging him for carries on the roster. With the way the Seahawks want to run the ball, it will be hard for Price to achieve that status.
The Seahawks plan to use two or three running backs throughout the season, as Zach Charbonnet should get carries once he returns to the field from his torn ACL recovery. Emanuel Wilson should also see some action after signing a one-year deal with the team during the offseason.
The Seahawks' committee should allow them to stay healthier throughout the year, but it hurts Price's chances of becoming one of the top running backs in the league in his rookie year. If he impresses and is clearly the best running back, Seattle might opt for a change in the middle of the year. The vision is that Price will be part of a whole running back room that will try to beat you in multiple ways.

title: Biggest Surprise From Seattle Seahawks Unofficial Depth Chart vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The defending champion Seattle Seahawks will be in action this Saturday as they host the Dallas Cowboys in Preseason Week 1 .
Even with their top players such as Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Sam Darnold, Leonard Williams, and Devon Witherspoon all returning, Seattle has multiple positions up for grabs. One of the most prominent spots is at running back, a position that was vacated when Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker signed with the Kansas City Chiefs .
Making things even more interesting at running back is the injury suffered by Zach Charbonnet. During Seattle's playoff run, Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL and hasn't been cleared for action. The Seahawks attempted to fill that void with rookie Jadarian Price, who they selected in the first round of the NFL draft out of Notre Dame.
Price worked behind Jeremiyah Love with the Irish, but has all the traits to be an effective lead back. His skill set fits well with the Seattle offense and he entered the offseason as the expected starter. On the first unofficial depth chart, however, that's not the case.
The depth chart, which was shared by Field Gulls, has Price as the RB2 behind third-year pro George Holani.
The first unofficial Seahawks depth chart is here! This was presumably put together prior to Emmanwori passing his physical, otherwise everything else is up to date. pic.twitter.com/HRzClSuxOF
Holani has been a standout for the Seahawks during camp, which comes as a surprise to no one. Holani has often been able to impress during offseason work as well as the preseason. Due to the depth at running back, he hasn't been able to do much in the regular season.
In two years, Holani has 25 attempts for 83 yards and one touchdown. This season could be his chance to carve out a larger role in the offense and if this depth chart is any indication, he will be given the chance to do exactly that.
The EDGE is another spot of interest, where Derick Hall is listed as the backup behind DeMarcus Lawrence while the starter across from Lawrence is Uchenna Nwosu.
Nwosu had seven sacks last season while starting 11 of the 16 games he appeared in, but Hall signed a three-year extension worth $42 million , suggesting he could be in for a starting spot. They also have Ty Okada listed ahead of rookie Bud Clark as the starting safety across from Julian Love.
Of course, this is an unofficial depth chart and there could be several changes before the regular season, but that doesn't mean there aren't some surprises.

title: Deebo Samuel Reveals Exactly Why He Rejoined the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers and Deebo Samuel are back working together after one year away.
Is Samuel's return a surprise? Not really. The 49ers front office signed him as soon as they knew Ricky Pearsall was going to undergo season-ending surgery on his PCL injury.
But both parties agreed to a very favorable one-year contract worth up to $7 million. It's since come to light that a fair whack of that money is incentive-based.
Samuel entered free agency after just one year with the Washington Commanders, and there were no reports of him being close to signing with another team.
But given the circumstances surrounding San Francisco right now, a reunion with the 49ers suddenly makes plenty of sense. As always, injuries dominate the headlines.
Samuel admitted that the culture was a key reason for coming back, the same reasoning as Dre Greenlaw .
"This is where I got drafted at, and the culture that John [Lynch] and Kyle [Shanahan] and those guys have built with the players that they have bought in, and the mentality that they have instilled in all the players, it's just a standard," Samuel shared on the NFL Network .
"And you can go back to last year—I was still keeping tabs on the guys. And with all the injuries and this, that, and the third that they was dealt, they still had a great season. And that's just the standard of next-man-up mentality. Everybody practices the same, everybody lives under one standard."
Samuel reacquainted himself with Brock Purdy after the pair previously helped take the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game and Super Bowl in 2022 and 2023. He also explained what he likes most about Purdy's game.
"I think Brock has been the most consistent, persistent, really good in decision-making, not making too many mistakes," Samuel said. "I think that's what he's really, really good at—getting the ball out on time, and giving receivers opportunities to step back to the ball even when you're covered. Let's see [if you can] make this play to build that trust, and also challenging the defense as well."
Samuel's return to the City by the Bay has been welcomed all around by staff and players alike, but it's best to temper expectations based on his first stint. He's older now and likely isn't operating at the same level he was during the prime years of his career.

title: 49ers Cornerback Battle Takes Center Stage in Preseason Opener
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' secondary decisions this offseason were some of the most interesting moves they made . The team appeared content to bring back the three starters from last year, but at the same time made a strong effort to push a lot of them under new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris.
Kyle Shanahan noted that most of the starters will not play in the preseason. Still, the cornerback room is not deep, and there is expected to be competition. So, who plays and what role they play will be important to follow when understanding how Morris views the secondary.
Deommodore Lenoir might be the only one of the starters definitely not expected to play. Second-year slot defender Upton Stout seems to be in good standing with the coaching staff as well.
The big question will be Renardo Green. The coaching staff challenged Green this offseason, and so far he has responded . However, the team likely needs to see more than just a few good training camp practices. Does that mean he suits up when most starters sit?
Then, who lines up across from him will be important to follow. It will likely be Jack Jones, who was brought in to push Green. Jones has had a good training camp, but the incumbent has been better.
Nate Hobbs could also push Jones and Green, but right now his role might be the backup slot behind Stout. If Stout sits, it could be a valuable chance for Hobbs to start in the slot. Then, he could potentially jump in for Green on the outside when they move to the next string of defenders.
Ephesians Prysock will be one of the players on the next string. He has been buried on the depth chart due to the depth added, but he should join fourth-year defender Darrell Luter as the depth pieces on the outside, assuming Hobbs does not shift outside. Second-year UDFA Jakob Robinson will man the slot behind Hobbs, as he pushes for a spot in year two.
Overall, it could look like Green and Jones outside with Hobbs in the slot to start. Then, Prysock and Luter on the outside, with Robinson in the slot to finish out the game. The team has no other options, so these six are going to get a lot of work. Who steps up, and who ends up getting all of the playing time?

title: The Quality Brock Purdy Has That the 49ers Love About Him
full_text:
Brock Purdy is in full swing as he enters Year 5 as the franchise quarterback of the San Francisco 49ers.
He's fired up and raring to go and has widely been considered one of the standout players at training camp so far. All the coaches have heaped praise on his work, which only adds to it.
But that's hardly surprising when he's already established himself as a top 8-12 quarterback in the league.
One of the best intangible qualities Purdy possesses is his relentless drive to get better as a quarterback. He's always looking for ways to improve his game, and that's hardly surprising given the competitive edge he's displayed throughout his career.
From afar, Purdy comes across as a confident and assured person, but he might not have the more outgoing personality of backup Mac Jones . That's not to say Purdy is boring, but rather that he appears more understated and constantly focused on becoming the best quarterback he can be on the field.
"I appreciate who Brock is as a leader and as a guy. He’s not a rah-rah guy in terms of, he’s not bringing a lot of vocal energy every day, but he quietly goes about his business, and he tries to hold people accountable," shared offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak to reporters.
"And yeah, Brock, he’ll snap, he’ll get on people. He’ll get on himself probably more than anyone. If you guys hear some things being said out there, it’s probably him talking to himself a lot of the time, too, which you love that – a guy who’s holding himself accountable.
"That’s who he is. It’s who he’s always been, you mentioned it. From the day he got here, he kind of had that personality and that edge to him and we love it. It’s what makes him a great competitor, so not taking that away from him. I love that he’s himself every day.”
He's only 26, and Purdy still has plenty to give in this game. It feels like his best years are likely still ahead of him, which makes everything he's already accomplished all the more impressive.
And perhaps that's what makes Purdy so intriguing. For everything he's already accomplished, taking the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game and the Super Bowl, there's still a hunger and desire to improve.
This year will be a big year for him.

title: What We Learned About 49ers Defense in Joint Practice with Titans
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The San Francisco 49ers concluded an intense joint practice against the Tennessee Titans , where the 49ers defense set the tone.
The first scrimmage period started with four fights in the first 10 minutes. The first fight began after the first play; Cam Ward threw a ball intended for a Titans wide receiver toward the sideline, and Renardo Green laid the receiver out, with a scuffle ensuing.
“I mean, I don’t want it (fights) because we have a rule on both sides: If you throw a punch, you’re out,” 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said. “So, I think we got two guys thrown out, I’m not sure … but you don’t really care about scuffles. You just hate losing guys.”
This set the tone for the 49ers defense as it took advantage of the Titans offense by being more physical and prepared.
The 49ers secondary looked strong, leaving few holes for Ward to throw into, notably giving fourth-overall pick Carnell Tate a hard day.
Safety Ji’Ayir Brown also intercepted Ward as he undercut a ball thrown to the middle of the field.
“I love our defensive back group. I don’t know if I’ve felt as confident about a back-end group in my career as I have right now,” Fred Warner said. “I think the way that group is meshing together, the way that they're playing sticky in coverage, playing the ball in the air … I think it’s one of the best I’ve seen this far. I’m really excited about what I’m seeing.”
The 49ers competition for their second cornerback spot opposite Deommodore Lenoir between Jack Jones and Green is as competitive as ever. Although Green had a strong day, Jones continues to respond with strong play.
The 49ers run defense struggled, showing weaknesses as Titans running backs found open grass on multiple occasions.
The Titans were able to move the 49ers defensive line, which created holes in the run game, something the 49ers have struggled with over the last couple of years.
On the other hand, the pass rush looked strong, as the 49ers seemed to be in the backfield all day, frustrating the Titans offensive line. The highlight was an Osa Odighizuwa would-be sack of Ward.
On the day, the 49ers defense had the upper hand against the Titans offense. The teams will continue to build toward the regular season in their first preseason game Aug. 13 at Levi’s Stadium at 6 p.m.

title: 49ers Might Face Rams In Australia Without Puka Nacua
full_text:
Facing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia to open the season wasn’t received fondly by the San Francisco 49ers when it was announced.
Nevertheless, that matchup is only a month away. Meaning the 49ers have to lock in and trick themselves into wanting to play there. Going all that way and losing will be devastating .
But there is a chance that winning the game will increase in likelihood. It turns out that Rams star receiver Puka Nacua could be inactive for the Week 1 matchup in Australia.
ESPN’s NFL insider Adam Schefter recently dropped that nugget on his podcast. Here’s what he had to say on the possibility of Nacua missing the game.
“Cases that I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who could potentially face discipline for some of the offseason headlines that accompanied him and some of those incidents last year with another woman,” Schefter said (h/t NBC Sports Bay Area ).
“What did and did not occur, we’ll leave that to the NFL to figure out what did and did not happen. But, it’s possible that when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka does not play in that game.”
I’m sure the 49ers would love for Nacua to miss that game. He’s a handful to game plan for and deal with. They’ll have no qualms about the Rams being without Nacua.
They’ll take every advantage they can get and won’t think twice about it, especially since the Rams recommended that the NFL make the 49ers their opponent for this game . It could be their form of retribution.
Still, there’s no telling if the NFL will suspend Nacua. My guess is they don’t, given the league’s history. Unless you’re caught using a performance enhancer, you’re probably not doing any time.
But who knows? I could also see Nacua getting suspended for two games, but nothing more than that. In comparison, 49ers receiver Demarcus Robinson was suspended for three games last year after a DUI arrest.
It depends on how the NFL views each offense. In any case, a ruling should come down within the next two weeks. Robinson was handed his suspension on Aug. 20, so Nacua’s ruling is looming.

title: 49ers Coach is Confident Injured Kaelon Black Won't Fall Far Behind
full_text:
It's been over a week since 49ers rookie Kaelon Black strained his abductor. He's been out of practice because of it, which is brutal for him.
He had a prime chance to establish himself as the primary backup to Christian McCaffrey, with Jordan James injured with fractured ribs. Now, he has to sit out until he's fit.
Aside from missing a chance at a backup role, Black will fall behind in the offense. It's already tough enough for a rookie to embed themselves in the 49ers' offense.
Missing a bunch of practices will only increase the difficulty for Black. However, 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak is confident the rookie won't fall too far behind.
An injury is a setback, no matter who it is. Especially when you're a rookie, and you're still learning the ropes, and you're still going through everything the first time, you want to be out there, and you want to be getting those reps," Kubiak said. "But Kaelon specifically, he's the right kind of guy. He's made of the right stuff. He prepares the right way.
"He's taking care of his body. He's out there at the walkthroughs, he's in the meetings, he's locked in. He's doing everything he can do to keep himself ready to go when he's healthy, and he will be. We've got full confidence he'll be ready."
This is a vote of confidence in Black from Kubiak. He probably isn't saying that just to say it. I think he truly believes Black can catch up to the offense.
It makes sense considering he played for the University of Indiana in his last two years of college. That's a tightly run and professional team. He knows what it takes.
The 49ers don't have to teach him that, and that's what Kubiak is seeing. It's why he has the confidence that Black can bounce back.
Still, Black missing so much time will hurt him to some degree. Even Kubiak has acknowledged that. But with how locked in he is, all Black needs is some practice to get back into the thick of it.
"I'm not going to lie and say it's not a problem. It's always a setback, but the good ones and pros will overcome that and they'll get themselves ready to go. So, that's what we're looking for.”

title: George Kittle’s Projected 49ers Week 1 Return Is Starting to Look Realistic
full_text:
It's seven months to the very day that San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle suffered an Achilles injury against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Injury-wise, this was by far the biggest of his career, and it marked a brutal end to the season, during which he missed six games due to a fully torn hamstring.
So, 2025 wasn't smooth sailing even though he propped up good numbers. It ended in devastating circumstances, but an offseason rehab regimen has made it look increasingly possible that he might return for Week 1.
Throughout the offseason, Kittle has insisted time and time again that he will be ready to go for Week 1 in Australia.
In February, it was extremely hard to believe. He had surgery, and normally, Achilles injuries take 9-12 months to recover from and sometimes players just aren't the same after it. It's a tough injury to fully recover from.
It was still hard to believe in the months that followed, but Kittle clearly looked ahead of schedule. Now at training camp, he is running routes, catching passes and reportedly doing some conditioning .
#49ers George Kittle looks close to returning 👀 🎥 @zepolila pic.twitter.com/mNHXZYOpWs
This video from Monday's training camp tells you everything you need to know about Kittle's current fitness.
I'm not a doctor, but I think everyone can agree that it's simply incredible to see just how far ahead he is.
There's one more month until the season opener and a possible return feels even more likely. The 49ers feel as though he could feature and these conversations must now be taken seriously.
And the impact of his return would be a huge boost for San Francisco. Injuries are beginning to pile up, especially at running back, where the 49ers are dealing with several concerns. Christian McCaffrey was also missing, although the extent of his injury remains unclear and his absence could simply have been a day off.
Ricky Pearsall is out for the entire season after his PCL issues resurfaced, leading to surgery. Christian Kirk and Mike Evans are also listed as questionable.
Kittle's accelerated progress will be such a huge boost if he is ready to go for the season opener. His unwavering dedication to making his return just eight months after suffering the injury is simply remarkable.
He dubbed the season opener in Australia a "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity," and he's doing everything possible to make sure he's back for it.

title: Raheem Morris Receives Another Vote of Confidence From a 49ers DB
full_text:
Another 49ers defensive back is loving how Raheem Morris’s defense is benefiting them.
It makes sense since Morris is a defensive-backs-oriented coach. First, it was Renardo Green , thrilled with the defense. Then, it was Ji’Ayir Brown , who raved about it. Now, it’s second-year safety Marques Sigle with another vote of confidence in Morris.
“With Raheem, he’s allowing us to be aggressive, play to our skill set,” Sigle said. “It’s making it for us to just not think and allowing us to be playmakers. I feel that’s better for us. I feel we have the type of guys to just go out there and play and not react.”
It shouldn’t be surprising that Morris’ defense is favorable to the secondary. That’s been a common factor for every defense he’s run on every team he’s been on. That’s his staple.
It’s part of what made him a great fit for the 49ers. Their cornerbacks fell off last season, outside of Upton Stout. Their safeties were massively underwhelming as well.
The 49ers needed their entire secondary to improve significantly this year. Now, with Morris at the helm, the entire secondary looks poised to break out this season. It could end up being the best season for a 49ers secondary under Kyle Shanahan.
The only time they had an incredibly strong one was in 2020. That was when Nick Bosa was out for the season with a torn ACL, among many other injured players that made the pass rush irrelevant.
This year’s group of defensive backs can be better than the 2020 one, even though they had Jason Verrett. The 49ers don’t have a secondary player as good as him on their roster.
But what they lack in stardom, they make up for in quantity. A trio of Stout, Green, and Deommodore Lenoir under Morris can be a top-five unit. And if Morris’ system can propel the safeties, they’re cooking with fire.
Given how every defensive back has been thrilled with Morris’ defense, I’d imagine they will all perform collectively at an adequate level. It’ll surpass last season at least, which isn’t an astounding bar to clear.
Still, Morris appears to be the right coach to unlock and push the 49ers’ defensive backs. Time will tell if he truly is the answer.

title: What the 49ers' Plan is for the Starters in the First Preseason Game
full_text:
The first preseason game is right around the corner for the San Francisco 49ers .
It's always an exciting buildup because it's the first time seeing what a team will look like. However, since it's a preseason game, there's no guarantee that the starters will play much, if at all.
In the past, the 49ers have either sat most of their starters in the first game or only let them play for a series or two. On Tuesday, Kyle Shanahan revealed what the 49ers' plan is for the starters.
"There won't be many starters playing," Shanahan said. "We'll see with injuries today and stuff. That doesn't mean none, but we've got to balance that out. We haven't told the players yet, so wait until we do that with them this afternoon.”
It's not surprising that most of the 49ers starters won't suit up against the Tennessee Titans. They got their quality reps when they held a joint practice with them .
That is what Shanahan has always valued more than anything. Since they received those reps, there's no point in the starters playing in the first preseason game.
Now, that doesn't mean every single starter will be inactive. The 49ers don't have that many players to afford that luxury, given all of their injuries.
I'd anticipate Renardo Green playing, a few offensive linemen like Jake Brendel, and even Ji'Ayir Brown. But players like Dre Greenlaw, Mike Evans, and Osa Odighizuwa, I wouldn't expect.
This is totally fine for the 49ers to do after they had a successful joint practice, according to reports. Most of the starters deserve this rest and protection from playing a pointless game.
Besides, the second preseason game is when Shanahan tends to play the starters mostly. That is where you'll see two or three series from the majority of starters.
Although I still wouldn't expect Christian McCaffrey, Trent Williams, Fred Warner, Greenlaw, and Evans to be out there. Those are players who are prohibited from preseason action.
If they are going to suffer an injury, it has to happen when it matters in the regular season. The last thing they want is for them to get hurt in an exhibition, costing them part of the year, if not more.
Plus, they're players who don't need the preseason ramp-up. They're revved up during training camp and don't hold back.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Reveals the Truth About Nick Bosa's Injury
full_text:
There was always something fishy about Nick Bosa missing 49ers practice for over a week with "soreness." That's not a diagnosis that typically keeps a player out for so long.
It turns out that Bosa has more than just soreness, which is what I suspected in a previous article . On Tuesday, Kyle Shanahan revealed the truth about Bosa's injury.
"Tendinitis. It's a pretty normal thing with ACLs," Shanahan said . "It's a normal thing. That's why we've got to be smart here for week to week. No concerns about him, it being more than that."
Well, that's interesting. If it was always tendinitis and it wasn't a concern, why conceal it? If it's so "normal," why is it initially being downplayed?
The 49ers treat injuries to players like a secret formula. Shanahan could've said this from the beginning and it wouldn't have been suspicision.
But now that Bosa has missed a couple more practices since he last spoke, he knows the 49ers can no longer downplay it or keep it hidden.
So, Bosa is week-to-week with tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee, but it's normal. If it's tendinitis and his knee is potentially swollen, this could be an issue throughout the season.
Bosa could play one game, then all of a sudden his tendinitis flares up for a week, keeping him out of the next game. It's a tricky scenario because of how unpredictable it is.
That means the 49ers can't count on Bosa to play all 17 games. He made it through six practices before his knee gave him issues.
How on earth is he going to play for most of a season? It feels like Bosa is more likely to play in seven games than 17. That's how concerning this is.
On one end, it's awesome that he didn't suffer anything significant. On the other end, this does carry some significance if it leads to him missing a handful of games or being limited.
Time will tell how this works out for Bosa and the 49ers. One thing is for sure: they need him out there every game. Their pass rush is irrelevant without him.
Rookie Romello Height can't be their top option on the edge. He'll only be effective when Bosa is on the field, which means everything is reliant on Bosa.
The 49ers better hope their secondary plays well this year because that is where the strength of their defense will be.

title: Emeka Egbuka's Injury Status Revealed With New Update After Buccaneers-Jets Practice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a stacked wide receivers room heading into 2026. That being said, any injury to that room would be tough for the Bucs' offense this upcoming season.
The Bucs are already dealing with some injuries among their wide receivers, as wideouts Tez Johnson (groin) and David Sills (knee), among others, have been banged up during camp. The Buccaneers potentially looked to take a serious hit to the room, though, when wideout Emeka Egbuka went down during Wednesday's practice and was attended to by trainers.
Egbuka got rolled up on during an end around and was on the trainer's table for quite a bit, and it left many wondering what his status was after trainers got a more in-depth look after practice.
As it turns out, Tampa Bay may have avoided a close call, and Egbuka looks to be mostly fine after the incident.
NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Wednesday that Egbuka suffered a toe injury that the team considers to be "minor", paving the way for him to return to action sooner rather than later.
#Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka’s injury that cut his practice today is a toe issue that’s considered minor, source says. That jibes with RB Bucky Irving telling @MJD earlier during our interview, “I think he’s pretty good. He just got rolled over on.” Thumbs up 👍 on Egbuka’s toe. pic.twitter.com/P8355zqSms
While the injury appears minor and Egbuka will likely miss a little bit of practice time before the regular season, toe injuries can be a bit tricky. Hopefully for Tampa Bay, Egbuka's injury doesn't take too long to heal and he can factor into the lineup for Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals on the road.
In the meantime, the Bucs will continue to rely on Jalen McMillan and veteran Chris Godwin in the wide receivers room. With Egbuka likely missing time, though, Tampa Bay's wideouts room remains thin — Tez Johnson, Kameron Johnson, Sills and now Egbuka are banged up, so wideout Ted Hurst will have a lot of reps to take over in the latter part of camp.
The Bucs face the New York Jets on Friday at 7 p.m. for their first preseason game of the year.

title: Fans May Have to Wait to See Buccaneers' Top Draft Pick Play in Preseason
full_text:
Fans in Tampa Bay collectively rejoiced the moment that Roger Goodell announced Rueben Bain Jr. would be the selection when the Buccaneers made their first pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Draft picks can be very contentious.
There are so many different players, positions and levels of competition to evaluate when considering which player will be the best fit for a given roster. Not only do these debates happen between NFL scouts and decision-makers, but also among fans as well.
However, when the Bucs selected Bain 15th overall this past April, it was pretty well unanimous amongst the fanbase that Tampa Bay had just hit a home run.
Not only was Bain a born-and-raised Floridian, but he played his college ball at Miami, where his dominating style of play off the edge helped the Hurricanes reach the National Championship game for the first time in almost a quarter of a century.
The Bucs have been in desperate need of an impact edge rusher for many years now. Bain's selection provides at least the potential for that dream to become a reality.
Bain's explosive power, relentless style of play, and versatility to both rush the passer and defend the run at a high level made for what could easily be considered the easiest decision in Jason Licht 's tenure as GM of the Bucs.
Although we've yet to see Bain make his NFL debut, the early returns have been extremely positive. Throughout minicamp, training camp and joint practices, Bain has earned the respect of his teammates, coaches, and the fans who have gotten the opportunity to watch him practice.
"I can't wait to see what he does this season." Even Reuben Bain Jr's teammates are excited to see what the rookie can do on the field this season after an impressive start to training camp. #WeAreTheKrewe #NFL #NFLNews | @FOX13News pic.twitter.com/Q5QH5Vlw8T
Everyone who has been impressed by what they've seen from Bain so far, though, is going to have to wait a little longer to see the dynamic defender in live game action.
On Tuesday, following the second day of Buccaneers' joint training camp practices with the New York Jets ahead of their preseason game on Friday, Todd Bowles informed the media that he doesn't see Bain playing much, if at all, in the game, per Jeff Dubrof.
Bowles doesn’t foresee Rueben Bain playing much if at all on Friday night #bucs
Although many fans who have been eagerly awaiting Bain's NFL debut may find themselves disappointed, this is a positive sign regarding the role that Bain has already carved out for himself on this football team.
Not only was Bain listed as a starter on the team's first unofficial depth chart which was recently released, but the fact that the team is likely to rest him in their first preseason game further cements his status as a likely starter on this football team.
Chances are, we will see Bain suit up for the Buccaneers this preseason. Just not yet.
This decision represents a logical big-picture approach to managing the explosive rookie's workload in his first offseason while ultimately limiting the injury risk he is exposed to. The positive takeaway from this particular decision is that fans can expect Rueben Bain Jr. to play a big role in Bowles' defense right away as a rookie.
If the talent, commitment and work ethic he's shown so far in his first few months as a pro are any indication of the NFL player he will become, then this is the right move.

title: One Buccaneers Player Who Missed Last Season Has Jason Licht Fired Up
full_text:
Buccaneers 2025 fourth-round pick David Walker has been very impressive throughout training camp to this point. Walker has been able to make a great number of plays in practice, having plenty of would-be sacks against backups and starters alike.
One person who is very excited to see what Walker can do this 2026 season is general manager Jason Licht.  According to Jason Licht, when speaking to WDAE, the excitement for Walker is "on an even plane" with that of rookie Rueben Bain Jr.
Now that is a pretty bold comparison for Licht to make, as Bain was the fifteenth overall pick in the most recent NFL Draft and Walker was a fourth-round selection last year. However, both players have looked very impressive in training camp so far and should be a very bright spot in a hopefully new and improved pass rush for the Bucs' defense this season.
Licht is not the only person in the Buccaneers organization to give praise to Walker. Speaking to the media on August sixth after practice, here is what head coach Todd Bowles had to say about what he's been impressed with regarding Walker.
"Just his energy and his athleticism [have] showed up," Bowles said. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves. He moves like an inside [linebacker], but he plays outside [linebacker] and he [has] great power. To see him out there playing fast and not worried about his knee is great."
Another player who had a very good impression of Walker was veteran pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad.
"He has a motor. The good ones, as far as [defensive] linemen and pass rushers, and all that good stuff, they play with a motor, and he plays with a motor. For his size, he knows who he is and the things that he [does], he [does] well. He's been having a [great] camp, so it's impressive."
Time will tell how much of an impact Walker will have this upcoming season. He's still competing for reps with a lot of players, including Muhammad, Bain Jr, and other veterans like Yaya Diaby, Anthony Nelson and even Chris Braswell if he does make the final roster. However, the organization certainly has a lot of high hopes for the young second-year player.

title: Will Baker Mayfield Play in Buccaneers' First Preseason Game vs. Jets?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gone through 10 days of training camp, including their joint practice with the New York Jets on Tuesday. After all of that, it's almost time for the team's first preseason game of the year.
The Bucs are set to face the Jets Friday, and when they do so, they'll be looking to evaluate many of their rookies for the first time under the lights. These games can be very important for that evaluation, and as a result, it's also important to make sure other players on the squad can play well enough around them to properly evaluate them.
With that in mind, head coach Todd Bowles has the decision on whether or not to play his starting quarterback in Baker Mayfield. The option is also worth considering in the wake of a potential injury to backup quarterback Jake Browning on Tuesday.
So will the Buccaneers play Mayfield in their first preseason outing this season?
Mayfield is not set to play during Tampa Bay's preseason game on Friday against the Jets. Initially, quarterback Jake Browning was set to start that game, but he injured his back during the first day of joint training camp, so his status on Friday is in jeopardy, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud.
Bucs No. 2 QB Jake Browning appeared to injure his back. Todd Bowles had no update but Browning was expected to start Friday vs Jets. He said Baker Mayfield will not play.
That makes sense. Mayfield is the team's starting quarterback, and it would be unusual to play him in the first preseason game of the year unless he specifically requested it as some quarterbacks do.
That being said, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield plays during the preseason at all. Last year, he skipped out on preseason entirely — he was slated to play during the team's second week of preseason against the Pittsburgh Steelers last year, but Bowles decided against it at the last minute and did not play him at all during the preseason.
There's a chance that a similar scenario could happen this preseason, too. For now, though, the Bucs will have to figure out what they plan to do on Friday if Browning isn't able to go — reps will be split between QBs Jalon Daniels and Connor Bazelak, if that's the case.
The Bucs play the Jets at 7 p.m. on Friday.

title: Baker Mayfield Wants His 'Lick Back' in Buccaneers 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers started out 6-2 in 2025, and things were looking up for quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield was an MVP candidate, and vibes were great in Tampa Bay.
Those vibes didn't end up continuing throughout the season, though. The Bucs went 2-7 over their last nine games and, presumably due to injuries, Mayfield's play deteriorated. Some thought that head coach Todd Bowles' job was in danger, but he kept his job and plans to coach the Bucs in 2026.
Mayfield and the rest of Tampa Bay's squad, who were there for the 2025 season, weren't happy about how it ended. Mayfield recently had a contract saga this offseason, where he placed a training camp deadline for an extension that he and the team did not meet, but he's stressed that he's all ball from here on out after that saga has come to a close.
Mayfield may be unhappy about his contract situation, but in a recent appearance on the 4th & South podcast with Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette, he seems far unhappier about what happened last season — and he's solely focused on fixing it.
Mayfield was very vocal about his disappointment after he couldn't get an extension done with the Bucs. He told Fournette and Landry that if some people are unhappy with that, it's too bad — but he promised to rectify the team's mistakes from last season this year.
"I've always worn my emotions and thoughts on my sleeve. If you like that, that's great. If you don't, that's too bad — I'm not gonna change for you," Mayfield said. "There's the business side of football. Yes, we all play this for a job, but they know that when it comes to gamedays, I'm ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026 — we didn't play well enough in 2025, so it's on go."
Baker Mayfield on contract negotiations not distracting him from how he’ll come to play in 2026 for Bucs. “They [team] knows when it comes to gamedays, I’m ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026. We didn’t play well in ‘25. It’s on go.” (via @4thAndSouthPod ) pic.twitter.com/zeGjg5V9rG
Tampa Bay and Mayfield could be in the position to do just that this season. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson could be a better option at offensive coordinator than Josh Grizzard, and new offensive weapons like running back Kenny Gainwell and wideout Ted Hurst could improve the offense in a big way.
There's still quite a bit of time until Mayfield can try and get that lick back. For now, though, the Bucs will continue joint training camp passes vs. the New York Jets this week before a preseason game on Friday.
