title: Multiple Fights Occur at Buccaneers Joint Practice vs. Jets
full_text:
Today was the first day of joint practices between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New York Jets, and to say that things got heated in practice is a bit of an understatement.
Multiple fights occurred during practice today between the two teams, with defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson being involved in one, per Jeff Dubrof, and offensive guard Luke Goedeke being involved in two, per Ralph Vacchiano .
The first fight that Goedeke was involved in included rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who wanted to go against Goedeke in one-on-one drills, which then resulted in said fight. This is what Goedeke had to say on the incident, per Pewter Report:
︀︀“Well, [David Bailey] called me out in one-on-ones and wanted to go against me and lost, and then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare], I believe, came from the side and just cheapshotted me."
Bucs RT Luke Goedeke on the practice fights with the Jets on Tuesday: “Well, [David Bailey] called me out in 1-on-1’s and wanted to go against me and lost. And then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare] I believe came from the side and just cheapshotted me." pic.twitter.com/AIP6fG7nw2
The Bucs were already dealing with some pushing and shoving matches occurring in their own training camp practices before making the jump to New Jersey to practice with the Jets. This is usually the time of year when teams get very antsy and are typically ready for live game reps and the regular season.
It is also important to remember that these two teams do have a bit of recent history. They played each other in a close matchup last season, where the Bucs would win 29-27. The Jets, however, came very close to winning said matchup on a blocked field goal that gave them the lead late. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would then be seen dancing down the sidelines as the Jets took the lead over the Bucs.
Also, the Bucs have spent a good amount of effort this off-season improving their mentality and grit when it comes to the roster. Players like A'Shawn Robinson were added to players like Luke Goedeke to give the team more of an edge and to help change some of the more laid-back attitude the team had in the past couple of seasons.
Overall, fights during practices are not ideal, but not surprising. Football is a very physical sport, and these things happen all the time. The Bucs and Jets face off on August 14th in the Bucs' first preseason matchup and should have another joint practice on the schedule soon. We'll see if more fighting occurs.

title: What Stands Out From the Buccaneers' First Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in New York to face off against the Jets during joint practice, which will culminate in a preseason game on Friday. The Bucs will have quite a few decisions to make once they see how their players look against other NFL teams over the next three weeks.
As of right now, though, they have at least a small idea. The Buccaneers put out their first unofficial depth chart of the year, and while it's mostly standard fare, there are a few interesting things to note.
Here's what we can glean from the Buccaneers' first depth chart of 2026:
The Bucs have released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 season. — Rueben Bain Jr. named starter — SirVoccea Dennis still listed as starter — Jacob Parrish starts over Benjamin Morrison at outside CB pic.twitter.com/AOHBHOFviO
Perhaps the biggest thing to note about the depth chart is what's going on at outside cornerback.
As it stands, defensive back Jacob Parrish looks to hold the starting outside corner spot alongside Zyon McCollum. Parrish, who excelled at the nickel corner spot last season for Tampa Bay to the tune of two interceptions, was moved to the outside room this offseason after the Bucs drafted Miami standout Keionte Scott to fill in at the nickel spot.
Parrish notably displaces Benjamin Morrison, who was set to fill that role alongside McCollum this offseason. Morrison injured his hamstring after the first OTAs practice and has not practiced in team drills since then, so he's had no opportunity to show his worth against Parrish so far. With that in mind, the ranking makes sense.
That isn't the only interesting development on the defensive side of the depth chart, though.
Many Buccaneers fans and NFL draft pundits are excited to see what second-round pick Josiah Trotter can do at the linebacker position for Tampa Bay this season. At the moment, though, he isn't listed as the team's starter.
Last year's starter, linebacker SirVocea Dennis, remains the incumbent starter on the first unofficial depth chart. Trotter has made some big plays in camp so far, but at the moment, it seems the team is valuing Dennis' experience in the system as training camp continues.
Edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. is listed as the starter on this depth chart, so it doesn't appear to be a matter of rookies not being placed as starters. That being said, Trotter has certainly made more splash plays than Dennis has over the course of camp, so it would be no surprise to see him overtake Dennis at some point this preseason.
The Bucs will wait to see how he plays in a game scenario, it seems. And if Trotter lives up to the hype from training camp so far, he should see himself climb the depth chart.

title: Why I'm Buying the Early Buccaneers Hype Around Ted Hurst
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in New York for joint practice sessions with the Jets after completing their first couple of weeks of training camp before their first preseason game.
There have already been a handful of standouts in camp, including the reemergence of David Walker and rookies Rueben Bain Jr. and Joshiah Trotter, who are showcasing exactly why the Bucs took them with their first two picks in the NFL Draft.
However, there has been another standout, this time on the offensive side of the ball, that I am buying the hype of: rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst.
The Bucs drafted Hurst in the third round, despite the young wideout coming from a lower-level program.
The thought is that it would take Hurst some time to adjust to the NFL and develop certain portions of his game.
And while there are still some areas of improvement as he continues his growth in acclimating to the league, the early reports are undeniable.
Hurst has been receiving early praise from his teammates and coaches alike, and for good reason.
With the Bucs' wideouts in and out of practice, for one reason or another, Hurst has stepped in for some first-team reps and continues to show why the Bucs took him in the third round.
He has looked fluid in and out of his breaks, which is spectacular given his six-foot-four frame, fast, mentally focused, strong at the point of attack, and great hands. And that doesn't even account for the fact that Todd Bowles loves how fast the rookie has picked up on the knowledge side of things.
Once looked at as a physical freak athlete that would need time to develop, it's time to really slow down and imagine how big of a role Hurst will have in the Bucs' offense that is already one of the more talented in the league.
While we are buying the early hype surrounding Hurst, he will have to continue this success into joint practices and the preseason to show he can do it against opposing defenses in live action.
Not only that, but continuing to be consistent will be key if he hopes to earn valuable reps alongside the likes of Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, Jalen McMillan, and even Tez Johnson.
Many have already started to make comparisons of Hurst to Buccaneers legend Mike Evans, and while we can see why, I don't believe he has to be Evans for him to be successful in Tampa Bay.

title: Is Todd Bowles's Patience Wearing Thin With Injured Cornerback?
full_text:
In contrast to the ongoing contractual issues surrounding some key veterans, the young players on the Buccaneers' roster appear to be trending in the right direction.
Not only are young defensive players like Jacob Parrish, Rueben Bain Jr., Josiah Trotter and Keionte Scott all making their impact felt during training camp, but offensive players like Tez Johnson, Ted Hurst, Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan are also turning heads.
Unfortunately, though, one promising young player for the Buccaneers who has not made a positive impression is cornerback Benjamin Morrison.
When Morrison slipped down partway through the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Bucs GM Jason Licht felt as though the talent was too much to pass up. Even if Morrison's injury history was the reason he was still on the board.
Although Morrison was able to recover from the hip surgery that cost him the majority of his final season at Notre Dame, it didn't take long for him to find the sidelines again as a pro.
Quad and hamstring injuries plagued Morrison throughout his rookie season, and when it was all said and done, he suited up for just 10 games total and made a minimal impact when he was on the field.
Heading into the 2026 offseason, Morrison — and the fans in Tampa — were optimistic that with a healthy training camp the young corner might finally be able to realize his talent at the NFL level.
Unfortunately, though, Morrison's OTAs and minicamp were cut short due to a soft tissue injury, and he's been on the sidelines for the entirety of training camp.
Following the Buccaneers' most recent practice this past weekend, Bucs' head coach Todd Bowles was asked about Morrison's recovery progress. Although he didn't say much, his response spoke volumes about how he feels.
"He's the same as usual," Bowles said.
Although Bowles isn't the type to openly criticize his players, this comment is a pretty clear indication that the Bucs' head coach's patience is wearing thin regarding Morrison's lack of availability.
Further emphasizing the frustration of all parties should be the fact that Morrison had a clear path to earning playing time this year, with the team having moved on from Jamel Dean, their best corner last year.
Does Morrison's most recent injury, or Bowles' comments about his availability, mean that Morrison couldn't carve out an important role on this football team? Absolutely not.
But based on how frequently Morrison has been on the sidelines as opposed to the practice field so far this offseason, it's safe to assume that he will have an uphill battle to earn his coach's trust, and ultimately, playing time on Sundays.

title: Buccaneers Sign New Cornerback, Part Ways With Injured Player
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gone through nine days of training camp already and are set to undergo some more tough joint practices against the New York Jets this week. To do that, they need healthy bodies.
The Bucs have done better in that regard than a lot of teams so far in camp, but one room has suffered. Tampa Bay's cornerback room has been beat up for a bit, and with a big joint training camp on the horizon, the team needs a healthy player to take some reps and land in the rotation.
The Bucs signed that player on Monday, and it's a familiar face. The team announced that it brought back cornerback Roman Parodie, and in return, waived CB Kemon Hall with an injury designation.
Bucs announce they’d signed CB Roman Parodie and waived/injured CB Kemon Hall.
The Buccaneers bring back Parodie from the 2025 preseason, where he was with the team and then subsequently released. Parodie attended Ohio University, where he recorded 124 total tackles, 28 passes defensed, four tackles for loss, four fumble recoveries, three interceptions and one forced fumble.
On the way out is Hall, whom the Buccaneers signed this offseason alongside former San Francisco 49ers CB Chase Lucas. The Bucs had hoped that both would provide depth and be able to play in a pinch if needed, but both of them became injured in training camp.
As a result, Hall and Lucas have both been waived with injured designations by Tampa Bay, and Parodie will take advantage. Parodie did not spend time with another team in 2025, but he did play for the Houston Gamblers of the UFL during the spring this past year.
He'll have his first chance to impress this upcoming week, when the Bucs face the Jets both in a joint practice and a preseason game. Parodie will likely get reps early, and Tampa Bay will be watching closely to see if he makes the most of them.

title: 4 Titans Players With the Most to Gain in Preseason Opener Against 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will play a football game for the first time in more than seven months on Thursday, as the team is set to open the preseason against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Tennessee had a joint practice with San Francisco on Tuesday and will now conclude its trip in Santa Clara with a preseason contest.
Head coach Robert Saleh said after practice on Tuesday that the Titans' starters will play Thursday night and even get more than one drive. It's critical for the starters to see the field a bit to prepare for the regular season, but still, this game isn't about them.
The main focus of Thursday's game is for players on the bubble to bolster their claims for a roster spot and raise their stock. With that in mind, let's take a look at four Titans who have the most to gain with a standout performance against the 49ers.
Entering camp, Williams was in danger of getting cut. However, he's been fantastic so far in camp, as Williams has significantly improved in pass coverage and is still playing with tenacity and power.
Saleh also commended Williams earlier in camp for losing 20 pounds this offseason , which explains why the Miami product is playing faster and fits well in the new-look defense.
If Williams carries his impressive play from practice into the first preseason game, he should secure a roster spot and make the Titans rethink the linebacker depth chart. Williams has outplayed Cody Barton and Mohamoud Diabate in camp, and if that continues, we could see the position group look a lot different than initially expected come Week 1.
Restrepo was the biggest winner of Tuesday's joint practice, as the 2025 undrafted free-agent receiver hauled in two touchdowns and led the team in catches with five. Restrepo has been making plays all camp and is pushing for a roster spot for the second straight year.
With Tennessee already having at least five roster locks at receiver in Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike, Restrepo is fighting for one of the final spots. Bryce Oliver will also likely make the roster due to his special teams ability.
However, if Restrepo posts a productive outing on Thursday, the Titans may consider keeping seven receivers and retaining the 24-year-old playmaker. Restrepo's connection with quarterback Cam Ward should also help him in roster arguments, but an exceptional preseason would go a long way for the young receiver's case.
Harrell has generated some pressure this camp, but overall, it's been a quiet last few weeks for the 2024 seventh-round pick.
Though Harrell hasn't made much noise in camp, the Michigan product ended the 2025 campaign on a high note , tallying 4.5 sacks in the final five games of the year and establishing himself as a key piece of the pass rush. However, he's fighting for a roster spot in Tennessee's deep edge rusher group.
Harrell must turn in a dominant preseason to ensure his future in Nashville for another year. The young pass rusher has proven that he can be an impact player in spurts, but Harrell must put it all together.
At this point, Levis would have to post a historic preseason to save his future with the Titans . The 2023 second-round pick likely won't be on the roster by September, but what Levis can do in the preseason, starting Thursday, is audition for his next team.
An efficient preseason where he takes care of the ball and leads the second-team and third-team offense on sustainable scoring drives could entice a team to give Levis another chance. The Kentucky product still possesses solid arm talent and mobility, but his decision-making and confidence are holding him back.
A team that wants to upgrade its backup quarterback situation or add a developmental signal-caller could take a flier on Levis and give the Titans a late-round pick in return. It would be a win-win for all parties involved.

title: Pro-Bowl LB Fred Warner Praises Cam Ward's Fearless Attitude for Titans
full_text:
Cam Ward isn't afraid to get his hands dirty. The Tennessee Titans quarterback has already garnered a reputation in the NFL for his brutal honesty, and according to San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner, that was on full display in the teams' recent joint practice.
In a clip from 95.7 The Game, the four-time Pro-Bowl defender praised Ward's fearless mindset, even as he stands across from one of the meanest defenses in the league. "I think Cam is one of the unique quarterbacks where he's not afraid to sit there and play that game with you," Warner said of Ward.
"I love joint practices, though. It's the best." Warner, after chirping with Ward all practice, was all smiles following the encounter. Ward also spoke on the matter, sharing a similarly positive outlook on their bickering.
“I think Cam (Ward) is one of the unique quarterbacks where he’s not afraid to sit there and play that game with you… I love joint practices, though. It’s the best (smirks).” 😈 Fred Warner on chirpin with Titans QB Cam Ward at joint practice pic.twitter.com/wgKJCtcjxJ
"That's what I want to see, because I want him to be at his best. So, when I'm at my best, I know what I can and can't do in a game," said Ward. "He helped me out a lot today, he's a great player."
Not every Titans player can share that optimism, as both Austin Deculus and Dan Moore Jr. got booted from practice due to their own altercations. But for Ward, it's healthy to get mixed up with an experienced defender this early in his career, especially if he doesn't take the beef to heart.
Ward embracing the trash talk also aligns well with Carnell Tate's "fast and violent" quote after the practice. Tennessee's rookie receiver saw the intensity as a benefit for the Titans more than anything else. The battle was a chance for Tennessee, in Tate's words, to prove "who we are."
Heading into Thursday's preseason opener against San Francisco, we'll be looking out for a Titans team playing with that tenacity on the whole.
After all, it'll be the same 49ers team that just attempted to bully the Titans all practice facing off against them again. Only this time, they'll have the benefit of a home field and a bastion of fans looking to witness their first win of the year.
On the opposite end of the spectrum, Ward and the Titans are trying to make an early statement to the NFL under their new head coach. That sets the stage for an unusually tense preseason matchup.
We'll have the coverage of tomorrow night's game here. Hopefully Ward's talkative tendencies carry over into that duel, as they seem to translate to similarly bold play on the field.

title: Carnell Tate Reaffirms Titans 'Fast and Violent' Mentality Ahead of Preseason Brawl With 49ers
full_text:
If the Tennessee Titans' joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers was any indication of what their preseason matchup is going to be like, we could be in for a real heater. Punches were thrown and two players were ejected (both from Tennessee's camp). After the intense run, Carnell Tate was asked if the clash served as a "reality check" for Tennessee.
"It didn't feel like a reality check at all," Tate responded quickly. "We went out there and proved to them who we are... We're the Titans, we came here to play fast and violent." Tennessee's X account took the quote and ran with it and, voila, we have our table dressing for Thursday night's opener.
Beyond the entertaining optics, however, lies a mindset that seems to have permeated the entirety of this Titans team. Keen fans will remember Robert Saleh using "fast and violent" to describe his hopes for Tennessee, all the way back in January.
Let ‘em know, Carnell! pic.twitter.com/b6vMO6DiD8
The phrasing has been used a few times since, but with the beginning of the season so near, it seems like Tennessee is actually beginning to implement it. Those words were present on the field yesterday, no doubt.
Tate repeating them once again confirms that this Tennessee team is prepared to bring the fire.
Given the Titans' struggles in yesterday's practice, this may seem like a moot point at first. Who cares how you think you're playing if you're actively being outplayed?
Yet, there may be some merit yet in Tennessee taking on such an aggressive mindset. Titans fans aren't all that far removed from Brian Callahan's most recent team; one that was criticized again and again for their distinct lack of fight and grit.
Tennessee's shutout loss to the Houston Texans in week four, 26-0, epitomized those failures. The entire point of bringing in a new leader was to do away with Callahan's failures on the sideline. It may not be such a bad thing to embrace this squad's self-imposed identity, even if they're not yet out of the rebuilding phase.
Assuming yesterday's practice reports were as telling as they seemed, the 49ers will have the upper hand in the preseason opener. But this is the first Titans team in a while that may benefit from having a hill to climb. In fact, they may even prefer it that way.

title: 4 Major Takeaways from Titans' Heated Joint Practice with 49ers: Day 3 Rookie Continues to Shine
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans and San Francisco 49ers held a heated joint practice on Tuesday. Both teams will square off again on Thursday night in a preseason contest at Levi's Stadium.
Tuesday's practice between the Titans and 49ers was incredibly physical, as there were multiple fights and it seemed like there was extracurricular activity after nearly every play. San Francisco clearly wanted to set the tone and get under Tennessee's skin.
Though tempers flaring was the main storyline of the day, there is still a lot to discuss from practice on Tuesday. Let's take a look at the key takeaways for the Titans.
After a quiet start to camp, Carmona has been making a ton of noise in recent practices , and Tuesday was no different. According to ESPN's Turron Davenport, the fifth-round rookie received early first-team reps at right guard during the scrimmage period against the 49ers. In practice, Carmona contributed a key block on a Cam Ward touchdown pass, though the rookie also committed a costly false start during an end-of-practice two-minute drill.
Tuesday marked the second straight practice Carmona worked with the starting offense, and head coach Robert Saleh praised the Arkansas product for earning his opportunities . However, Saleh also confirmed that right guard is still an open competition.
"You gotta earn it to get in there [with the first-team], but he's been doing a nice job," Saleh said about Carmona. "But like I said, with that right guard spot, we're gonna keep working to find the best player for it."
Carmona is definitely in the running for the starting right guard gig with Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater. We can now officially call this position battle a three-player race entering the preseason opener.
It was an up-and-down for quarterback Cam Ward and the offense. According to Davenport and Buck Reising of A to Z Sports, the passing game was in sync early , as Ward started with a few completions to wide receivers Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate. Rookie running back Nicholas Singleton also had a few nice runs .
However, it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. Will Levis threw an interception , Mitchell Trubisky struggled to evade pressure, and Ward also had his missteps. The Titans' QB1 tossed a pick-six to 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown and failed to lead Tennessee to a score on the aforementioned two-minute drill to end the day. Ward went 16-of-23 on the day , with a touchdown to Ridley and running back Tony Pollard, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com.
One guy who had a splendid day was wide receiver Xavier Restrepo, who led the team with five catches, including two touchdowns, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com. Restrepo is continuing to showcase his playmaking ability and is building a compelling roster case.
It's clear Brian Daboll's offense has a lot to work on, but it wasn't all bad at the same time either. The group should learn from Tuesday and use it to bolster their attack.
The Titans' secondary has had its struggles in camp containing Tate and Elic Ayomanor, but there hasn't been much panic. However, facing a new opponent on Tuesday, the unit didn't look much better.
ESPN 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner reported strong days for San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy and wide receivers Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling. Reising also noticed Robinson beating Titans safety Amani Hooker for a touchdown.
Additionally, Bonta Hill of NBC Sports Bay Area & California said that Purdy hit on a lot of downfield strikes on Tuesday, and David Lombardi of The San Francisco Standard jotted down multiple touchdowns for 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel during red-zone drills.
Though we're still early in the camp and the preseason, the Titans can't afford to be prone to allowing explosive plays in 2026, especially with the amount of money they committed to starting corners Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott. The secondary needs to step up sooner rather than later.
This was one of the most intense joint practices we've seen in a while. The benches cleared early in practice when 49ers cornerback Renardo Green shoved Wan'Dale Robinson out of bounds. Coaches were able to break things up, but that was a sign of things to come.
There were too many skirmishes and back-and-forths to include, but the major takeaway was offensive tackles Austin Deculus and Dan Moore Jr. getting ejected from practice. According to Nick Suss of The Tennessean, Deculus threw a punch at a 49ers defender within the first 10 minutes and was kicked out. About an hour later, Moore was also thrown out for getting into a fight with 49ers defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa.
San Francisco brought the heat, and though Tennessee responded, it's clear Saleh's squad was flustered at times. We should see growth from the Titans in this area, as the team is still pretty young and just needs more experience.
Saleh confirmed after practice that the Titans starters will play in the preseason contest on Thursday. Saleh added that he'll also leave the starters out there for more than a series, so they should get some good work in.
Overall, it wasn't an awful joint practice from the Titans, but it's evident that they have some stuff to clean up before Week 1. The 49ers have been a consistent playoff contender for nearly a decade, so Tuesday was a fantastic opportunity for the Titans to see where they stand with a few weeks to go in camp.

title: Tempers Flare in Titans Practice With 49ers as Tennessee's QBs Seriously Struggle
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans prepared for their preseason debut against the San Francisco 49ers this week by taking part in a joint practice out west. If today's unofficial meeting between the two teams is any indication, we could be in for a real mess on Thursday, and for more reasons than one.
Not only did tempers flare to an extreme degree in the practice, with both Austin Deculus and Dan Moore being outright ejected, but the Titans quarterbacks reportedly struggled to find their footing overall. Per Turron Davenport, Will Levis threw an interception to Jakob Robinson. Tennessee's long-time depth piece under center has had a rough offseason thus far.
Elsewhere, Cam Ward gave up a pick six to San Francisco's Upton Stout, missing a wide open Carnell Tate, according to Cesar Bass. The cherry on top was Mitch Trubisky being swarmed by the 49ers defense as, in Davenport's words, "No one stopped the pass rush."
Ward would ultimately end up escaping with two touchdowns, but to say that it sounds like a long day for Tennessee's offense overall would be an understatement. It's not quite fair to forge any real worries out of reported practice struggles, but you couldn't be blamed for suspecting that Thursday's game could pan out poorly for the Titans as a result.
Of course, Robert Saleh is fresh off of his latest stint serving as the 49ers' defensive coordinator. That means this practice, and more importantly Thursday's game, each serve as a bit of a homecoming for the head coach.
Having one of his offensive lineman be thrown out of a practice for throwing a punch probably wasn't Saleh's ideal start, but he and Tennessee have time to turn things around before their actual matchup with San Francisco.
Besides, on their home (practice) field facing off against a coach that just ditched their unit, it isn't a huge surprise that the 49ers defense came out and bared their teeth. After all, that bunch has been consistently known as one of the best in the entire NFL. Try not to take this news to heart, Titans fans.
However, everyone will be looking for a little more composure when Tennessee actually takes the field... to say the least. Preseason or not, throwing punches and picks won't cut it for a team expected to take a major leap this season.
Regardless of the eventual outcome, improvement from the personnel under center would go a long way to quiet the hearts of folks reading the practice reports from today. Levis, if he ends up with playing time, could use a leap following his shortcomings at Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage last week.
None of this is worth panicking over. At the same time, however, the team's optics were far from pretty coming out of this practice. All eyes are on Thursday's game.

title: 3 Players Primed for an Offensive Breakout in the Titans Preseason
full_text:
With preseason competition officially upon us, the Tennessee Titans are getting ready to trot out a Robert Saleh roster in live competition for the first time. Fans have impatiently waited all offseason for a sneak peek, but as the preseason usually goes, we'll likely be looking at depth above all else.
Still, that doesn't mean there won't be opportunities for guys to break out prior to regular season play. Beyond a few minutes for Cam Ward and his starters, we've circled three names that could see a seriosu uptick in production on the offensive side of the ball this preseason.
Titans faithful, watch out for this trio of playmakers, starting Thursday vs. the 49ers this week.
Osborn might be the sneakiest pick on this list. The speedy wide receiver, entering his fifth season in the NFL, had previously made a respectable name for himself with the Minnesota Vikings as a rotation piece.
An uneventful pitstop with the New England Patriots last year dampened his stock, but Osborn's seven-touchdown rookie campaign continues to suggest a ceiling he's yet to return to. He should get a solid share of touches in the preseason and, given Osborn's past and the circumstances of his one-year deal, there's reason to think he could finally snap back into previous form in Tennessee.
Singleton, who was taken in the fifth round of this year's NFL Draft, has a long-term path to taking over the Titans running back room on the whole. He's an extremely talented back with four years of experience at Penn State to back him up. In three of those campaigns, he scored at least 12 touchdowns.
Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are holding things down in that unit for now, but don't be surprised if Singleton comes out swinging in the preseason. Saleh will want to know what he has in this rookie, and Singleton's collegiate metrics point to a player capable of getting hot early in the league.
Restrepo has become a popular roster hopeful for Titans fans, if not only for his college connection with Ward. As he continues to battle for a roster spot, Restrepo's preseason showing could make or break his ultimate bid.
Expect the second-year receiver to come out hungrier than ever, and given his (relative) veteran status on the team, you can also expect Restrepo to get a ton of touches. Few on the roster, if anyone, will have a better chance to prove their place than Restrepo this preseason.

title: Pat McAfee's Comparison for Carnell Tate Should Leave Titans Fans Ecstatic
full_text:
The Carnell Tate train has thoroughly caught fire as clips from the Tennessee Titans training camp begin to emerge online. The rookie receiver is making an early case for Offensive Rookie of The Year with viral toe-taps and one-handed snags that are sending Tennessee fans into a frenzy. But it isn't only those in and around Nashville that are taking notice.
On yesterday's segment of his show, Pat McAfee touched on the Tate trend, dropping only positive remarks about Cam Ward's newest weapon. "This Ohio State wide receiver factory they got cooking might have found the next Terry McLaurin here," McAfee declared, shortly after lauding Tate's acrobatics in practice.
"Not as hyped as everybody else," McAfee went on, "but still unbelievable. That could be Carnell Tate's trajectory, quickly." Football fans may know McAfee for his televised antics first and foremost, but as a former player himself, this praise doesn't present as a grain of salt.
Tate, while a little lengthier than McLaurin, shares his collegiate past as a Buckeye with the Washington Commanders pass-catcher. As McAfee noted, this isn't necessarily a loud comparison, but don't let the non-superstar nature of this bid fool you.
McLaurin is a long-term professional stud, and Titans fans should be thrilled with such an outlook this early in Tate's run.
Not only has McLaurin been to the Pro Bowl twice, but he's also got a hefty share of 1,000 yard seasons to his name. In fact, from 2020-2024, McLaurin met this metric five straight times. The 30-year old playmaker has put together a bejewled career that anyone would be lucky to replicate.
In Tate, the Titans have a receiver worthy of those lofty expectations, if he isn't expected to surpass them.
Taking a player with the fourth overall pick comes with expectations attached, after all. Whether or not it's fair to saddle a rookie with the weight of an offense, or even a franchise (see Cam Ward), is irrelevant to what struggling teams most often ask of their new guys.
Fortunately for Tate, while he certainly appears worthy of a task like that, he won't have to lead the Titans alone. Brian Daboll's offense appears fully equipped to allow Tate to ease into his role as Ward looks to the likes of Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm, and others from under center.
Buckeyes are as Buckeyes do. Tate is the latest Ohio State receiver in a long line of successful draft picks, and his scenario in Tennessee suggests that McAfee's projection is right on the money.

title: 5 Titans Players to Watch Closely in Tennessee's Joint Practice and Preseason Opener vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have a busy week ahead of them in Santa Clara. Robert Saleh's group will square off against the San Francisco 49ers in a joint practice on Tuesday and then play a preseason game with Kyle Shanahan's group at Levi's Stadium on Thursday.
Tuesday's joint practice and Thursday's preseason opener will be the first time we see this new-look Titans squad against another team . Tennessee's starters should see a ton of action in the practice, while depth players and those on the roster bubble will likely dominate most of the preseason game.
With the Titans ramping up camp and finally kicking off the preseason in the coming days, let's take a look at five players to watch closely this week.
Grouping these two may seem odd, but how could I not? Ward and Tate have already built a strong rapport through the first few weeks of camp , with the pair connecting on three touchdowns during Tennessee's most recent practice on Sunday.
Ward and Tate won't see much action in the preseason contest, but the joint practice will be a different story. Tate will likely be matched up against the 49ers' top cornerback, Deommodore Lenoir, who will be a solid test for the No. 4 overall pick. Lenoir has started 64 games over five years since joining San Francisco as a fifth-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
As for Ward, it'll be interesting to see how he picks apart this 49ers defense led by defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. When healthy, San Francisco's defense figures to be one of the top units in the league, but with superstar edge rusher Nick Bosa missing multiple practices in a row due to soreness , they aren't at full strength.
Regardless, Ward and Tate don't have an easy practice ahead of them on Tuesday. They will need to be at their best for the Titans' offense to flourish against a 49ers defense that is still formidable, so Tuesday's practice will tell us how far along Brian Daboll's unit is in its progression, especially his quarterback and No. 1 receiver.
Restrepo is fighting for a roster spot , and though he hasn't had an eye-popping camp, the Miami product has stayed consistent and isn't having many bad days , either.
Though Restrepo should garner some reps during Tuesday's practice, more eyes will be on him during Thursday's game. Restrepo will receive a ton of work, and if he can stand out as a playmaker while also adding value on special teams, the 24-year-old will bolster his roster case.
With the amount of talent in the receiver room, the Titans could opt to keep seven players in the position group instead of the usual six, which would significantly increase Restrepo's roster odds. However, he can't worry about that right now. All Restrepo must focus on taking full advantage of his opportunities, especially in preseason action.
Carmona had his breakout day of camp on Sunday , as the fifth-round rookie finally earned first-team reps and made the most of them. According to A to Z Sports, Carmona contributed multiple crucial blocks on a long run by running back Tyjae Spears, and his helmet came off in the process.
If Carmona can play with that same intensity this week, he could spoil the party for Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater, who have been competing for the starting right guard spot for most of camp.
Like Restrepo, Carmona will see more action in the preseason contest on Thursday. We'll see how the Arkansas product performs as he has a legitimate opportunity to work his way into starting discussions on the offensive line.
The first big test of Latham's make-or-break Year 3 begins Tuesday. With the 49ers' defensive line currently ravaged by injuries , the offensive line, especially Latham, has no excuses to struggle this week and should impose its will.
Outside of being involved in a skirmish with All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons last week and a few updates here and there, we haven't heard too much about Latham since he came off the PUP list, which is usually a good thing for an offensive lineman. Latham has the frame and talent to be a dominant right tackle in this league, but the Alabama product must stay healthy in 2026 and continue his momentum from a strong finish to 2025, when he allowed zero sacks in Tennessee's final four games.

title: Titans Unveil Color Combo as New Uniforms Debut in Preseason Duel With 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' preseason duel this Thursday with the San Francisco 49ers is exciting for a number of reasons, not the least of which being the team's long-awaited uniform debut. After the Titans announced their new look earlier this offseason, folks from every fanbase widely lauded the look. Now, we know exactly what combo Tennessee is rocking in their first playing in the kit.
The Titans will pop out in white-on-white up top, with their helmets and jerseys both matching the typical road look. The baby blue pants will complete the getup, fully presenting the team's first aesthetic change of any sort since 2018.
Even then, it wasn't as serious an overhaul as the one that the franchise has undergone this year. The Titans' rebrand will be exasperated when seen against a 49ers team known for their own classic, virtually unchanged aesthetic, Tennessee's updated outerwear will clash loudly in the team's technical first contest this season.
Titans to begin their new aesthetic era in ... WHITE WHITE TITANS BLUE pic.twitter.com/qET8q2x7D0
Jim Wyatt also reported that the Titans will go with white socks to tie the bow off on their improved fashion statement. Every detail matters, especially for a franchise making its first statement since wiping the slate clean in every sense of the word.
This complete redo couldn't come at a better time for what has been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past two seasons. Tennessee's combined 6-28 record, marred most recently by Brian Callahan's midseason firing, turned the team into a league-wide laughing stock.
The Titans weren't able to keep up in the AFC South, let alone the rest of the NFL. Under Robert Saleh, however, this is undoubtedly a much different team. Will it be a better team? Everybody sure hopes so, and the team's laundry list of draftees and signees should have a positive impact on the winning column.
But regardless of the eventual result, the Titans' updated palette helps the feeling that the franchise has fully committed to turning the page. Fans were bought into Cam Ward already, but add an impressive run in free agency and guitar strings on the team's helmets? This is a brand new ordeal.
So long as everything goes to plan, it'll be a brand new result, too. As the wait to see this team take the field finally winds down, don't blame Titans fans for dropping a few thousand likes online for a color combo reveal. Let Nashville have this one.

title: Jayden Daniels Draws Line With LSU Over No. 5 Jersey
full_text:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has become involved in an unexpected dispute with his alma mater, LSU. According to ESPN , the dispute stems from the quarterback, who won the 2023 Heisman Trophy in an LSU uniform, being upset that the school has allowed another player to wear his No. 5. Daniels’ attorney, Adam Kenner, informed LSU in a letter dated August 5 that the school can no longer use his name, image, and likeness. This story has two separate elements — the legal demand concerns LSU’s continued use of Daniels’ NIL, while a statement from Daniels’ spokesperson says the larger dispute centers on the school giving sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett the No. 5 jersey. Pickett wore No. 3 last season and was wearing the No. 5 jersey when the Tigers opened preseason practice last week, which prompted questions about the swap. "The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU's decision to give Jayden's number to another player," the statement from Daniels' spokesperson said. "Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university."
Daniels’ camp believes he is being treated differently from Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, whose No. 9 has not been issued by LSU since his Heisman Trophy and national-championship season in 2019. Former LSU coach Brian Kelly, who was fired in October, acknowledged that Pickett had been promised the number during his recruitment but said he refused to issue it because Daniels objected. "I just wasn't prepared to do it until we got a full commitment from another Heisman Trophy winner," Kelly said. "We didn't want to issue No. 9, so you can't treat one differently from the other." LSU's first-year head coach Lane Kiffin believes the school should honor its recruiting commitment to Pickett. "DJ is in [No.] 5, and that was a situation that was promised to him in recruiting here, for him to sign here," Kiffin said. "I've done a lot of research on that with the family and the representatives and the people, so really I didn't have a decision to make. It was promised to the kid; it wasn't done for whatever [reason]. I'm not going to get into that. "I'm not going to judge something [that was done] when I wasn't here. But when a kid is promised something to come to a school, he should wear it. So, at that point, I don't think that's really my decision. We should honor what he was told." LSU’s own jersey-retirement policy basically states that an athlete must have completed competition for five years before being nominated for jersey retirement, and he or she must have "demonstrated truly unusual and outstanding accomplishments, such as winning a Heisman Trophy or National Player of the Year award, and it should be based on the total LSU career." The No. 20 jersey worn famously by halfback Billy Cannon , who was LSU's first Heisman Trophy winner in 1959, is the only number that cannot be worn again by a football player.
Separately, Daniels' attorney says the NIL agreement that was in place between Daniels and LSU had a shelf life of 180 days after his last college game, which has long since expired. Kenner's position is that LSU no longer has contractual permission to use Daniels' name, image, and likeness. The irony in this one is semi-strong for fans of the burgundy and gold, with the news that Stefon Diggs was requesting to use Joe Theismann's No. 7 , forcing Washington's hand to eventually respond to situations involving iconic numbers that are soft-retired. Of course, the situation also has a clear difference: Theismann has deferred the decision to the Commanders, while Daniels’ camp is making it clear that he believes the player whose legacy created the significance of the number should have a voice in what happens to it. The news has nothing to do with Daniels' professional career, but offers a pretty revealing look at how strongly the Commanders quarterback feels about protecting the legacy he left behind in Baton Rouge.

title: The Good and Not So Good From Commanders vs. Dolphins Joint Practice
full_text:
Wednesday marked the 11th Washington Commanders Training Camp practice and also the team's joint practice session with the Miami Dolphins. Washington's records confirmed this was indeed the first official NFL joint practice held on the Ashburn grounds. Given the ability to finally test its new offense, new defense, and developing roster against unfamiliar players rather than their own teammates, Wednesday's practice carried way more weight than the previous ten. The first outside test went very well, with multiple areas, including an incredible day by Jayden Daniels , a deep and productive receiver room, and a defense that spent much of the morning in Miami’s backfield. Washington still had difficulty generating an interior running game, while some offensive-line execution issues remained visible.
long ball to Burks ✊ @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Hlb14ySbYg
Jayden Daniels looked much like the same player who has been checking every box for the last ten practice sessions on Wednesday. Daniels finished 12-for-16 in team periods, with two incompletions coming on defensive pass breakups, another on a batted red-zone pass, and one badly thrown pass. Daniels looked comfortable from under center and particularly in the play-action boot game, throwing accurately while moving outside the pocket rather than needing to settle into traditional dropbacks. Daniels hit Van Jefferson deep, found Terry McLaurin for roughly 30 yards on the sideline, and connected with Chig Okonkwo for another 27-yard gain. The Treylon Burks over-route on second-and-6 was one of the best examples of how the offense is supposed to work: play action created space behind the linebackers, and Daniels layered the ball into Burks. Daniels went 4-for-5 with two underneath completions to Diggs and another precise throw to Okonkwo to move the chains during the two-minute period.
🎥 Jason Marshall Jr. vs. Terry McLaurin in 1v1s in joint practice today. ( @CommandersMusee ) #PhinsUp pic.twitter.com/nTK5ug1aBg
The Washington receiver room showed out against Miami with their best day of camp to date. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both dominated receiver/DB one-on-ones, winning all of their matchups. Diggs was clearly the class of the group; his route running consistently created separation that carried over into team periods, and he also caught a touchdown from Daniels near the back of the end zone during red-zone work. Treylon Burks had a productive day , and Van Jefferson showed some strong sideline skills as he continues to show why Dan Quinn is consistently mentioning his name. Antonio Williams continues to make defenders look silly with his twitchy moves; today he caught a red-zone touchdown pass after lining up in the backfield next to Mariota. The rookie just finds a way to produce no matter how they feed him the ball. Diggs and McLaurin give Washington its stars, but Wednesday suggested the supporting receiver group may have more usable options behind them than it appeared to have before camp.
another Tone tuddy 🙂‍↕️ @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/k5o1ZR5khh
Washington's defensive front disrupted pretty much everything Miami attempted on the morning. Miami's offensive line probably understands how the Commanders' o-linemen have felt the last ten days after spending the morning getting pushed around. It was hard to keep up with the number of pressures, tackles for loss, and disruptive plays, but there were a lot. Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson spent most of the session harassing Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. Chaisson had multiple would-be sacks and made life hard on Miami's blockers. Daron Payne was another player who was able to get after Willis. Joshua Josephs continued his tour of chaos, getting into Quinn Ewers’ face quickly enough on play action that it would have resulted in another sack in live football. The fact that Josephs was able to get the same result via contact against Miami's players tells us his camp surge is real. Mike Sainristil’s pick-six against Willis was likely the play of the day. Jake Moody and Drew Stevens both bounced back with bigger eyes on them Wednesday after sharing their worst days of camp Monday. The two both went 6-for-6, with field goals from 33, 38, 43, 48, 52, and 60 yards, with the 60-yarder representing their longest attempts of camp. Stevens is still very much in the driver's seat in terms of overall camp body of work, but Moody's rebound of a day tells me he is not done yet.
Every team needs a guy with Amik Robertson’s confidence. Robertson believe the Commanders dominated the Dolphins in joint practice. pic.twitter.com/jEKsrg2gIQ
Washington has time before the season starts, but the interior line issues they are currently tracking have some concerning flaws. Since it's early, I'll try to watch for improvement, but it is definitely currently the team's weakness without Nick Allegretti on the field . For the most part, pass protection was not an issue, but the team was getting little to no push up front, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt continuously stuffed without much space up the gut. It's hard to know what exactly the issue was without being in the huddle; at this point, all we can do is make note of it and see what we see in the preseason. After losing Laremy Tunsil and while continuing to sort out the center position, Washington seeing its interior run game consistently lose against unfamiliar defenders is concerning. The offense is still working through some technical issues, with the first-team period containing at least one false start call, which they have had continuous issues with in camp. Rookie center Matt Gulbin had multiple bad snaps , not a good sign in a situation where Washington is trying to fix the center problem, or at least provide depth without anyone running away with the job. While neither issue erased the overall good day, these self-inflicted mistakes could come back to haunt this team once the regular season begins. Daniels looked every bit as comfortable against Miami as he has against his own defense, while Washington’s receivers gave him options at every level. The defensive line also carried their havoc-wreaking ways over into the joint session, making Miami's offensive linemen struggle for everything. Washington closed the session with something concrete to attack now, namely an interior running game and offensive execution that need improvement before Friday’s preseason opener.

title: Three Commanders Players on the Outside Looking In Who Could Still Force Their Way Onto the Final 53
full_text:
The Washington Commanders kicked off their first joint practice with the Miami Dolphins today, the latest step in the lead-up to the teams' preseason debut on Friday. Their priorities from competitive and developmental standpoints will soon be thrust before a national audience, potentially revealing the Commanders' preferences regarding the tough decisions coming their way.
In a little over two weeks, Washington's evaluators will have to make a slew of cuts to trim the roster down to the final 53 contributors, and their retooled roster is fortunately crowded enough to complicate some of the fringier decisions. Depending on how the next few practices and scrimmages go, a few second-, third-, and fourth-stringers have the chance to elevate into or maintain their positions as regular-season staples.
The 6'4 tight end out of UCLA went undrafted two years ago, but he's remained a familiar face around D.C. ever since getting gifted a chance to build on his athletic gifts in Washington.
Despite only attracting three targets and collecting a mere 18 total yards across 20 career outings, he's made an intriguing case for himself as the newest dark horse to uplift Jayden Daniels' offense thanks to some electric training camp highlights. Yankoff seemingly catches everything thrown his way with a little extra pizzazz, something the quarterback would appreciate even after the team's recent Stefon Diggs acquisition .
knee slide goes crazy @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/FAg9gcP1oz
The only complication standing in Yankoff's way is the already-deep position group he's forced to contend with. They already have an agile pass-catcher in Chig Okonkwo , a blocking specialist in John Bates , and their very own untapped wild card in Ben Sinnott . Should Yankoff look to earn a place as a regularly appearing option or red zone threat, he'll have to spend the next few weeks continuing to commit to his niche in convincing the staff to expand the room into a foursome.
Before Diggs signed, the Commanders had spent most of their offseason looking for playable wide receivers in the league's bargain bin. One of the names they brought in early on in free agency, Dyami Brown, has much more to prove beyond seizing a bench role alongside a familiar group of guys.
The Commanders' third-round draftee from 2021 spent four years puttering around D.C. as a backup wideout, eventually enjoying a career-high 30 receptions during the Commanders' whirlwind 2024 campaign. Following that run to the NFC Championship Game, he opted to bet on himself by jumping to the Jacksonville Jaguars, but his subpar catch rate contributed to his being pulled from that starting lineup shortly before the Jaguars' strong late-season finish.
If he has any chance left to break his way back onto a 53-man roster , it'll be in Washington, the last (and only) place he ever enjoyed 300 receiving yards in a season. And though the veteran has a chance to join Daniels' scoring corps, the competition he's up against is subtly stiff.
Outside of obvious starters Diggs and Terry McLaurin , he'll also face a slew of similarly-hand-drafted options in Antonio Williams , Luke McCaffrey , and Jaylin Lane . Again, if we could eliminate someone else from falling through the cracks in upstart prospect Williams, there's a chance that either McCaffrey or Lane falls short in impressing the Washington masses due to their similar return-friendly skill sets and lack of short-field creativity, while the reclamation project that is Treylon Burks only barely seems safer than journeyman Van Jefferson .
Pro Football Plus: Spotlight on WR #6 Dyami Brown, he talks about how talented the WR room is and how he sees himself as they head into the first preseason game of season. Always fun chopping it up with him. pic.twitter.com/65bF1mAQN3
Should a few of those factors break in his favor, Brown may have a direct channel back to his old in-house standing.
Add the Commanders' safety depth to their list of jumbled positions without much in the way of clear headliners.
Here's what we know: Nick Cross , one of Washington's crown jewels of the offseason, will play a key starting role along the defensive backfield. Jeremy Reaves , Quan Martin , and Will Harris will return in their own regularly rotating roles. Those four names should fill out the majority of the squad's safety snaps, but a third-stringer could certainly help by adding another viable option.
Something to monitor… Percy Butler has been getting some decent run with the 1’s today… Replacing Reaves primarily …
The Commanders have done their due diligence in giving Percy Butler chances against real competition during their scrimmages, but he, too, has a long way to go before fortifying himself as a made man. Despite four seasons' worth of healthy chances, the speedy disruptor's yet to separate from the pack, notching just 14 tackles over 16 appearances and a lone start in 2025.
Most of those aforementioned safety options not named Cross haven't been great in coverage in camp, let alone on the field as members of the Commanders' lackluster secondary of old, so it doesn't bode well for Butler that he remains this far down the totem pole amidst such a so-so group. But given the holes that need filling, he still has a chance to beat out Malik Spencer for a shot at the final 53.

title: Commanders' Stefon Diggs Already Exceeding Dan Quinn's High Expectations
full_text:
Just days after arriving, receiver Stefon Diggs is already exceeding the extremely high expectations that the Washington Commanders had for him. That's not to say he has finished learning the system yet; Washington continues to work him into an installation that was already several days in when he was signed.
Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs' football smarts and instincts have already surpassed his expectations. He's good against man and zone and there have been more explosive plays since he joined the team. pic.twitter.com/pkOFtWS4KV
On Tuesday, when Quinn was asked whether he has noticed more explosiveness from Washington's offense since Diggs arrived , his response gives a good feel for where the staff is with him. "Well, I would say yeah, in some ways I have," said Quinn with a twinkle in his eye. "There's already been some explosive play passes. The interesting thing about Steph , like a smart player, is he good against zone? He knows how to sit down. Like he's good against both, you know, in terms of zone, man-to-man. He knows, you know, how to get himself open." "His football smarts and instincts are — I thought they were going to be like really high, and they're already past that," said Quinn about Diggs. "So, we're in the early days. He's still learning it, but yeah, he's already making an impact for sure." Exceeding already high expectations is a good way to get noticed. Doing it while still technically behind everyone else, who had the entire offseason and opening portion of camp to ramp up with the language and timing of the new system, is a good way to show you are still at the top of your craft. With Daniels and Diggs already working on chemistry in practice, things are on the right track. It is important to remember that Washington does not need Diggs to completely master the offense before his experience, instincts, and route awareness begin creating something the passing game did not have before his arrival.
Diggs comin’ at ya pic.twitter.com/KLVn6e81Nf
Quinn also believes the younger receivers can benefit from having both McLaurin and Diggs available. "But also, there's a good byproduct of things that he's adding," Quinn said. "What can they do? You know, like adding another veteran receiver to your room. Like, they lean on Terry a lot. Now having the ability to, you know, go through things with Steph — that's pretty valuable for Antonio and Luke and, you know, Jay in a lot of ways too." The effect is already operating in both directions because Washington's receivers are helping Diggs translate the new terminology while Diggs is bringing years of knowledge about concepts he has already run elsewhere.
It's still early, and Diggs has only just begun the process of developing timing with Daniels and learning the details of Washington's system. The evolving roles of the Commanders' receiver room will start taking a more solid shape in the coming weeks. Washington expected Diggs to bring unusually high football intelligence and veteran instincts; Quinn just didn't expect those traits to stand out this quickly.

title: Joe Theismann Leaves Stefon Diggs’ No. 7 Decision to Washington — Commanders Daily
full_text:
A few days ago, newly signed receiver Stefon Diggs posted online, saying he wants to use the iconic No. 7 that former Redskins quarterback Joe Theismann wore during his career, including Super Bowl XVII. The number has remained out of circulation except for brief usage by the late Dwayne Haskins, who asked Theismann directly to use it.
Tuesday, Theismann addressed the situation while speaking with 106.7's Grant Paulsen: "The jersey belongs to the football team. I was honored to wear it. I will leave it to the Commanders to make that decision." Now, for those of you keeping score at home, Theismann did not explicitly give Diggs permission to wear No. 7, but he also did not object, instead putting the decision entirely in Washington’s hands.
Talking with @Theismann7 about Stefon Diggs wanting wear his No. 7 that isn't currently in circulation: "The jersey belongs to the football team.. I was honored to wear it.. I will leave it to the Commanders to make that decision.."
This situation brings a decades-long debate back to life among fans who believe numbers should be enshrined and those who do not. One thing the organization needs to get away from is "soft retiring" numbers by not officially retiring them, but also not giving them out. Number legacies either need to be captured and never used again, or embraced and passed on. A good example of a reused number through the years is 17 . Among those who have worn that number are Turk Edwards (who is in the Hall of Fame), Billy Kilmer, Doug Williams, Jason Campbell, and now, in this era, Terry McLaurin. In this situation, Theismann is making the right call by leaving the decision up to the team because it does two things at once. It puts the pressure back on the organization to finally decide the fate of the jersey number while allowing Theismann to come across as a team-first guy in the process. This is low-key a big moment for the new ownership group in terms of how they handle the legacy of the numbers moving forward. Daniel Snyder left the issue to fester in conversations among fans; let's hope, like many of the other things that left with him, that those days are over. To move forward on this, Washington has to ask itself a question. Do they believe adding Diggs is enough reason to put one of its most protected numbers back into circulation? If so, do it and move forward without crossing over this bridge again in the future. If not, retire the No. 7 next season and honor your legend while he is still alive.
Laremy Tunsil has made his intentions clear: after surgery, he is still going to help the younger guys on the offensive line even though he cannot currently help on the field. ESPN's John Keim reported Tuesday that Andrew Wylie said Tunsil told the offensive line he would return to Ashburn for treatment after surgery so he could remain around the team and continue helping the younger linemen he has been tutoring.
One thing to note on Laremy Tunsil: Andrew Wylie said he told the OL that he would return to Ashburn for his treatment post surgery so he can be around the team. Can still help the younger OLinemen he’s been tutoring.
Tunsil tore his left triceps muscle and is out indefinitely , which prompted the team to shift Brandon Coleman back to left tackle. This is beyond what most players would do and means that, while Washington loses his snaps, the team does not completely lose the influence and experience gained when they brought him into the offensive-line room. His third set of eyes could be far more helpful than any coach.

title: Brandon Coleman Steps Up and Daronte Jones Transforms the Defense | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
The Burgundy Roundup brings together the best Washington Commanders reporting, analysis, interviews, and other worthwhile reads from around the web, along with selected coverage from Commanders On SI.
While Day 10 of Commanders Training Camp was a shorter, padless session, it did have its moments. Several veterans received maintenance days, which shifted reps to younger players and roster-battle candidates ahead of Wednesday's joint session with Miami. On the day: Joshua Josephs continued forcing his way into the conversation, Antonio Williams produced multiple touchdowns, and Washington’s backup tight ends made several plays. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Allegretti with a helmet and jersey https://t.co/QpjXGnHc55 pic.twitter.com/YyoH89zT8k
The Commanders could use more tight ends to help Brandon Coleman -- Tunsil was part of a double-team pass block only 31.5% of the time; Coleman was part of one 42.1% of the time in each of his first two seasons. Washington also will use more play-action passes from under center -- designed to fool coverages and slow the pass rush. There's also quarterback Jayden Daniels, about whom one AFC executive said "covers up for a lot of sins." Indeed, in practice Daniels has excelled at sliding in the pocket to avoid pressure and find an open target. It helps, too, that Washington just signed receiver Stefon Diggs to pair with Terry McLaurin -- both of whom can create quick separation. And that would help offset the loss of a player such as Tunsil. But Coleman's play will matter as well. He did post a 92.3% pass block win rate the past two seasons. He also had a run block win rate of 77.2%, above the league average of 72.3% in that same period. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
John is joined by Commanders Safety Jeremy Reaves. They discussed Daronte Jones new defense, the Commanders defense this upcoming season, rookie Sonny Styles, and more!
Diggs wins with refined route running, tempo, and elite footwork. While the 32-year-old wide receiver has lost a step in terms of pure speed, he still has the ability to get the better of cornerbacks on the outside. That said, he thrives in the short to intermediate parts of the field and should be expected to run plenty of deep overs, high crossers and dig routes. Diggs is particularly adept at adjusting his routes to capitalize on space versus both man and zone coverage, with David Blough stating, “In just a couple days – he had four catches the other day, at least 2-3 today – the ball finds him because he finds space.” To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Daronte Jones, 47, was hired from Minnesota after excelling under Brian Flores, who oversaw a defense known for its complex disguises and loaded fronts . Plenty of that has carried over to Washington, where Jones has deployed fronts with three, four and five linemen and mixed and matched along the way. Jones has coached at every level during his two-decade coaching career, from high school through multiple college levels and the pros. He believes his teaching ability is one of his biggest strengths, which he attributes to working in the Louisiana high school system. “When you create a lesson plan, you have to pretty much hit on everyone’s learning styles because everyone learns differently,” Jones said. “We try to do that as coaches so that you’re hitting on every player in that room.” To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Dan Quinn calls Van Jefferson "exacting", and said QBs appreciate him always being in the right spot. Treylon Burks has slimmed down and Quinn said lighter has been able to go longer and faster for him. pic.twitter.com/zvGMuro840
"I'm getting to play everywhere. The shade, the two wide, the three, the four, the five, the six. I'm playing it all, man. I'm loving how I'm getting to just give guys different looks and be all over the place, man. And I think it's going to play to my strengths well, man. You know, give a lot of guys fits." title: Commanders Add LB Curtis Jacobs After Signing DT Byron Cowart
full_text:
The Washington Commanders worked out eight defensive players on Monday. The team liked what it saw from defensive tackle Byron Cowart and signed him Tuesday morning. Tuesday afternoon, they returned to that list and signed linebacker Curtis Jacobs.
We have signed LB Curtis Jacobs pic.twitter.com/ZnWtCxTxpr
The eight players in the workout group were DE Carlos Watkins, DT Byron Cowart, DT Fabien Lovett, DT Justin Rogers, LB Amari Burney, LB Power Echols, LB Devin Harper, and LB Curtis Jacobs. Washington has now signed two of those eight players, one defensive tackle and one linebacker. Jacobs has appeared in 12 NFL games, starting two, for the Patriots and Titans, respectively. He also has spent time on a few practice squads and was a draft pick of the DC Defenders of the UFL, where he had 46 tackles , added a sack, and recovered a fumble across 12 games, including the playoffs. Jacobs was signed for positional depth behind Kain Medrano and Ale Kaho; he can also provide some special teams help. Cowart was signed earlier Tuesday morning following DJ Davidson's unexpected retirement, which created an opening along the defensive front .
STAYING IN DC 😤 Curtis Jacobs is signing with the Washington Commanders! #UFLtoNFL pic.twitter.com/rGOnsQrBxd

title: The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ Tenth Training Camp Practice
full_text:
While Day 10 of Commanders Training Camp was a shorter, padless session, it did have its moments. Several veterans received maintenance days, which shifted reps to younger players and roster-battle candidates ahead of Wednesday's joint session with Miami. On the day: Joshua Josephs continued forcing his way into the conversation, Antonio Williams produced multiple touchdowns, and Washington’s backup tight ends made several plays.
Also do not see Rasul Douglas, Odafe Oweh, Jeremy McNichols, Jeremy Reaves, Amik Robertson….. https://t.co/1qgXlRDQL5
Josephs has been coming on strong as of late, and Tuesday offered up even more evidence that he will be involved somewhere in the edge rotation this season. Starting with the opening fourth-and-goal competition from the 9-yard line: Jayden Daniels completed the pass to Chig Okonkwo, but Josephs beat Brandon Coleman with a rip move quickly enough that the play might have been a sack in live football. Later in the day, Josephs was able to disrupt things again with another would-be sack, this time on Marcus Mariota. It will be interesting to watch Josephs line up against the Dolphins tackles Wednesday to get a good sense of what we are working with there. His quickness and motor are impressive. Antonio Williams took full advantage of several top receivers taking little or no work Tuesday by scoring multiple touchdowns, including one from Marcus Mariota during seven-on-seven work. He added another when Athan Kaliakmanis found Williams for a touchdown during the two-minute period. Stefon Diggs' arrival crowded the receivers room, thinning the chances guys below the top two get, meaning these are the days those guys need to dominate.
Tone in the end zone 🙌 @a_williams2022 | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/23c2UKwVwg
John Bates' injury-related absence has highlighted the battle for the fourth tight end, with more opportunities along the way for Lawrence Cager and Colson Yankoff. Cager grabbed two touchdowns from Mariota, including a seam route on the first play of the two-minute period that left him open for an uncontested score. Yankoff continued to receive a healthy number of targets and added to a camp in which his athleticism and receiving ability have consistently stood out. The two have been forcing the Commanders to decide whether they want a fourth tight end and then who it should be, all at the same time.
knee slide goes crazy @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/FAg9gcP1oz
Daniels was still able to create some positive plays despite the lighter session. That included a fourth-and-goal completion to Chig Okonkwo and other notable additional connections with Van Jefferson and Dyami Brown. Washington was not looking for a huge day for Daniels; maintaining the offense’s rhythm while Washington managed veteran workloads was enough heading into the joint session with Miami.
Trey Amos is dealing with the ankle injury suffered over the weekend, and being ruled out of Wednesday’s joint practice is less than ideal for him and the team's current situation. Amos only recently returned to the practice field, and the Miami session would have provided valuable competitive reps against unfamiliar receivers before the preseason opener. Washington expects to find out more on Amos’ recovery over the next few days. Nick Allegretti not being ready for the Miami session or the preseason game is a major disappointment. While it will give the team knowledge of what is behind him, it will also expose Daniels if there is a breakdown. Every missed Allegretti practice means another day for Washington to evaluate the center combinations it has been using in his absence. On a lighter note, Quinn said Allegretti should return to the field Sunday, and both he and John Bates were in uniform at practice Tuesday, working off to the side.
Good to see Allegretti out here getting some work in on the side field today. Hopefully it’s a positive step toward getting him back on the field soon. 🙌 pic.twitter.com/HfjtLsrRgs
Washington's maintenance plan made Day 10 into a session with more snaps for younger players. Several, including Josephs, Williams and the reserve tight ends, were able to do something with them. Wednesday will give the team a much more useful test against Miami rather than lining up against teammates. Amos’ absence was by far the biggest disappointment from Tuesday, while Allegretti’s expected Sunday return at least gives the staff a clearer timetable at center.
